findings.title: docker-compose.yml pins an image tag that has never existed in GHCR: the publish workflow only ever pushes v-prefixed tags, so the documented `docker compose up -d` quick start fails with manifest unknown
findings.description: docker-compose.yml:53 sets `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0`. The only thing that ever pushes to that registry is .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml, which fires on `push: tags: v*` (lines 5-6), sets `VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME}` (line 40), and pushes `$IMAGE:${VERSION}` and `$IMAGE:latest` (lines 53-54). GITHUB_REF_NAME for a tag push is the literal tag, so every published tag carries the leading `v`. I queried the public GHCR tag list anonymously (ghcr.io/v2/vulnradar/vulnradar/tags/list): it contains v1.9.2 through v3.7.2 plus `latest` plus the cosign `sha256-...` signature tags, and no bare `3.0.0`. README.md:79 and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:640 (Step 4) both instruct the operator to run `docker compose up -d` against this file, and app/docs/setup/page.tsx:684 gives `docker compose pull && docker compose up -d` as the Update operation. The compose comment at lines 48-51 also tells the operator to run `docker pull ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0` to fetch a digest. All of these reference a tag the registry does not have.
findings.impact: A self-hoster following the README or the setup docs never gets a running container. `docker compose up -d` aborts on the app service with `manifest unknown` before anything else in AUDIT-014#host-01 or #host-03 is even reached. This is upstream of every other self-host finding: the documented path stops at the image pull. AUDIT-013#deps-06 and AUDIT-014#host-05 both noticed the pin is stale or a no-op; neither noticed the tag does not exist at all.
findings.recommendation: Either change docker-compose.yml:53 to `ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:v3.7.2` (matching what docker-publish.yml actually pushes) or strip the `v` at publish time in docker-publish.yml:40 (`VERSION=${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}`) and push both `v`-prefixed and bare tags. Fix the pull command in the comment at docker-compose.yml:49 to match. Then add a CI step that asserts the tag referenced by docker-compose.yml resolves in the registry, so the next drift is caught before release.

findings.title: VERDICT: the documented self-host does not work. On an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and nothing in the running app ever writes the schema-meta row it demands
findings.description: Static trace only (docker and psql are not installed on this machine, nothing was executed). Boot path for a container started against an empty Postgres: Dockerfile:114-115 ENTRYPOINT tini + CMD npm start -> next start -> instrumentation.ts register() (instrumentation.ts:28). At instrumentation.ts:91 it runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS vulnradar_schema_meta, at :99 it SELECTs the single row, and at :105 `if (metaRes.rows.length === 0)` it prints the SCHEMA VERSION NOT SET box and calls process.exit(1) at :144. The 2,900 lines of CREATE TABLE statements start at :279, after that gate, so they never run. A repo-wide grep for vulnradar_schema_meta finds exactly two writers: scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:302 and scripts/migrate/_meta.mjs:69 (writeMeta). Neither is the app. The app never inserts that row under any code path, so the gate can never be satisfied by booting. The two commands the error box offers are also both dead ends on an empty DB: scripts/migrate/_detect.mjs:56 returns version:null when no fingerprint tables are present, and migrate.mjs:355 then aborts with "Could not detect a known schema version"; there is no empty-to-1.0.0 step in scripts/migrate/versions/. Only npm run db:create can bootstrap, and it is a side-by-side clone tool (scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:6-18) that creates a DIFFERENTLY NAMED database ("default ends in _v3", :725) and reads its DDL from resolve(ROOT, "instrumentation.ts") (:69), so it needs the source checkout, not the image. docker-compose.yml:100 sets restart: unless-stopped, so the app container crash-loops forever. Four separate docs assert the opposite: README.md:79-82, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:259-264 ("instrumentation.ts runs CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS for every table ... Look for Database schema verified successfully"), app/docs/setup/page.tsx:652-654, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1144-1147 ("Schema auto-creates on first boot; meta row is written on first scan via db:migrate"). The log line they tell the operator to look for exists at instrumentation.ts:3199, unreachable past the :144 exit.
findings.impact: A new self-hoster who follows README.md exactly gets a Postgres container that comes up healthy and an app container that restart-loops with a red box telling them to run one of two commands, one of which cannot work on an empty database and the other of which is not present in the image (see host-02). There is no documented path from a fresh checkout plus a Postgres string to a running instance. This is the headline claim of the project's Self-Hosting section and it is false as written.
findings.recommendation: In instrumentation.ts, split the metaRes.rows.length === 0 branch at :105 into two cases. If the public schema contains no application tables at all (query information_schema.tables for 'users'), treat it as a fresh install: fall through to the CREATE TABLE sequence at :279 and INSERT the meta row with schema_version = MIN_SCHEMA_VERSION at the end, next to the existing success log at :3199. Keep the current exit(1) only for the genuinely ambiguous case of a populated database with no meta row. Then correct README.md:78-82 and the three docs pages to describe whichever behaviour ships.

findings.title: The Dockerfile runtime stage copies five paths and never copies scripts/, so db:create, db:migrate, the admin Backup button and the self-updater's migrate step are all unrunnable inside the published image
findings.description: Static trace. The runner stage (Dockerfile:62) copies exactly five paths from the builder: public, .next, node_modules, package.json, next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79). scripts/, instrumentation.ts and the rest of the source tree are not copied. Every npm script in package.json:29-40 resolves to node scripts/<something>.mjs, so inside the container all of them fail with a module-not-found on a path that does not exist. Concretely: (1) README.md:82 tells the operator to run `docker compose exec app npm run db:create`, which runs node scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs (package.json:31), absent; and because of host-01 the container is not even running, so `docker compose exec` fails first with a container-not-running error. (2) app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:545-548 tells the operator to run npm run db:migrate "inside the app container" after a schema change; same absence. (3) The admin panel Backup button, documented at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:407-414 and promoted in .env.example's DATABASE BACKUPS block, goes POST /api/v3/admin/backup -> lib/backup/run-backup.ts:33, which spawns join(appRoot, "scripts", "backup-db.mjs"); absent, so the job always fails. (4) The self-updater runs npm run db:migrate -- --yes at lib/updater/apply.ts:353; absent. Dockerfile:88-92 installs postgresql-client specifically so that "scripts/migrate/migrate.mjs backs up the database to databases/ before applying any schema changes", a package installed for a script the image does not contain. AUDIT-013#deps-05 already noted a different Dockerfile comment describing something that does not exist; this is the same class of drift but with functional consequences.
findings.impact: Every documented in-container maintenance operation fails: initialise the database, migrate after an upgrade, take a backup from the admin panel, and self-update. Combined with host-01 there is no way to recover a self-hosted instance from inside the container at all, and the operator must have a separate Node + source checkout with network access to the same Postgres.
findings.recommendation: Add `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/scripts ./scripts` and `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/instrumentation.ts ./instrumentation.ts` to the runner stage after Dockerfile:79 (create-fresh-db.mjs:69 reads instrumentation.ts as its v3 schema source, so both are needed). Also copy lib/ if any script imports from it. Then re-verify that `docker compose exec app npm run db:create` resolves before README.md:82 is left pointing at it.

findings.title: Every semantic colour used as text fails WCAG AA in light mode, including the severity badge at 1.66:1, while /legal/accessibility publishes a WCAG 2.1 AA conformance claim
findings.description: The light and dark themes share one value for every accent token. app/globals.css:178 sets --primary: 213 94% 68% and the .dark block at :230 repeats the identical triplet. The same is true of --severity-critical/high/medium/low (:204-207 vs :249-252, identical) and --warning (:219 vs :264). Those values were tuned for a near-black ground, and the in-app idiom is to paint the colour as TEXT on a 10 to 15 percent tint of itself: components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78 pairs tone.text with tone.surface, and SeverityBadge at :106-114 applies both to the same span. I computed the sRGB contrast ratios directly from the token triplets in globals.css against --card (light 213 22% 95%, dark 224 18% 9%). Light mode: severity medium 1.66:1, high 2.15:1, low 2.67:1, critical 2.79:1, info 3.40:1. Dark mode the same badges are 7.77, 5.34, 4.88, 4.17 and 4.20:1. The same split hits the rest of the accent layer in light mode: text-primary on bg-card is 2.25:1 and on the bg-primary/10 active-nav pill used by app/admin/page.tsx:1078 and app/profile/page.tsx:757 it is 2.08:1; text-[hsl(var(--warning))] on its own /10 tint (app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:377, components/teams/teams-types.ts:64) is 1.90:1; text-[hsl(var(--success))] on card (components/history/history-stats.tsx:77, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:224) is 2.98:1; text-destructive on card is 3.37:1 and on destructive/10 is 2.97:1. Only the neutral layer is safe: muted-foreground is 5.02:1 on card and foreground is 15.86:1. globals.css:179-185 shows the team already reasoned about contrast in the opposite direction (they darkened --primary-foreground because white on the primary fill measured about 2.5:1) but never checked colour-as-text on a light surface. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:54 states conformance with WCAG 2.1 Level AA and :73 says "We maintain sufficient color contrast ratios between text and backgrounds". Merged from a11y-02 and a11y-03, which an independent agent derived with its own contrast calculator and reached the identical 1.66:1 for the medium severity badge. Their additional specifics: text-primary measures 1.99:1 against the light page background across 478 usages including the links inside the accessibility statement itself, and the severity tokens are used as TEXT colour 83 times via text-[hsl(var(--severity-*))]. Only --severity-info differs between the two theme blocks; every other accent token is byte-identical. Verified during the merge: app/globals.css:178 and :230 both read `--primary: 213 94% 68%`.
findings.impact: A user on the light theme cannot read the single most important visual encoding in the product. The MEDIUM severity chip on a finding row is 1.66:1, roughly the contrast of pale yellow on white, so the word disappears and only the 6px dot survives, which is exactly the colour-alone encoding the severity-badge docblock at :30-34 says it exists to avoid. Every link, every active sidebar item, every SSL-grade cell and every success or warning count on /dashboard, /history, /assets, /shares and /browser is in the same state. The published accessibility statement is measurably false, which matters for a security product sold to teams who ask for a VPAT.
findings.recommendation: Split the accent tokens into a fill value and a foreground value instead of retuning the fills (retuning --primary would move every bg-primary button and the focus ring). In app/globals.css add to :root only: --primary-text: 213 94% 43%; --destructive-text: 0 84% 43%; --success-text: 142 76% 26%; --warning-text: 38 92% 29%; --severity-critical-text: 0 84% 41%; --severity-high-text: 25 95% 33%; --severity-medium-text: 45 93% 27%; --severity-low-text: 210 90% 40%. Each of those lightness values is the first one that clears 4.5:1 against its own existing 10 to 15 percent tint on --card. In the .dark block define the same eight names as aliases of the current fills so dark mode is byte-identical to today. Then change components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:41,49,57,65,73 so `text` reads text-[hsl(var(--severity-X-text))] while `solid` (dots, rails, SeverityDistribution segments) keeps the current fill, and add the four new utilities to the tailwind.config.mjs colour map so text-primary-text and friends exist. Finally sweep the literal token uses: text-primary in app/admin/page.tsx:1078, app/profile/page.tsx:757, text-[hsl(var(--success))] in components/history/history-stats.tsx, assets-stats.tsx, shares-stats.tsx and app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:224, and text-[hsl(var(--warning))] in app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:377 and components/teams/teams-types.ts:64.

findings.title: The skip link in the root layout targets #main-content, which the three shared page shells never render, so it is inert on the docs, the SEO pages, /host, /shared and /public-scans
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:171-176 renders a single skip link with href="#main-content" on every route. Only 19 page files define that id: app/dashboard, /history, /profile, /admin, /teams, /repos, /shares, /assets, /attack-surface, /badge, /pricing, /landing, /browser/[id], the four /checkout pages and app/admin/ai-chats/[id]. The three shared shells that render the remaining pages do not. components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60-62 opens <main className={...}> with no id and no tabIndex, and it is the shell for app/changelog, app/compare, app/contact, app/host/[hostname], app/public-scans, app/security and app/shared/[token]. lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19 is <main className="flex-1">{children}</main>, also with no id, and it is the shell for app/checks, app/checks/[id] (about 750 generated pages), app/checks/category/[category], app/alternatives, app/alternatives/[competitor], app/tools, app/tools/api-scanner and app/tools/link-checker. components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:76-78 names its main id="docs-content", not main-content, covering all 20 docs pages. app/donate/page.tsx:24 has no <main> element at all. Both counterexamples that do work, components/auth/auth-layout.tsx:25-28 and components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:95-98, set id="main-content" and tabIndex={-1} together, which is the correct pattern. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:93 states "Skip navigation links allow users to bypass repetitive content". Merged from a11y-04, which additionally names the changelog shell among the surfaces whose skip-link target does not exist.
findings.impact: A keyboard or screen-reader user pressing Tab on the site's whole public and documentation surface, including the two shareable report pages (/host/[hostname] and /shared/[token]) that are the product's main outbound link, activates the skip link and the focus does not move. They then tab through the full nav on every page. The pages where this works are almost entirely the signed-in ones, so the visitors most likely to be evaluating the product are the ones it fails for. The accessibility statement claims otherwise.
findings.recommendation: Three one-line edits. components/shared/public-page-shell.tsx:60: add id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} to the <main>. lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:19: same, <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="flex-1">. components/docs/docs-shell.tsx:77: rename id="docs-content" to id="main-content" and add tabIndex={-1}, then update any in-page anchor that referenced docs-content (grep shows the docs TOC does not, so this is safe). Wrap app/donate/page.tsx:24's content div in <main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>. Then add a test in tests/ that renders each shell and asserts one element with id="main-content", so a fourth shell cannot regress it.

findings.title: Every arrow and section sign in a PDF report renders as mojibake, because the Helvetica fonts are declared with no /Encoding while UTF-8 bytes are written straight into the content stream
findings.description: generatePdfReport declares its two fonts as `<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Helvetica >>` and `/Helvetica-Bold` (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:449-452) with no `/Encoding` entry, so a viewer falls back to the font's built-in single-byte StandardEncoding. Text reaches the content stream unchanged: escPdf (:50-52) escapes only backslash and parentheses, addText writes the raw JS string into a literal at :86, and the whole document is emitted with `new TextEncoder().encode(pdf)` at :513, which is UTF-8. Every multi-byte character therefore arrives as N separate single-byte glyph codes. Non-ASCII characters are not hypothetical in this data: lib/scanner/checks-data holds 96 of them, and they sit in exactly the fields the PDF prints. secrets-extended.json entry [5] fixSteps[0] is "Revoke the token immediately via GitHub Settings → Developer Settings → Personal Access Tokens", and at least ten more fixSteps in that file use U+2192 (PyPI, Cloudflare, Tailscale, Algolia, Mapbox, PagerDuty, Datadog, Supabase). email.json[11].explanation contains "RFC 5321 §5.1". headers.json[96].codeExamples[0].code contains two arrows. Those fields are printed at pdf-report.ts:372 (fixSteps), :364 (explanation) and :386 (codeExamples). U+2192 is E2 86 92 in UTF-8, so one arrow becomes three glyphs. Note the /Length values are byte-correct (:460), and the xref byte-offset fix documented at :486-490 already exists, so the file is structurally valid: this is purely a rendering defect. Neither the Markdown (lib/reports/markdown-report.ts) nor the SARIF (lib/reports/sarif-report.ts) export has this problem, so the PDF is the only format that corrupts the text.
findings.impact: The PDF is the artifact a user forwards to a manager or a client, and /docs/reports/page.tsx:134 sells it as exactly that ("hand a PDF to a stakeholder"). The garbling lands on the remediation steps of secret-exposure findings, which are the highest-stakes instructions the scanner produces. A leaked-GitHub-token finding tells the reader to go to "GitHub Settings a†' Developer Settings", which reads as a broken tool and undermines the report's credibility at the exact moment it is being used to argue for a fix.
findings.recommendation: Two-line fix plus one guard. In lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:449-452 add `/Encoding /WinAnsiEncoding` to both font objects, then transcode text to CP1252 bytes before writing it: extend escPdf (:50) to map each code point through a small WinAnsi table and emit anything unmappable as a PDF octal escape (\\NNN), falling back to an ASCII transliteration for characters WinAnsi has no slot for (U+2192 -> "->", U+2018/2019 -> "'", U+201C/201D -> '"', U+2026 -> "..."). Because the string is then single-byte, also change line 460 and 470 to compute /Length over the transcoded bytes. Add a test in tests/lib/reports/ that renders a finding whose fixSteps contain U+2192 and U+00A7 and asserts the emitted stream contains no byte above 0x7F outside an escape.

findings.title: Delete the elapsed-seconds clock from the scanning card, and with it the 500ms re-render loop and the fake timer-driven progress it secretly also feeds
findings.description:
This is the executable removal spec for AUDIT-011#scan-05, which filed the problem but conditioned the fix on AUDIT-011#scan-01 landing first. The section brief overrides that: remove the timer regardless. New material below is the full dependency set that scan-05 did not trace.

The clock is four pieces, all still at the lines scan-05 cited. components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 seeds `const [startedAt] = useState(() => Date.now())`. :119 holds `elapsed`. :148-151 runs `setInterval(() => setElapsed(Date.now() - startedAt), 500)` for the whole life of the component, forcing a full re-render of the card and its 18-to-20-row checklist twice a second purely to repaint one string. :271-273 renders it through `formatElapsed` (:77-81), which floors to whole seconds, so a displayed `17s` means at least 17.0 real seconds. `formatElapsed` has exactly one call site (verified by grep across app/, components/, lib/, tests/).

The part scan-05 missed: `elapsed` is not only the readout. :157-161 derives `simulatedStep = Math.floor(elapsed / STEP_MS)` and `simulatedSettling`, and :189-193 uses both whenever `hasRealProgress` is false. So deleting only the render at :271-273 leaves a dead 500ms interval and a fabricated progress bar behind it.

`hasRealProgress` (:153) is `categoriesTotal > 0`, which comes from the poll. Two windows where it is false and the bar is therefore pure fiction at STEP_MS = 1200ms per step: (a) every scan's first 0 to 2000ms, because app/api/v3/scan/route.ts computes `categoriesTotal` at :339 and then throws it away, returning only `{ scanId, status: "running" }` at :454, so the client cannot know the denominator until the first poll lands; (b) the entire authenticated-scan path, because app/dashboard/page.tsx:585 gates polling on `if (!auth)`, so `setScanProgress` is never called for a POST to API.SCAN_AUTHENTICATED and `categoriesTotal` stays 0 for the whole run.

On a slow or stalled connection the two failure modes compound: see scanui-05. The bar freezes at its last polled step while the clock keeps counting, which is the worst possible combination of the two signals.
findings.impact: The product's headline claim is speed, and the single number a user watches on every scan contradicts it. Removing the readout alone is not enough: it leaves a twice-a-second re-render of a 20-row list running for the length of every scan, and leaves a progress bar that is honest during a polled scan and invented during the first two seconds of it and for the whole of every authenticated scan, with nothing on screen distinguishing the two.
findings.recommendation:
In components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx delete, in this order: the render block at :271-273, `formatElapsed` at :77-81, the `elapsed` state at :119, the interval at :148-151, `startedAt` at :118, and `STEP_MS` at :42 together with `simulatedStep`/`simulatedSettling` at :157-161 and the `else` branch at :189-193.

That leaves `hasRealProgress` needing to be true from the first frame. Make it so with a one-line server change: `app/api/v3/scan/route.ts` already has `categoriesTotal` in hand at :339, so include it in both returns at :442 and :454 (`{ scanId, status: "running", categoriesTotal }`). In app/dashboard/page.tsx `runScan`, seed `setScanProgress({ currentCategory: null, categoriesCompleted: 0, categoriesTotal: data.categoriesTotal ?? 0 })` immediately after `setRunningScanId(scanId)` at :594. Do the same in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts if it returns the same shape.

The authenticated path has no progress source at all, so do not fake one: pass a new `indeterminate` prop when `auth` is set, and render the family list with no per-row state and the bar as a single `motion-safe:animate-pulse motion-reduce:opacity-100` track, with the line "Signing in, then running every family". An honest indeterminate state is better than a 1200ms-per-step fiction.

Do not replace the clock with the server-reported engine duration on this screen either. `result.duration` already lands on the completed view as the "Scan duration" stat (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:303-310), which is the right place for it: a number that appears after the fact reads as a measurement, the same number ticking up during the wait reads as a countdown. What goes in its place is scanui-02.

findings.title: History search, tag filter, pagination and the "N scans on record" count all operate on a hard 100-row window, so a scan that is still inside retention is unfindable
findings.description: GET /api/v3/history returns at most HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS rows (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:128 and :138, ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC LIMIT), and that setting defaults to 100 (lib/config/config-values.ts:640, CONFIG_HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS = 100). app/history/page.tsx:222-236 fetches that one capped page into `scans`, and every user-facing operation then runs client-side over it: the URL search box at :406, the tag filter at :408, usePagination(filtered, pageSize) at :423, and the header count at :580 which renders `{scans.length} scans on record`. The same capped call feeds the Compare host picker (app/compare/page.tsx:40-52), so hosts older than the newest 100 scans never appear there either. Free plan allows 25 scans a day and elite 500, so the window fills in days or hours. Merged from qols-15, filed independently while auditing information hierarchy. Its additional detail: /dashboard shows the true COUNT(*) from the same session, so the two pages disagree with each other about how many scans the account has.
findings.impact: A user who scanned staging.example.com three weeks ago and has run 150 scans since types "staging" into the history search and is told nothing matches, for a scan that exists and is inside their retention window. No message explains that only part of their history was loaded. The count under the History heading also plateaus at 100 permanently and reads as the account's true scan total, so paid users see a number that contradicts their usage. Compare silently cannot diff older hosts for the same reason.
findings.recommendation: Move search, tag filter and pagination server-side. Add `search`, `tag`, `page` and `limit` query params to app/api/v3/history/route.ts and push the substring match into the SQL WHERE clause alongside the existing retention predicate, returning `{ scans, total }`. In app/history/page.tsx replace the client `filtered` computation at :404-410 with a debounced fetch keyed on the filter state, drive usePagination from the server `total`, and source the :580 count from `total` rather than `scans.length`. Do the same for Compare: add GET /api/v3/history/hosts returning host plus scan-count rows so app/compare/page.tsx:40 stops pulling the full list. Until that lands, at minimum render "showing the most recent 100 scans" above the filter row so an empty result is explainable.

findings.title: Rescan in history starts a background job and then shows nothing at all: no progress, no result, no error, and the menu item is never disabled
findings.description: handleRescan (app/history/page.tsx:267-278) POSTs to /api/v3/scan and on res.ok awaits fetchHistory() then clears `rescanning`. But POST /api/v3/scan is a background job that returns { scanId, status: "running" } immediately (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:443 and :454), so the history refetch fires milliseconds after the job is queued and cannot contain the finished scan. Nothing here polls /api/v3/scan/status/[id], unlike the dashboard which does at app/dashboard/page.tsx:597. The trigger (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221-231) is a DropdownMenuItem with no `disabled`, so it stays clickable while `rescanning` is set. Failure is invisible too: there is no !res.ok branch and the bare catch at :276 swallows everything.
findings.impact: The user opens the row menu, clicks Rescan, sees a spinning icon for about a quarter of a second, and the list is identical. Nothing says a scan started, nothing says when it finished, nothing says if it was refused. The rational reaction is to click again, which burns another scan against the daily cap with no warning, and a rate-limit or plan-cap 429 produces exactly the same visible outcome as success.
findings.recommendation: Make Rescan behave like the dashboard's own scan. After the POST, put the returned `scanId` into state and reuse the poll loop from app/dashboard/page.tsx:128-165 (extract pollScanStatus into lib/scanner/poll-scan-status.ts and import it from both), showing the row in a scanning state driven by the server's categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal, then replace the row in place on completion. Add disabled={rescanning === scan.id} to the DropdownMenuItem at components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221. Add a !res.ok branch that surfaces data.error, routing the daily-limit case into the PremiumUpgradeModal the dashboard already mounts at app/dashboard/page.tsx:972. The cheaper interim fix is to navigate to /dashboard?scan=<url> on click and let the existing scanning UI own the whole thing.

findings.title: On a phone a history row has no actions at all: rescan, open-URL and view-details are desktop-only, and on desktop the trigger is invisible until hover
findings.description: The entire row action cluster is wrapped in a div classed `hidden sm:flex items-center justify-end w-12 shrink-0` (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:199), so below 640px the DropdownMenu at :200-242 containing View details, Rescan and Open URL is not rendered at all. The only remaining affordance on a phone is tapping the row body at :80. The severity breakdown (:152) and the source badge (:145) are `hidden sm:flex` too. Above 640px the trigger is `h-8 w-8 p-0 opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` (:206), so it is invisible until the pointer enters the row, and a touch device never produces a hover.
findings.impact: Rescanning a URL you scanned last week, the most common repeat action in this product, is impossible from a phone. There is no fallback: the mobile row shows no URL-open link and no per-scan menu. Phone users can read history but never act on it. The mobile meta strip at :246 also drops the per-severity counts in favour of a bare findings total, which removes the one signal that decides whether a row is worth opening.
findings.recommendation: Below sm, render a trailing chevron button at h-11 w-11 on each row that opens a Sheet (components/ui/sheet.tsx already exists and today has exactly one consumer, components/scanner/header.tsx:215) listing View details, Rescan, Open URL and Copy URL as full-width 44px rows. Above sm, change :206 from `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` to `sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100` so the button is always present on touch, matching what components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118 already gets right. Also surface the worst-severity count on the mobile meta strip so the row still tells you what it found.

findings.title: Every share and privacy mutation fails silently, so a failed "revoke share link" or "make private" is indistinguishable from a successful one
findings.description: Four mutations that change who can see a scan all discard failure. app/shares/page.tsx:121-143 (revoke share link) calls setConfirmRevoke(null) at :124 before the request fires, has no !res.ok branch, and logs to console at :140, so the dialog closes either way and the failure path looks exactly like success minus the row disappearing. app/shares/page.tsx:99-119 (toggle publicly-listed) is console.error only at :117, so on failure the Switch at components/shares/shares-row.tsx:162 silently snaps back. components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:331-349 (make public/private) has no !res.ok branch and a catch commented "Silently fail" at :345. components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:282-307 (create share link) guards on `if (res.ok && data.token)` at :297 with no else, and its catch at :302 is also commented "Silently fail".
findings.impact: A user who clicks Revoke on a share link, confirms, and sees the dialog close believes a public report URL is dead. If the DELETE 500s or 403s the link is still live and still serving their scan. Same shape for Make private: the menu item returns to its previous label with no explanation, so the user cannot tell whether the scan is still feeding the public /host page. A failed share creation looks like a broken button: the item says "Sharing...", reverts to "Share this scan", and no modal appears.
findings.recommendation: Give all four a real failure path: an !res.ok branch that reads data.error, and a catch that surfaces it. The cheapest consistent vehicle is the toast already mounted at app/layout.tsx:195 (see qolf-06). For the revoke specifically, move setConfirmRevoke(null) at app/shares/page.tsx:124 to after a successful response and keep the dialog open showing the error on failure, exactly as app/history/page.tsx:288-290 already does for Clear history. Delete both "Silently fail" comments rather than propagating them: the one at components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:303 cites the old ShareButton as precedent for the behaviour.

findings.title: Saving scan notes and renaming a team both discard the user's text on failure while closing the editor as if it saved
findings.description: handleSaveNotes (app/history/page.tsx:389-397) PATCHes /api/v3/history/{id} and does `if (res.ok) setScanNotes(notes)` with no else and no try/catch anywhere in the chain, so a network failure is an unhandled promise rejection. Its caller components/history/history-notes.tsx:22-27 awaits it then unconditionally runs setSaving(false) and setEditing(false), collapsing the editor. The dashboard copy at app/dashboard/page.tsx:375-387 is the same shape with an explicit `catch { /* ignore */ }`. app/teams/page.tsx:428-456 (rename team) is the only handler on that page with no !res.ok branch, an empty catch at :451, and a finally at :453-456 that closes the name editor regardless.
findings.impact: A user types a paragraph of remediation notes on a scan, clicks Save, the editor closes, and the notes are gone with no message. Because the editor closed, the natural read is that it worked. The team rename case is worse in one respect: on failure the heading snaps back to the old name with no explanation, so a rejected rename (duplicate name, insufficient role) reads as the UI having eaten the edit.
findings.recommendation: Change onSave in components/history/history-notes.tsx to return a boolean and only close the editor on true, keeping the textarea populated and rendering the server error inline underneath on false. In app/history/page.tsx:389 and app/dashboard/page.tsx:375 add the !res.ok branch reading data.error plus a real catch. In app/teams/page.tsx:428 move setEditingName(false) out of the finally into the res.ok branch and route the error into the page's existing actionError banner (declared :78, rendered :515-532), which every other handler on that page already uses.

findings.title: Admin "Run Cleanup Now" deletes rows across the whole database with no confirmation, while resetting a single setting in the same file opens a dialog
findings.description: runCleanup (components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:371-383) POSTs to /api/v3/admin/cleanup directly from the button's onClick at :605, with no dialog of any kind. The adjacent copy at :597-599 states what it does: it deletes expired keys, old scan history per plan retention, audit logs older than 365 days, and other stale database rows, across every account. In the same component, resetting one system setting back to its default (an action that is undone by simply re-entering the value) does get a full ConfirmDialog at :756, reached from components/admin/features/settings-field.tsx:268. Every other destructive admin action in the repo is gated by either AdminPasswordConfirmDialog or SaveConfirmationModal; this and the staff-invite revoke at components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:186 are the only two holes.
findings.impact: The single most destructive control in the product, a database-wide purge affecting every user's scan history, is one mis-click on an unremarkable outline button in a settings panel, and there is no undo (qolf-09). An operator scrolling the system settings page and clicking what looks like a maintenance utility deletes other people's data. The inconsistency makes it worse: because trivial actions on the same page open dialogs, the absence of one here reads as a signal that this button is safe.
findings.recommendation: Wrap runCleanup in the AdminPasswordConfirmDialog (components/admin/shared/admin-password-confirm-dialog.tsx) that already gates delete_scans and delete_user, and have the dialog body render a dry-run count first: add a GET mode to /api/v3/admin/cleanup that returns the row counts it would delete per table, so the operator confirms against real numbers rather than a description. Add the same gate to the staff-invite revoke at components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:186. Then remove the ConfirmDialog on reset-to-default at :756, which is buying nothing.

findings.title: /admin is 20 tabs grouped by data model inside one 1,683-line client component, so the three tasks an operator actually performs each cross three to seven of them
findings.description:
The whole admin surface is one client component. `VALID_TABS` (app/admin/page.tsx:112-133) declares 20 destinations, `ActiveTab` (:152-172) repeats the same 20 as a union, and `NAV_GROUPS_RAW` (:689-835) sorts them into 6 groups: User Management (users, teams, admins), Security (access-rules, blocked-data, security-alerts, audit), Communications (broadcast, notifications, ai-chats, support-tickets), Content (content), Billing (billing-overview), System (settings, updater, backup, queue-status, error-logs, email-logs, engine-feedback). Every group name is a data-model noun, not a job. The System group alone holds 7 unrelated destinations that share nothing except not fitting elsewhere: an update installer, a backup runner, a scanner-queue gauge, two log viewers, a settings editor and a detection-tuning tool. Content is a group of one. Billing is a group of one. The panel body is 20 sibling `{activeTab === X && <Manager/>}` lines (:1182-1674) with no route split, and AUDIT-012#fe-11 already measured the cost: 22 eagerly imported managers in one 1,333 KB route. The growth is visible in the leftovers: a 31-entry toast-label map inlined at :530-562, a stale 5-tab table still exported from components/admin/config.ts:7-17 (AUDIT-013#dead-01), and an empty app/api/v3/admin/bulk directory (AUDIT-011#bulk-06).

Measured click cost of the three most common operator tasks today.

A) Resolve a support ticket that needs the requester's account state. 1 click Support in the nav, 2 click the ticket, 3 select and copy the requester email (support-inbox.tsx:253 renders `owner_email` as plain text, no link), 4 click Users in the nav (handleTabChange at :869-876 calls setSelectedUser(null) and rewrites the URL, so the open ticket is gone), 5 click the search box and paste, wait the 300 ms debounce at :599, 6 click the user row, 7 click Support again, 8 click the ticket again to re-read it. Seven clicks plus a copy-paste, and the ticket view is rebuilt from scratch twice.

B) The morning check, is anything wrong right now. The panel lands on `activeTab = "users"` (:203). Scanner Queue is 1 click, Error Logs 2, Security Alerts 3, Backups 4, Email Logs 5, Support 6. Six clicks, six panels that each refetch on mount with their own poll interval, and the operator does the staleness arithmetic on the backup date themselves. Only one of the 20 nav items carries any status indicator at all (the updater dot, :1087-1092).

C) Apply a support fix to one user, for example reset a daily scan limit. Type in the search box, 1 click the row, then scroll past Overview, Account Management, Staff Role and Badges and Admin Notes to reach Support Actions (user-detail-panel.tsx:1872), 2 click the right card out of 21 laid out in a `grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3` (:1894), 3 confirm. Three clicks, but the cost is scanning 21 near-identical cards, not the clicks.
findings.impact: An operator cannot form a mental model of the panel from its navigation, because the navigation describes the database rather than the work. Cross-referencing is the normal case in support and the panel makes it the expensive case: task A costs seven clicks and destroys the operator's place twice. Task B, the one that protects the service, costs six clicks and is therefore skipped, which is how the failures AUDIT-012#obs-02 and AUDIT-012#obs-03 found stay invisible. New destinations get appended to whichever group is least wrong, so the drift compounds.
findings.recommendation:
Regroup by operator job and split the route. Seven sections, 17 destinations, one home.

1. Operations (new default landing, replaces users as the initial tab at app/admin/page.tsx:203). Home view described in qols-02. Children: Scanner Queue, Error Logs, Email Logs, Backups, Updater. This merges the five System-group destinations that are all one question, is the machine healthy.
2. People. Users (search-first, see below), Teams, Staff and Invites (today's Active Staff plus the invite modal from staff-list.tsx).
3. Support. Tickets, AI Chats. Moves ai-chats out of Communications: reading a user's conversation is support and moderation work, not messaging.
4. Trust and Safety. Security Alerts, Access Rules, Blocked Data, Hosts and Shares (today's single-item Content group). Merges four scattered destinations into the one job, deciding what a user or an IP is allowed to do.
5. Billing. Billing Overview, plus a gifted-subscriptions list (today gifts are only visible per-user through user-detail-panel.tsx:2251).
6. Messaging. Broadcast, Notifications. Both are tell users something; today they sit in Communications next to two support tools.
7. Configuration. Settings, Engine Feedback, Audit Log.

Searchable rather than browsable: Users, Audit Log, Error Logs, Email Logs, AI Chats are all logs you query. Users should open on a search field with recent-activity results underneath, not a paginated directory of every account.

Mechanics: give each destination its own route segment under app/admin/(section)/, which deletes the 20-branch conditional at :1182-1674 and fixes AUDIT-012#fe-11 for free. Move the tab table out of app/admin/page.tsx into a single exported ADMIN_SECTIONS in components/admin/config.ts (replacing the stale ADMIN_TABS at config.ts:7-17), keyed by permission exactly as NAV_GROUPS_RAW already does, and derive VALID_TABS, ActiveTab and the mobile TOC from it.

After the restructure: task A becomes 1 click (the requester name in the ticket header opens an inline account panel, see qols-03) with zero navigation. Task B becomes 0 clicks, the home view is the landing page, and a click only to drill into whatever is red. Task C stays 3 clicks; the win there is time-to-find, addressed separately in qols-06.

findings.title: The admin landing view is ten headcount aggregates, none of which can go red, so there is no screen anywhere that answers whether anything is wrong right now
findings.description:
The panel opens on the users tab (app/admin/page.tsx:203) and the only thing above the user table is two StatBar rows of five counters each (:1108-1179): Total Users, Total Scans, Scans 24h, 2FA Enabled, Disabled, New Users 7d, Active API Keys, Active Webhooks, Schedules, Shared Scans. Every one is a plain COUNT from the stats query at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:329-338. Not one can indicate a fault, and the code comment at app/admin/page.tsx:1103-1107 concedes they are not even clickable because the admin API takes only page, limit and search.

The signals that could go red exist but are each one nav click away and none is summarised anywhere. Scanner backlog: components/admin/features/queue-status-manager.tsx:72 computes `backedUp` and renders a destructive badge at :108-116, but only while that tab is mounted. Backup freshness: backup-manager.tsx:199-201 prints the newest file's mtime as plain text with no expected-interval comparison, so a backup that stopped running three weeks ago looks identical to one that ran this morning apart from a date the operator has to reason about. Security alerts, error logs, email delivery failures and support tickets are the same shape. Of the 20 nav items rendered at :1059-1094 exactly one carries a status indicator: the updater dot at :1087-1092.

This matters because AUDIT-012 found two failures that are silent by construction: #obs-02, a scheduled database backup that fails on every run still reports success to the failure escalator and writes no log line; #obs-03, worker failure escalation only sees pass-level throws, so a worker where every item failed resets its streak to zero and never alerts. Both are precisely the class of fault a health view exists to catch, and neither has any surface in the panel today.
findings.impact: Nobody finds out the service is degraded from the admin panel. Backups can be dead for weeks (obs-02) and the Backups tab will show a stale date that reads as normal. A worker where every item errors (obs-03) shows no signal at all. The scanner queue can be backed up and the operator only learns when a user complains. On a service with about 50 real users and no on-call rotation, the admin panel is the whole monitoring story, and its front page is a vanity dashboard.
findings.recommendation:
Add app/admin/(operations)/page.tsx as the panel's default landing view and change the initial activeTab at app/admin/page.tsx:203 to it. Render one status list, not a card grid: rows of `label / value / state`, each row green, amber or red, ordered worst-first, following the divided-list idiom in design-language.md D4 rather than adding a ninth stat strip. Rows to include, all buildable from endpoints that already exist:

- Scanner queue: reuse computeBackedUp and the stale-age thresholds already in components/admin/features/queue-status-utils.ts (STALE_PENDING_MS, STALE_RUNNING_MS). Red when backed up, amber when the oldest pending scan exceeds the stale threshold.
- Failed scans in the last 24 h: `counts.failedLast24h` from GET /api/v3/admin/queue-status. Amber above zero, red above a configurable share of completed.
- Backup age: from GET /api/v3/admin/backup's lastBackupAt, compared against the configured schedule interval rather than printed raw. Red when older than two intervals. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-02.
- Worker last success: add a per-worker last-success timestamp read and show age. This is the row that would have surfaced AUDIT-012#obs-03.
- Unresolved security alerts, error-log volume in the last hour, bounced or failed emails in the last 24 h, open support tickets, outstanding staff invites, update available.

Each row links to the tab that owns it. Mirror the worst state onto the nav item as a coloured dot, reusing the exact markup already at app/admin/page.tsx:1087-1092 so the operator sees a fault from any tab. Keep the ten headcount counters, but demote them to a collapsed Growth strip below the status list or move them to Billing Overview; they answer a business question, not an operational one.

findings.title: The `main` branch has no branch protection and no ruleset, so not one CI job is a required check and every ci.yml comment claiming a step blocks merges is false
findings.description: I queried the public GitHub API for this repository. `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/branches/main` returns `protected: false` with `protection.required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"` and empty `contexts` and `checks` arrays; `GET /repos/VulnRadar/vulnradar.dev/rules/branches/main` returns an empty array, so no repository ruleset applies either. ci.yml runs five jobs on `pull_request: branches: [main]` (lint, typecheck, test, extension, build) and its comments assert they gate merges: line 43 "format drift should block merges", lines 65-66 "removed `continue-on-error: true`. Typecheck must block merges", line 70 "block merges on high/critical CVEs in runtime deps". None of these are required checks, so a red CI run is advisory only and the merge button stays green. The same absence means .github/CODEOWNERS is decorative: CODEOWNERS auto-requests reviewers but only enforces review when "Require review from Code Owners" is set in branch protection, and it is not. Direct pushes to main are also unrestricted.
findings.impact: The entire CI investment (SHA-pinned actions, a Prettier gate, a hard typecheck, an `npm audit` gate on 71 runtime dependencies, an extension build, a Next.js build) enforces nothing. Broken TypeScript, a failing test suite, or a high-severity CVE in a production dependency can be merged or pushed straight to main with a single click, and the next `v*` tag turns that into a published image and a GitHub release. It also means the two-person review flow the CODEOWNERS file describes is not actually required for lib/auth, lib/billing, or .github.
findings.recommendation: Add a ruleset (or classic branch protection) on `main` that requires the Lint, Typecheck, Test, Extension, and Build check names, requires at least one approving review, requires review from code owners, and blocks force pushes and direct pushes. Commit the ruleset JSON under .github/ so the configuration is reviewable in-repo rather than living only in the web UI.

findings.title: Dependabot auto-merge calls `gh pr merge --auto` into an unprotected main, so with zero required checks a dependency bump merges the instant it opens, before CI has run
findings.description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:32 runs `gh pr merge --auto --squash "$PR_URL"` for any dependabot PR whose `update-type` is `version-update:semver-patch` (line 30) and which lacks the `dependabot-merge-ignore` label. The workflow header at line 3 states the guarantee: "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes." `--auto` does not wait for CI; it waits for the PR to become mergeable under the branch's protection rules. Per ci-02, `main` has `protected: false`, `required_status_checks.enforcement_level: "off"`, empty `contexts`, and no ruleset, so a dependabot PR is mergeable at the moment it opens and auto-merge fires immediately, with lint, typecheck, test and build still queued or running. The workflow grants itself `contents: write` and `pull-requests: write` at lines 11-13. Separately, ci.yml's `npm ci` steps (lines 37, 62, 101, 138, 193) run with no `--ignore-scripts` and .npmrc contains only `audit-level=high`, `fund=false`, `update-notifier=false`, so package lifecycle scripts execute in CI. (If the repository's "Allow auto-merge" setting happens to be off, `gh pr merge --auto` errors instead and the entire workflow is dead on every dependabot PR; that is the alternative reading and is also a finding.)
findings.impact: A compromised patch release of any of the 71 runtime dependencies is merged to main with no human review and without a single CI job having passed, and its install scripts then run in every subsequent CI job. The next `v*` tag builds that main into the published GHCR image and the signed release tarball, so the compromise propagates to every self-hosted install through the in-app updater. The `npm audit --audit-level=high` gate at ci.yml:71 only catches advisories that already exist, which by definition a fresh malicious release does not have. The stated safety property ("after CI passes") is not enforced anywhere in the repository.
findings.recommendation: Fix ci-02 first: `--auto` is only meaningful once required status checks exist. Then either require Lint/Typecheck/Test/Build as checks on main, or replace `--auto` with an explicit gate in this workflow (a `needs:` on a job that re-runs the suite, or `gh pr checks --watch` before merging). Also restrict auto-merge to devDependencies, or add a cooldown so a package released in the last N days is never auto-merged.

findings.title: No CI job ever builds the Dockerfile, runs docker compose, or boots the app against a Postgres, which is exactly how the two critical self-host breaks reached a published release
findings.description: .github/workflows/ci.yml defines five jobs and contains no occurrence of `docker`, `compose`, `hadolint`, or `trivy`, and declares no `services:` block, so there is no Postgres in CI. The only place the Dockerfile is ever built is .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49, which fires on `push: tags: v*`, that is, after a release has already been cut. Two consequences are already realised in this audit: AUDIT-014#host-01 (instrumentation.ts:105 exits 1 on an empty database before creating a table) requires a real Postgres to observe and nothing in CI has one; AUDIT-014#host-02 (Dockerfile:75-79 never copies scripts/) requires building and inspecting the runtime stage and nothing in CI does. There is also an install-mode divergence: ci.yml's build job runs plain `npm ci` (line 193) while Dockerfile:24 runs `npm ci --silent --ignore-scripts`, so a green CI build does not prove that the image's dependency install produces a working tree.
findings.impact: The self-hostable half of the product, which is the entire open-source value proposition, has zero automated verification. Two critical breaks shipped to a signed, published release without any job failing. Every future change to the Dockerfile, docker-compose.yml, instrumentation.ts boot DDL, or the scripts/migrate runner is unverified until a self-hoster hits it.
findings.recommendation: Add a `selfhost` job to ci.yml that (1) builds the image with `docker build .`, (2) brings up `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d` against a real postgres:16.4-alpine, (3) polls `/api/v3/health` until it reports the database is reachable, and (4) runs `docker compose exec app npm run db:create` so the documented init command is exercised. Make it a required check per ci-02. A hadolint step on the Dockerfile and `docker compose config -q` on both compose files are cheap additions in the same job.

findings.title: docker-compose.yml has no env_file, so 11 of the 48 environment variables the app reads are forwarded and the rest of .env is silently ignored, while the self-hosting docs state the app reads .env via env_file
findings.description: Static analysis, measured with a Node script over `git ls-files` (48 distinct process.env.* names in app/, lib/, components/, scripts/, middleware.ts, instrumentation.ts, excluding NODE_ENV/PORT/HOSTNAME/NEXT_RUNTIME and test-only names). The app service at docker-compose.yml:52 declares only an `environment:` map (:55-72) and no `env_file:` key. Compose reads the project .env file for ${VAR} substitution INSIDE the compose file, but only the keys listed in that map are actually placed in the container's environment. The map forwards 11 app variables: DATABASE_URL, DATABASE_SSL, NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, API_KEY_ENCRYPTION_KEY, SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM, NEXT_PUBLIC_TURNSTILE_SITE_KEY, TURNSTILE_SECRET_KEY (plus CONTACT_EMAIL and NODE_ENV). Not forwarded, despite all being documented in .env.example and read in source: AI_PROVIDER, AI_BASE_URL, AI_MODEL, AI_API_KEY (lib/ai/provider.ts), STRIPE_SECRET_KEY, STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET, NEXT_PUBLIC_STRIPE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, AUTH_SECRET, DISCORD_CLIENT_ID/CLIENT_SECRET/BOT_TOKEN/GUILD_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, GITHUB_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, TRUSTED_PROXY_CIDR, DATABASE_SSL_CA, AVATAR_STORAGE_DIR, BACKUP_DIR, BACKUP_ENCRYPTION_KEY, BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS, BACKUP_OFFSITE_UPLOAD_URL, NVD_API_KEY, WEB_RISK_API_KEY, URLHAUS_AUTH_KEY, LOGO_URL, SUPPORT_EMAIL, DISABLE_CSP, SECURITY_ALLOW_NON_BROWSER_API, and the four NEXT_PUBLIC SEO/verification vars. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244 states flatly "The app reads .env via env_file", and the same page then instructs the operator to put AI_BASE_URL / AI_MODEL / AI_API_KEY in .env (:213-217) and STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET in .env followed by `docker compose restart app` (:372-377). Neither reaches the process. docker-compose.dev.yml:46-61 has the identical map and the identical gap. This is the mechanism behind AUDIT-012#obs-08's "Invalid signature" symptom: on the shipped compose the webhook secret cannot be set at all.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who configures AI, Stripe, Discord/Google/GitHub OAuth, a trusted proxy CIDR, a custom backup directory or a threat-intel API key in .env exactly as the docs say gets no error and no effect. Features silently stay off, and the failure looks like a bug in the feature rather than in the plumbing. OAuth being unreachable also removes the only sign-in path that works without SMTP (see host-04).
findings.recommendation: Add `env_file: [.env]` to the app service in both docker-compose.yml (after :54) and docker-compose.dev.yml, keeping the explicit `environment:` map for the values that are composed rather than passed through (DATABASE_URL, NODE_ENV). If passing the whole file is undesirable, extend the map to cover every key in .env.example and correct app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244.

findings.title: Without SMTP a self-hoster can create an account but can never log in: signup leaves email_verified_at NULL, the verification email throws in production, and login refuses unverified accounts
findings.description: Static trace. lib/email/email.ts:81 builds the SMTP transport only when SMTP_HOST && SMTP_USER && SMTP_PASS are all set, otherwise `transporter` is null. sendEmail then logs a warning and, when process.env.NODE_ENV !== "production", returns successfully (:407-418); in production it throws `new Error("Email service not configured")` at :427. Both Dockerfile:106 and docker-compose.yml:56 set NODE_ENV=production, so the production branch is the one self-hosters hit. app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:215-222 sends the verification email inside a background catch that only console.errors, so signup returns 200 and the user row is created with email_verified_at NULL (the signup INSERT never sets it; grep across app/api/v3/auth/ shows the only setters are the OAuth callback, the staff-invite route, and app/api/v3/auth/verify-email/route.ts:77, which needs the token from the email). app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:164 then blocks the login with `unverified: true`. app/api/v3/auth/resend-verification/route.ts calls the same sendEmail and throws the same way. The two escape hatches are both closed on the default compose: OAuth sign-in sets email_verified_at immediately but its credentials are not forwarded to the container (host-03), and there is no admin setting to disable verification (grep for REQUIRE_EMAIL/EMAIL_VERIFICATION over lib/config finds only CONFIG_EMAIL_VERIFICATION_HOURS, a TTL). Every doc labels SMTP optional: app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:185 "# Optional: SMTP", docker-compose.yml:62 "# SMTP (optional, for emails)", app/docs/config/page.tsx:1160 "(Optional) Configure SMTP". The First Admin User procedure at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:268-284 tells the operator to sign up and then run one SQL statement (UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'), and omits the UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() that is actually required to log in at all.
findings.impact: The most likely self-hoster profile, someone with a Postgres string and no mail server, reaches a working signup form, creates the account the docs tell them to create, and is then locked out with a message about an email that was never sent and cannot be resent. There is no in-app recovery. The instance is unusable and the cause is not discoverable from the UI.
findings.recommendation: Either mark the account verified at signup when no SMTP transport is configured (check the same SMTP_HOST/USER/PASS triple lib/email/email.ts:81 uses and set email_verified_at = NOW() in the signup INSERT), or add an explicit setting that skips verification. At minimum, add `UPDATE users SET email_verified_at = NOW() WHERE email = '...';` alongside the role UPDATE at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:280 and stop calling SMTP optional there and in docker-compose.yml:62.

findings.title: The documented self-host upgrade path is a no-op: the app service declares no build context, so `git pull && docker compose build app && docker compose up -d` re-pulls the same pinned 3.0.0 image
findings.description: Static analysis. The app service in docker-compose.yml:52-53 declares `image: ghcr.io/vulnradar/vulnradar:3.0.0` and no `build:` key, unlike docker-compose.dev.yml:40-44 which does. app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 documents the upgrade as `cd vulnradar.dev; git pull; docker compose build app; docker compose up -d`. With no build context, `docker compose build app` cannot build anything from the pulled source, and the subsequent `up -d` reconciles against the pinned image tag, so the freshly pulled source has no effect whatsoever on what runs. The same shape breaks README.md:78-79, which labels `docker compose up -d` as "# 3. Build and run" immediately after a `git clone` at :70: the clone is only used for .env and lib/config/config-values.ts edits, and config-values.ts is baked into the image at build time (README.md:95 "Edit and rebuild"), so those edits also never take effect on the prod compose path. app/docs/setup/page.tsx:607-613 makes the same promise, offering `git clone` as the "Or build from source locally" alternative to curling the compose file, when both branches land on the same non-building compose. This extends AUDIT-013#deps-06, which recorded the 3.0.0-vs-3.7.2 pin: the new part is that the documented mechanism for getting off that pinned version does not build and the fork-customisation workflow the README sells is unreachable from the shipped compose.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who forks and rebrands the app per README.md:88-102 sees none of their config-values.ts edits, and an operator following the documented upgrade steps believes they have upgraded while still running the 3.0.0 image. Neither failure produces an error message.
findings.recommendation: Give the app service in docker-compose.yml a `build:` section alongside `image:` (context ., dockerfile Dockerfile, args NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL) so `docker compose build app` works and `up -d` prefers the local build, or change app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:535-541 and README.md:78 to the pull-only path (`docker compose pull && docker compose up -d`) and point fork customisation at docker-compose.dev.yml explicitly.

findings.title: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL is inlined at build time and the published image is built without the build-arg, so every self-hosted instance renders vulnradar.dev in 15 client components regardless of the runtime env var
findings.description: Static analysis. lib/config/constants.ts:191 is `export const APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL;`, with CONFIG_APP_URL = "https://vulnradar.dev" (lib/config/config-values.ts:141). Next.js replaces NEXT_PUBLIC_* with a literal at build time in any module that reaches the client bundle. A scan of every "use client" file under app/, components/, lib/ and hooks/ finds 15 that reference APP_URL, including components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx, components/demo/demo-hero.tsx, components/scanner/footer.tsx, components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx and ten /docs pages. Dockerfile:16 declares ARG NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL and :32 forwards it to ENV, but .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml passes no build-args at all, so the published ghcr.io image, which is the image docker-compose.yml:53 pulls, has the fallback literal baked into those bundles. Setting NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL in docker-compose.yml:59 changes only server-side reads. The comment at lib/config/constants.ts:177-184 states "Self-hosters set NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL (see the Dockerfile's build ARG ...)" and lists the consumers as emails, sitemap.xml, robots.txt and canonical/OG tags, which is accurate for the server half but does not cover the 15 client files. .env.example:19 describes the variable as "Used in emails, redirects, and client-side code", which is the part that does not work on the prebuilt image.
findings.impact: On a self-hosted deployment at scanner.example.com, the docs pages, API examples, demo hero and footer shown to that operator's own users all print https://vulnradar.dev, so copied curl commands and links point at the upstream SaaS rather than the operator's instance. For a rebranded GPL fork this is a functional and a branding failure, and it is invisible in the logs.
findings.recommendation: Either pass `build-args: NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml and tell self-hosters that the prebuilt image is hard-coded to the upstream URL (so they must build locally), or make APP_URL runtime-resolvable for client code: expose it through a server-rendered value in the root layout or an existing runtime-config endpoint and have the 15 client components read that instead of the compile-time constant.

findings.title: The API reference's headline request field `probes` was deleted from the scan routes in commit d0c815f7 and is now a silent no-op in every code sample
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:43 makes `"probes": ["ssh:22", "smtp:587"]` the request-body example for POST /scan, :40 says "Service probes are opt-in via the probes field", :52 and :56 describe the six services in detail, and the curl (:938) and JavaScript (:958) code samples both send it. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:232 destructures only `{ url, scanners, isPublic }` plus body.captureScreenshot (:236) and body.portScan (:241); `probes` appears nowhere in the route, in lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts's ExecuteScanParams (:207-251), or anywhere else in app/ or lib/ (verified by grep). Commit d0c815f7 "refactor: remove Service probes (consolidated into Scan common ports)" removed "the `probes` payload field, the API `probes` parse in scan/crawl/authenticated routes, the runServiceProbes executor path" and deleted lib/scanner/service-probes.ts, but touched no docs file. The same dead field is still in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:706-712 (so the playground prefills it), app/docs/page.tsx:119/143, app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:448-457, and lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md:1027/1892, which is what the in-product AI assistant answers from.
findings.impact: A developer following the first example on the API reference sends a body whose main feature flag is silently discarded: no error, no probes, no way to tell it did nothing. The replacement capability (body.portScan, gated on verified domain ownership, app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:241/310-324) is documented nowhere, so the feature is unreachable from the docs in both directions. The in-product AI assistant repeats the dead field verbatim.
findings.recommendation: Delete the `probes` field from the POST /scan endpoint card (app/docs/api/page.tsx:41-44, notes :52 and :56), from both code samples (:938, :958), and from the ScanRequest schema in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:706-712. Add `portScan: boolean` and `captureScreenshot: boolean` to the request body and notes, stating that portScan is held to the same verified-domain gate as active-probes and returns 403 DOMAIN_NOT_VERIFIED. Then re-run `node scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs` so lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md stops teaching it.

findings.title: The API playground prefills POST /scan and POST /scan/crawl with `"scanners": [""]`, which selects zero check categories and burns a real quota unit on an empty scan
findings.description: lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:713-718 declares ScanRequest.scanners as `{ type: "array", items: { type: "string" } }` with no `example` on either the array or its items. lib/api/playground.ts's buildExample falls through to `case "array": return s.items ? [buildExample(spec, s.items)] : []` and then `case "string": return ""`, producing `[""]`. app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:83-91 stringifies that into the request-body textarea and :284 seeds the editable body with it, so the prefilled POST /scan body is `{"url":"example.com","probes":["ssh:22"],"scanners":[""]}`. app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:242-243 treats a non-empty array as an explicit selection (`selectedScanners = [""]`), and lib/scanner/engine.ts:104-119's getPlannedSyncCategories builds `new Set([""])` and filters ALL_CATEGORIES against it, yielding zero categories. POST /scan/crawl reuses the same ScanRequest schema (openapi-spec.ts:102).
findings.impact: The first thing a developer does on the playground page ("pick an endpoint, paste a key, and read the live response", app/docs/api/page.tsx:1187) starts a real scan that runs almost no checks, still charges one dailyScans unit and one API-key request, and returns a summary of zero findings. That reads as "the scanner found nothing" rather than "you sent an invalid selector", because the route never validates the category strings.
findings.recommendation: Add `example: ["headers", "ssl"]` (or omit the field from the example by giving the whole ScanRequest an object-level `example`) in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:713-718, and defensively drop empty/unknown entries in app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:242-243 so `[""]` normalizes to null rather than to "run nothing".

findings.title: Every API code sample and the OpenAPI `servers` URL hardcode https://vulnradar.dev on any build without NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL, including the published Docker image
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts:191 resolves `APP_URL = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL || CONFIG_APP_URL`, and lib/config/config-values.ts:141 sets CONFIG_APP_URL to "https://vulnradar.dev". NEXT_PUBLIC_* is inlined by Next at build time, and .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49-51 runs `docker build -t $IMAGE:${VERSION} -t $IMAGE:latest .` with no `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`, even though Dockerfile:16/32 declares the ARG. So the published GHCR image bakes vulnradar.dev into APP_URL. app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts:11 calls `buildOpenApiSpec(APP_URL)`, which lands in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:25 as `servers: [{ url: "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3" }]` (its own docstring at :12-13 claims "baseUrl is the deployment's origin so a self-hosted instance advertises its own server"). app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 reads `spec.servers[0].url` as its baseUrl and :298/:316 fetch that absolute URL. Every curl/JS sample on app/docs/api/page.tsx:935-984, the rate-limits backoff samples (app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:379/413), and the reports curl samples (app/docs/reports/page.tsx:296/449) interpolate the same APP_URL.
findings.impact: On a self-hosted instance run from the official image, every documented curl command targets the public SaaS instead of the operator's own deployment, and the playground's "Send request" button issues a cross-origin request to vulnradar.dev that fails CORS with the opaque message "Request failed (network, CORS, or an invalid URL)". The playground's own setup text ("the key ... is sent only to https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3") then tells the operator their key goes to someone else's server.
findings.recommendation: Pass `--build-arg NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` in .github/workflows/docker-publish.yml:49, or (better, since the image is shared) make app/api/v3/openapi.json/route.ts call resolveAppUrl(request) from lib/config/runtime-config.ts instead of the compiled APP_URL, and have app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:62 fall back to `window.location.origin + "/api/v3"` when the spec's server host does not match the current origin.

findings.title: Crawl scans are documented as capped at 15 pages in three places; the real cap is a per-plan 25/50/100/250 and unlimited when billing is off
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:322 says "Up to 15 pages per crawl" and :332 cites "Max 15 pages (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts)". No `MAX_PAGES` identifier exists in that file (verified by grep). app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:256-272 resolves `crawlPageLimit = BILLING_ENABLED ? getCrawlPageSelectionLimit(await getUserPlan(userId)) : -1`, and lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:19-24 defines CRAWL_PAGE_SELECTION_LIMITS as free 25, core_supporter 50, pro_supporter 100, elite_supporter 250; the engine-side ceiling is CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_MAX_PAGES = 500 (lib/config/config-values.ts:603). The same wrong number is in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:96 ("Crawl and scan up to 15 pages of a site") and in the CLI help/docs (cli/lib.mjs:126, app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135).
findings.impact: A user reading the docs caps their own crawl at 15 pages and never discovers they are entitled to 25 on the free plan or 250 on Elite, which is the single largest per-plan difference in the crawl feature. Self-hosters, for whom the cap is removed entirely, are told a limit that does not exist on their deployment.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fixed 15 in app/docs/api/page.tsx:322 and :332 and in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:96 with the per-plan table from lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts, note that billing-disabled deployments are unlimited, add the 403 CRAWL_PAGE_LIMIT error (app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:265-271) to the endpoint card's error list, and fix the same string in cli/lib.mjs:126 and app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135.

findings.title: The rate-limits page publishes a 100/hour per-IP limit on "any /api/v3/*" that is enforced on only five routes
findings.description: app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:230-234 lists a row "API requests per IP (any /api/v3/*)" with 100 attempts / 60 minutes, under a heading (:189-196) that presents the whole table as IP-based limits enforced from CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_*_ATTEMPTS pairs. The named limit is RATE_LIMITS.api (lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:254, CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_API_REQUESTS = 100 / _WINDOW_MINUTES = 60). Grepping every consumer of `RATE_LIMITS.api` finds exactly five call sites: app/api/v3/auth/update/route.ts:44, app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:36, app/api/v3/landing-contact/route.ts:28, app/api/v3/scan/reputation/route.ts:138, app/api/v3/support-tickets/[id]/route.ts:177. middleware.ts contains no rate-limit call at all. Two of the five are not even per-IP: scan/reputation keys on `scan-reputation:${userId}` and auth/update keys on `${userId}:${clientIp}`. The row below it, "POST /api/v3/scan (and friends) 100/60", is likewise keyed per user (`scan:${session.userId}`, app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:165) and is skipped entirely on the Bearer-API-key branch (the checkGlobalRL call sits inside the session-cookie `else` at :150-176).
findings.impact: The published contract says any /api/v3 endpoint is capped at 100 requests/hour per IP. It is not: 150 of the 155 routes have no such gate, and API-key callers have no scan burst limit at all. An operator sizing capacity, or a security reviewer reading the page, is given a guarantee the code does not make. AUDIT-013 already recorded unmetered paths; this is the doc side of the same gap.
findings.recommendation: Either apply RATE_LIMITS.api in middleware.ts for the whole /api/v3 tree, or rewrite the two rows in app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:230-239 to name the five routes that actually carry it, mark which limits are keyed per user rather than per IP, and state that the scan burst limit applies to session auth only.

findings.title: Four docs pages tell a fresh self-hoster to run SQL that demotes the auto-provisioned super_admin to admin, and no UI path can ever restore it
findings.description: lib/auth/auth.ts:284 (and the two sibling insert paths at :365 and :384) assign the role with `CASE WHEN NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM users) THEN 'super_admin' ELSE 'user' END`, so the very first account created on a fresh instance is already super_admin (level 50 in STAFF_ROLE_HIERARCHY, lib/config/client-constants.ts:39-48). Four docs pages nonetheless tell the operator to sign up the first user and then promote it with `UPDATE users SET role = 'admin'`: app/docs/setup/page.tsx:428, app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:281, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1155 and app/docs/developers/page.tsx:501. That statement is a demotion, not a promotion: super_admin (50) becomes admin (40). app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:642-647 then filters SUPER_ADMIN out of validRoles for the set_role action, with the comment 'super_admin is un-assignable through this endpoint (or any UI path)'. No docs page mentions the automatic bootstrap or how to undo the demotion.
findings.impact: Every operator who follows the documented install to the letter silently gives up the god-mode role on their own instance. hasGodMode (lib/auth/permissions-client.ts:293) protection, the super-admin-only guards at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:431/544/549, and the un-deletable-account property are all lost, and the only way back is raw SQL that no document describes.
findings.recommendation: Delete the promote-to-admin SQL step from all four pages and replace it with one sentence: the first account created on a fresh instance is automatically super_admin, sign up and open /admin. If a manual promotion step is still wanted for a non-first account, use `role = 'admin'` only with an explicit warning never to run it against the bootstrap account, and document `UPDATE users SET role = 'super_admin' WHERE id = 1` as the only recovery.

findings.title: README and five docs sites still describe the lib/types/config.ts + lib/config/config.ts layer that commit 2cee4042 deleted nine days ago, including a typecheck safety net that no longer exists
findings.description: Commit 2cee4042 (2026-08-20) removed 'lib/config/config.ts + lib/types/config.ts (the dead loadConfig/getConfigValue/DEFAULT_CONFIG layer, superseded by the registry/getSetting resolver)'. There is no lib/types/ directory in the tree at all, and grepping lib/ for loadConfig or getConfigValue returns nothing. Six doc sites still describe it as live: README.md:99 ('lib/types/config.ts derives the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG from them') in the paragraph headed 'Single source of truth'; app/docs/config/page.tsx:125-136 renders a lib/config/ directory tree that lists config.ts and lib/types/config.ts while omitting registry.ts, runtime-config.ts, env.ts and brand.ts, the four files that actually drive configuration today; app/docs/config/page.tsx:1173-1178 promises 'Build time: npm run typecheck exercises every CONFIG_* through the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG in lib/types/config.ts. Renaming or removing a constant fails typecheck'; app/docs/architecture/page.tsx:176-184 lists both deleted files as steps 2 and 3 of the config chain; app/docs/developers/page.tsx:769-773 warns against 'Editing lib/types/config.ts defaults'; and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:578-581 offers a troubleshooting row whose stated cause is 'Renamed a CONFIG_* constant without updating the typed DEFAULT_CONFIG'.
findings.impact: A self-hoster or contributor reading the canonical explanation of how configuration works is sent to two files that do not exist and told about two exported functions that do not exist. Worse, app/docs/config/page.tsx:1173-1178 advertises a compile-time guarantee that was deleted with the file: renaming or deleting a CONFIG_* constant no longer fails typecheck through any DEFAULT_CONFIG, so someone who trusts that safety net can ship a broken rename. The docs also never name registry.ts or runtime-config.ts, which is where configuration actually lives now.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the config chain in all six places as config-values.ts -> registry.ts (SETTINGS_REGISTRY) -> runtime-config.ts (database ?? env ?? default) -> constants.ts / client-constants.ts, with env.ts as the boot-time validator. Redraw the tree in app/docs/config/page.tsx:125-136 from the real ls of lib/config/. Delete the DEFAULT_CONFIG typecheck claim at :1173-1178 and the self-hosting troubleshooting row at :578-581, or replace them with whatever real gate exists.

findings.title: .github/SUPPORT.md instructs bug reporters to delete package-lock.json and reinstall, the one operation that strips the 28 Linux native-binding entries and breaks CI and the Docker build
findings.description: package-lock.json contains 58 platform-scoped optional packages, 28 of them Linux: @next/swc-linux-{x64,arm64}-{gnu,musl}, @rolldown/binding-linux-*, @img/sharp-linux-* and @img/sharp-libvips-linux-*.
