Every CI job installs with `npm ci` on ubuntu-latest (.github/workflows/ci.yml:37, :62, :101, :137, :193) and Dockerfile builds on a Linux base, so all of them resolve those entries out of the committed lockfile. .github/SUPPORT.md:19 tells anyone about to file a bug to 'Delete node_modules and package-lock.json, then npm install from scratch'. Run on Windows, that regenerates the lockfile without the Linux entries and additionally re-resolves every version away from the pinned set. Nothing in CONTRIBUTING.md, README.md or app/docs/setup/page.tsx warns about this: app/docs/setup/page.tsx:129 warns only 'Use npm, not pnpm or yarn', which is the adjacent hazard, not this one.
findings.impact: A contributor or maintainer who follows the official support instructions on a Windows or macOS machine and commits the regenerated lockfile breaks `npm ci` on every CI job and the Docker image build with a 'Cannot find native binding' failure for next/font, and the breakage looks like a code problem rather than a lockfile problem. The repo has hit this before.
findings.recommendation: Change .github/SUPPORT.md:19 to `rm -rf node_modules && npm ci` (which never rewrites the lockfile). Add a short 'Lockfile' section to CONTRIBUTING.md stating that package-lock.json must only ever be regenerated on Linux, that a lockfile diff removing any *-linux-* entry must be rejected in review, and that npm ci is the only supported install for reproducing a bug. Optionally add a CI step that fails when the diff drops a linux optional dependency.

findings.title: The self-hosting troubleshooting table tells an operator locked out by broken SMTP to call POST /api/v3/auth/2fa/disable, which requires the session they cannot obtain
findings.description: app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:593-596 documents the symptom 'Login succeeds but 2FA code never arrives', cause 'SMTP not configured', fix 'Set SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/PASS/FROM in .env and restart, or disable 2FA via /api/v3/auth/2fa/disable'. app/api/v3/auth/2fa/disable/route.ts:17-19 calls getSession() and returns 401 when there is none, then at :38-52 requires the account password in the body. A user stopped at the second factor has not completed login: the interim state is a separate signed token handled by lib/auth/pending-2fa.ts, not a session cookie, so getSession() returns null and the call is a guaranteed 401. The second half of the fix is therefore unusable in exactly the situation the row describes, and the first half (configure SMTP) is the same instruction the operator already could not satisfy.
findings.impact: An operator who self-hosts without SMTP and enabled email 2FA is permanently locked out of their own instance, and the only recovery the documentation offers cannot be executed. This compounds AUDIT-014#host-04. The repo does ship a database-side escape (npm run db:repair-2fa) but it only touches rows proven corrupt by scripts/_lib/_lib.2fa-diagnostics.mjs, so it does not help a healthy-but-unreachable email 2FA row, and it is documented nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Replace the second clause of the fix in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:596 with a database recovery that actually works from outside the app: `UPDATE users SET totp_enabled = false, two_factor_method = NULL, totp_secret = NULL, backup_codes = NULL WHERE email = '...';` run through psql, with a note that this is the only path when no session can be established. Add the same recovery to a new troubleshooting section, and document npm run db:repair-2fa and npm run db:diagnose-2fa alongside it.

findings.title: All 29 "Build" tier admin settings (APP_NAME, APP_URL, LOGO_URL, FOOTER_TEXT, every SEO_*) are written to system_settings and then read by nothing, while the admin banner and /docs/config both promise the change applies on the next build
findings.description: lib/config/registry.ts declares 267 settings; 29 carry `tier: "build"` (APP_NAME, APP_SLUG, APP_DESCRIPTION, TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL, APP_URL, APP_REPO, DISCORD_INVITE_URL, CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL, FIREFOX_ADDON_URL, LOGO_URL, PRIMARY_COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR_DARK/LIGHT, FOOTER_TEXT, the 13 SEO_* keys, BULK_SCAN_CLIENT_URL_LIMIT, MAX_AVATAR_UPLOAD_BYTES). The admin write path accepts every key that passes isSettingKey and upserts it (app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts:316-341). Reading them back is the problem. I enumerated every getSetting/getSettings call site across app/, lib/ and components/ with a Node scan: 157 distinct keys are resolved through lib/config/runtime-config.ts, and not one of them is a build-tier key. The only reader of any build-tier row is resolveAppUrl (lib/config/runtime-config.ts:143), which does `values.get("APP_URL")` for OAuth redirect_uri and is called by exactly 7 sign-in routes. Everything else reads the synchronous constants in lib/config/constants.ts:170-231, which resolve from process.env or the CONFIG_ literal and never touch Postgres. No build step reads the table either: package.json's prebuild runs only the four knowledge compilers, and `system_settings` appears nowhere under scripts/ except the schema DDL. So the banner at components/admin/features/system-settings-manager.tsx:515-518 ("Saving here updates the database immediately, but the change only shows up after the next build and deploy"), the identical claim at app/docs/config/page.tsx:596-603, and the APP_URL help text at lib/config/registry.ts:377 are all false: the next build reads NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL or the CONFIG_ literal, never the row that was saved. The registry's documented `database value ?? environment override ?? shipped default` chain (runtime-config.ts:3, repeated at app/docs/config/page.tsx:607) is also inert for these keys in both of its first two steps, because resolve() is only reachable through getSetting/getSettings.
findings.impact: A self-hoster follows /docs/self-hosting, creates the first admin, opens /admin > Settings > Branding, types their own product name, logo and footer line, saves, sees a success toast and an explicit banner telling them it will appear on the next deploy, rebuilds, and gets VulnRadar's branding back. There is no error and no way to tell the write did nothing. The same is true of the APP_URL field, which is the single most load-bearing deployment value in the product: an operator who sets it there and rebuilds still ships canonical tags, sitemap entries, robots host, OG/Twitter URLs, JSON-LD @id, badge embed snippets and every transactional email link pointing at vulnradar.dev. Combined with AUDIT-014#host-05 (the compose app service has no build context, so the documented Docker path can never rebuild at all), the admin panel is the only branding surface a Docker self-hoster has, and it is a no-op.
findings.recommendation: Two options, pick one and make the UI match it. (a) Make them real: give every build-tier key a server-side read path through getSetting in the server components that render it (app/layout.tsx metadata, components/seo/structured-data.tsx, app/sitemap.ts, app/robots.ts, app/manifest.ts, lib/email/email.ts), accept that client components still need NEXT_PUBLIC_ inlining, and drop the tier distinction for the server-rendered half. (b) Make them honest: stop persisting build-tier keys. Have the PATCH handler in app/api/v3/admin/features/route.ts reject any key whose registry tier is "build" with a 400 naming lib/config/config-values.ts as the place to change it, render those fields read-only in system-settings-manager.tsx, and rewrite the banner at :515 and app/docs/config/page.tsx:596-603 to say "edit lib/config/config-values.ts and rebuild; this page cannot change them". Either way, delete the false "next build and deploy" wording from all three places.

findings.title: The browser extension is compiled against a literal https://vulnradar.dev with no build arg, no setting and manifest host_permissions to match, so a self-hoster cannot point it at their own instance at all
findings.description: extension/src/lib/constants.ts:3 sets `apiHost: "https://vulnradar.dev"` as a plain `as const` literal. Every network call, every deep link and every privacy statement derives from it: extension/src/lib/api.ts:93 and :167 build request URLs, service-worker.ts:180 and :183 open history/dashboard tabs, content/reputation-card.ts:271 and :348 render links, onboarding/welcome.ts:41-86 prints it three times, options/options.ts:365 and :1123 print it again. Nothing overrides it: extension/vite.config.ts defines no `define` block and no env plumbing, extension/scripts/build.mjs references no VITE_ or process.env variable, and the options page has no host field (options.ts:1123 states as fact "The extension talks to https://vulnradar.dev only"). Both manifests pin it a second time: extension/manifest/chrome.json:42 and extension/manifest/firefox.json:52 are `"host_permissions": ["https://vulnradar.dev/*"]`, so even patching constants.ts alone leaves every request blocked by the browser. A third copy exists at service-worker.ts:418-421, where EXCLUDED_HOSTS is a literal list of sandbox.vulnradar.dev / vulnradar.dev / www.vulnradar.dev rather than being derived from apiHost, so a repointed build would auto-scan its own instance and still skip vulnradar.dev. /docs/extension never mentions self-hosting; it links only to the two public store listings (app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113 and :139), which install the vulnradar.dev-locked build.
findings.impact: The extension is advertised on a self-hosted instance's own /docs/extension page, and installing it from either store gives the operator's users a tool that sends their scan targets to vulnradar.dev, authenticated with an API key from vulnradar.dev, that will never work against the instance they actually run. A self-hoster who wants it has to fork the extension, edit four files, rebuild, and side-load an unsigned unpacked extension on every machine, which Chrome disables on restart for non-store extensions in managed environments. There is no documentation for any of that. Compare the CLI (cli/lib.mjs:57, `--api-base`) and the GitHub Action (.github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml:15-18, `api-base-url`), which both take the repoint as a first-class input; the extension is the only client that does not.
findings.recommendation: Add a `VULNRADAR_API_HOST` build-time define in extension/vite.config.ts and extension/scripts/build.mjs (`define: { __API_HOST__: JSON.stringify(process.env.VULNRADAR_API_HOST || "https://vulnradar.dev") }`), read it in extension/src/lib/constants.ts:3, and template the same value into `host_permissions` in a small step in extension/scripts/build.mjs the way `__VERSION__` is already templated. Derive EXCLUDED_HOSTS at service-worker.ts:418 from `new URL(VULNRADAR.apiHost).hostname` plus its `www.` form instead of the literal list. For the no-rebuild case, add an optional "Instance URL" field to the options page backed by `optional_host_permissions: ["https://*/*"]` plus a browser.permissions.request() prompt, and note the whole mechanism in app/docs/extension/page.tsx so a self-hoster does not have to read the source to discover it does not work.

findings.title: SUPPORT_EMAIL is documented as an env override and registered as a runtime admin setting, but 8 of its 9 call sites read the build-time constant, and in the 4 client components the env read is compiled out so the footer permanently shows support@vulnradar.dev
findings.description: Three surfaces promise SUPPORT_EMAIL is configurable: .env.example:87-88 ("Falls back to CONFIG_SUPPORT_EMAIL in lib/config/config-values.ts"), app/docs/config/page.tsx:987-994 ("CONTACT_EMAIL, SUPPORT_EMAIL: override the addresses used by contact/support emails"), and lib/config/registry.ts:432-438, which registers it `tier: "runtime"` with the explicitly UI-facing help text "Address shown to users who need help and used as the reply-to on support mail". Exactly one call site honours the runtime setting: app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:23-24 uses getSettings(["SUPPORT_EMAIL", ...]). The other eight read the build-time export at lib/config/constants.ts:638 (`process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL || CONFIG_SUPPORT_EMAIL`): lib/email/email.ts:167, :287, :801, :816, :830, :840 (every transactional email footer and every security-alert "email us" line), lib/support/ticket-notify.ts:39 (the To: address for support tickets), components/seo/structured-data.tsx:98 (JSON-LD contactPoint), components/contact/contact-quick-links.tsx:17-18, plus four "use client" components: components/scanner/footer.tsx:244 (sitewide), components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:293, components/demo/demo-error.tsx:46 and app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:72. In a client bundle Next.js only inlines NEXT_PUBLIC_-prefixed variables, so `process.env.SUPPORT_EMAIL` becomes a falsy constant and the `||` folds away at build time. I confirmed this in the checked-in build output: .next/static/chunks/9711-3989d97c24edd68e.js contains `O="support@vulnradar.dev",R="legal@vulnradar.dev",I="security@vu...` with no process.env reference left. LEGAL_EMAIL, SECURITY_EMAIL and ENTERPRISE_EMAIL (constants.ts:639-641) have no env path at all and are baked into that same chunk, although their runtime settings do reach the /legal/* pages and /api/security-txt via getSetting.
findings.impact: A self-hoster sets SUPPORT_EMAIL in .env exactly as documented and gets a split-brain instance: outgoing email, support-ticket routing and the JSON-LD contact point use their address, while the footer on every single page, the dashboard error state, the demo error and the checkout success page keep telling their users to email support@vulnradar.dev. Those users then email a third party about a product they do not run, which is a support-load and privacy problem for both sides and reads as a phishing-shaped inconsistency. The admin-panel SUPPORT_EMAIL field makes it worse: it is labelled runtime tier, so it saves with no build warning at all, and changes precisely one page out of nine.
findings.recommendation: Two fixes. (1) For server-rendered surfaces, switch to the runtime setting so the admin field means something: lib/email/email.ts should take the support address as a parameter resolved by its callers via getSetting("SUPPORT_EMAIL"), and components/seo/structured-data.tsx, components/contact/contact-quick-links.tsx and lib/support/ticket-notify.ts should call getSetting directly (all three are server components/modules already). (2) For the four client components, the address has to be inlined at build time, so rename the env var to NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPPORT_EMAIL in lib/config/constants.ts:638 and .env.example:88 (keeping SUPPORT_EMAIL as a server-only fallback), or pass the address down from a server parent as a prop. Whichever is chosen, correct app/docs/config/page.tsx:989-993 so it does not claim a plain SUPPORT_EMAIL override reaches the UI.

findings.title: The AI assistant reads its five knowledge files from process.cwd()/lib/ai/, but the Dockerfile runner stage never copies lib/, so /docs, /changelog, /checks and /legal are empty in every published image and tell the operator to run a command the image does not contain
findings.description: app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:18-26 defines readKnowledgeFile(...segments) as `readFileSync(join(process.cwd(), ...segments))` guarded by existsSync, returning "" on a miss. Five call sites use it: :61 lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md, :74 lib/ai/changelog-knowledge.md, :87 lib/ai/checks-index.md with :89 falling back to checks-knowledge.md, :102 lib/ai/legal-knowledge.md, and :284-287 checks-knowledge.md for the /finding explainer. Those files exist in the repo (lib/ai/*.md, 244 KB to 975 KB each) and are regenerated by the prebuild compilers in package.json. They are not JS imports, so nothing bundles them into .next. The runner stage of the Dockerfile copies exactly five paths: /app/public (:75), /app/.next (:76), /app/node_modules (:77), /app/package.json (:78) and /app/next.config.mjs (:79). lib/ is not among them, and next.config.mjs:4 explicitly disables `output: "standalone"`, so Next.js output file tracing is not copying them either. In the published image every one of those five reads misses and the route returns the failure summary written at :66 and :80: "Documentation not available. Run `npm run build:knowledge` to generate it." Per AUDIT-014#host-02 scripts/ is not copied into the image either, so that npm script cannot run there: it invokes node scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs.
findings.impact: Four of the AI assistant's slash commands and the per-finding explainer silently return nothing on every Docker deployment, which is the deployment path the docs recommend. The user sees a confident "not available" message pointing at a remediation command that fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND inside the container, so the operator burns time on a fix that cannot work. This is also a hosted-instance risk if production ever moves to this image: the /changelog context block alone is 250 KB of product knowledge the assistant is designed around, and its absence degrades quietly rather than erroring. Extends AUDIT-014#host-02, which found the same missing-scripts root cause for db:create, db:migrate and the Backup button; this is a second, user-facing consequence of the same COPY list.
findings.recommendation: Add `COPY --from=builder --chown=nextjs:nodejs /app/lib/ai/*.md ./lib/ai/` to the Dockerfile after line 79 (a narrow copy, roughly 1.4 MB, not the whole lib/ tree, which is already compiled into .next). Then change the fallback summaries at app/api/v3/ai/context/route.ts:66, :80, :95 and :107 to a message that does not name an npm script, since the container cannot run one: "Knowledge base not available on this instance." If a broader fix is preferred, have scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs emit a .ts module exporting the string instead of a .md file so the content is bundled into .next and the runtime filesystem read disappears entirely.

findings.title: About 30 per-probe scanner timeouts are bare 3000/4000/5000/6000 literals with no config entry, and a timed-out probe returns an empty finding array so a slow target silently reports clean
findings.description: lib/scanner/async-checks.ts contains 30 hardcoded per-probe deadlines, counted by pattern: 11 x setTimeout(reject, 4000), 5 x setTimeout(reject, 3000), 1 x setTimeout(reject, 6000), 6 x AbortSignal.timeout(5000), 4 x AbortSignal.timeout(4000), 1 x AbortSignal.timeout(6000), plus timeout: 5000 (:2005) and timeout: 4500 (:2277). lib/scanner/subdomain-discovery-engine.ts adds 11 more (:441 15000, :476-:670 seven at 10000, :708 12000, :858 4000, :869 3000), lib/scanner/checks/tls.ts three more (:136 5000, :268 and :382 4500), lib/scanner/checks/content.ts one (:2287 6000). None of these resolve through lib/config/registry.ts, even though the registry already carries ten scanner deadline settings (SCAN_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, SCAN_ASYNC_CHECKS_TIMEOUT_MS, SCANNER_ASYNC_BRANCH_TIMEOUT_MS, SCANNER_THREAT_INTEL_API_TIMEOUT_MS, CRAWL_PAGE_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS, and friends, registry.ts:1769-1959) that an operator can already edit. The failure mode is the important half: checkMTASTS races dns.resolveTxt against setTimeout(reject, 3000) at :1133-1138, and its catch at :1147-1155 only returns a finding for ENODATA/ENOTFOUND/ENOENT, so the literal string 'timeout' falls through to `return []` at :1154. checkTLSRPT (:1293-1299) has the identical shape. A probe that times out therefore produces no finding and no warning, indistinguishable from a probe that ran and found nothing. Not the same as AUDIT-011#scan-01 (the 15s subdomain cap on the critical path), AUDIT-012#perf-01 (the 5s NVD/OSV calls and the 300s watchdog) or AUDIT-013#dup-01 (the duplicated 10s body-reader timeout); this is the remaining per-check inventory.
findings.impact: A self-hoster scanning a slow, geographically distant, or rate-limiting target loses DNS and TLS checks silently: the scan says the site has no MTA-STS finding rather than saying the check did not complete. That is a false negative on a security scan, presented with full confidence, and the operator has no setting anywhere in the admin panel that can widen the window.
findings.recommendation: Add two registry keys covering the families (a SCANNER_DNS_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS for the setTimeout(reject, N) races and a SCANNER_HTTP_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS for the AbortSignal.timeout(N) fetches), resolve them once per scan in lib/scanner/async-checks.ts and thread them into each probe, and change the catch blocks (async-checks.ts:1147, :1301 and their siblings) to distinguish a timeout from a clean negative so the result carries an explicit 'check did not complete' marker instead of an empty array.

findings.title: The 'delete all scan history' confirmation states a count that is the display cap, not the row count, so a user with 400 scans is told 100 will be deleted and 400 are
findings.description: GET /api/v3/history caps its result with the admin setting HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:111, :128, :139; default CONFIG_HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS = 100 at lib/config/config-values.ts:640) and returns no total count alongside it. app/history/page.tsx:224 fetches that endpoint into `scans` and never learns a row was dropped. Three surfaces then present scans.length as the account total: the page subtitle at :580 ('{scans.length} scans on record'), the summary at :661-:663, and HistoryStats at :588. The worst of the three is the destructive confirmation at :659-:664, which reads 'This deletes all {scans.length} scans on this account, findings and notes included. This cannot be undone.' The DELETE handler it triggers has no LIMIT at all (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:220-222, `DELETE FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 AND (scan_type IS NULL OR scan_type != 'github')`), so it removes every row. The same shape sits on /assets: app/assets/page.tsx:153-:154 renders '{assets.length} distinct hosts you've scanned' over a list built from the same HISTORY_LIST_MAX_ROWS-capped scan query (app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:197-:206), with a second bare literal ALL_HOSTS_MAX = 500 (:105) capping the public scope. Client pagination compounds it: components/ui/pagination-control.tsx:11 offers page sizes up to 100 and app/history/page.tsx:633 passes totalItems={filtered.length}, so the control reports the cap as the truth.
findings.impact: A user on an unlimited-retention plan reads 'This deletes all 100 scans' and loses 400. The number in a one-way destructive confirmation understates its blast radius, which is the one place a number must not be approximate. Separately the Assets inventory, sold as a host inventory, silently omits every host whose last scan is older than the newest 100 scans.
findings.recommendation: Return a `total` (a COUNT(*) over the same WHERE clause, without the LIMIT) from GET /api/v3/history and GET /api/v3/assets, render that in the subtitle and the delete dialog, and pass it as totalItems to PaginationControl. Where the list is genuinely truncated, say so ('showing the 100 most recent of 412') rather than reporting the cap as the total.

findings.title: The only focus indicator is an inset ring in exactly the same colour as the primary button fill, so keyboard focus is invisible on every primary CTA in both themes
findings.description: app/globals.css:370 is the single source of the visible focus indicator for the whole product: `:focus-visible:not([tabindex="-1"]):not([data-radix-collection-item]) { @apply outline-hidden ring-2 ring-ring ring-inset; }`. It removes the native outline and replaces it with a 2px ring drawn INSIDE the element's own border box (the comment at :349 says ring-inset was chosen deliberately over the previous ring-offset-2 pair). The ring colour is `hsl(var(--ring))`, and `--ring` is defined identically to `--primary` in both themes: globals.css:178 `--primary: 213 94% 68%` / :196 `--ring: 213 94% 68%` (light) and :230 / :242 (dark). components/ui/button.tsx:12 gives the default Button variant `bg-primary`, and its own base class only sets `focus-visible:outline-hidden` with no replacement, so the base rule is the only indicator it gets. An inset ring in hsl(213 94% 68%) drawn on top of a fill of hsl(213 94% 68%) has a contrast ratio of exactly 1.00:1. Nothing anywhere restores the outline: `ring-offset` appears only in the comment at globals.css:349 and in one Radix toast class (components/ui/toast.tsx:80). lib/ui/animations.ts:92 `focus.ring` and the three per-component FOCUS_RING constants (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:79, inline-auth-form.tsx:46, crawl-url-selector.tsx:19) all use the same `ring-ring` colour and do not set --tw-ring-inset back, so they inherit the inset the base rule sets on the same element. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:76-79 publishes: "Focus Indicators: Visible focus indicators help users navigate with keyboards."
findings.impact: A keyboard-only user tabbing through Sign in, Sign up, Start scan, Save, Confirm, or any other default-variant Button sees no change at all: the ring is the same blue as the button. On the auth screens the submit button is the last stop in the form, so the user tabs off the password field and has no way to tell whether focus landed on the button or moved past it. WCAG 2.1 AA SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible fails on the single most-used control in the product, and the published accessibility statement asserts the opposite.
findings.recommendation: In app/globals.css, give --ring a value distinct from --primary (a light-theme value near hsl(213 60% 35%) clears 3:1 on every surface in the light palette, and a near-white value clears it on bg-primary), or drop `ring-inset` from the rule at :370 and pair `ring-2 ring-ring` with `ring-offset-2 ring-offset-background` so the ring is drawn against the page rather than the control's own fill. If ring-inset must stay for the clipping reason documented at :349, add a `[&.bg-primary]`-style override, or set `focus-visible:ring-primary-foreground` on the default variant in components/ui/button.tsx:12.

findings.title: ScanResult.incomplete is captured, persisted and typed on every surface but rendered by nothing, so a scan whose DNS/TLS/live-fetch branch timed out tells the user "every enabled check ran and none of them fired"
findings.description: The scanner records which async branches did not finish. lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4651-4656 builds `incomplete[]` from every branch whose `timedOut` flag is set; lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:746 reads it and :846 writes `...(incomplete.length > 0 ? { incomplete } : {})` into scan_history.result_meta. It survives the whole read path: lib/scanner/types.ts:258 declares it on ScanResult, lib/scanner/history-detail.ts:21 declares it on the API response and :71 maps it back onto ScanResult, app/api/v3/host/[hostname]/route.ts:41 returns it, and app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:113 explicitly threads it into the ScanResult it builds. Grepping `incomplete` across app/, components/, lib/ and extension/src returns not one JSX or template reference: no component reads the field. The declaration's own doc comment (lib/scanner/types.ts:251-257) states the contract it is violating verbatim: "A category listed here means 'not checked', not 'checked and clean': the UI should say so rather than treat a missing finding from that area as a clean result." What the user gets instead, when for example the DNS and TLS branches both time out on a slow resolver: components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:197 calls getSafetyRating(result.findings), zero remaining findings resolves to VERDICT.safe, and :45-52 prints "Nothing exploitable found". Below it, components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:220 sees findings.length === 0 and renders :228-235, "Nothing found on this scan / Every enabled check ran against this host and none of them fired." On the dashboard the override at components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:268-287 says the same thing louder: "Zero findings on this host / Every enabled check ran and none of them fired." The only trace of the truth anywhere on screen is the "Engine confidence" stat (scan-summary.tsx:295-302) dropping from 97% to 94% (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:368), an unexplained three-point difference in an unlabelled number.
findings.impact: This is the single most damaging failure in this class for a security scanner: a partially failed scan is presented as a clean bill of health, with an explicit sentence asserting that every check ran. A user whose TLS branch timed out reads "Nothing exploitable found" and ships. The same result feeds the public /host/[hostname] page and read-only /shared/[token] links, so the false all-clear is what a third party sees too, and the danger score and severity distribution are computed from the same truncated finding set. The data needed to prevent this is already in the database on every affected scan.
findings.recommendation: Render `result.incomplete` in components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx, above ScanSummary (:142) so it is read before the verdict, using the same warning block already built for `result.redirect` at :120-140 (border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/25 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/5, AlertTriangle, title plus reason plus mono detail line). Copy in the house voice: title "Part of this scan did not finish", body "The DNS and TLS checks ran out of time, so nothing from those areas was checked. This report is not a clean result for them, it is a gap. Rescan to fill it in." with the branch labels rendered as the mono detail line. Then gate the zero-findings block: when `incomplete` is non-empty, replace both empty-state copies (scan-result-detail.tsx:228-235 and dashboard-results.tsx:268-287) with "No findings from the checks that completed" and drop the "Every enabled check ran" sentence, which is false in that case. Suppress VERDICT.safe's "Nothing exploitable found" headline the same way in components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:197, since getSafetyRating cannot distinguish a clean scan from a truncated one.

findings.title: An async check branch that throws is recorded as complete, so a crashed DNS or TLS branch produces zero findings, an empty incomplete[] and full engine confidence
findings.description: boundedBranch (lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4428-4458) wraps each of the three async branches. Its success handler at :4441 returns `{ label, findings, timedOut: false }`; its rejection handler at :4442 returns `{ label, findings: NO_FINDINGS, timedOut: false }`. The timeout racer at :4453 is the only path that sets `timedOut: true`. runAsyncChecksDetailed then builds the incompleteness report from that flag alone (:4652-4655: `if (r.value.timedOut) incomplete.push(r.value.label)`). So a branch that rejects, a DNS resolver error, a TLS socket error, an unhandled exception anywhere inside the branch, is indistinguishable at that layer from a branch that ran to completion and found nothing. The in-code comment at :4438-4439 states the intent as "A rejecting branch contributes no findings, same as a timed-out one", but a timed-out one at least sets the flag and a rejecting one does not. Downstream that means lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:746-750 computes `getEngineConfidence(findings, asyncTimedOut || incomplete.length > 0)` with both operands false, so lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:368 uses the full base of 97 rather than 94, and :846 writes no `incomplete` key at all. This is the same bug class AUDIT-012#obs-01 filed for per-check exceptions inside runSyncChecks (lib/scanner/engine.ts:172), but at whole-branch granularity and with the extra bite that the mechanism specifically built to report incompleteness is bypassed rather than merely unlogged.
findings.impact: A permanently broken or transiently failing DNS/TLS/live-fetch branch reports the strongest possible result the product can produce: no findings from that area, no incompleteness marker, and 97% engine confidence. On a self-host with no outbound DNS, or an instance where one branch throws on a particular input shape, every scan reads as a clean TLS and DNS posture forever. Because the failure sets no flag, even the fix in state-01 would not surface it, and there is no log line either (obs-01), so nobody can find out from either side.
findings.recommendation: Change the rejection handler at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4442 to `() => ({ label, findings: NO_FINDINGS, timedOut: true })`, or better, add a distinct `failed: true` field and push the label into `incomplete` for both cases, so "timed out" and "crashed" are separable in result_meta while both reaching the UI as "not checked". Log the rejection reason with the branch label at the same point, which is what obs-01 asks for. The UI change is then free: the block proposed in state-01 already renders whatever is in `incomplete`.

findings.title: Deep (crawl) scans structurally cannot report incompleteness: the async layer is raced against a 15s timer that resolves to an empty array, and engine confidence is hardcoded to the complete value
findings.description: The crawl executor takes the bookkeeping-free path everywhere. lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:17 imports `runAsyncChecks`, not `runAsyncChecksDetailed`, whose own doc comment at lib/scanner/async-checks.ts:4617-4620 says "Use this from a route that surfaces scan completeness to the user; runAsyncChecks below is the same work without that bookkeeping". The crawl result is surfaced to the user through the exact same components as a single scan (app/dashboard/page.tsx:640-649 maps crawl.pages[0] straight into the ScanResult that DashboardResults renders). Then :203-217 races that call against `new Promise(resolve => { asyncTimeoutHandle = setTimeout(() => resolve([]), 15000) })`, so when the 15 second ceiling wins, every DNS, TLS and live-fetch finding for that page is silently replaced by an empty array with no record that it happened. Finally :747 hardcodes `engineConfidence: getEngineConfidence(allFindings, false)`, passing `false` for asyncTimedOut unconditionally, and the crawl's result_meta (:747-757) never writes an `incomplete` key at any point. Grepping `incomplete` in execute-crawl-scan.ts returns nothing.
findings.impact: Deep scan is the paid, slower, more thorough mode, and it is the one mode that cannot tell the user when it came back short. A crawl of a site with slow DNS or a slow TLS handshake reports zero TLS and DNS findings alongside "97%" engine confidence and the "Nothing exploitable found" verdict, with no timeout marker anywhere in the stored record. Because the 15 second ceiling is per page, a multi-page crawl silently drops a different subset of checks on each page, so the same crawl re-run produces different findings with no explanation, which breaks the product's headline promise that the same URL produces the same result.
findings.recommendation: In lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts switch line 17 and 206 to `runAsyncChecksDetailed`, collect the per-page `incomplete` labels alongside `findings`, union them across pages, pass the union's non-emptiness as the second argument to getEngineConfidence at :747 instead of the literal `false`, and write `...(incomplete.length > 0 ? { incomplete } : {})` into the result_meta at :747-757 exactly as lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:846 does. The outer 15s race at :203-217 should resolve to a sentinel that marks the page incomplete rather than to `[]`, so a timed-out page is never mistaken for a page with nothing to report. The UI then needs no further change once state-01 lands.

findings.title: Two loaders in the repo detail view skip setLoading(false) on the non-ok branch, so an API error leaves a permanent skeleton and makes the correctly written error and empty states unreachable
findings.description: components/repos/repo-detail.tsx has the best state ladder in the repo, :242-255 renders skeleton, then loadError, then empty, then data, and both of its loaders defeat it. `loadScans` (:85-102) sets `setLoadingScans(true)` at :86, parses the body at :92, and on `!res.ok` at :93-96 sets loadError and `return`s. There is no `finally`; `setLoadingScans(false)` is at :101, after the try/catch, so the early return skips it. `loadingScans` stays true forever, and the render at :242 checks `loadingScans` before `loadError`, so the error message that was just set can never be shown: the three Skeleton bars at :243-247 render indefinitely. `loadScanDetail` (:113-129) repeats it exactly: `setDetailLoading(true)` at :116, `if (!res.ok) { setScanDetail(null); return; }` at :119-122, and `setDetailLoading(false)` at :128 after the try/catch. The "scan could not be loaded" branch at :236 is gated on `!detailLoading`, so it is likewise unreachable. Note the trigger is specific and common: `await res.json()` runs before the `res.ok` check, so a non-JSON error body throws into the catch (which does reach the reset), while the app's own JSON error envelopes (403 when the repo is not in the working set, 404, a 500 with `{error}`) take the broken path. The catch clauses were written correctly; only the non-ok branches leak.
findings.impact: A user who opens a repo they no longer have access to, or hits a 500 on GET /api/v3/scan/github, sits on a skeleton that never resolves for as long as the page is open. There is no spinner timeout, no retry, and no message, and the specific error string the server sent is stored in state where nothing can render it. The same shape hits the per-scan detail view inside the repo timeline. A permanent skeleton reads as a hung app, so the user reloads, which reproduces it.
findings.recommendation: Convert both functions to try/catch/finally and move `setLoadingScans(false)` (:101) and `setDetailLoading(false)` (:128) into `finally` blocks. Also move `const data = await res.json()` (:92) below the `res.ok` check and guard it with `.catch(() => ({}))`, matching app/teams/page.tsx:151 and components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:229, so a non-JSON error body reaches the same designed error state as a JSON one. While there, give loadScanDetail its own error string rather than reusing the null-means-missing signal, so :236 can distinguish "deleted" from "failed to load".

findings.title: The profile page substitutes empty arrays and silent nulls for every failed sub-request in its ten-way Promise.all, so a backend blip shows a user zero API keys, zero webhooks, zero schedules and a wrong scan-privacy default
findings.description: app/profile/page.tsx:270-292 fires ten requests through Promise.all. Only `userRes` is checked for failure (:294-297, redirect to /login). Every other response is folded into a plausible default when it is not ok. :302-310 does `keysRes.ok ? await keysRes.json() : { keys: [] }` and the same for webhooks and schedules; :322-360 wrap notifPrefs, billingInfo, dataReqInfo, privacy, share privacy and posture digest in bare `if (res.ok)` blocks with no else. `loading` then flips false (the page renders past :621) and the Developer tab receives empty arrays as if they were the truth. Downstream: components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:648 clears its skeleton, :652-657 renders the sub-tab count badges from those arrays (no badge at all, since the badge is gated on `count > 0` at :683), components/profile/tabs/developer/webhooks-section.tsx:198-203 renders "Nothing is listening yet", and components/profile/tabs/developer/schedules-section.tsx:265-268 renders "No recurring scans yet". Worse, profile-developer-tab.tsx:252-256 computes `atKeyLimit` from the same empty array, so the plan's active-key ceiling is evaluated against zero. The privacy case is the sharpest: `scansPrivateByDefault` is initialised to null at app/profile/page.tsx:191-193 and only set at :344 inside `if (privacyRes.ok)`, and components/profile/tabs/profile-privacy-tab.tsx:46-50 resolves it as `preloadedScansPrivateByDefault ?? false`, with the sync effect at :73-77 doing the same, and :300 renders `checked={!scansPrivateByDefault}`. A user whose account is set to private-by-default is therefore shown "public by default" whenever GET /api/v3/account/privacy returns non-ok. digestEmailEnabled and sharePubliclyListedByDefault take the identical path.
findings.impact: This is a settings page telling a user, with no caveat, that things they configured do not exist. Someone whose schedules row fails to load believes their recurring scans were deleted and recreates them, producing duplicates. Someone whose keys row fails believes their API key is gone, and because atKeyLimit is computed from zero the UI invites them to create another one that the server will then reject. The privacy case is the one that actually harms: the page asserts "your scans are public by default" to a user who set them private, which is a false statement about a privacy setting on the page whose whole job is to state that setting correctly. AUDIT-011#admin-08 filed this exact shape for five admin panels; this is the same defect on the surface every ordinary user sees.
findings.recommendation: Switch app/profile/page.tsx:281 to Promise.allSettled and track a per-section load failure, then render a per-section error instead of the empty state. Concretely: add a `sectionErrors: Set<string>` to the page state, populate it in the ok checks at :302-360, and pass it to each tab. In profile-developer-tab.tsx render a bordered inline error above the list, reusing the destructive band already at app/teams/page.tsx:515-525, with copy "Couldn't load your API keys. This is not the same as having none, so nothing has been deleted." plus a Retry button calling fetchData. For the privacy tab, change profile-privacy-tab.tsx:46-50 to keep the toggle disabled and show "Couldn't read this setting" while the preloaded value is null, rather than resolving null to false; never render a privacy claim from a fallback. Do not let atKeyLimit be computed while the keys request failed.

findings.title: No visitor can ever scan their own URL without an account: the demo hardcodes window.location.origin, and all ~780 SEO pages funnel their only CTA into it
findings.description: app/demo/page.tsx:30-43 defines handleSelfScan(), which reads `const siteUrl = window.location.origin` at :38 and POSTs that to API.DEMO_SCAN. There is no URL input anywhere in the demo: components/demo/demo-hero.tsx:22-28 resolves the same origin after mount purely to display it as a read-only Target row (:69-72), and the only control is a single Run scan button (:44-53). The server does not impose this. app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts:114-133 reads `url` from the request body, accepts any http/https URL, and gates it with checkAccessRules (:136-149), safeFetch with a single-hostname redirect allowlist (:156-166), and an IP rate limit of DEMO_SCAN_LIMIT=5 per DEMO_WINDOW_HOURS=12 (config-values.ts:1029-1030). So the restriction to VulnRadar's own site is a UI decision, not a security control. Meanwhile every organic entry point funnels here: lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:107-137 ScanCta renders a primary button labelled "Run a free scan" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO, and it is used by app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:343, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx, app/checks/page.tsx, app/alternatives/page.tsx, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx, app/tools/page.tsx, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:148 and app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx, which is roughly 780 pages. app/tools/page.tsx:14 titles that surface "Free Online Security Tools, No Signup" and app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:38 answers its own FAQ with "Yes. Paste the API URL and VulnRadar runs the checks", yet neither page contains a single <input> or <form> (verified: zero matches for <input|<form|<Input in both files). The demo's own closing CTA states the problem out loud at components/demo/demo-cta.tsx:21 with the heading "That was our site. Try yours.", and the only button under it is Create a free account. Signup is not a short path either: app/signup/page.tsx:46 tells the user "You get a verification email, then the scanner", so the hosted flow is signup, leave the site, open mail, click, log in, then scan.
findings.impact: This is the single biggest conversion gap in the product. A visitor who arrives from a query like "online api security scanner" reads a page that promises pasting a URL, clicks the one primary button, and lands on a page whose only possible action is scanning vulnradar.dev. The intent that brought them is unserviceable without an email address and an out-of-band verification click, and the free single-URL scanners this product competes with (Security Headers, Mozilla Observatory, SSL Labs) all serve it in one field with no account. Roughly 780 pages of deliberate SEO investment terminate in a dead end.
findings.recommendation: Add a URL field to the demo and keep the self-scan as the secondary story. In components/demo/demo-hero.tsx, replace the read-only Target row with a controlled input plus an authorization checkbox, and in app/demo/page.tsx replace handleSelfScan's `window.location.origin` at :38 with the field value. The server needs no change. Gate abuse with the Turnstile the app already ships plus the existing 5-per-12h IP limit, and satisfy app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:53-55 with a required checkbox rather than by removing the feature. Copy to ship, hero H1: "Scan a URL. No account." Lead: "Paste any URL you are authorized to scan. The full check set runs against it from our servers and the whole report comes back, evidence and fixes included. Five runs per connection, then an account keeps the history." Field label: "URL to scan", placeholder "https://example.com". Checkbox: "I own this site or have written permission to scan it." Secondary button under the field: "Or scan VulnRadar itself", which preserves the existing dogfood flow. Keep components/demo/demo-info.tsx verbatim, it is the strongest trust copy in the repo, and retitle its H2 from "Why we let you scan us" to "We are a target on this page too" so it still reads correctly when the primary target is the visitor's URL. Then change the hero CTA order at components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:83-104: primary becomes "Scan a URL, no account" pointing at ROUTES.DEMO, secondary outline becomes "Create a free account" pointing at ROUTES.SIGNUP.

findings.title: Four marketing surfaces claim scans finish in under 3 seconds while the shipped scan path still awaits a 15s subdomain discovery, so the visitor watches the claim fail on the first scan
findings.description: The under-3-seconds claim is published in five places: app/landing/page.tsx:31 (the page meta description, "get a security report in under 3 seconds"), app/landing/page.tsx:77 (the FAQ answer "Under 3 seconds for a standard scan", which is also emitted as FAQPage structured data via FaqStructuredData at :110), components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:61 (the stat strip entry ["<3s", "per scan"]), components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:46 ("Most scans are done in under three seconds"), and README.md:8. components/landing/landing-api-example.tsx:23 also ships a sample response with "duration": 2841. AUDIT-011#scan-01 established the engine does not meet that on the signed-in path, and the cause is still present: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-795 still awaits autoSubdomainsPromise, capped at 15000ms by lib/scanner/subdomain-auto.ts, and components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:118 still starts the client stopwatch that AUDIT-011#scan-05 measured at 15 to 20 seconds. Verified at those exact lines in the current tree. The only surface where the claim holds is the demo, and only because app/api/v3/demo-scan/route.ts skips subdomain discovery entirely, which means the visitor sees 3 seconds in the demo and 17 seconds on their first real scan.
findings.impact: The product's headline differentiator is contradicted by the product roughly thirty seconds after the visitor reads it, on the first scan they run as a signed-up user. A specific number that turns out to be wrong by 5x is worse than no number, because it teaches the reader that the rest of the page's very specific claims (stable IDs, deterministic severities, real evidence) may be equally decorative. The FAQ answer is also syndicated as FAQPage structured data, so the false number is what an answer engine quotes.
findings.recommendation: Fix the engine, do not soften the copy: AUDIT-011#scan-01 specifies a roughly 10-line change at lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:791-802 and lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:698 that makes every one of these five claims true again. If that will not ship this cycle, remove the number rather than publish a false one. Interim copy: app/landing/page.tsx:31 becomes "Paste a URL and get ${TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL} deterministic checks back across headers, TLS, cookies, DNS, and secrets. Same URL, same finding IDs, every run. No agent to install." app/landing/page.tsx:75-78 FAQ becomes question "How long does a scan take?" answer "Checks run in parallel rather than in sequence, and the report shows the exact duration for your target. Slow DNS or a long certificate chain is what moves the number." components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:58-63 drops the speed stat and becomes [[checkCount, "checks"], [categoryCount, "categories"], ["0", "models in the detection path"], ["GPL-3.0", "licensed"]], which keeps the mono tabular-nums idiom and swaps the one number the product cannot back for the one differentiator it can. components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:45-49 becomes "Everything runs in parallel, so the wall clock is the slowest module, not the sum of them. The report tells you exactly how long yours took."

findings.title: robots.txt Disallows /shared/ and /host/ for every user agent, so Twitter, Facebook and Slack refuse to fetch a shared scan report and it unfurls with no preview at all
findings.description: lib/seo/routes.ts:107 defines DISALLOWED_PATHS, which includes "/shared/" (line 121) and "/host/" (line 122). app/robots.ts:60 spreads that list into the `User-agent: *` group, so the published robots.txt contains `Disallow: /shared/` and `Disallow: /host/` with no exception group. The three biggest link unfurlers all document that they obey robots.txt: X's card crawler (Twitterbot), Facebook's facebookexternalhit, and Slack's Slackbot-LinkExpanding. LinkedInBot and Discordbot behave the same way. The result is that the two URL shapes the product exists to have people share are the exact two shapes those fetchers are told not to touch. Indexing is already prevented independently: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 and app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 both call privatePageMetadata(), which emits `noindex, nofollow, nocache` (lib/seo/metadata.ts:85). So the robots.txt Disallow is doing a job the meta tag already does, and paying for it with the previews. The correct split is the standard one: robots.txt governs crawling, the robots meta tag governs indexing.
findings.impact: Sharing a scan report is a core, documented feature (app/docs/sharing/page.tsx) and the primary way this product could spread. Today a user pastes a /shared/<token> or /host/<hostname> link into Slack, X, LinkedIn or Facebook and gets a bare blue link with no title, no image and no description, because the fetcher reads robots.txt first and stops. Not a weak preview: no preview. Every share is a link that looks broken, which suppresses click-through on exactly the traffic the product gets for free.
findings.recommendation: In app/robots.ts, add a fourth rule group before the wildcard group for the link unfurlers: `{ userAgent: ["Twitterbot", "facebookexternalhit", "Slackbot-LinkExpanding", "Slackbot", "Discordbot", "LinkedInBot", "TelegramBot", "WhatsApp", "redditbot", "Iframely"], allow: "/", disallow: [...DISALLOWED_PATHS.filter(p => p !== "/shared/" && p !== "/host/"), ...QUERY_DISALLOW] }`. Keep /shared/ and /host/ in the wildcard group's Disallow and keep the noindex meta on both pages: indexing stays blocked by the meta tag, which is the mechanism that actually controls it. Pair this with seo-02 so the preview that now renders is worth rendering.

findings.title: Self-hosting is the differentiator that beats six of the eight commercial peers, it is asserted in six separate marketing surfaces, and AUDIT-014#host-01 proves it does not currently work
findings.category: competitive positioning: list (b), the load-bearing advantage
findings.description: Of the eight commercial DAST vendors researched (Detectify, Intruder, Probely/Snyk, Pentest-Tools.com, Acunetix/Invicti, Burp Suite DAST, Snyk, Astra), only Burp Suite DAST and Acunetix/Invicti offer real self-hosting; the other six are SaaS with at most an internal-scanning agent (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "Deployment" section). GPL-3.0 plus a working self-host is therefore the single structural advantage that no amount of engineering by a small team could otherwise buy. The product asserts it in six places: components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:39 ("Self-hosting is one Dockerfile and a Postgres connection string"), app/landing/page.tsx:82 (FAQ: "Yes. The whole thing is GPL-3.0 and runs on your own infrastructure"), app/landing/page.tsx:57 (the definitional FAQ answer), components/landing/landing-use-cases.tsx:21 ("a self-host path if the SaaS is a non-starter"), lib/seo/alternatives.ts:46 (the shared VR.hosting string reused on all five /alternatives pages), and lib/seo/alternatives.ts:103, :250, :317 (per-competitor FAQ answers repeating it). AUDIT-014#host-01 (critical) found that on an empty database instrumentation.ts exits 1 before creating a single table, and AUDIT-014#host-02 found the Dockerfile runtime stage never copies scripts/, so db:create and db:migrate are unrunnable inside the published image. Merged from mkt-03, which filed the same fact from the marketing surface. Its point stands and is folded in here: the recommendation is to keep the self-hosting copy rather than weaken it, because the marketing surface is itself the argument for prioritising the host-01 and host-02 fixes. If they cannot be fixed quickly, the copy has to change instead, since it is currently false on the landing page and in the README.
findings.impact: Every competitive claim on the site rests on a capability that a new self-hoster cannot currently exercise. A developer who reaches /alternatives/detectify, reads "self-host it yourself with no plan limits", clones the repo and fails at first boot does not file a bug: they conclude the open-source claim is decorative and leave. This is the one advantage the eight commercial peers structurally cannot copy, and it is the one that does not work.
findings.recommendation: Treat AUDIT-014#host-01 and #host-02 as competitive-blocking, not just deploy bugs: fix them before any further marketing or SEO work in section 19. Then add a CI job that runs the documented self-host path end to end (fresh Postgres container, docker compose up, assert /api/v3/health returns healthy) so the claim cannot silently rot again. Only once that job is green, promote self-hosting from a paragraph in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx to a named comparison row in lib/seo/alternatives.ts's shared VR object, phrased against the verified fact: "Self-host it. Six of the eight commercial web scanners cannot be run on your own infrastructure at any price."

findings.title: The product ships two mutually exclusive corner-radius conventions, so the scan result view and /profile are visibly different products sitting one nav item apart
findings.description: audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section C5 records the ladder: rounded-2xl for one flagship block, rounded-xl for content cards, code blocks, tables and the readout, rounded-lg for small cards and chip links, rounded-md for buttons. I counted every rounded-* literal per directory. components/scanner: 83 rounded-md, 4 rounded-lg, 0 rounded-xl. components/history: 21 rounded-md, 3 rounded-lg. components/shares, components/assets, components/host, components/teams and components/billing are the same shape (6, 6, 1, 10 and 36 rounded-md respectively). Against that, components/profile is 72 rounded-lg + 24 rounded-xl + 14 rounded-md, and components/admin is 132 rounded-lg + 19 rounded-xl + 26 rounded-md. These are not buttons: filtering to bordered card containers, the scanner family draws its panels at rounded-md (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862, dashboard.tsx:260,342,417,453, response-headers.tsx:46, dns-records-panel.tsx:207, port-scan-panel.tsx:126, threat-intel-panel.tsx, software-inventory-panel.tsx, results-list.tsx:463), while components/profile and components/admin draw the equivalent panels at rounded-lg or rounded-xl (18 and 9 of them respectively), and components/ui/card.tsx:12 (the shared primitive, used by 42 files) is rounded-lg. The landing page, the documented yardstick, uses rounded-xl for content cards. So the same nav bar leads to a 6px-radius scan report and a 12px-radius billing card.
findings.impact: Radius is one of the two or three cues a person uses to decide whether two screens belong to the same application. A user who scans a site and then opens Profile crosses a visible seam. It also makes every new component a coin flip for the author, which is how the split got to 83 versus 132 in the first place.
findings.recommendation: Adopt the landing ladder as written in design-language.md C5 and move the scanner family up, not the profile family down, because the shared primitive components/ui/card.tsx and 42 of its consumers are already on rounded-lg. Concretely: in components/scanner, change the bordered panel containers (issue-detail.tsx:608,719,837,862; dashboard.tsx:172,260,342,417,453; response-headers.tsx:46; dns-records-panel.tsx:207; port-scan-panel.tsx:126; results-list.tsx:463,598; scan-result-detail.tsx:228; crawl-pages-info.tsx:54; dashboard-error-state.tsx:182; scan-summary.tsx) from rounded-md to rounded-xl, and the same in components/history, components/shares, components/assets, components/host and components/teams. Leave rounded-md on the actual controls (inputs at results-list.tsx:379, buttons at :408,615) where it is correct. Then write the three-rung ladder into CLAUDE.md's spacing section so it is reviewable: rounded-xl = panel, rounded-lg = small card or chip, rounded-md = control, rounded-full = pill, rounded-2xl = one flagship block per page.

findings.title: Seven different page-H1 treatments across 71 pages, and the documented Page H1 scale appears on no signed-in page at all
findings.description: design-language.md B2 records the Page H1 (non-hero) as `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`, cited from app/pricing/page.tsx:77. I extracted the className of every <h1> in app/ and components/. Seven distinct treatments ship: (1) the documented one, on app/pricing/page.tsx:77, app/checks/page.tsx:75, app/checks/category/[category]/page.tsx:126, app/alternatives/page.tsx:40, app/alternatives/[competitor]/page.tsx:85, app/tools/page.tsx:56, app/tools/api-scanner/page.tsx:79, app/tools/link-checker/page.tsx:80, all of them public SEO pages; (2) `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-foreground` on app/history/page.tsx:576, app/assets/page.tsx:148, app/shares/page.tsx:160, app/repos/page.tsx:360,465 and app/public-scans/page.tsx:118; (3) `text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/legal/page.tsx:57 and app/teams/join/page.tsx:29; (4) `text-2xl sm:text-3xl font-semibold tracking-tight` on app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/compare/page.tsx:212, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32; (5) `text-lg font-semibold` with no tracking-tight on app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:144,161,218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:143,251; (6) `font-bold` variants on app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:52,82,145 and its three sibling checkout pages, app/checkout/success/checkout-success-content.tsx:98 and app/security/page.tsx:48; (7) `text-2xl sm:text-4xl` (skipping the 3xl step) on app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:195. Only the SEO family matches the spec. Every page a paying user actually works in is on one of the other six. text-balance, which design-language.md B3 says goes on every heading, is present only on the SEO family, checks/[id] and two modal titles.
findings.impact: A user moving Dashboard to History to Profile to Admin sees the page title change size three times for no reason, so nothing tells them what a page title is. Two of the seven treatments use font-bold, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work.
findings.recommendation: Two tiers, written down, then applied. Tier A (marketing, docs, SEO, legal, pricing): keep the documented `text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`. Tier B (in-app working pages, where the H1 sits above a dense table and must not eat the fold): standardise on `text-xl sm:text-2xl font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance text-foreground`, which treatment (2) already uses on five pages and which is the largest existing cluster. Change app/profile/page.tsx:679, app/admin/page.tsx:1021, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:30, app/badge/page.tsx:101, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:218 and app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:251 to Tier B, and app/security/page.tsx:48, app/legal/page.tsx:57, app/changelog/page.tsx:22, app/contact/page.tsx:56 and app/donate/page.tsx:32 to Tier A. Delete every font-bold in an <h1> (checkout pages are covered separately in dsn-05). Add both strings to CLAUDE.md under a Typography heading next to the existing Button and Spacing conventions, which is the only reason the button geometry stayed consistent and the heading scale did not.

findings.title: The four checkout pages are the least spec-conformant surface in the product and they are the revenue path: container mx-auto, py-8 md:py-12, font-bold headings and md: breakpoints, all four times over
findings.description: app/checkout/credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/github-credits/page.tsx, app/checkout/browser-credits/page.tsx and app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx (plus components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx) fail four of the fourteen tell-tale checks in design-language.md G simultaneously, and they are the only files in app/ that do. Check 2 (container): they are the only five files in the repo using Tailwind's `container` class, at credits:119,142, github-credits:121,140, browser-credits:123,142, [productId]:168,192 and checkout-skeleton:13,24, always as `container max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4`, where the documented default is `max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` and the responsive px step is missing. Check 1 (section rhythm): `py-8 md:py-12` at credits:142 and its three siblings, against the documented `py-16 sm:py-20`; md: rather than sm: is used for every breakpoint on these pages while the rest of app/ uses sm:. Check 7 (heading scale): `text-2xl font-bold mb-2` at credits:52,82, `text-2xl md:text-3xl font-bold mb-2` at :145, `text-lg font-bold` at :190 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :226, with the same lines in all three credit pages and [productId]:81,100,120,150,198,257. design-language.md B3 records that font-bold appears nowhere in the reference work. The three credit pages are otherwise near-identical files, which AUDIT-013#dup-06 already filed from the code-duplication angle (roughly 1,900 duplicated lines across the three checkout components and three pages); the design consequence is that a single fix has to be made three or four times and has not been.
findings.impact: This is the screen where a user hands over a card. It is visibly heavier and more cramped than the pricing page they arrived from: a bolder title, half the vertical room, a narrower measure and no sm: padding step, so on a 640px phone the page has 16px gutters where /pricing has 24px. It reads as a different, older product at the exact moment trust matters most, and the same four defects have to be fixed four times because the pages were copied.
findings.recommendation: Fix this together with AUDIT-013#dup-06's collapse rather than separately. When the three credit pages fold into one parameterised CreditCheckout page, give the surviving page: `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1} className="w-full max-w-4xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6 py-12 sm:py-16">` (max-w-4xl is defensible for a single-task form; drop the `container` class, which does nothing here but add Tailwind's own padding), the Tier A page H1 from dsn-04 (`text-3xl sm:text-4xl font-semibold tracking-tight mb-5 text-balance`), `text-lg font-semibold` for the tier price at credits:190, and `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` for the Total today figure at :226. Change every md: breakpoint on these pages to sm: to match the rest of app/. Apply the same to app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx and components/billing/checkout-skeleton.tsx so the skeleton and the loaded page still line up.

findings.title: Six implementations of one inline stat strip, at three different value type sizes and two container geometries, and two byte-identical copies of the STAT_ICON_TONES table
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-12, which caught the Cell duplication between components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17 and the three identical stats skeletons, from the code angle. It missed four more copies and did not record the visual result. The full set: components/history/history-stats.tsx:18 defines a third byte-identical Cell; components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94 defines StatCell (the same markup with items-start instead of items-center and no textTone); components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75 defines Stat (same again at StatIcon size="sm" with a text-sm value and flex-1 basis-24 instead of a grid); components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:52 defines StatBar, a sixth. The value type size differs three ways for the same element: text-2xl in history-stats/assets-stats/shares-stats/dashboard.tsx:108, text-sm in scan-summary.tsx:88, text-lg in stat-card.tsx:82. The container differs two ways: `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` in the four app-side copies versus `flex flex-wrap rounded-lg border border-border/50 bg-border/50 gap-px overflow-hidden` at stat-card.tsx:62. On top of that, the STAT_ICON_TONES lookup is duplicated verbatim, nine keys and all their class strings, at components/shared/stat-icon.tsx:11-24 and components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-24; stat-icon.tsx's own docblock at :4-10 says it exists to stop each file inventing its own colours and then names stat-card.tsx as the pattern it is copying rather than importing from it.
findings.impact: This is the mechanism by which one product stops looking like one product, applied to the element a user meets first on five different pages. The counts row on /dashboard, /history, /assets and /shares is 24px tall type in a 6px-radius box; the same row on /admin is 18px type in an 8px-radius box with a half-opacity border; the same row inside a scan summary is 14px type in a flex strip. Nothing distinguishes them semantically, so a reader learns the pattern four times. Two copies of the tone table mean the next colour added lands in one of them.
findings.recommendation: Promote a single components/shared/stat-strip.tsx exporting `StatStrip({ items, size })` and reusing the existing StatIcon, with size="md" giving today's `text-2xl font-semibold leading-none tabular-nums tracking-tight` value and size="sm" giving `text-sm`, and one container: `flex flex-wrap gap-px overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-border` (rounded-xl per dsn-03). Delete Cell from components/history/history-stats.tsx:18, components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:9 and components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:17, StatCell from components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:94, Stat from components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:75, and rewrite components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx's StatBar as a thin wrapper that adds only the onClick/aria-pressed filtering behaviour its docblock at :46-51 describes. Delete the STAT_ICON_TONES block at components/admin/shared/stat-card.tsx:11-26 and import StatTone and the tones from components/shared/stat-icon.tsx. Collapse the three stats skeletons AUDIT-013#dup-12 lists into one StatStripSkeleton beside it so the loading state cannot drift from the loaded state again.

findings.title: Five empty-state grammars, four of which are byte-identical wrappers around the same markup with a different icon and sentence
findings.description: Five distinct empty-state treatments ship. (1) The app family, `flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center` with a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/60, a text-sm font-semibold title, a max-w-xs text-xs body and an optional sm Button: components/history/history-empty-state.tsx:25 and :48, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx:20 and :41, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx:7, components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:5, components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56 and :72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:269 and components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:228. The four standalone files are the same JSX with only the icon and copy swapped, and each is its own module. (2) The admin family, components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:19-45 EmptyState: no dashed border and no card at all, a 12x12 rounded-full bg-muted/50 circle holding a 6x6 icon at text-muted-foreground/50, py-16 px-4, text-sm font-medium title, text-xs max-w-sm body. Used by roughly 14 admin panels plus app/admin/page.tsx:1301,1502. (3) components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx:8, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/30 py-14 px-6`. (4) components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251, `rounded-lg border border-dashed border-border px-4 py-10` with no background at all. (5) components/profile/tabs/developer/api-keys-section.tsx:250, `rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-muted/20 p-5 sm:p-6` left-aligned. Radius spans md, lg and xl; the surface spans bg-card/50, bg-card/30, bg-muted/20 and nothing; the icon is bare in one family and in a circle in the other.
findings.impact: Empty states are the first thing a new account sees on five pages in a row (/history, /assets, /shares, /teams, the results list) and they are the first thing an admin sees in fourteen panels. Two unrelated grammars for the same moment make the admin panel read as a bolted-on second application, which is exactly how it is built. Four separate one-file modules means a copy change or an a11y fix has to be made four times.
findings.recommendation: Add components/shared/empty-state.tsx exporting `EmptyState({ icon, title, description, action, variant })` with the app family's geometry as the default (`flex flex-col items-center gap-3 rounded-xl border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-14 text-center`, rounded-xl per dsn-03) and variant="inline" dropping the border and background for use inside a card that already has one, which is what the admin EmptyState is really doing. Delete components/history/history-empty-state.tsx, components/assets/assets-empty-state.tsx, components/shares/shares-empty-state.tsx and components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx and call the shared component from the four pages with their icon and copy inline; delete the inline copies at components/teams/teams-list.tsx:56,72, components/scanner/results-list.tsx:598, dashboard-results.tsx:269 and scan-result-detail.tsx:228; re-export the shared component from components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx as EmptyState with variant="inline" so the fourteen admin call sites need no edit, and delete its body at :19-45. Fold components/badge/badge-empty-state.tsx and components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:251 in too.

findings.title: Twenty-three distinct inline alert geometries across 53 files, with four radii, three border opacities and two off-scale background opacities, because there is no Alert primitive
findings.category: one-off components / inline alerts (53 files across app/ and components/, no primitive in components/ui/)
findings.description: components/ui/ has no alert.tsx. 53 files hand-roll the inline error banner. Extracting every className that pairs a destructive border with a destructive background and has padding and a radius gives 23 unique strings, including: `rounded-md border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 text-sm text-destructive`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 px-3 py-2 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/5 px-3.5 py-3 ...`, `rounded-lg border border-destructive/20 bg-destructive/5 px-3 py-2.5`, `flex items-start gap-3 p-4 rounded-xl border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10` (app/teams/page.tsx:518), `rounded-xl border border-destructive/25 bg-destructive/3 p-4 sm:p-5`, `p-4 rounded-2xl mb-5 bg-destructive/10 text-destructive` and `flex flex-col gap-3 rounded-lg border border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/6 p-4`. Radius spans rounded-md, rounded-lg, rounded-xl and rounded-2xl; border opacity spans /20, /25 and /30; background spans /3, /5, /6 and /10; padding spans p-3, p-4, px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5, px-3.5 py-3 and px-4 py-3. bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 are not steps on Tailwind's opacity scale, so they are one-off arbitrary values. The success side has the same problem plus a second syntax split: `bg-[hsl(var(--success)/0.1)]` and `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` both appear for the same colour, and the success banner exists at rounded-md and rounded-lg with px-3 py-2, px-3 py-2.5 and px-3.5 py-3. AUDIT-013#dup-14 filed the state-management half of this (50 components hand-roll a useState banner pair while a full Radix toast stack serves one consumer); this is the visual half and it stands whichever way that decision goes.
findings.impact: Error and success feedback is the highest-stakes UI in the product because it appears when something has gone wrong, and it looks different on every screen it appears on. Nothing signals "this is the app telling you something" consistently. A designer changing the error treatment has to touch 53 files and will miss some, and the two off-scale opacities mean two of the banners are already a shade nobody chose deliberately.
findings.recommendation: Add components/shared/inline-alert.tsx exporting `InlineAlert({ tone, title, children, onDismiss })` with tone in error | success | warning | info. One geometry: `flex items-start gap-2.5 rounded-lg border px-3.5 py-3 text-sm`. One tone table using the dsn-01 foreground tokens: error `border-destructive/30 bg-destructive/10 text-[hsl(var(--destructive-text))]`, success `border-[hsl(var(--success))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--success-text))]`, warning `border-[hsl(var(--warning))]/30 bg-[hsl(var(--warning))]/10 text-[hsl(var(--warning-text))]`, info `border-primary/25 bg-primary/5 text-foreground`. Include the leading lucide icon (AlertTriangle / Check / AlertTriangle / Info) and role="alert" so every call site gets the announcement free. Migrate in batches by directory, starting with components/profile (the setError/setSuccess tree at components/profile/types.ts already threads one pair everywhere, so it is the cheapest) and app/teams/page.tsx:518, app/profile/page.tsx:695, app/repos/page.tsx:333 and app/attack-surface/page.tsx:45. Standardise the token syntax on `bg-[hsl(var(--success))]/10` (Tailwind opacity modifier) rather than the two-syntax mix, and delete the bg-destructive/3 and bg-destructive/6 arbitrary values.

findings.title: Six modal scrims and five modal card geometries, and two of the scrims are opposite colours in light mode: bg-black/80 versus bg-background/80
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-013#dup-07, which inventoried the sixteen hand-rolled modals for missing focus trap, Escape and scroll lock. The visual half was not recorded. Six distinct scrims ship: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-black/80` (components/ui/dialog.tsx:23, alert-dialog.tsx:20, sheet.tsx:24); `bg-black/60 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:838, ip-rules-manager.tsx:273, staff-list.tsx:290 and :634, teams-list.tsx:168, gift-subscription-modal.tsx:66); `bg-black/50 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1534); `bg-background/80 backdrop-blur-xs` (components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:121, components/shared/notification-center.tsx and the scanner modals); `bg-background/95 backdrop-blur-xs` (the mobile nav drawers); and none at all (components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx wrapper). In dark mode black/80 and background/80 look similar. In light mode --background is 213 25% 90%, so bg-black/80 dims the page to near-black while bg-background/80 washes it to near-white: two modals opened one after another invert the whole screen. The cards differ too: components/ui/dialog.tsx:39 is `border bg-background p-6 shadow-lg sm:rounded-lg max-w-lg`; the admin hand-rolls are `bg-card border border-border rounded-xl p-6 shadow-2xl`; components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:41 and crawl-url-selector.tsx:107 are `rounded-md border border-border bg-card shadow-lg`; components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:127 is `rounded-md shadow-2xl`; components/shared/notification-center.tsx:133 is `rounded-2xl shadow-2xl`. So the surface is bg-background or bg-card, the radius is lg, md or 2xl, and the shadow is lg or 2xl. design-language.md D1 records that shadows in this system are near-invisible (shadow-xs) and that rounded-2xl is reserved for one flagship block.
findings.impact: Opening two dialogs in a session, for example the AI choice modal on /dashboard and then the crop dialog on /profile, shows two different products, and in light mode the page behind them goes dark for one and light for the other, which reads as a rendering bug rather than a style choice. It also means the eleven hand-rolled modals AUDIT-013#dup-07 wants migrated onto Radix cannot be migrated without a visible change, which is a reason the migration keeps not happening.
findings.recommendation: Pick one scrim and put it in components/ui/dialog.tsx: `fixed inset-0 z-50 bg-background/80 backdrop-blur-xs` reads correctly in both themes, unlike bg-black/80, and it is already what the newer in-app modals use. Change dialog.tsx:23, alert-dialog.tsx:20 and sheet.tsx:24 to it. Set the card to `border border-border bg-card p-6 shadow-lg sm:rounded-xl max-h-[90vh] overflow-y-auto` (bg-card, not bg-background, so the panel separates from the scrim; rounded-xl per dsn-03) at dialog.tsx:39 and alert-dialog.tsx:37. Then migrate the eleven hand-rolled modals AUDIT-013#dup-07 lists onto it, starting with components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:66, which sits in the same directory as a Dialog-based sibling. Drop shadow-2xl everywhere; it appears nowhere in the reference work.

findings.title: Seven visual treatments for a row of tabs, only two of which use the Radix Tabs primitive, and /profile's sidebar is /admin's with the focus ring removed
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-011#prof-01 (which filed /profile's mobile tab strip for having no accessible name below 640px) with the rest of the class.
