Seven treatments: (1) components/ui/tabs.tsx:16-33, a segmented control on `bg-muted p-1` with an active `bg-background shadow-xs` at rounded-sm, h-10, px-3 py-1.5, imported by exactly two files (components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:29 and system-settings-manager.tsx:12); (2) components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896-916, the same idiom hand-rolled at a different size, `flex gap-1 rounded-md bg-muted p-1` with active `bg-card shadow-xs`, rounded, px-2.5 py-1, text-xs; (3) app/assets/page.tsx:160-183, a third segmented variant, `inline-flex rounded-md border border-border bg-card p-0.5` with active `bg-primary text-primary-foreground`, a solid brand fill where the other two use a neutral raise; (4) components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29-44, underline tabs, `flex gap-1 border-b border-border/50` with `-mb-px border-b-2 border-primary px-3 py-2`, and no role or aria-current at all since they are Links; (5) components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx:30-47, underline plus fill plus top radius, `rounded-t-lg` with active `bg-secondary/30 border-b-2 border-primary`, px-4 py-2; (6) app/profile/page.tsx:723-739, the mobile strip, underline again but at px-3.5 py-3 with a `border-b border-border/80` rail rather than /50; (7) app/profile/page.tsx:743-768 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052-1097, the desktop vertical sidebar, `bg-primary/10 text-primary font-medium` pills at rounded-lg. Treatment (7) is nearly the same code twice: admin uses px-2.5 py-2 and includes `focus-visible:outline-hidden focus-visible:ring-2 focus-visible:ring-ring` at :1076; profile uses px-3 py-2.5 and has no focus classes at all, so on /profile the eight sidebar links receive no visible focus except whatever the global :focus-visible rule at app/globals.css:370 supplies, and the sidebar widths differ (lg:w-48 versus lg:w-52).
findings.impact: Tabs are the primary navigation idiom of the signed-in product and there is no such thing as "a tab" here. /assets renders its scope toggle as a solid blue pill, which under design-language.md's accent-restraint doctrine spends the page's one accent on a filter switch; two segmented controls that are visually the same are built two different ways so a keyboard fix lands on one; and the vertical sidebar that /profile and /admin share was copied rather than extracted, which is how /profile lost the explicit focus ring.
findings.recommendation: Two shared components, not seven. (a) components/shared/segmented-control.tsx wrapping Radix Tabs with the components/ui/tabs.tsx:16 geometry plus a size prop ("sm" giving px-2.5 py-1 text-xs for dense use); replace components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:896 and app/assets/page.tsx:160 with it, and change the assets active state from bg-primary to the neutral `bg-background shadow-xs` raise the primitive already uses. (b) components/shared/section-nav.tsx holding the vertical sidebar markup currently duplicated at app/profile/page.tsx:743 and app/admin/page.tsx:1052, taking `items`, `groups` and `width`, with admin's focus-visible classes and admin's px-2.5 py-2, and use it on both pages. Keep the underline treatment for cross-page navigation only (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx), give it `aria-current="page"` on the active Link, and switch components/docs/docs-code-tabs.tsx to the same underline geometry (drop rounded-t-lg and bg-secondary/30) so there is one underline tab and one segmented tab in the whole product. AUDIT-011#docs-11's tabpanel/aria-controls fix should land on (a) once, not on each copy.

findings.title: The onboarding tour is the most AI-generated-looking surface in the product and it is the first thing every new account sees: a chart-ramp rainbow of icons, icon-in-a-rounded-square, font-bold and Title Case SaaS copy
findings.description: components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:24-79 defines eight steps and gives each one a colour off the chart ramp: step 2 text-[hsl(var(--chart-2))] (160 degrees, teal), step 3 --chart-3 (30, orange), step 4 --chart-4 (280, purple), step 5 --chart-5 (340, pink), then --chart-2 and --chart-3 again for steps 6 and 7. That fails tell-tale 4 (primary is blue and rationed, accent on at most two elements per section) and misuses the chart ramp, which app/globals.css:197-201 defines for data series, as UI decoration; the repetition at steps 6 and 7 proves the colours encode nothing. The icon is then set in a tinted rounded square at :215-221, `inline-flex p-2 rounded-md bg-muted/50` plus the step colour, which is the exact icon-in-a-rounded-square grammar CLAUDE.md and design-language.md E1 name as the giveaway; every one of the eight steps gets one, and the sidebar at :175-200 repeats the coloured icon a second time per step. :223 uses `text-lg font-bold`, a weight design-language.md B3 records as appearing nowhere in the reference work, and :127 uses shadow-2xl on a rounded-md card, failing tell-tales 7 and 10. The copy fails F1's voice rules outright: "Your all-in-one web vulnerability scanner. Let's walk you through the key features so you can get the most out of VulnRadar" (:28), "Scan Any Website" (:32), "Track Your History" (:39), "Team Collaboration" (:65), "You're All Set!" (:72), "Integrate VulnRadar into your CI/CD pipeline for continuous security monitoring" (:53), "Happy scanning with VulnRadar!" (:74). Every title is Title Case where the product's own headings are sentence-case declarative statements ("This is a finding, in full", "What actually happens when you hit scan"), and every description states a benefit rather than a mechanism.
findings.impact: This modal is the first VulnRadar interface a new user ever sees, before the dashboard. It sets the expectation for the whole product and it contradicts every rule the landing page follows, so a visitor who was sold by the landing copy meets a generic onboarding carousel one click later. The rainbow is also the only place in the app where four unrelated hues appear together, which undermines the accent restraint the rest of the product maintains.
findings.recommendation: Keep the structure, which is genuinely good (a named step list on the left rather than a dot pager, and the docblock at :143-145 says why), and fix the surface. Delete the `color` field from every entry in STEPS and render all icons at text-muted-foreground with the active one at text-primary, so the accent marks position and nothing else; that also removes the last two consumers of --chart-2 through --chart-5 outside a chart. Delete the `inline-flex p-2 rounded-md bg-muted/50` icon plate at :215 and put the icon inline before the title at h-4 w-4. Change :223 to `text-lg font-semibold tracking-tight text-balance` and :127 to `rounded-xl shadow-lg` (see dsn-09). Rewrite the eight titles as sentence-case statements and the bodies as mechanism, in the voice of design-language.md F1: for example step 2 "Paste a URL and hit Scan" / "310 checks run in parallel against the live response. Every finding comes back with a stable ID and a config snippet you can paste.", step 3 "Every scan is kept" / "Filter by URL or tag. Tag a scan production or staging and the tag survives a rescan.", step 4 "Diff two scans of the same URL" / "Same URL, same finding IDs, so the diff is the list of things that actually changed.", step 8 "Go run one" / "Nothing else to configure." Remove "all-in-one", "Happy scanning" and the CI/CD sentence.

findings.title: Two callout components with overlapping variant names map warning to two different colours and use border-2, a width used nowhere else in the system
findings.description:
components/docs/docs-callout.tsx:22-47 and components/legal/legal-callout.tsx:10-26 are two callout components with a `variant` prop whose vocabularies overlap but do not match: docs has info | warning | success | error, legal has warning | danger | info. `warning` exists in both and resolves to different colours: docs uses --warning (38 degrees) at :34-36, legal uses --severity-medium (45 degrees) at :12-14. `error` and `danger` are the same thing under two names. The geometry is unrelated too: docs is `rounded-r-lg border border-l-4 border-border/50 p-4` with a coloured left rule, a 3.5 icon and a text-xs font-semibold label, and its docblock at :14-19 explains the choice ("the left rule does the work; there is no icon-in-a-rounded-square, because four of those down a page is decoration"). Legal is `max-w-prose rounded-xl border-2 p-5` with no icon and a text-base font-semibold h3. border-2 appears on exactly one other non-decorative element in app/ and components/ (an avatar ring and a spinner), so it is a one-off width. Both are correct on tokens, so this is purely a grammar split. It also produces a heading-level inconsistency: the legal callout emits an

inside legal sections that already have their own h3s, while the docs callout emits a

.
findings.impact: A reader who goes from /docs/self-hosting (which uses the docs callout heavily) to /legal/acceptable-use sees the same kind of aside drawn with a different border weight, a different radius, no icon and no coloured rule, and the warning aside changes hue. The duplicated vocabulary also means a future "add a note about X" ticket gets two different implementations depending on which directory it lands in.
findings.recommendation:
Delete components/legal/legal-callout.tsx and re-export DocsCallout from components/shared/callout.tsx (moved out of components/docs/ since two sections use it), mapping the two legal call sites: app/legal/acceptable-use/page.tsx:51 variant="warning" stays warning, app/legal/dmca/page.tsx:62 variant="info" stays info, and app/security/page.tsx:63 variant="info" stays info. Keep the docs geometry and the four-variant vocabulary (info | warning | success | error), since it is the one with a written rationale and 60-odd call sites. Add an optional `as="h3"` prop if a legal callout genuinely needs to be a heading in the document outline; otherwise leave it as the

label the docs version uses. Retire the name `danger`.

findings.title: The profile Social tab and the two OAuth profile modals are a brand-chrome island: full-bleed vendor gradients, decorative white blobs, text-white and font-bold, unlike anything else in the app
findings.description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:604 opens the Discord card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#5865F2] via-[#4752C4] to-[#3C45A5] px-6 py-5` and :777 opens the GitHub card with `relative bg-linear-to-br from-[#24292e] via-[#1b1f23] to-[#0d1117] px-6 py-5`, both with `titleClassName="text-white"` and `subtitleClassName="text-white/70"`, a `h-10 w-10 rounded-xl bg-white` icon plate at :154, a `bg-white/15 backdrop-blur-xs ring-1 ring-white/20` plate at :607 and a `bg-white/20 text-white border-white/30` badge at :622. components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx:90-125 and components/modals/github-profile-modal.tsx:97-125 go further: a full-bleed brand header, three absolutely positioned `rounded-full bg-white/20` decorative circles at :92-94 and :99-101, a `border-4 border-background ring-4` avatar at :120, `text-xl font-bold text-white` at :107 and `text-2xl font-bold` at :125. Nowhere else in app/ or components/ is there a gradient header, a decorative blob, a border-4 ring or text-white outside a scrim. The rest of the product paints on bg-card with a border and spends colour on one element per section. The literal hexes are legitimate third-party brand colours (design-language.md A3 permits them), so the problem is not the values, it is the composition: five nested branded surfaces to say "you can sign in with Discord".
findings.impact: /profile is one of the two or three most-visited signed-in pages, and its Social tab looks like a different design system dropped into a slot. The gradient headers also make the two cards the loudest thing on a page whose actual content (2FA, API keys, billing) is quieter, so visual weight is inverted against importance. The three floating white circles are pure decoration in a product whose illustration doctrine (design-language.md E2) is "the actual mechanism of the product, rendered as itself".
findings.recommendation: Bring both cards back to the house grammar and keep the brand colour as a single accent. Replace the gradient header at profile-social-tab.tsx:604 and :777 with the standard card header used elsewhere in the tab tree, `flex items-center gap-3 border-b border-border/60 px-5 py-4`, holding a `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` plate filled with the vendor colour (bg-[#5865F2] / bg-[#181717]) and the vendor glyph in white, then `text-base font-semibold text-foreground` for the label and `text-xs text-muted-foreground` for the subtitle; that keeps the brand recognisable in exactly one element per card. Drop titleClassName / subtitleClassName / headerClassName from the OAuthIdentityCard props entirely once both callers stop overriding them. Keep the connect button's brand fill at :721 and :780 (it is the one action that should read as the vendor's) but drop shadow-xs. In components/modals/discord-profile-modal.tsx and github-profile-modal.tsx, delete the six decorative `bg-white/20` circles at :92-94 and :99-101, replace the gradient header with the same bordered header, change `text-xl font-bold text-white` to `text-lg font-semibold text-foreground` and `border-4 ... ring-4` to `ring-2 ring-border`.

findings.title: The AI chat renders code blocks and inline code on bg-black/30, which is a mid-grey slab on the light theme instead of the documented code surface
findings.description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:226 renders every markdown <pre> in an assistant reply as `bg-black/30 border border-border/30 rounded-md p-2.5 my-2 text-[11px] font-mono` and :241 renders inline code as `bg-black/30 px-1 py-0.5 rounded border border-border/20`. components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx:43 and :58 carry byte-identical copies (AUDIT-013#dup-11 filed the duplication; this is about the colour). bg-black/30 is a fixed 30 percent black regardless of theme. On the dark theme it composites over --card (224 18% 9%) to something marginally darker than the panel, which is roughly the intent. On the light theme it composites over --card (213 22% 95%) to about #A7AAAD, a mid-grey slab, and the surrounding message text is --foreground at 220 20% 10%. design-language.md B2 records the shipped code idioms: inline code is `font-mono text-xs px-1.5 py-0.5 rounded bg-background border border-border/60 text-foreground` and a code block is `rounded-xl border border-border/60 bg-muted/40`. Neither uses a fixed black. The same file has one more theme-blind value at :304, `hover:bg-black/20` on the copy button.
findings.impact: Anyone using the light theme sees the AI assistant answer questions in grey boxes that look like unloaded images, and a config snippet (the thing the assistant is most often asked for) is the least readable part of the reply. The AI chat is a supported, promoted feature on every page, so this is a per-page defect on the light theme rather than a corner case.
findings.recommendation: Change all four sites (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:226,241 and components/ai-chat/message-content.tsx:43,58) to the documented code idiom: <pre> to `bg-muted/60 border border-border/60 rounded-lg p-2.5 my-2 text-[11px] font-mono text-foreground overflow-x-auto whitespace-pre`, inline <code> to `bg-background border border-border/60 px-1 py-0.5 rounded text-[0.82em] font-mono text-foreground`. Change :304's `hover:bg-black/20` to `hover:bg-muted`. Do this as part of AUDIT-013#dup-11's collapse (delete the chat-widget copies and import the message-content ones) so the fix cannot land on only one of the two.

findings.title: The PDF report is branded in the dead cyan brand: BRAND_COLOR is #1AB3CC at 189 degrees, not the shipped blue #60a5fa
findings.description: lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:26-27 hardcodes `BRAND_COLOR = [0.1, 0.7, 0.8]` (#1AB3CC, hue ~189) and `BRAND_DARK = [0.05, 0.35, 0.4]` (#0D5966, hue ~189). Those two constants carry the entire brand identity of the document: the 8pt cover accent bar (:145), the wordmark set in 28pt (:150), the 2pt rule under it (:155), the rule at the top of every findings page (:311, :409), and the "DETAILED FINDINGS" / "Remediation Steps" / "Code Examples" subheads (:318, :370, :379). The real brand is blue #60a5fa, agreed by app/globals.css:178, lib/config/config-values.ts:188, lib/config/brand.ts:19-21, public/og-image.svg and the store PNGs, and recorded in audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section A2. This is the same class of defect as app/global-error.tsx:10's `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` and it extends AUDIT-011#design-01, which filed only the stale CLAUDE.md line and not the two code sites that still ship the old colour. lib/config/brand.ts already exists and describes itself (:1-13) as "the single source of truth for out-of-app surfaces", but pdf-report.ts does not import it.
findings.impact: The one document that leaves the product and gets forwarded to someone who has never seen the app is teal. A reader who then visits the site sees a blue product. Nothing on the PDF matches the OG card in a Slack unfurl, the extension, or the emails, so the brand reads as three unrelated tools.
findings.recommendation: Import BRAND from lib/config/brand.ts into lib/reports/pdf-report.ts and add a hex-to-PDF-rgb helper (`function rgb(hex: string): [number, number, number]`), then replace BRAND_COLOR with rgb(BRAND.primaryLight) (#60a5fa) and BRAND_DARK with rgb(BRAND.primary) (#3b82f6). Do the same for TEXT_PRIMARY / TEXT_SECONDARY / TEXT_MUTED, which are currently three more ad-hoc greys, mapping them to a light-surface equivalent of BRAND.text / textMuted / textFaint. While there, fix app/global-error.tsx:10 the same way (a literal "#60a5fa", since that file cannot import at runtime safely, with a comment pointing at brand.ts). Add a lint-visible comment in brand.ts naming pdf-report.ts as a consumer so the next colour change catches it.

findings.title: The extension declares its design tokens three separate times and the three copies disagree with each other and with the app
findings.description: The extension defines the same `--vr-*` token set in three places with no shared source. (1) extension/src/popup.css:5-66 declares it four times over: `:root`, a `prefers-color-scheme: dark` block, `[data-theme="light"]` and `[data-theme="dark"]`. (2) extension/src/options.css:5 `@import`s popup.css, so it inherits (1), which is correct. (3) extension/src/content/reputation-card.ts:454-500 redeclares the whole set inside CARD_CSS on `.card`, and it does not agree with (1): light `--vr-bg` is `#ffffff` there against `#dfe5ec` in popup.css, light `--vr-border` is `#e2e5ec` against `#c3cbd5`, dark `--vr-bg` is `#14171f` against `#0e111a`, and `--vr-primary-fg` is `#ffffff` against `#15192a` (popup.css:15-18 documents that white-on-primary was fixed for a 2.5:1 contrast failure, and CARD_CSS reintroduces exactly that pairing). Against the app the whole extension set is approximate rather than equal: app dark --background is 224 20% 6% = #0C0E12 vs #0e111a; dark --card 224 18% 9% = #13151B vs #13161f; dark --border 224 15% 16% = #23262F vs #232735; dark --foreground 210 20% 95% = #F0F2F5 vs #eaeef4; light --foreground 220 20% 10% = #14181F vs #15192a; light --border 213 16% 78% = #BEC6D0 vs #c3cbd5. --radius is 0.5rem (8px) in the app against --vr-radius 10px / --vr-radius-sm 6px. Only --vr-primary (#60a5fa) is exactly right. The extension is a separate npm package with its own package.json, package-lock.json and vite.config.ts, so it cannot import from lib/, which is why this drifted; audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md A3.3 already recorded the store PNGs as a fourth near-black navy, and this is the code behind it.
findings.impact: The reputation card is injected into arbitrary third-party pages and is the extension surface most people see first, and it does not match the popup they open next: a white card against the popup's blue-tinted #dfe5ec, and a lighter dark card against the popup's near-black. The white-on-#60a5fa primary button inside CARD_CSS reintroduces a contrast pairing the popup already fixed as sub-3:1. Any future retune of app/globals.css silently leaves the extension behind, and there is nothing in the build that would catch it.
findings.recommendation: Create the shared abstraction that is missing: a generated token file the extension owns but does not author. (a) Extend lib/config/brand.ts with a `light` half and a `metrics` block (radius 8px, radiusSm 6px, radiusPill 999px, the font and mono stacks) so it covers both themes, since it already calls itself the source of truth for out-of-app surfaces. (b) Add scripts/build-extension-tokens.mjs that reads brand.ts and writes extension/src/tokens.css containing exactly the four blocks popup.css:5-66 hand-writes today, with a `/* GENERATED - do not edit */` banner. (c) Wire it as a `pretest`/`prebuild` step in extension/package.json so a drifted checkout fails loudly, and add it to the repo's own build so the two cannot separate. (d) Replace popup.css:5-66 with `@import url("./tokens.css")`, and in reputation-card.ts delete the redeclaration at :458-464 and :496-500, inlining the generated values via a `TOKENS_CSS` string import instead (the content script is bundled IIFE by extension/scripts/build.mjs, so a string constant is fine where a CSS import is not). The card keeps its own elevation shadow, which is justified for a floating overlay, but nothing else.

findings.title: The extension renders severity as solid-fill marketing pills, the exact treatment the app's severity badge documents itself as avoiding, from a fourth and fifth hardcoded palette
findings.description: extension/src/popup.css:454-484 styles `.badge` as `border-radius: var(--vr-radius-pill)` with a fully saturated background and `color: #fff` per severity. components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx is the app's single source of truth and its own docblock (quoted in audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md D3) says the badge uses `rounded`, not `rounded-full`, "so it does not read as a marketing pill", and encodes severity as a tinted surface at /10-/15 with a matching text colour, a border at /30-/40, an h-1.5 dot, and a weight that varies with an `emphasis` field. The extension does the one thing that idiom exists to avoid. Separately the severity hexes are declared in four places inside the extension with no single source: extension/src/lib/types.ts:24-30 (SEVERITY_HEX, used for the finding row's left rail via format.ts:9), popup.css:464-484 (.badge.*), extension/src/content/reputation-card.ts:198-203 (SeverityChips), and extension/src/popup/popup.ts:313-322 (an inline score-colour ladder). Critical (#ef4444) and high (#f97316) match --severity-critical / --severity-high exactly; low is Tailwind blue-500 #3b82f6 against the token's 210 90% 56% = #2A8FF4, and info is Tailwind gray-500 #6b7280 against the dark token's 215 15% 55% = #7B899E. `.badge.medium` also hardcodes a text colour of `#1f1f1f`, which is not a token in either system.
findings.impact: A user who scans in the extension and then opens the same scan in the dashboard sees the same finding rated with a different visual grammar: a loud filled pill in one place, a quiet tinted chip in the other. Colour is also doing all the work in the extension, where the app deliberately encodes severity by weight as well as colour, so the extension's severity read is weaker for anyone with a colour vision deficiency. The four uncoordinated copies mean a severity retune has to be applied in four files by hand.
findings.recommendation: Collapse to one source and adopt the app's grammar. In extension/src/lib/types.ts extend SEVERITY_HEX into a `SEVERITY_TONE` record mirroring components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:37-78: `{ solid, text, surface, border, emphasis }`, with solid taken from the generated token file in dsnx-03 (so low becomes #2a8ff4 and info #7b899e). Restyle popup.css `.badge` as `border-radius: var(--vr-radius-sm); border: 1px solid <border>; background: <surface>; color: <text>; font-weight: 600; text-transform: uppercase; letter-spacing: 0.02em; font-size: 10px; font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums` with a 6px dot in `solid`, driven by inline custom properties set from SEVERITY_TONE rather than five CSS rules. Delete the inline colour objects at reputation-card.ts:198-203 and popup.ts:313-322 and read SEVERITY_TONE instead. Keep the finding row's 3px left rail (popup.ts:508) as is: it already matches store_1.png and reads well.

findings.title: Transactional emails carry no List-Unsubscribe header, and the in-body unsubscribe button reaches only three of the roughly fifty-five templates
findings.description: sendEmail (lib/email/email.ts:387-441) calls transporter.sendMail with from, to, subject, text, html and replyTo only. There is no `headers` option anywhere in the file and no occurrence of List-Unsubscribe. The unsubscribe affordance exists purely as an HTML button in layout() at :118-126, and it renders only when an `unsubscribeToken` is threaded through. Grepping every caller, exactly three pass one: lib/notifications/notifications.ts:105-112, app/api/v3/teams/members/route.ts:257-264 and app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:52-56. The file exports roughly 55 template functions. Every other email, including scanCompleteEmail (:1299), criticalFindingsEmail (:1396), scheduledScanCompleteEmail (:1458) and postureDigestEmail (:1562) when sent outside the notifications helper, renders a footer with no unsubscribe control at all. Compounding it, that footer's own copy at :167 reads "Choose what we send you in your account settings" and does not link to account settings; the only link in the sentence is the mailto for SUPPORT_EMAIL.
findings.impact: Gmail and Yahoo's bulk sender rules require a one-click List-Unsubscribe (RFC 8058) on mail of this shape, and mailbox providers use its absence as a spam signal. With roughly 50 registered users the volume is below the hard enforcement threshold today, so this is a deliverability risk that grows silently rather than a live outage. The user-facing half is worse and is live now: a recipient of a scan-complete or digest email is told to change a setting and given no way to get there, so the only remaining exit is the spam button, which is the single worst outcome for sender reputation. Self-hosters inherit the same footer for their own users.
findings.recommendation: In lib/email/email.ts:433 add `headers` to the sendMail call: when unsubscribeToken is present, `{ "List-Unsubscribe": `<${unsubscribeUrl}>, <mailto:${SUPPORT_EMAIL}?subject=unsubscribe>`, "List-Unsubscribe-Post": "List-Unsubscribe=One-Click" }`, and make /unsubscribe accept POST as well as GET so the one-click path works. Build unsubscribeUrl once in sendEmail and pass it into layout() rather than deriving it there. Then make the token the default rather than the exception: give sendEmail an optional `userId` and have it look up users.unsubscribe_token itself (the query already exists at lib/notifications/notifications.ts:97-100), so every non-security template gets the footer control without each call site remembering. Keep security notices (password changed, 2FA, new login) exempt by an explicit `transactional: true` flag rather than by accident. Finally, change the footer sentence at :167 to link the words "account settings" to `${APP_URL}/profile#notifications`.

findings.title: No email has preheader text, so every VulnRadar message previews in the inbox as the wordmark plus the first words of the heading
findings.description: layout() (lib/email/email.ts:107-180) opens the body with the logo lockup at :151-156 and drops straight into the card at :159. There is no hidden preview span: the file contains zero `display: none` declarations. Gmail, Apple Mail, Outlook and every mobile client render the subject followed by the first visible text of the body, so the preview line for every one of the roughly 55 templates begins with "VulnRadar" (the wordmark at :154, which is real text, not an image) followed by whatever emailHeading() emitted. For scanCompleteEmail that means the inbox line is "VulnRadar Scan complete" rather than the finding counts, which are the only thing the recipient wants from the preview. The severity chip row (severityChipRow, :315-332) that carries those counts is well below the fold of the preview.
findings.impact: Inbox open rate on the scan-complete, critical-findings and posture-digest emails is decided by a preview line that currently repeats the sender name and the subject. A recipient scanning an inbox cannot tell a clean scan from one with two criticals without opening the mail, which is the exact judgement the digest exists to let them make at a glance.
findings.recommendation:
Give layout() a second content parameter and render a preheader immediately after ``, before the logo row: `
${escapeHtml(preheader)}
` followed by a run of ` ﻿` repeated about 30 times so the client does not pull body copy in behind it. Thread a `preheader` field through SendEmailOptions alongside subject/text/html. Then set it per template with the fact the recipient needs: scanCompleteEmail -> "2 critical, 5 high on example.com. Scanned 3 seconds ago."; criticalFindingsEmail -> the top finding title; emailVerificationEmail -> "The link works for 24 hours."; email2FACodeEmail -> "Expires in 10 minutes" and never the code itself; postureDigestEmail -> the week-over-week delta. Default to the first sentence of the plain-text body when a template does not set one, which is a one-line fallback and better than nothing.

findings.title: One static OG image serves every page on the site, so a shared scan, a check page and the pricing page all unfurl identically
findings.description: app/layout.tsx:69-84 is the only `openGraph` block in the entire app/ tree (verified by grep across app/ for both .ts and .tsx), and it points every page at the single static `/og-image.png` built by scripts/build-og-image.mjs from public/og-image.svg. There are zero `opengraph-image.tsx` or `twitter-image.tsx` route files anywhere under app/. That means /shared/[token], /host/[hostname], /compare, /pricing, all 20 /docs sections and the roughly 750 /checks SEO pages every unfurl with the same card, whose baked copy reads "Scan any website for security issues in seconds. Just a URL." over a mock result for "your-domain.com" showing a risk score of 2 and five invented findings. The card itself is strong work (audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md names it one of the three best artifacts in the repo) and it is right for the site root, but it is the only card that exists.
findings.impact: Sharing a scan is a core flow, and the share link is the product's main organic distribution: a user pastes /shared/<token> into a Slack channel or a ticket, and everyone who sees it gets a generic marketing card for a fictional domain instead of the hostname and the finding counts they were being shown. The same applies to the roughly 750 /checks pages, which are the main organic SEO surface: every one of them competes for the same unfurl, so nothing in a search or social preview distinguishes "Missing HSTS" from "Exposed .git directory". This compounds AUDIT-012#fe-01, which already found only 5 of 311 routes prerendered.
findings.recommendation: Add three `opengraph-image.tsx` route files using next/og ImageResponse, all rendering one shared layout so they read as a family with the existing SVG (bg #0a0e18 to #0e1526, card #141d30, stroke #26344d, mono wordmark top-left, headline in #ffffff with the accent clause in #60a5fa, severity dots straight from the --severity-* scale exactly as og-image.svg:93-101 already does). (1) app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx: the scanned hostname as the headline, the risk score chip, and one severity distribution bar with the real counts, all read from the same share query the page uses. (2) app/checks/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx: the check title, its severity chip, and its category, from the checks registry. (3) app/host/[hostname]/opengraph-image.tsx: the hostname and its current reputation score. Set `export const size = { width: 1200, height: 630 }` and `alt` on each. Keep the static PNG as the root and docs fallback. Because ImageResponse only supports a subset of CSS, build it as flex boxes with explicit widths, and load no external font: the site already ships in system-ui (AUDIT-011#design-02), so next/og's default is consistent with the product rather than a deviation.

findings.title: app/global-error.tsx is a different design from the other two error pages: different palette, no wordmark, no status numeral, no digest, and no light mode
findings.description: app/error.tsx and app/not-found.tsx are the same composition: a mono wordmark lockup with ThemedLogo, a `border-y border-border/50 py-8` band holding a `font-mono text-6xl font-semibold tabular-nums` status numeral (500 / 404), a short honest sentence, a two-up button row, and a row of three or two `text-primary` footer links, all on tokens and all with `focus.ring` (error.tsx:33-127, not-found.tsx:15-89). app/global-error.tsx shares none of it: it opens with a 6rem circle holding a warning icon at :51-60 (an icon-in-a-rounded-shape, which CLAUDE.md and design-language E1 name as an anti-pattern), has no wordmark at all, no numeral, no error.digest block despite error.digest being available in its props, and it hardcodes `#09090b` / `#fafafa` / `#a1a1aa` / `#71717a` / `#52525b`, which is the Tailwind zinc ramp, not the app's #0C0E12 / #F0F2F5 navy. Its two links are coloured `BRAND_TEAL = "#0891b2"` (:10), a brand the product no longer has. It is also dark-only: a light-mode user hitting the global boundary drops into a black page. Inline styles there are correct and the file's own comment (:6-9) explains why, but the values are wrong, and nothing forces the two files to stay in sync. Separately, both error.tsx:103 and not-found.tsx:47 label the secondary route back as "Go to Dashboard", which is the product's internal noun for what an anonymous visitor arriving on a 404 from a search engine experiences as the scan page.
findings.impact: The global boundary is the page a user sees when the app has failed hardest, and it is the one that looks least like the product: teal links on zinc, no logo, no error id to quote to support. A user who does reach it cannot copy a digest, so a support conversation starts with "it broke" and no correlation id. The publicly reachable and indexable 404 sends an anonymous visitor to a button labelled with a word that only means something to an existing user.
findings.recommendation: Rebuild app/global-error.tsx as a literal-hex mirror of app/error.tsx rather than a separate design. Keep the inline-style constraint, but source the values from lib/config/brand.ts by transcribing them with a comment pointing back: background #0b0e14, card #12151c, border #252a34, text #f1f5f9, muted #9aa6b8, link #60a5fa (delete BRAND_TEAL). Add a `@media (prefers-color-scheme: light)` block via a small inline `<style>` element in the same file so the light palette (#dfe5ec / #eff2f5 / #14181f) is available without CSS variables. Replace the 6rem icon circle with the same structure error.tsx uses: an inline SVG VulnRadar mark plus the wordmark in `ui-monospace` at 20px/600, a 1px top and bottom rule at rgba(255,255,255,0.08), a monospace 60px "500", the heading "Something broke on our end", and the digest in a bordered mono block with a copy button (navigator.clipboard, guarded). Add a comment in both files naming the other as the sibling that must match. Separately, change the secondary CTA label in both error.tsx:105 and not-found.tsx:49 from "Go to Dashboard" to "Scan a URL", which is what the page actually does and matches the voice rule that copy names the mechanism.

findings.title: The PDF report draws its severity breakdown with ASCII hash characters even though the file has a rectangle primitive, and uses a sixth hand-rolled severity palette
findings.description: lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:269-279 renders the cover page's severity breakdown as five text rows of the form `CRITICAL     3 ###`, where the bar is `"#".repeat(Math.min(count, 30))` at :271 set in Helvetica. The file defines `addRect` at :124-134 and uses it exactly once, for the 8pt cover accent bar at :145, so the vector primitive needed to draw a real bar already exists and is not used. The app's canonical aggregate is SeverityDistribution (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), whose own docblock says it "reads as one bar rather than five cards, and the segment widths carry the information". The PDF instead produces five rows whose widths are capped at 30 and therefore stop carrying information above 30 findings. The colours come from SEVERITY_COLORS at :18-24, a sixth independent severity palette in normalized RGB triplets: critical [0.84,0.15,0.15] = #D62626 against the token #EF4444, high [0.95,0.4,0.1] = #F26619 against #F97316, medium [0.85,0.65,0.1] = #D9A61A against #E7B008, low [0.2,0.5,0.9] = #3380E6 against #2A8FF4, info [0.5,0.5,0.55] = #80808C against #7B899E. Every one of the five is wrong. This is the export-format half of AUDIT-013#dup-02, which found severity ordering redeclared across nine tables; cite that finding for the ordering, this one is about the colour values and the rendering. Checked and clean: the ordering here is correct (critical to info, from SEVERITY_LEVELS at :262-268), the findings arrive already severity-sorted from lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:711, and the "Informational" label that lib/seo/seo-ui.tsx:30 uses on /checks does not reach any export, since the PDF prints `sev.toUpperCase()` (:273) and Markdown uses "Info" (lib/reports/markdown-report.ts:36).
findings.impact: The severity summary is the first thing anyone opening the report looks at, and it is rendered as terminal art in a vector document. A target with 40 criticals and 3 lows shows a 30-hash bar next to a 3-hash bar, understating the ratio by more than 4x. The five wrong colours mean the reader cannot match a bar in the PDF to a chip in the app by eye.
findings.recommendation: Delete SEVERITY_COLORS at :18-24 and derive it from BRAND.severity in lib/config/brand.ts via the hex-to-rgb helper added in dsnx-02, so all six surfaces share one set of values. Replace the loop at :269-279 with a real bar: one `addRect(margin, y, contentWidth, 10, [0.90,0.90,0.92])` track, then a left-to-right run of `addRect` segments each `contentWidth * count / total` wide in that severity's colour, then a legend row below it built from addText plus a small `addRect(x, y, 6, 6, colour)` dot per present severity, showing `3 critical  ·  5 high` and skipping zero counts exactly as severityChipRow does in lib/email/email.ts:315-332. That is the same information architecture as SeverityDistribution and the same one already shipping in the emails, so the three agree.

findings.title: PDF text wrapping breaks only on spaces, so any URL, header value or token longer than the line budget runs off the right edge of the page
findings.description: wrapText (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:54-68) splits the input on " " and accumulates words until the running length would exceed maxChars. When a single word is itself longer than maxChars, the branch at :59-61 flushes the current line and assigns the oversized word to `current`; nothing ever splits it, so it is pushed whole at :66 and drawn as one line by addText at :86 starting at x = margin with no clipping and no right bound. The line budget is `Math.floor(contentWidth / (size * 0.5))` (:77), which at size 8 (the size used for Evidence at :355, Risk at :359 and fixSteps at :372) is 123 characters. Findings routinely carry longer unbroken strings in exactly those fields: a full Content-Security-Policy directive list, a redirect chain URL, a query string, a base64 script hash, or a JWT-shaped token in a secrets finding's evidence. Anything past roughly 123 characters is drawn past pageWidth - margin and is lost at the page boundary.
findings.impact: The evidence string is the product's stated differentiator ("every finding carries the raw evidence it was derived from, so you can check our work rather than take it on faith"), and in the PDF the longest and most specific evidence is the evidence that silently gets truncated at the paper edge with no ellipsis and no indication anything is missing. A reader checking the work on a forwarded report sees a sentence that stops mid-token.
findings.recommendation: In wrapText, after the flush at :60, add a hard-break loop for the oversized word: while `word.length > maxChars`, push `word.slice(0, maxChars)` and continue with the remainder, preferring a break after any of `/ ? & = ; , .` within the last 12 characters of the slice so URLs and CSP directives break at a readable point. Separately, render code and evidence in a monospace font rather than Helvetica: add a third font object `<< /Type /Font /Subtype /Type1 /BaseFont /Courier >>` next to :449, expose it as /F3, and use it for the Evidence line (:355) and the codeExamples block (:384-387), with maxCharsPerLine computed as `contentWidth / (size * 0.6)` for that font since Courier is fixed-width. That also preserves the indentation the current word-wrap destroys in code samples. While in the file, move the `addPageHeader()` call so it fires on any page break, not only between findings: the guard at :328 only runs before each finding, so a finding that spans a page leaves the continuation page with no header rule.

findings.title: Nothing replaces the removed timer: the status endpoint returns progress but no findings, so the wait has no payoff until it ends
findings.category: scanning page: replacement for the timer
findings.description:
This is the replacement proposal AUDIT-011#scan-05 asked for and did not specify. It is scoped strictly to what the API produces today, verified by reading the endpoint and the producer.

WHAT EXISTS NOW. GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id] builds `responseBody` at app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts:162-168 with exactly five keys while a scan is live: `status`, `currentCategory`, `categoriesCompleted`, `categoriesTotal`, `elapsedMs`. On `completed` it adds the whole `result`; on `failed` it adds `error`. The client reads three of them (app/dashboard/page.tsx:146-150) and drops `elapsedMs` on the floor. The producer is `createProgressTracker` in lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139, whose hook fires once per CATEGORY as `start` and once as `done`, writing `current_category` / `categories_completed` / `categories_total` to scan_history. The hook's type is `(category: string, phase) => void` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355): it carries no check count and no findings.

So of the three things the brief asked for, the API supports exactly one and a half today:
1. "Which check category is running" -- SUPPORTED. `currentCategory` is a real Category id, and lib/scanner/category-meta.ts already holds a client-safe label and one-line blurb for all 18, importing only a type.
2. "How many of the ~797 checks are done" -- NOT SUPPORTED as checks; supported as families. `categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal` is real and exact (route.ts:332-339 derives the denominator from `getPlannedSyncCategories` plus `getPlannedAsyncBranches`, never estimated). Per-check counts are computed but only at the end: lib/scanner/engine.ts:206-211 returns `checksRun` and `checksSkipped` after the whole loop, and they reach the user only as the "Checks run" stat on the finished view (components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx:295-302).
3. "Findings streaming in as discovered" -- NOT SUPPORTED AT ALL. `runSyncChecks` accumulates into a local `findings` array (engine.ts:156) and nothing reads it until `dedupeFindings` at :205. scan_history.findings is written once, by `finalizeScanSuccess` (scan-jobs.ts:240-245), in the same UPDATE that flips status to `completed`. There is no partial-findings column and no partial-findings field on the poll response.
findings.impact: After scanui-01 the card would show a family name, a bar, and nothing else, which is less information than the clock it replaced. The scan is the product's whole value proposition and for its entire duration the user is shown zero of its output, then all of it at once, then (until AUDIT-011#scan-08 is fixed) a blur over the top of it. The visible work is a large part of a scanner's perceived worth and this page currently spends the wait proving nothing.
findings.recommendation:
Build it in three tiers, each independently shippable.

TIER 1, zero backend change, ship with scanui-01. Three real numbers in a mono definition list, all already on the wire:
  FAMILIES  12 / 18      (categoriesCompleted / categoriesTotal)
  RUNNING   DNS          (CATEGORY_META[currentCategory].label)
  NEXT      Email        (the next entry in the client's own planned family list)
plus the one-line `FAMILY_STEP` sentence for the running family, which is already written and is good copy ("Grepping responses for keys and tokens"). Keep those strings; they are the best thing in the current component.

TIER 2, one generated file, still no server change, gives a real check count. scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs already iterates lib/scanner/checks-data/<category>.json per category (see its loop and the write at :283-286) and emits lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts, which is client-safe (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT = 797`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT = 18`, no runtime imports). Add one export: `export const EXACT_CHECKS_BY_CATEGORY: Record<string, number> = {...}`. The client then sums the counts of the families already marked done and renders `CHECKS 531 / 797` in `font-mono tabular-nums`, rising in real steps. Label it honestly: this counts the checks in the families that have reported, so it will slightly overstate against the final `checksRun` (page checks whose `requirementsMet` gate fails are counted as skipped at engine.ts:186-188). Either accept a final reconciliation to the real `checksRun`, or emit legacy-only counts and label the row `RULES`.

TIER 3, the real prize, and it needs a backend change. Stream findings as they are discovered:
  a) Widen `ScanProgressHook` (lib/scanner/types.ts:352-355) to `(category, phase, snapshot?: { found: number; newFindings: { severity: Severity; title: string }[] })`.
  b) In lib/scanner/engine.ts, at the `onProgress?.(category, "done")` call at :203, pass the findings pushed during that category's iteration (the loop already has them; slice `findings` from the index recorded before `onProgress?.(category, "start")` at :166).
  c) In `createProgressTracker` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:117-139) append those into a new `scan_history.partial_findings JSONB NOT NULL DEFAULT '[]'` column in the same fire-and-forget UPDATE that already runs there, keeping the existing `WHERE status IN ('pending','running')` guard so a late write after completion is a no-op. Add the column in instrumentation.ts beside the other scan_history additions, and to scripts/migrate (see AUDIT-013#migrate-01: this is exactly the kind of column that gets missed).
  d) In app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts add `responseBody.partialFindings = row.partial_findings` in the live branch only (never in the `completed` branch, where `result.findings` is authoritative). Cap it server-side at ~40 entries and store only `{severity, title}`, never evidence or remediation, so a 2-second poll stays small.
  e) On completion, clear `partial_findings` in `finalizeScanSuccess`'s UPDATE so a re-poll of a finished scan does not carry two lists.
The one honesty trap: `dedupeFindings` (engine.ts:205) runs after the last category, so a streamed count can go DOWN at the end. Present the live list under the label "Found so far" and let the completed view's real summary replace it wholesale, rather than animating a number downward.

What NOT to do: do not synthesise a percentage from `elapsedMs`, and do not use `elapsedMs` at all on this screen. It is the same number scanui-01 removes, just served from the server.

findings.title: The scanning card is a boxed progress bar over a two-column grid of 20 identical status rows, which is the templated pattern the design language names, and its labels clip on a phone
findings.description:
Measured against audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md and its 14-point checklist. The scanning state is app/dashboard/page.tsx:910-922, a single centred `<div className="flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16">` wrapping components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx.

DEVIATIONS, each verified at a line:

1. Tell-tale 5 and E1. scanning-indicator.tsx:307-344 is a `grid grid-cols-1 ... sm:grid-cols-2` of up to 20 rows, every row structurally identical: a 14px `rounded-full` glyph followed by a truncated label. That is the named anti-pattern in list form. The design language's alternatives for exactly this job are the divided list (`divide-y divide-border/50`), the mono-term `<dl>`, and the real table (D4). Four of the nine landing sections use no card grid at all.

2. Tell-tale 4, accent restraint. The doctrine is at most two accented elements per section, documented twice in code comments (landing-categories.tsx:6-11, landing-open-source.tsx:18-19). This card has: the mode pill (:262, `border-primary/20 bg-primary/10 text-primary`), the bar fill (:300, `bg-primary`), and one primary-tinted circle per completed row (:321, `border-primary/40 bg-primary/15 text-primary`) plus the running one (:322, `border-primary bg-primary`). By the last second of a full scan that is roughly 22 primary-tinted elements in one card.

3. Tell-tale 1 and C1. Section rhythm is `py-16 sm:py-20`. The scanning state uses `pt-10 sm:pt-16` with no bottom padding of its own (app/dashboard/page.tsx:911), a third value.

4. C5 radius ladder. `:259` is `rounded-md`, which resolves to `calc(var(--radius) - 2px)` via tailwind.config.mjs:75-79 and is the BUTTON radius. The spec's content card is `rounded-xl`. components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:562 and components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:182 make the same choice, so all three surfaces of this page are consistent with each other and none matches the spec.

5. C1 divider opacity. "`border-border/50` is the divider, not `border-border`. Full opacity is reserved for the footer's outer edge and card outlines." The internal dividers here are `border-b border-border` (:261) and `border-t border-border` (:307), both full opacity. The house content card (D1) uses `border-b border-border/60` internally.

6. D3 pill idiom. `:262` is `rounded border ... px-2 py-0.5 text-xs font-medium`. The house pill is `rounded-full`, `text-[10px]`, mono or `uppercase tracking-wider`, border at /25 to /30. The severity badge is the one deliberate `rounded` exception and this is not it, so it is a third pill grammar.

7. B2 type scale, and it is also an a11y defect (filed separately as scanui-08): the card has no heading of any kind. `ScanHero` (the page's only `<h1>`) lives inside the `status === "idle"` branch at app/dashboard/page.tsx:887 and is unmounted the instant scanning starts.

8. MOBILE, the one measurable usability defect here. The row label at :331-338 is `min-w-0 truncate` inside a `grid-cols-1` column below the `sm` breakpoint, so it clips on one line with no wrap, no `title` attribute and no tooltip. The strings it clips are the longest ones in FAMILY_STEP: "Parsing page content for mixed content and inline script" (55 chars), "Probing forms & endpoints for XSS, SQLi, SSTI & more" (51), "Looking for leaked paths, versions and stack traces" (50). Derived from the class list rather than measured in a browser: at a 375px viewport the available text width is roughly 375 minus 32 (main `px-4`) minus 32 (card `px-4`) minus about 22 (glyph plus `gap-2`), so about 289px, against roughly 300 to 310px needed for 55 characters at `text-xs`. At 640px and up the same strings sit in a half-width column and clip harder. Also, at one column the list is 20 rows tall, so on a 667px phone the card runs past the fold for a state that lasts a few seconds.

9. Tell-tale 14, motion. globals.css:141-151 collapses CSS `animation-duration` and `transition-duration` under `prefers-reduced-motion`, so the bar's `transition-[width] duration-500` (:300) is covered. The `requestAnimationFrame` settle ramp at :227-248 is not: it writes `style={{ width }}` from JS over SETTLE_ANIMATION_MS and ignores the media query entirely.

10. Structural. The three states are three mutually exclusive full-page branches (app/dashboard/page.tsx:885-958). Submitting the form unmounts ScanHero, ScanForm and the whole Dashboard widget block and replaces them with one small centred card; completion unmounts that card and mounts DashboardResults. Nothing is shared between them, so the page's contents are wholly swapped twice per scan.
findings.impact: This is the highest-traffic transient surface in the product: every scan passes through it, and it is the surface the section brief singles out as reading AI-generated. The mobile clipping is a real loss of information, not a matter of taste: on a phone the user cannot read what is currently running. The three-way content swap means the page never feels like one thing filling in, which is what a scanner should feel like.
findings.recommendation:
Rebuild as one surface that transforms in place. Concretely, so a developer can build it without re-deciding anything. STRUCTURE. Keep the page container `w-full max-w-6xl mx-auto px-4 sm:px-6` (already `CONTAINER` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:61). Replace the `flex justify-center pt-10 sm:pt-16` wrapper with `py-16 sm:py-20` (C1 standard rhythm) and do not centre: left-align, like every other app surface. HEADING BLOCK, mirroring ScanHero's geometry so the swap from idle is a text change, not a layout change:

Scanning {hostname}

797 checks across 18 families. Findings appear here as each family reports, before the run finishes.

Pull 797 and 18 from lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts (`EXACT_CHECK_COUNT`, `EXACT_CHECK_CATEGORY_COUNT`), never hardcoded (tell-tale 8). BODY, 2-column asymmetric split (E2 idiom, mirrors the hero): `grid gap-8 lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_minmax(0,1.15fr)] lg:gap-12`. LEFT: the run readout, in the ResponseReadout grammar (components/shared/response-readout.tsx:161-216), which is the house signature and already renders "the literal shape of scanning". `overflow-hidden rounded-xl border border-border bg-card font-mono`. - Header, `flex items-baseline gap-2 border-b border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-3`: `GET` in `shrink-0 font-semibold text-primary`, then `min-w-0 flex-1 truncate text-foreground` hostname, then the mode label as plain `text-xs text-muted-foreground` (drop the pill entirely; it is the least important thing on screen and it is costing an accent). - Body, `px-5 py-4`: one line of `text-sm text-foreground` carrying the current family's FAMILY_STEP sentence (keep those strings verbatim, they are the best copy in the file), then the bar, then a mono-term `
` (D4 pattern 2): `
` with rows FAMILIES `12 / 18`, CHECKS `531 / 797`, FOUND `7`, values in `font-mono tabular-nums text-foreground`. - Bar: `h-1.5 w-full overflow-hidden rounded-full bg-muted` with a `bg-primary transition-[width] duration-300 ease-out` fill. Reuse the geometry of `SeverityDistribution` (components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190), which is already the canonical "one bar, not five cards" aggregate. - Family list, replacing the 20-cell grid: a `divide-y divide-border/50` list, each row `flex items-baseline justify-between gap-3 py-2`. Left is `CATEGORY_META[c].label` (lib/scanner/category-meta.ts, client-safe, 14 chars at most: "Info disclosure"), right is `font-mono text-xs tabular-nums` check count for that family. State encoded by weight, not by 20 tinted circles: pending `text-muted-foreground/50`, done `text-muted-foreground` with the count in `text-foreground`, running `text-foreground font-medium` on a row carrying `border-l-2 border-primary pl-3`. That single rail is the only accent in the list, which brings the card to three accented elements total (the `GET` word, the bar fill, the one rail). - Footer, `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 border-t border-border/60 bg-muted/20 px-5 py-2.5 text-xs`: cancel on the left as `

findings.title: The scan-failed card's primary button is labelled "Try again" but only returns to an emptied form, cancel silently drops you to idle after burning a daily scan, and authenticated scans cannot be cancelled at all
findings.category: scanning page: failure and cancel paths
findings.description:
Three separate defects on the same page's exit paths.

(a) "Try again" does not try again. app/dashboard/page.tsx:932 passes `onRetry={handleReset}` to DashboardErrorState. dashboard-error-state.tsx:279 wires the primary button to `onRetry`, and :283 wires the secondary "Back to scanner" button to the same `onRetry`. Both call `handleReset()` (page.tsx:851-872), which only resets state and clears `?scan=`. Neither re-runs anything. Worse, the form is unmounted while `status === "failed"` (it is inside the `status === "idle"` branch at page.tsx:885-907), and components/scanner/scan-form.tsx:315 initialises `const [url, setUrl] = useState("")` with no query-param seed, so remounting hands back an empty input. The error card literally displays the failed URL two elements above (dashboard-error-state.tsx:206) and the button underneath throws it away. The scanner selection survives, because `mode`, `screenshot`, `port_scan` and `active_probes` are seeded from the query string at scan-form.tsx:320-371 and are only cleared on the SUCCESS path (page.tsx:290-296).

(b) Cancel has no confirmation and no distinct state. `handleCancelScan` (page.tsx:802-808) fires the DELETE, sets `runningScanId` null and `setStatus("idle")`. The whole page snaps back to the scan form with nothing on screen saying the scan was cancelled. Meanwhile the server side is not a no-op: the DELETE handler (app/api/v3/scan/status/[id]/route.ts) calls `finalizeScanFailure(row.id, "Cancelled")`, which writes `status = 'failed'`, `error_message = 'Cancelled'` and a real `duration`, leaving the row permanently in scan_history with `findings_count = 0` and `summary = '{}'`. The daily quota was already charged at app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:394 (`incrementDailyCountCapped`) and there is no decrement anywhere in lib/rate-limiting/daily-limits.ts or the scan routes. So cancelling costs one of the day's scans (25 on free) and leaves a phantom zero-finding row, and the UI tells the user neither fact.

(c) Cancel is unavailable exactly when it is most wanted. page.tsx:919 renders `onCancel={runningScanId ? handleCancelScan : undefined}`, and `setRunningScanId(scanId)` only happens at :594, after the POST round trip resolves. So for the first several hundred milliseconds of every scan there is no cancel control, and it then pops into existence, shifting the card's height by the `mt-3` plus button row at scanning-indicator.tsx:347-358. For the authenticated path the `if (!auth)` gate at :585 means `setRunningScanId` is never reached at all, so an authenticated scan, which is the slowest kind because it drives a real login first, has no cancel control for its entire run.
findings.impact: A failed scan makes the user retype the URL that is printed on screen in front of them, behind a button that promises otherwise. A cancelled scan gives no acknowledgement, silently spends one of a free account's 25 daily scans, and leaves a zero-finding row that is indistinguishable from a clean result in History (see scanui-06). An authenticated scan cannot be stopped once started.
findings.recommendation:
(a) Give DashboardErrorState a real retry. Add an `onRetry` that re-invokes `runScan` with the same `url`, `mode`, `categoryFilter`, `captureScreenshot` and `portScan` (all still held in `scanningUrl`, `scanningMode`, `scanningCategories`, `pendingScreenshot`, `pendingPortScan` at page.tsx:229-253) and keep `handleReset` on a separate `onBack` prop for the secondary button. Two buttons that call the same handler with different labels is the actual bug; one of them has to change. Do not offer retry for `kind === "rate_limit"` or `kind === "validation"`, where retrying identically cannot help; show "Back to scanner" alone there.

(b) Add a `cancelled` value to `ScanStatus` and have `handleCancelScan` set it instead of `"idle"`. Render the cancelled state per scanui-03: the readout stays, the body line becomes "Cancelled after 6 of 18 families. The partial run is in your history.", and the footer action is "Run it again". If the product intends cancelling not to cost quota, that is a separate change in `finalizeScanFailure`'s caller, but the copy must match whichever is true: if it does cost, say "This still counted against today's scans."

(c) Render the cancel control from the moment `status === "scanning"`, `disabled` with `aria-disabled="true"` until `runningScanId` is set, so its box never appears or disappears. Set `runningScanId` for the authenticated path too, or, if that endpoint genuinely cannot be cancelled, render the control with a tooltip saying so rather than omitting it.

findings.title: The status poll's fetch has no timeout or abort signal, so one stalled request leaves the scanning page frozen past its own six-minute ceiling with a bar that never moves
findings.description:
`pollScanStatus` (app/dashboard/page.tsx:128-165) loops `while (Date.now() - startedAt < maxWaitMs)` and calls `const res = await fetch(API.SCAN_STATUS(scanId));` at :142 with no second argument: no `AbortSignal`, no `AbortSignal.timeout`, no racing timer. The give-up ceiling (`SCAN_MAX_WAIT_MS = 6 * 60 * 1000` at :87, `CRAWL_MAX_WAIT_MS = 16 minutes` at :88) is only evaluated between iterations, so a single request that stalls without erroring never reaches it. The retry budget does not help either: `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES = 3` at :126 counts thrown requests, and a hanging request never throws.

What the user sees while that happens is the worst pairing of the two signals on the card. `hasRealProgress` is already true from the last successful poll, so components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:170-188 pins `targetStep` at the last reported family and the bar stops moving, while the independent 500ms interval at :148-151 keeps the elapsed clock climbing. A frozen bar next to a rising clock.

The inverse case is also mis-tuned. With `CONFIG_SCAN_STATUS_POLL_INTERVAL_MS = 2000` (lib/config/config-values.ts:555) and a three-strike budget, roughly six seconds of flaky connectivity is enough to abandon a scan that is still running perfectly well server-side, and the message it throws at :157 ("Lost track of the scan while it was running.") does not mention that the scan continues and its result will appear in History. The sibling timeout message at :162-164 does say exactly that, so the good wording already exists in the same function.
findings.impact: On a train, a hotel wifi, or a phone handing off between cells, the scanning page either hangs indefinitely on a spinner-equivalent, or gives up after about six seconds and tells the user the scan was lost when it was not. Both outcomes strand a scan that the user has already been charged a daily quota unit for.
findings.recommendation: In `pollScanStatus`, pass a per-request deadline: `fetch(API.SCAN_STATUS(scanId), { signal: AbortSignal.timeout(pollIntervalMs * 4) })`. An aborted fetch throws, so it feeds the existing `consecutiveFailures` path with no other change. Raise `MAX_CONSECUTIVE_POLL_FAILURES` from 3 to about 6 (roughly 12 to 20 seconds of tolerance) and reuse the timeout branch's wording for the give-up message: "Lost the connection to this scan. It is still running, and the result will be in your history in a few minutes." Also thread an `AbortController` from the caller and abort it on unmount, which is the fix AUDIT-012#fe-09 already asked for (polling continues for up to 16 minutes after the user navigates away); one controller solves both.

findings.title: Leaving the scanning page abandons the scan with no way back, and the in-flight row then renders in Recent scans and History as a finished scan with 0 findings in 0ms
findings.category: scanning page: navigate away and back
findings.description:
The scan's entire progress state lives in the DashboardContent component: `status`, `runningScanId` and `scanProgress` are all `useState` (app/dashboard/page.tsx:204, 219, 234) and the poll loop is a local `async` function. There is no persistence, no `sessionStorage`, and nothing that queries for the user's own in-flight scans. So a soft navigation, a refresh, or a phone backgrounding the tab long enough to be evicted drops the whole thing: coming back to /dashboard shows `status === "idle"`, the empty scan form, and no indication that a scan of theirs is still running server-side. It does keep running (that is the point of the background-job design, see app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:405-419) and it does eventually complete, so the user has no way to watch it and no signal that watching would even be possible.

What they see instead is worse than nothing. The row is INSERTed as `pending` before any work starts (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:365-379) and `scan_history.scanned_at` defaults to `NOW()` (instrumentation.ts:428), so it exists immediately and sorts to the top of every list ordered by `scanned_at DESC`. Neither list filters on status:
  - app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41-44 selects `public_id AS id, url, summary, findings_count, duration, scanned_at, source FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY scanned_at DESC LIMIT $2`, with no `status` predicate. This feeds the "Recent scans" widget on the very page the user just came back to (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx).
  - app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120-139 has the same shape and the same omission (`WHERE sh.user_id = $1 AND (sh.scan_type IS NULL OR sh.scan_type != 'github')`).
The column defaults at instrumentation.ts:420-423 are `summary '{}'`, `findings_count 0`, `duration 0`, and `finalizeScanSuccess` (lib/scanner/scan-jobs.ts:244-248) is the only thing that fills them. So a running scan, a cancelled scan (`finalizeScanFailure` at :363-381 sets `status='failed'` but never touches `summary` or `findings_count`) and a watchdog-killed scan all render identically to a genuinely clean result: the site's name, "0 findings", "0.0s".
findings.impact: The most natural recovery action, going back to the scanner, is punished twice: the user loses the scan they were watching, and the page they land on tells them that scan found nothing. On a phone, where the browser evicting a background tab is routine, this is the normal path rather than the edge case. A cancelled scan leaves the same false clean-bill-of-health row permanently.
findings.recommendation:
Two changes, independently useful.

1. Make the lists honest. Add `status` to both SELECTs (app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:41 and app/api/v3/history/route.ts:120 and :129) and render non-completed rows distinctly rather than as zero-finding results: `running` and `pending` get a muted "Running" chip in place of the findings summary, `failed` gets a `text-[hsl(var(--severity-medium))]` "Did not finish" chip. Do not filter them out, because a user needs to see that a scan happened; just stop them wearing a clean result's clothes. Check whether the aggregate queries in the same file (the severity roll-up at :46-54 and the top-findings query at :55-63) should also exclude non-completed rows; they sum over `summary` and `findings`, which are `'{}'`/`'[]'` for those rows, so they are currently harmless but will silently break if partial findings are ever stored (see scanui-02 tier 3).

2. Let the user rejoin a running scan. `GET /api/v3/scan/status/[id]` already returns everything needed and is already owner-scoped (`getOwnedScan`). Either (a) write the in-flight `scanId` to `sessionStorage` in `runScan` right after `setRunningScanId(scanId)` (page.tsx:594), clear it in the `finally` at :620-622, and on mount resume `pollScanStatus` against it if the row is still `pending`/`running`, or (b) add a `?scan_job=<publicId>` param that the existing `syncFromUrl` effect (page.tsx:302-342) recognises as a third meaning alongside target and history-id. Option (a) is smaller and survives a plain refresh; option (b) additionally makes the running scan linkable. Either way the recovered state should render the same readout scanui-03 specifies, so nothing new has to be designed for it.

findings.title: The scanning state has no heading anywhere in the document, no aria-busy, and announces up to twenty polite live-region updates in two seconds while never announcing that the scan finished
findings.category: scanning page: accessibility of the transient states
findings.description:
Verified structurally by reading every component mounted during `status === "scanning"`.

1. NO HEADING. The page's only `<h1>` is in ScanHero (components/scanner/scan-hero.tsx:7), which is inside the `status === "idle"` branch (app/dashboard/page.tsx:887) and is unmounted the moment scanning begins. ScanningIndicator contains no heading element. Header (components/scanner/header.tsx) contains none. app/dashboard/layout.tsx is a passthrough. The only headings left in the document are three `<h3>` in the footer (components/scanner/footer.tsx:63, 114, 163). So while a scan runs, `<main id="main-content" tabIndex={-1}>` (page.tsx:879-883), which is the skip-link's own target, contains zero headings, and the document outline starts at h3 in the footer. The `failed` state is the same: DashboardErrorState's title is an `<h2>` (dashboard-error-state.tsx:194) with no h1 above it.

2. LIVE-REGION SPAM. scanning-indicator.tsx:279-286 puts `aria-live="polite"` on the current-step paragraph, whose text changes every time `displayStep` advances. `displayStep` is ratcheted by a `setInterval` at `MIN_STEP_DISPLAY_MS = 120` (:58, :205-212). For a scan that completes between two polls, which the component's own comment at :46-57 says is the common case, `targetStep` jumps to the end and the ratchet then fires up to 20 announcements in about 2.4 seconds. Polite announcements queue rather than interrupt, so a screen reader user hears family names still being read out after the results have already rendered.

3. NO COMPLETION ANNOUNCEMENT. Grepping components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx and components/scanner/scan-summary.tsx finds no `aria-live`, no `role="status"` and no `sr-only` announcement. The indicator unmounts, DashboardResults mounts, and nothing tells a non-sighted user the scan is over or what it found. Focus is not moved either, so the keyboard user's focus is wherever it was, on a control that no longer exists.

4. `role="progressbar"` (:291-298) declares `aria-valuemax={steps.length}` and `aria-valuenow={displayStep + 1}`, but the visible fill is `displayPercent`, which is `(displayStep + 1) / steps.length * 92` (:219-222). At step 10 of 20 the announced value is 50 percent and the rendered bar is 46 percent. There is no `aria-busy` on the container and no `aria-valuetext` giving the family name.
findings.impact: The core flow of the product is announced as an unstructured page with no headings, then narrated as a burst of twenty queued strings, then goes silent at exactly the moment there is something to say. A screen reader user gets the least useful part of the experience loudly and the most useful part not at all. The published accessibility statement is already contradicted elsewhere (AUDIT-011#docs-07); this is the same claim failing on the highest-traffic surface.
findings.recommendation:
1. Give every state a heading, per scanui-03's heading block: `

Scanning {hostname}

` for scanning, "Scan of {hostname}" for the result, "{hostname} did not finish" for the failure, with DashboardErrorState's current `

` kept as the sub-heading beneath it. 2. Move `aria-live` off the per-step paragraph. Mark the step text `aria-hidden` and add one `

` that is throttled to the FAMILY level, not the ratchet, and reads "12 of 18 families done. Running DNS." Update it only when `categoriesCompleted` actually changes, so a fast scan produces two or three announcements instead of twenty. Put `aria-busy="true"` on the readout container while scanning. 3. Announce completion. On the `status` transition to `done`, render a `role="status"` `sr-only` region with "Scan complete. 7 findings: 1 high, 4 medium, 2 low." built from `result.summary`, and move focus to the results heading with a `ref` plus `focus()`. Do the same for `failed` with `role="alert"`. 4. Either drop `role="progressbar"` in favour of the `role="status"` text (the numbers are already on screen in a `

` after the rebuild), or make the two agree: keep `aria-valuemin=0 aria-valuemax=100`, set `aria-valuenow` to the same rounded percent the fill uses, and add `aria-valuetext={"12 of 18 families"}`.

findings.title: The scanning page, its progress component and its poll loop have no tests at all: tests/components/scanner contains exactly one file, for an unrelated helper
findings.description:
Grepping the whole tests/ tree for `ScanningIndicator`, `scanning-indicator`, `pollScanStatus` and `dashboard/page` returns nothing. `tests/components/scanner/` contains a single file, `ai-review-gate.test.ts`, which covers lib/scanner/ai-review-gate.ts and nothing on this page. So none of the following is covered anywhere: the real-progress branch versus the simulated-progress branch at scanning-indicator.tsx:170-193, the `displayStep` ratchet at :205-212, the settle ramp at :227-248, `pollScanStatus`'s consecutive-failure budget at app/dashboard/page.tsx:154-159, its max-wait ceiling at :140, the `cancelledRef` race handling at :603-629, or any of the four status branches at :885-958.

This matters specifically because scanui-01, scanui-02 and scanui-03 propose rewriting all of it. The repo has 362 test files and 89,192 test lines, so the tooling and the habit exist; this surface is simply a hole in it.
findings.impact: The highest-traffic transient surface in the product can be rewritten with no regression signal. The subtle parts, the ratchet and the two progress branches, are exactly the kind of logic that looks right and behaves wrong, and their existing behaviour is only documented in code comments.
findings.recommendation:
Write the tests before the rebuild, so they pin the behaviour worth keeping. Minimum set, all pure and fast:
  - `pollScanStatus`: returns on `completed`; returns on `failed`; throws the correct message after N consecutive rejections; throws the max-wait message when the clock passes `maxWaitMs`; calls `onProgress` with the exact fields for every successful poll. Use a fake timer plus a stubbed `fetch`; no database, per the project rule.
  - Add a case for the scanui-05 fix: a fetch that never settles must abort and count as a failure rather than hanging the loop.
  - `ScanningIndicator` render tests with `@testing-library/react`: with `categoriesTotal > 0` the family count matches the props exactly; with `categoriesTotal === 0` the indeterminate state renders (after scanui-01, no simulated step counter); the cancel control is present and disabled before `onCancel` is supplied; the live region announces once per family change and not once per ratchet tick.
  - One test asserting a heading exists in every state, which is the scanui-08 regression guard.

findings.title: The product ships a mounted toast system with exactly one consumer, and four unrelated feedback mechanisms compete for the rest
findings.description: components/ui/toast.tsx, components/ui/toaster.tsx and components/ui/use-toast.ts are 360 lines of working toast infrastructure, and <Toaster /> is mounted app-wide at app/layout.tsx:195. Grepping useToast across app/ and components/ returns exactly one consumer: components/profile/modals/billing-verification-modal.tsx:138. Everything else uses one of four other idioms: a setError/setSuccess string pair lifted to the page and rendered as a static banner (app/profile/page.tsx:124-125 rendered :688-716, app/teams/page.tsx:78 rendered :515-532, app/repos/page.tsx:113-114 rendered :328-338, app/attack-surface/page.tsx:18-19 rendered :44-53); a separate admin-only toast (components/admin/shared/toast.tsx) used by seven admin managers; per-component local error booleans (components/scanner/results-list.tsx:139); and console.error or nothing at all. Only app/repos/page.tsx:144 auto-dismisses. Only two files use the typed helper in lib/api/client.ts.
findings.impact: There is no single answer to "what happens when this fails", which is why so many mutations end up with none at all (qolf-04, qolf-05). It also costs an engineer: adding feedback to a new mutation means picking one of five conventions and threading setError props down the component tree, which is exactly the friction that produces the next silent catch.
findings.recommendation: Standardise on the toast that is already mounted. Add lib/ui/notify.ts exporting notifySuccess(title) and notifyError(title, description) over toast() from components/ui/use-toast.ts, and adopt it in the ten worst offenders named in qolf-04, qolf-05 and qolf-30 first. Keep the profile page's inline banner only for persistent states (verification required, plan gate), not transient results. Retire components/admin/shared/toast.tsx in favour of the same wrapper. Note components/ui/toast.tsx:19 positions toasts `fixed top-0 w-full` on mobile, which covers the fixed header from components/scanner/header.tsx:119, so move the mobile position to bottom before rolling this out.

findings.title: There is no command palette and no keyboard shortcut layer anywhere in a developer tool with eight top-level sections
findings.description: A repo-wide grep for cmdk, CommandDialog, useHotkeys and global keydown handlers finds no command palette and no application-level shortcut registration. The only document-level keydown listeners in app/ and components/ are modal Escape and focus trapping (lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts:54 and :91), the AI chat widget's own textarea handling (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:833 and :1070), and two mobile nav overlays (components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:58, components/admin/shared/admin-mobile-toc.tsx:140). There is no global search either: components/scanner/header.tsx renders logo, eight nav links (:25-34), a notification bell, a theme toggle and log out, with no search input at any breakpoint. app/docs has no search of any kind: components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx and docs-shell.tsx contain no input element.
findings.impact: Reaching a past scan means navigating to History and typing into a filter that only covers the newest 100 rows. Reaching scheduled scans means Profile, then the Developer tab, then the Schedules sub-tab. Reaching one check's documentation means /checks, expanding one of eighteen accordions, then browser find. Each of these is a single fuzzy-search entry for the audience this product targets, and its absence is the most visible way the app reads as less finished than the landing page that sells it.
findings.recommendation: Add a Cmd/Ctrl-K palette mounted next to <Toaster /> in app/layout.tsx. cmdk is the conventional choice and the repo already uses Radix throughout, so components/ui/dialog.tsx supplies the shell.
