Seed it with five groups: Navigate, from the NAV_LINKS array at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34 plus the profile tab list at app/profile/page.tsx:625-665; Actions (New scan, Compare scans, New API key, New schedule); Scans, hitting the server-side history search from qolf-01, matched on URL and tag; Checks, over the static registry that already backs app/checks/page.tsx, jumping to /checks/{id}; and Docs, over the tree in components/docs/docs-nav.ts. Then add a shortcut sheet on `?` and the three shortcuts that matter on a results page: `/` to focus the findings search (components/scanner/results-list.tsx:372), j and k to move between findings, Escape to return to the list.

findings.title: There is no undo anywhere in the product, and clearing all history is a single icon button beside the search box
findings.description: A repo-wide grep for undo across app/, components/ and lib/ returns five hits and none is an undo affordance: three are code comments, one is a docs sentence stating there is no undo (app/docs/account-security/page.tsx:503), and one is an unsaved-state toggle label in the admin badge editor (components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1198). Every destructive path is therefore confirm-then-permanent. Clear all history deletes every scan on the account in one DELETE (app/history/page.tsx:280-295, dialog :640-694) and its trigger is a single icon button sitting immediately beside the search input in the filter row (components/history/history-filters.tsx:76-88). Delete scan removes the scan, its findings and its notes (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:505-515). Remove member, Delete team, Delete schedule and Delete webhook are the same shape (app/teams/page.tsx:340 and :250, components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:388 and :368).
findings.impact: Clear all history is the one that will eventually cost a user everything they have, and it is two clicks from a control adjacent to the search box they use constantly. For a product whose entire value is that finding IDs are stable across runs so a diff between two scans means something, losing the history destroys the diff, and there is nothing to recover from.
findings.recommendation: Add a soft-delete window for the three that need it most, in this order. (1) Clear all history: add a deleted_at column to scan_history, have the DELETE handler stamp it rather than delete, exclude stamped rows from the list query at app/api/v3/history/route.ts:117-142, and show a persistent "Cleared 143 scans. Undo" bar for 30 seconds after the dialog closes, purging stamped rows on the existing retention sweep. (2) Delete scan: same mechanism surfaced as an undo toast (qolf-07). (3) Remove team member: re-adding is possible via invite but loses their scan association, so stamp and offer undo. Once undo exists for an action, drop that action's confirmation dialog: an undo bar plus an AlertDialog for the same action is one interruption too many. Also move the Clear All button out of the filter row into a danger section below the list, away from the search input it currently sits beside.

findings.title: No search or filter state anywhere in the app is URL-backed, so opening a finding and pressing Back silently resets every filter you set
findings.description: lib/ui/url-state.ts provides a complete solution including the LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT bridge (:19-49) and a useQueryParam hook (:170), but that hook has only two consumers repo-wide: app/repos/page.tsx:134 and components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx. Everywhere else `page` and `scope` are hand-wired into the URL while every search box and filter is plain useState: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 (severity set, category, sort direction, grouping, search), app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and :72, app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35, app/compare/page.tsx:37, app/admin/page.tsx:197. The findings list is the sharp case: selecting a finding calls setQueryParam(FINDING_QUERY_PARAM, issue.id) with the default pushState at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:273, creating a history entry, and both host pages swap ResultsList out for IssueDetail (app/history/page.tsx:465-473). Pressing Back unmounts IssueDetail, remounts ResultsList, and every filter returns to its default at :114-120, while scroll position is deliberately preserved across that same remount at :262-267.
findings.impact: Reviewing a scan goes: filter to Critical and High, open the first finding, read it, press Back, and the list is unfiltered again while the scroll position is restored to where you were in the shorter filtered list, dropping you at an arbitrary offset in a longer one. On a 200-finding crawl that happens on every single finding. Nothing filtered can be shared or bookmarked either: a link to "the criticals on this scan" or "my staging scans" does not exist.
findings.recommendation: Swap the useState declarations for the useQueryParam hook that already exists. In components/scanner/results-list.tsx:114-120 back sev, cat, sort, group and q with query params, omitting each when it equals its default so a clean scan URL stays clean, and write them with { replace: true } so filter changes do not pollute the back stack (the finding param at :273 keeps pushState, which is correct). Do the same for filter and tag in app/history/page.tsx:66-67 and the search state in app/teams/page.tsx:49, app/assets/page.tsx:35 and app/compare/page.tsx:37. Also add LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT to the two page-sync effects that listen only for QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT and popstate, app/public-scans/page.tsx:99-100 and app/assets/page.tsx:60-61, since clicking their own tab in components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx while already on that page at ?page=3 is exactly the soft-navigation case the bridge was written for and which app/history/page.tsx:213 already handles.

findings.title: There is no path from a finding you just fixed back to verifying it: no rescan on the issue view, and Compare is reachable only from the top nav
findings.description: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx renders a full remediation lifecycle (Open / In progress / Fixed, persisted at :349 and keyed on the stable finding id per the docblock at :253-259) but contains no action that re-runs the scan or re-checks that finding. The only rescan in the product is the history row menu, which is desktop-only and a no-op (qolf-02, qolf-03). Compare is linked from exactly two places, components/scanner/header.tsx:29 and components/scanner/footer.tsx:85, never from a scan or a finding. Reaching a diff from an open finding is: back to the findings list, back to history, Compare in the nav, find the host in the picker (app/compare/page.tsx:238), pick two scans if the host has more than two (:268), press Compare (:276). Six interactions, and the host you were just looking at is not preselected.
findings.impact: Find, fix, verify is the loop this product exists to serve, and verify is the only leg with no direct route. In practice users mark a finding Fixed and never confirm it, which makes the remediation status a self-reported label rather than a verified one, and leaves the strongest claim the product makes ("the same URL produces the same finding IDs and the same ratings on every run, which is the only reason a diff between two scans means anything", components/landing/landing-how-it-works.tsx:32-35) unreachable from inside the product.
findings.recommendation: Add two entries. First, a "Re-check this" button on the issue detail beside the remediation control at components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:829: it runs the same scan the dashboard does against result.url, polls status, and on completion reports whether this finding id is present in the new run, then offers "Open the new scan" and "Mark fixed". Second, add "Compare with previous scan" to the scan actions menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:532-661, beside the existing Share entry), resolving the previous scan for the same host server-side and navigating straight to /compare?a=<prev>&b=<current>, which app/compare/page.tsx:72-93 already accepts as a deep link. Both collapse six interactions to one and both reuse existing endpoints.

findings.title: The Developer nav entry that made scheduled scans discoverable is dead code: DEVELOPER_HREF is not in NAV_LINKS, so 25 lines of header logic can never run
findings.description: components/scanner/header.tsx:23 defines DEVELOPER_HREF as `${ROUTES.PROFILE}?tab=developer` under a comment at :18-22 explaining that scheduled scans, webhooks, domains and API keys "had no top-level entry, so recurring monitoring, the whole point of a scheduled scan, was two clicks deep under Profile and effectively undiscoverable". NAV_LINKS at :25-34 lists eight entries and DEVELOPER_HREF is not one of them. Consequently handleNavClick (:69-79) always returns at its first line `if (href !== DEVELOPER_HREF) return`, because no rendered link ever equals that constant; the `if (href === DEVELOPER_HREF)` branch in isNavActive (:82) is unreachable; and the locationSearch state with its popstate and QUERY_CHANGE_EVENT effect (:45-58) plus the onDeveloperTab derivation (:59-60) exist only to feed that unreachable branch.
findings.impact: Scheduled scans, webhooks, verified domains and API keys are back to three navigations deep with no top-level entry, which the code comment itself identifies as the problem this was supposed to fix. Recurring monitoring is the feature that turns a one-off scanner into something a team keeps paying for, and nothing in the product's chrome points at it. Twenty-five lines of header code also carry maintenance cost and read as intentional to the next person editing the file.
findings.recommendation: Add { href: DEVELOPER_HREF, label: "Developer" } to NAV_LINKS at components/scanner/header.tsx:25-34, which restores every code path in the file. Nine desktop items is one too many for the absolutely-centred nav at :153, so move Badge (:32) into the Developer tab where it belongs, since it is a per-scan embed rather than a section. If the entry is genuinely not wanted, delete DEVELOPER_HREF, handleNavClick, the locationSearch state and effect, and the onDeveloperTab derivation rather than leaving them, and surface schedules another way, for example a "Schedule this scan" entry in the scan actions menu that deep-links to /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules with the URL prefilled.

findings.title: Six report exports including a synchronous hand-rolled PDF writer run straight from the menu click with no busy state, no progress and no success signal
findings.description: components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx defines exportJson (:185), exportCsv (:224), exportPdf (:254), exportSarif (:262), exportMarkdown (:270) and exportCompliance (:276), each wired directly as onSelect on a DropdownMenuItem (:536, :542, :550, :559, :565, :571) with no busy flag and no post-action feedback. exportPdf calls generatePdfReport(result), declared `export function generatePdfReport(result: ScanResult): Uint8Array` at lib/reports/pdf-report.ts:11: a fully synchronous 514-line PDF writer that loops over every finding (:321), every fix step (:371), every code example (:380) and every wrapped code line (:385) on the main thread. The markdown, SARIF and compliance generators are similarly synchronous over the same arrays. Compare with the same file's other long operations, all of which do have busy state: Share (:288), Verify with AI (:427), Generate AI summary (:473) and Delete (:507).
findings.impact: On a deep crawl with hundreds of findings the menu closes and the tab freezes for a beat with no spinner, no disabled item and no progress. If the download is then blocked by the browser, or the tab is background-throttled, the user gets nothing at all and no explanation. The five non-PDF formats have a milder version of the same problem: no confirmation that anything happened, so a user whose downloads go to a folder they do not watch cannot tell success from a no-op.
findings.recommendation: Add an `exporting` state keyed by format. Set it before the call, mark the menu item disabled with a Loader2 icon and an "Exporting..." label exactly as the Share item already does at :578-582, yield once with `await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 0))` so the spinner paints before the synchronous generator runs, then clear it and confirm with a toast naming the file. For scans over roughly 200 findings move generatePdfReport into a Web Worker so the main thread stays responsive: the function is pure over ScanResult and returns bytes, so it ports unchanged. Note the export set is also gated inconsistently, with PDF behind featurePdfReports at :545 while SARIF, Markdown and the compliance report are not.

findings.title: The findings search matches only title and description, so pasting the stable check id the product sells as its differentiator finds nothing
findings.description: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:326-333 filters findings on f.title and f.description only. f.id is not searched, nor f.category, nor f.evidence. That id is the value proposition stated on the landing page (components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:77-80, "a finding ID that does not change between runs") and it is what every export carries: components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:200 puts f.id in the JSON export, lib/reports/sarif-report.ts uses it as the SARIF rule id, and the roughly 750 SEO pages are addressed by it at /checks/{id} (app/checks/page.tsx:178).
findings.impact: The natural workflow, copy a rule id out of a CI SARIF upload, a GitHub code-scanning alert or a /checks page and paste it into the scan to see whether it fired here, returns zero results, and the user concludes the finding is absent when it is present. The same search is used on all five surfaces that render ScanResultDetail (app/history/page.tsx:496, app/demo/page.tsx:119, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:272, app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:302, components/scanner/dashboard-results.tsx:229), so the gap is everywhere at once.
findings.recommendation: Extend the predicate at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:326-333 to also match f.id and the resolved category label, and change the input placeholder at :372-382 to name what it matches ("Search findings or paste a check id"). While there, add the two filters whose data is already rendered but not filterable: remediation status, bulk-assignable at :690-704 and shown per row at :862-871, and AI verdict, counted at :299-307 and rendered at :872-883, so a reviewer can hide possible_fp rows.

findings.title: No user-facing list in the product has a sort control, and history has no severity, date-range or source filter despite carrying all three fields
findings.description: components/history/history-filters.tsx renders exactly three controls: a URL search box (:36), a tag dropdown (:46) and Clear All (:76). Repo-wide only four files contain any sort state (components/scanner/results-list.tsx, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx, components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx, components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx) and only the first is on a non-admin surface. Every user list is therefore locked to a fixed server order: history ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:127), shares ORDER BY scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/shares/route.ts:28), assets ORDER BY last_scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141), public scans ORDER BY sh.scanned_at DESC (app/api/v3/public-scans/route.ts:94). Yet the history row already renders per-severity counts from s.summary (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:57-72) and the API already selects sh.source (app/api/v3/history/route.ts:119) and never exposes it.
findings.impact: "Show me every scan that turned up a critical" and "show me last week" are the two questions a security team asks of a scan history, and neither is answerable, so triage is scroll-and-read. Two defaults are also on the wrong axis: /shares sorts by when the underlying scan ran rather than when the link was created or expires, and /assets sorts by most-recently-scanned, which surfaces the host you already know about and buries the stale one, when "not scanned in N days" is the single most useful view of an asset inventory.
findings.recommendation: On the history filter row add a severity segmented filter (Any / Critical / High and above / Clean) derived from s.summary, a date-range select (Last 7 days / 30 days / All), a source filter over the source column the API already returns, and a sort select (Newest, Worst severity, Most findings, Host A-Z). Push all of them into SQL alongside the server-side search from qolf-01 rather than filtering the capped client array. Change the /assets default order at app/api/v3/assets/route.ts:141 to stalest-first or add an explicit "Needs a rescan" filter, and order /shares by share creation. Back all of it with useQueryParam per qolf-10 so a filtered view is linkable. On mobile these do not fit inline, so put them behind one "Filters" trigger opening components/ui/sheet.tsx with the active-filter count on the trigger.

findings.title: The profile page's success and error banner renders at the top of the page while the actions that set it are hundreds of pixels below, so a failed delete looks like nothing happened
findings.description: The comment at app/profile/page.tsx:687 calls it "Toast messages", but it is a static, non-sticky div rendered at :688-716 in normal document flow above the two-column tab layout that starts at :719. Every mutation in the Developer, Security, Social, Billing, Privacy and AI tabs writes into that single error/success pair (declared :124-125, threaded down as props at :778-779, :799-800, :814-815, :830-831, :846-847, :867-868, :886-887, :908-909). Nothing scrolls it into view and nothing auto-dismisses it. The Developer tab alone is 849 lines with API keys, webhooks and schedules stacked vertically, so deleting a schedule near the bottom sets setSuccess("Scheduled scan removed.") (components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:402) or setError(data.error || "Failed to remove the schedule.") (:398) into a banner well outside the viewport.
findings.impact: The success case is merely wasted, since the row also disappears. The failure case is the problem: the schedule stays in the list, no message appears anywhere the user is looking, and the click reads as having done nothing. The same applies to a failed webhook delete, a failed key rotate and a failed 2FA disable, all of which sit near the bottom of long tabs.
findings.recommendation: Either make the banner sticky, wrapping :688-716 in `sticky top-[calc(4rem+var(--vr-banner-h,0px))] z-30` so it follows the scroll below the fixed header, or move these messages onto the toast from qolf-07 and keep the inline banner only for persistent states. If the banner stays, add scrollIntoView({ block: "nearest", behavior: "smooth" }) on transition to a non-null error, and auto-clear success after roughly 5 seconds the way app/repos/page.tsx:144 already does.

findings.title: Bulk scan counts a queued background job as a completed scan, so the summary says "12 of 12 scanned" before any scan has produced a result
findings.description: handleBulkScan (app/dashboard/page.tsx:733-782) loops the URLs, POSTs each to /api/v3/scan and increments `successful` on `res.ok && !data.error` at :758. That POST returns { scanId, status: "running" } (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:443 and :454); it never returns a result and never waits for one, and nothing in this loop polls /api/v3/scan/status/[id], unlike the single-scan path at :597. The summary then reports the count as finished work: components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx:22-24 renders "Bulk run finished. {successful} of {total} scanned."
findings.impact: A bulk run of twenty URLs claims twenty scanned the instant the last POST is accepted, while twenty scans are still executing server-side. Any that subsequently fail (unreachable host, TLS error, watchdog timeout) are counted as successes and never reported. "Open in history" (components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx:49-54) then lands on a list that does not yet contain them, which reads as data loss. The progress counter at :744 is misleading for the same reason: it measures requests issued, not scans done.
findings.recommendation: Collect the returned scanIds and poll them. Replace the `successful` increment at :758 with pushing data.scanId into an array, then after the submit loop poll each id (or add a GET /api/v3/scan/status?ids=1,2,3 batch endpoint, which is one query) and count terminal states, driving bulkProgress from completions rather than submissions. Change the copy in components/scanner/dashboard-bulk-result.tsx:22 to distinguish the two phases: "Queued 20 scans" while polling, then "18 finished, 2 failed" when they settle. If polling is not wanted, the honest copy today is "20 scans queued. They will appear in History as they finish."

findings.title: The findings toolbar and severity filter both overflow their container on a 390px phone, so the primary triage controls need horizontal dragging or are clipped outright
findings.description: components/scanner/results-list.tsx:398 is a `flex items-center gap-2` row holding three buttons, all `h-9 px-3 text-xs` and all explicitly shrink-0: "Most severe first" (:399), "Group by severity" (:420) and "Select" (:440). The parent at :366 is `flex flex-col sm:flex-row`, so below 640px this inner row is full width, and the three labels plus padding and gaps need roughly 385px inside the roughly 358px available at a 390px viewport minus the px-4 container. Because every child is shrink-0 and the row has no overflow-x-auto, the content pushes out of the card. Immediately below, the severity filter at :463 is `flex overflow-x-auto` with five buttons at min-w-[76px] (:475), a 380px minimum in the same 358px box, so the Info column is always clipped. The category chips at :516 are h-7, 28px tall.
findings.impact: Reading a scan result is the main thing users do on a phone, and the controls that make a 200-finding list navigable are the part that breaks. The severity strip doubles as the legend and is the only place per-severity counts appear once the row-level breakdown is hidden (qolf-03), so a clipped last column loses information, not just a control.
findings.recommendation: Below sm, collapse sort, group, severity and category into one "Filters" button opening components/ui/sheet.tsx, with a count badge showing how many filters are non-default, leaving only the search input and that trigger inline. Keep "Select" as a separate 44px button since it is a mode, not a filter. Inside the sheet render the severity rows full width so the counts are readable, and raise the category chips from h-7 to h-9. Above sm keep today's inline layout, which is fine.

findings.title: Row action clusters across shares, webhooks, schedules, domains and team members are 28 to 32px icon buttons packed 4px apart, several hover-gated and therefore invisible on touch
findings.description: The same shape repeats on every list row. components/shares/shares-row.tsx:118 puts a 32px copy button (:119) and a 32px overflow menu (:136) 4px apart, and that menu is the only route to Revoke Access. components/profile/tabs/developer/webhooks-section.tsx:318 is a shrink-0 cluster of a Switch plus 28px edit (:331), test (:341) and delete (:356). components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:346 is the same with DNS record (:348), Verify now (:367) and a 28px trash (:381), and that row is the entire body of /attack-surface (app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54). components/profile/tabs/developer/schedules-section.tsx:317 and :337 are 28px pause and delete. Several are additionally opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100, which never resolves on touch: components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:146 (the only route to removing a member), components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:206, and components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:85 (a p-1 copy button of roughly 20px on the scan results page). components/ui/pagination-control.tsx uses 32px arrows (:123, :138, :182, :197), 32px page numbers (:164) and 28px page-size buttons (:100), on every paginated list in the app.
findings.impact: Every one of these is under the 44px guidance, and in the worst cases a destructive action sits 4px from a benign one: on the webhooks row "send a test delivery" and "delete this webhook" are adjacent 28px targets. On the domains and webhooks rows the shrink-0 cluster reserves 140 to 205px, so at 390px the identifier the row is about (the webhook URL, the domain name) truncates to a few characters and the user picks between actions without being able to read which record they apply to. Where the cluster is hover-gated it is not merely small but absent, so removing a team member is unreachable from a phone.
findings.recommendation: Below sm, restructure these rows as two-line cards: identifier and status badge on line one at full width, actions on line two as either full-width 44px buttons or a single 44px overflow trigger opening components/ui/sheet.tsx. components/assets/asset-row.tsx:35 and components/scanner/response-headers.tsx:126 already do the `flex flex-col` by default plus `sm:grid` pattern correctly and are the in-repo reference. Change every `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100` on an action button to `sm:opacity-0 sm:group-hover:opacity-100`. In components/ui/pagination-control.tsx, below sm collapse to Prev, a "3 / 12" label and Next at h-11, hide the first and last arrows, and move the page-size buttons into the filter sheet.

findings.title: The History/Assets/Attack Surface/Public Scans tab bar neither wraps nor scrolls, and the profile's eight-tab nav drops its labels entirely below 640px
findings.description:
components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:29 is `
` with four tabs at px-3 py-2 (:37) labelled My History, Assets, Attack Surface and Public Scans (:8-13). There is no flex-wrap, no overflow-x-auto and no whitespace-nowrap, so at 390px the four labels exceed the roughly 358px available and the flex children shrink until the text wraps inside each tab, producing a ragged two-line nav. This component is the primary navigation on four top-level pages. The profile page solves the identical problem correctly one file away, wrapping its mobile tab strip in `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-hide -mx-4 px-4` at app/profile/page.tsx:723. But that same strip then hides the label at :737 (`{tab.label}`), so below 640px the eight profile sections render as eight bare 16px lucide glyphs on buttons (:726) that carry no aria-label either.
findings.impact: The tab bar is how a phone user moves between their scans, their asset inventory and their verified domains, and it renders as a broken two-line block. On the profile page the user must identify Security, Social, Billing, Developer, Notifications, Privacy and AI purely from unlabelled monochrome icons, and a screen reader gets no name for any of them, which contradicts the published accessibility statement at app/legal/accessibility.
findings.recommendation: For components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx wrap the row in `overflow-x-auto scrollbar-hide -mx-4 px-4`, add whitespace-nowrap to each Link, and raise py-2 to py-3 so the target reaches 44px, copying app/profile/page.tsx:723-741 verbatim. For app/profile/page.tsx:737 delete the `hidden sm:inline` and keep the label at every width: the strip already scrolls horizontally, so width is not the constraint that motivated hiding it. If labels really must go, add aria-label={tab.label} to the button at :726.

findings.title: Eight irreversible user-facing actions have no confirmation, including one that destroys the user's own third-party API key and one that deletes a triage note
findings.description: handleReset (components/profile/tabs/profile-ai-settings-tab.tsx:152-180) DELETEs the account's AI config with no dialog, from two triggers: a Button at :308 and a bare 12px text link at :486. That row holds the user's own provider API key, which the UI only ever renders as apiKeyLast4, so once deleted the key is unrecoverable from here. Seven more irreversible actions are equally ungated. Resetting a finding's remediation status to open issues a DELETE (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:341-347) that drops the stored note, assignee and due date. Ending a live browser session destroys it and books the metered seconds (app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:160, trigger :453). Declining a team invitation deletes the invite row so the invitee cannot return without a fresh invite, and it sits immediately beside Accept (app/teams/page.tsx:226, trigger components/teams/team-invitations.tsx:89). Dismissing a bell notification is a server-side permanent removal (components/shared/notification-center.tsx:382, triggers :537, :560, :571) with no archive. Removing an avatar deletes the image (components/profile/tabs/profile-general-tab.tsx:94), while the admin equivalent clear_avatar does get a dialog. Dismissing an auto or AI-assigned tag deletes the scan_tags row from a roughly 10px X (components/history/scan-tags.tsx:103). Cancelling a running scan discards the in-flight result (app/dashboard/page.tsx:802).
findings.impact: The AI config reset is the sharpest: a user clicking a small "Reset to VulnRadar AI" text link loses a key they must go back to their provider to reissue, with no warning and no undo. The remediation reset is the quietest data loss: a triage note explaining what was done about a finding disappears because the user changed a status dropdown back to Open. Both are made worse by the inconsistency, since the same product opens a dialog for pausing nothing and unverifying an email (qolf-22).
findings.recommendation: Confirm the two that destroy content the user authored or supplied: AI config reset, with copy naming what goes ("Your OpenAI key and model choice are removed. You will need to paste the key again."), and remediation reset, but prefer keeping the note and just changing the status server-side, since deleting it is a schema choice not a user intention. Give an undo bar (qolf-09) rather than a dialog to notification dismiss, tag dismiss and avatar removal, which are frequent and low-stakes individually. For decline-invite, separate it visually from Accept in components/teams/team-invitations.tsx:89 and give it a one-line confirm. Leave cancel-scan and end-browser-session unconfirmed but label the cost inline ("Ends the session, remaining time is not refunded").

findings.title: Confirmation is spent on additive admin actions while destructive neighbours are ungated, and three grants require a full change-diff modal or a password
findings.description: Five admin actions that only grant capacity open the full SaveConfirmationModal (components/shared/save-confirmation-modal.tsx, wired at components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:2825) complete with a change-diff table and an email-the-user toggle: reset_daily_limit (:2033), reset_ai_usage (:2053), reset_github_review_usage (:2073), reset_free_github_trial (:2093) and clear_rate_limits (:1962). Nothing is destroyed by any of them. toggle_ai_ban is unconditionally in PASSWORD_GATED_ACTIONS (components/admin/config.ts:318), so un-banning a user from AI chat, a purely additive restore, demands password re-entry. Revoking a gift subscription is double-confirmed: a two-click inline "Are you sure?" at components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:191-226 whose Yes button at :212 then opens SaveConfirmationModal. Unverify email (:2134), Send notification (:2223) and Gift subscription (:2304) all route through the same heavy modal. Meanwhile the genuinely destructive database cleanup in the same admin surface has no dialog at all (qolf-06). Two adjacent inconsistencies exist in user-facing code too: components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx confirms "Sign out everywhere" (:1686) but not revoking a single session (:273), and app/teams/page.tsx confirms Remove member (components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:165) but not Cancel invite two rows below it (:258).
findings.impact: Confirmation dialogs only work if their presence means something. Here the operator learns that everything opens a modal, including granting someone extra scans, so the dialog stops carrying information and gets clicked through reflexively, which is exactly when the ungated database purge lands. The gift-subscription double confirm is pure friction on an already rare action.
findings.recommendation: Remove the confirmation from the five quota grants at components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1962, :2033, :2053, :2073 and :2093, and from unverify_email at :2134, replacing each with an undo toast ("Daily limit reset. Undo"). Make toggle_ai_ban conditionally gated in components/admin/config.ts:318 so only the ban direction needs a password. Delete the inline two-click confirm at components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:191-226 and keep only the SaveConfirmationModal. Add confirmation to revoke-single-session (components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx:273) and cancel-invite (app/teams/page.tsx:364) so each pair is internally consistent, or remove it from their neighbours: the rule to apply is confirm on irreversible, undo on reversible, nothing on a toggle.

findings.title: Four mutations have no in-flight protection at all, so rescan, tagging and cancel-invite can be fired repeatedly while the first request is still open
findings.description: Adding and removing a scan tag has no busy state anywhere in the chain: app/history/page.tsx:305-331 has no flag, no try/catch and no !res.ok branch, and components/history/scan-tags.tsx:80 fires onAdd without awaiting it and closes the input immediately, while the remove buttons at :98-106 and :120-127 carry no disabled. The history Rescan trigger has a rescanning flag (app/history/page.tsx:268) but the DropdownMenuItem that fires it (components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221-231) never consumes it as disabled. app/teams/page.tsx:364-386 (cancel invite) has no per-invite busy flag and its button at components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:254-258 has no disabled. components/scanner/header.tsx:100-106 (log out) fires the POST without awaiting it before redirecting. These four are the only unprotected mutations found across profile, teams, scanner, history, shares and repos; every other mutation on those surfaces already sets a busy flag and disables its trigger.
findings.impact: Because none of these show anything while in flight (qolf-02 for rescan, silent for tags), a slow request looks like a dead button and the user clicks again. For Rescan that spends a second scan against the daily cap. For tags, two racing POSTs to /api/v3/scan-tags both return the tag array and the last response wins, so a fast add-then-remove can leave the UI showing a tag the server deleted or the reverse, with no error path to notice it.
findings.recommendation: Add disabled={rescanning === scan.id} to components/history/history-scan-row.tsx:221. In components/history/scan-tags.tsx make onAdd and onRemove return promises, await them, hold a local pending flag and disable the input and the per-tag remove buttons while it is set. In app/history/page.tsx:305 and :321 add the !res.ok branch reading data.error plus a catch. Add an invitesBusyId state in app/teams/page.tsx:364 and thread it to components/teams/team-members-list.tsx:254 as disabled. The rest of the codebase already sets the convention to copy.

findings.title: A new account meets an eight-step feature-tour modal before it can reach the scan box, and the tour's copy is exactly the generic voice CLAUDE.md bans
findings.description: OnboardingTour is mounted first in the dashboard tree (app/dashboard/page.tsx:876) and opens on any account where onboardingCompleted is false (components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:83-92), rendering a full-screen backdrop at :122. STEPS at :24-77 is eight entries. The signup-to-first-scan path is already landing, signup form, verification email, verify page which auto-redirects after a 2 second timer (app/verify-email/VerifyEmailClient.tsx:76-79), and then this modal. The copy is generic in exactly the ways CLAUDE.md and audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section F prohibit: "Your all-in-one web vulnerability scanner. Let's walk you through the key features so you can get the most out of VulnRadar" (:28), "Great for verifying that you fixed vulnerabilities" (:46), "You're All Set!" (:71), against a landing page whose voice is "Paste a URL. Get findings, not a grade out of ten." (components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:105-107).
findings.impact: The first thing a new user sees inside the product is eight screens of feature marketing about teams, webhooks and CI integration, none of which they can evaluate before running one scan. Skipping is one click, so most users will skip and learn nothing, and the ones who do not spend eight clicks before reaching the box. It is also the first impression that contradicts the landing page's voice, which is the strongest work in the repo.
findings.recommendation: Delete the blocking modal and let the account land on the scan form, which components/scanner/scan-hero.tsx already introduces. Replace it with two cheaper things. First, a single dismissible strip above the form for a brand-new account, in the landing page's voice, along the lines of "Paste any URL. Nothing to install: the request goes out from our servers, not your browser." Second, one-time contextual hints attached to the features they describe and shown after the moment each becomes relevant: a "Compare this against your last run" pointer the second time the same host is scanned, an "API keys and schedules live here" pointer the first time the Developer tab opens. The existing POST /api/v3/auth/onboarding completion flag (:96) and the tour-replay entry at components/profile/tabs/profile-general-tab.tsx:441 can both stay, with the replay opening a static "What's here" page instead of a wizard. The step list at :139-203, which shows the whole shape at once and lets you jump anywhere, is the good part and is worth keeping as that page.

findings.title: Neither the docs nor the roughly 750-page checks index has any search, so finding one check by name means expanding eighteen accordions and using browser find
findings.description: app/checks/page.tsx is a server component with no client JS. Its only navigation aids are eighteen category cards (:114-133) and eighteen details accordions listing every check (:148-187). There is no text input on the page and no severity filter, even though a SeverityPill is rendered for every row at :172. The docs section is the same: components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx and components/docs/docs-shell.tsx contain no input element, so twenty documentation sections are navigable only through the hand-maintained tree in components/docs/docs-nav.ts.
findings.impact: The checks pages are the product's main organic surface and the canonical reference for what each finding means, and a human who lands on the index wanting HSTS has to expand accordions and use browser find. The severity data is on every row and cannot be filtered, so "show me every critical check" is unanswerable. For docs, twenty sections with no search is the most conspicuous omission for a self-hostable product whose setup, config and self-hosting instructions all live there.
findings.recommendation: For /checks add a small client island above the accordions: an input plus five severity toggles filtering a prebuilt index of { id, title, severity, category } derived from the same registry the page already reads. Keep every details block rendered in the server HTML so the SEO surface is unchanged and the island only hides non-matching rows, so crawlers still see all roughly 750 links. Match the check id as well as the title, for the same reason as qolf-14. For docs, build a static JSON index at prebuild time next to the existing scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs step and ship a client-side fuzzy search in components/docs/docs-sidebar.tsx. Wiring both indexes into the command palette from qolf-08 means one search box answers navigate, find a check, and find a doc.

findings.title: The admin users table has no filters at all and its sort control only reorders the ten rows currently loaded, so sorting page 1 of 40 sorts 10 users
findings.description: sortedUsers at app/admin/page.tsx:648-663 sorts the already-fetched users array in memory, and the comment at :646-647 states it outright: "Client-side sort of the currently loaded page of users. Does not trigger a refetch; only reorders what's already on screen." Pagination is server-side (page :194, usersPageSize :196, default 10) and the header control at :665-671 gives no indication that its scope is the page. The table has no filters whatsoever: no role, plan, disabled, banned, verified or 2FA filter, despite all of those being columns the API already selects (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:148-158) and the detail panel already displays. The debounced server search (:599, 300ms) matches only u.email and u.name (app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:350), so a user cannot be looked up by id, Stripe customer id, IP, or any OAuth identity on the same row. The same page-local search limitation exists in components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:141-150 and components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx:122-130, though both of those are honest about it in their own UI (audit-log.tsx:342, ai-chats-manager.tsx:237).
findings.impact: An operator clicking the Joined header to find the oldest account gets the oldest of ten, presented identically to a real sort, and will act on a wrong answer. With roughly 50 users the blast radius is small today, but this is the moderation surface and the two questions it cannot answer, who is on a paid plan and who is disabled, are the two an operator asks most.
findings.recommendation: Push the sort to the server: add sort and dir params to GET /api/v3/admin, whitelist the sortable columns, map them into the ORDER BY at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:351, and delete the client sortedUsers memo at app/admin/page.tsx:648. Add plan, role and status (active / disabled / banned / unverified) as server-side filter params rendered as selects beside the search box at :1268. Widen the server search predicate at app/api/v3/admin/route.ts:350 to cover u.id::text, stripe_customer_id, google_email, github_login and discord_username, keeping the existing LIKE-metacharacter escaping at :127. Until any of that lands, relabel the header control "Sort this page" so it stops asserting something untrue.

findings.title: The notification bell has no read state, no mark-all-read, no archive and 24px dismiss targets, and both of its actions fail to console
findings.description: components/shared/notification-center.tsx is the only notifications surface in the product; there is no full-page view. It has no read/unread distinction, no mark-all-read, no filter and no pagination, just max-h-96 overflow-y-auto at :505. Both mutations swallow failure: acceptTeamInvite (:361-377) catches to console.error at :371, and dismissUserNotification (:382-392) catches to console.error at :388 and only removes the row after the await, so a failed dismiss leaves the item in place with no message. The dismiss controls are p-1 buttons (:573, :619, :747) wrapping small icons, roughly 24px, and dismissing is the only affordance a notification has.
findings.impact: Dismissing is destructive and one-way here since there is no archive, so a mis-tap on a 24px target next to a scrollable list permanently loses a team invite notification. A failed dismiss looks like the tap missed, so the user taps again. Accepting a team invite that fails leaves the user staring at an unchanged panel with no idea whether they joined.
findings.recommendation: Add read_at to the notifications table plus a PATCH /api/v3/notifications { markAllRead: true }, render unread rows with the existing left accent treatment, and add a Mark all read text button in the panel header. Change dismiss to set read rather than delete, and add a /profile?tab=notifications archive listing everything, which also gives the panel a "See all" footer link. Replace both console.error catches with the toast from qolf-07. Raise the p-1 buttons at :573, :619 and :747 to h-11 w-11 below sm.

findings.title: The users table is the only place in the admin panel that links to a user record, so the support inbox, audit log, error logs and AI chats all render an account as unclickable text
findings.description:
`/admin?tab=users&user=<id>` is a real deep link: the users table row action builds it at app/admin/page.tsx:1468 and the mobile list at :1515, and handleQueryChange parses it back at :418-424. Nothing else in the panel uses it. A repo-wide grep for `admin?tab=` outside app/admin/page.tsx returns exactly one hit, app/admin/ai-chats/[id]/page.tsx:116, and that one goes back to the ai-chats list, not to a user.

Every other panel that knows which account it is talking about throws that away. support-inbox.tsx:253 prints `{t.owner_email}` inside a plain div. The audit log has target_email and target_name on every entry (components/admin/types.ts:156-157) and renders them at audit-log.tsx:422-445, but the click handler filters the audit log by that email (:428-431) instead of opening the account. error-logs-manager.tsx and email-logs-manager.tsx have no user linkage at all. ai-chats-manager.tsx links to the conversation (:386, :408) but not to its author.

Because handleTabChange (app/admin/page.tsx:869-876) calls setSelectedUser(null) and rewrites the query string on every tab switch, going to look up an account and coming back means rebuilding whatever you were reading.
findings.impact: Every cross-reference is done by hand through the search box, which is the single most repeated interaction in support work. Task A in qols-01 measures it at seven clicks plus a copy-paste, with the ticket thread reloaded twice. It also makes mistakes easy: the operator is pasting an email into a search field and trusting that the row that comes back is the same account the ticket came from.
findings.recommendation:
Two changes. First, make the account reference a link everywhere it appears: support-inbox.tsx:253, audit-log.tsx:422-445 and :499-516 (keep the existing filter-by-target action as a secondary control and make the name itself the link), plus error-logs-manager and email-logs-manager once those rows carry a user id. Reuse the exact anchor pattern already at app/admin/page.tsx:1467-1482, href `/admin?tab=users&user={id}` with the ctrl/meta passthrough so middle-click opens a real tab. This requires the routes behind those panels to select the user id alongside the email; support-tickets already joins the owner.

Second, and better for the ticket case specifically, add an account slide-over rather than a navigation. Extract the Overview card from components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:513-700 (avatar, plan and role badges, the four quick stats, the security chips) into an `<AccountSummary userId>` component that fetches `GET /api/v3/admin?section=user-detail`, and mount it in a Sheet from the ticket header. The operator sees plan, quota, disabled state and recent scans without leaving the thread: task A drops from seven clicks to one.

findings.title: Sending a staff invite that grants the admin role takes one unconfirmed click, while resetting one settings value to its default opens a modal
findings.description:
handleSendInvite (components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:156-186) POSTs to /api/v3/admin/staff-invites straight from the Send invite button at :718-730. There is no confirmation dialog anywhere in that file: a grep for confirm in staff-list.tsx returns nothing. The role select at :702-711 is populated from INVITABLE_STAFF_ROLES (:79-83), which excludes only USER and SUPER_ADMIN, so `admin` is selectable. Server side, app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts:49 calls requireAdmin() and nothing else: no password re-auth.

Compare the equivalent action through the other path. Granting a role via PATCH /api/v3/admin is in PASSWORD_GATED_ACTIONS (components/admin/config.ts:308-326, which lists set_role, make_admin and remove_admin), so the caller must re-enter their own password, and the client puts it behind AdminPasswordConfirmDialog (user-detail-panel.tsx:2804, :2852). Same privilege, two paths, opposite friction.

At the other end, routine reversible actions are gated. system-settings-manager.tsx:756-767 opens a full ConfirmDialog to delete one stored override so a setting falls back to its default. security-alerts-manager.tsx:399-442 opens a SaveConfirmationModal with a two-row change-diff table to mark an alert reviewed. backup-manager.tsx:121-137 starts a real pg_dump child process with no confirmation at all, which is the right call for a non-destructive but expensive job and shows the panel has no consistent rule.

Note AUDIT-012#auth-03 and #authz-10: the invite email links to /staff-invite/[token], a page that does not exist, so today no invite can actually be accepted. That caps the current exposure but does not change the interaction design, and the moment that page ships the gap is live.
findings.impact: The panel's confirmation weight does not track risk, which trains operators to click through dialogs. The one action that hands out administrative access to an arbitrary email address is the one with the least friction, and it bypasses the password re-auth that the codebase already built for exactly this privilege change.
findings.recommendation:
Set the rule by consequence, not by history.

Needs confirmation plus admin password re-auth (add `send_staff_invite` to PASSWORD_GATED_ACTIONS in components/admin/config.ts:308 and enforce it in app/api/v3/admin/staff-invites/route.ts alongside requireAdmin): sending a staff invite; every action already in that Set.

Needs confirmation, no password: delete team (already correct, teams-list.tsx:516-526), send or resend a broadcast (already correct, mass-email-manager.tsx:683), block a user from a security alert, purge a host, revoke a share, delete scans for a blocked value, clear the error or email log, import a settings file.

Does not need a modal: reset one setting to its default (system-settings-manager.tsx:756, make it an inline undo toast instead, the value is recoverable), mark a security alert reviewed (security-alerts-manager.tsx:399 when action is manual_review, drop the change-diff table and make Resolve immediate with an Undo in the toast), revoke a pending staff invite (staff-list.tsx:185, already unconfirmed and correctly so), start a backup (already unconfirmed and correctly so).

findings.title: The admin user detail page presents 21 support actions as identical icon-in-rounded-square cards in a three-column grid, so Delete Account is visually one peer of Clear Avatar
findings.description:
The Support Actions card (components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1872) renders 21 ActionCard instances across four `grid grid-cols-1 sm:grid-cols-2 lg:grid-cols-3 gap-2` blocks headed Session and Security (:1891), Usage and Limits (:2017), Account Management (:2107) and Danger Zone (:2324). ActionCard itself (components/admin/shared/action-card.tsx:47-58) is an `h-9 w-9 rounded-lg` tinted square holding an `h-4 w-4` icon, then a label and a caption. That is the exact construction audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md tell-tale 5 marks as a fail, and CLAUDE.md's What to avoid list names twice (generic icon-in-rounded-square for every feature item, and grids of identical icon cards). The landing page, the yardstick, has zero instances of it across nine sections.

The only separation between the four groups is a `text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider text-muted-foreground` line. Delete Account (:2460), Delete All Scans (:2407), Delete Webhooks (:2425) and Delete Schedules (:2442) sit in a grid of the same geometry as Clear Avatar (:2149) and Reset AI Usage (:2047); the only difference is a destructive border tint from the `variant` branch at action-card.tsx:38-40.

The page also names two different things the same. tocItems at :502-510 offers Account Management as one of five jump targets, pointing at the card with id account-management at :816 whose heading is Account Management (:821). Inside Support Actions, a different group is also headed Account Management (:2107). The jump list sends you to the wrong one.
findings.impact: The operator's eye has no ranking to follow, so finding one action out of 21 is a linear scan of a uniform grid rather than a glance. It also flattens risk: the most destructive action in the product renders at the same size, in the same grid, with the same affordance as clearing an avatar. And the page's own jump list points at the wrong Account Management.
findings.recommendation:
Rebuild Support Actions as a divided list, the pattern design-language.md D4 records as the house idiom, and split the destructive set out.

1. Replace the three non-destructive grids with one `divide-y divide-border/50` list. Each row is `flex items-center justify-between gap-3 py-3`: label and one-line description on the left in `text-sm` and `text-xs text-muted-foreground`, an `h-8` ghost button on the right. Drop the icon squares entirely. Keep the three group headings as `border-t` section rules.
2. Add a filter input above the list that matches on label, since 17 rows is past the point of scanning. This is what actually cuts task C's time-to-find.
3. Move Danger Zone (:2324-2470) out of the grid into a separate card below Support Actions with `border-destructive/20`, collapsed by default behind a Show destructive actions disclosure, rows rendered as `variant="destructive"` buttons rather than cards.
4. Rename the Support Actions subgroup at :2107 to Account State, so it stops colliding with the Account Management card at :821, and verify the tocItems entry at :504 still resolves to id account-management.

findings.title: The scan result view renders the findings list last, below the verdict summary and up to eight secondary panels including a screenshot, a DNS table and a notes editor
findings.description:
ScanResultDetail is the shared body for all four scan-result surfaces (dashboard, history, /shared/[token], /host/[hostname]). Its render order (components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:118-237) is: redirect warning, ScanSummary (:142), afterSummary slot (:144, the host trend chart), CrawlPagesInfo (:146), then the More about this host block (:150-210) holding ScreenshotPanel, ResponseHeaders, DnsRecordsPanel, PortScanPanel, ThreatIntelPanel, SoftwareInventoryPanel, the subdomain slot and the panelFooter slot, and only then ResultsList at :220.

On the owner's own scan the panelFooter is HistoryTagsCard plus HistoryNotes (dashboard-results.tsx:251-267), and both are fully expanded cards, not collapsed rows, so the block between the summary and the first finding is up to six collapsed accordion headers plus a tags card plus a notes editor. The six panels are individually correct: each is collapsed by default (`useState(false)` in screenshot-panel.tsx:83, response-headers.tsx:32, dns-records-panel.tsx:106, port-scan-panel.tsx:64, threat-intel-panel.tsx:34, software-inventory-panel.tsx:33) and three of them return null when they have no data. The problem is the ordering, not the panels.
findings.impact: The report's primary artefact, the list of things to fix, is the last thing on the page on every surface the product has. A reader who scans top-down passes a screenshot, a header dump, a DNS table, a port list, a threat feed, a software inventory, a tag editor and a notes box before reaching a single finding. On the public /host report, which is the shareable link and the SEO surface, the same ordering means a first-time visitor sees infrastructure trivia before the security result.
findings.recommendation: Reorder scan-result-detail.tsx's fragment to summary, findings, then evidence panels: move the `ResultsList` block (:220-237) to sit directly after `{afterSummary}` at :144, and move the More about this host block (:150-210) below it. Keep CrawlPagesInfo above the findings, since it selects which page's findings you are reading. Split the panelFooter slot in two: leave tags with the header chrome next to the scanned URL in dashboard-results.tsx:158-207 where it is metadata about the scan, and move HistoryNotes to the very bottom below the panels, since writing a note is something you do after reading, not before. Give the More about this host heading (:153) a one-line subtitle stating what it is, for example `Infrastructure captured during this scan`, so a reader who has already read the findings knows whether the section is worth opening.

findings.title: The findings list orders on severity band alone, and the exploitability data the scanner already computes is either buried one click deep or never displayed at all
findings.description:
The list groups by severity, not by check category, and defaults to most-severe-first: `grouped` is true at components/scanner/results-list.tsx:119, `sortAsc` is false at :118, and the comparator at :335-337 reads only SEVERITY_PRIORITY. Within a band the order is the array order the scanner produced. So the answer to whether the report ranks by severity or by category is severity, which is right, but it stops there.

The scanner computes three exploitability signals that never reach the list. `inKev` (lib/scanner/types.ts:169), true when a CVE named in the finding is in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, is rendered in exactly one place: components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:748-755, inside an opened finding. `epssScore` (types.ts:162) is rendered at issue-detail.tsx:756-763, same place. `cvssScore` and `cvssVector` (types.ts:179-181) are, by their own doc comment, backfilled onto every finding in every completed scan by attachCvssScores, and a grep for cvssScore across all of app/ and components/ returns zero render sites. Three signals stored on every finding, one of which is never shown anywhere in the product.

Consequence: a high-severity finding that CISA has confirmed is being exploited in the wild right now sorts identically to a high-severity finding that is theoretical, and the reader cannot tell them apart without opening both.
findings.impact: The report cannot answer its own core question, what do I fix first, past the granularity of five severity buckets. On a scan with a dozen highs the user picks essentially at random. The product already paid for the KEV lookup and the EPSS call (AUDIT-011#scan-04 measured the EPSS call as an uncached blocking-path request) and then throws the answer away above the fold.
findings.recommendation:
Three changes, all in components/scanner/results-list.tsx.

1. Add exploitability as the secondary sort inside each severity group, at the comparator at :335-339: after the SEVERITY_PRIORITY comparison, order by `inKev` true first, then descending epssScore, then descending cvssScore. This is a five-line change and it makes the top of each group meaningful.
2. Surface the signal on the row. Add a small `text-[10px] font-semibold uppercase tracking-wide text-[hsl(var(--severity-critical))]` chip reading `Exploited` when `inKev` is true, next to the existing severity badge, and show `cvssScore` as `font-mono tabular-nums` at the row's right edge alongside the existing category label. Follow the pill idiom in design-language.md D3 and do not add a second colour vocabulary; KEV borrows the critical token, CVSS is plain muted numerals.
3. Add an `Exploited first` toggle beside the existing sort and group toggles at :401-435, using the same button geometry, so a reader can collapse straight to the actively exploited set.

While there, add `cvssScore` to the issue-detail header at issue-detail.tsx:729-763, next to the existing KEV and EPSS chips, so the number that is computed for every finding is visible somewhere.

findings.title: The dashboard's headline risk number is a lifetime sum across every scan, so fixing an issue and rescanning makes it go up
findings.description:
The dashboard's third stat cell is Critical and high (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:274-279), computed at :240 as `sb.critical + sb.high` from the API's severityBreakdown. That breakdown is `SUM((summary->>'critical')::int)` over every row in scan_history for the user, with no dedupe by URL and no restriction to the latest scan per host (app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:46-54). The same applies to Findings by severity (dashboard.tsx:417-450) and to Most common findings, whose query counts every findings array element across every scan (route.ts:55-62).

Mechanically: a user with one host carrying two high findings scans it, fixes one, rescans. Scan 1 contributed 2, scan 2 contributes 1, the dashboard now reads 3. Fixing a finding and verifying the fix strictly increases the number the page presents as the account's risk. The same effect makes Most common findings a ranking of which host the user rescans most often, not which issue is most prevalent.

The rest of the page is the same shape: Scans run and Hosts covered are lifetime counters, Started from the API is a lifetime counter, and Findings by severity is the same lifetime sum drawn as a bar list. The only element that answers what changed since I was last here is the 14-day activity strip (:289-337), and it charts scan volume, not findings.
findings.impact: The most prominent number on the signed-in landing page moves the wrong way in response to the exact behaviour the product wants: fix, rescan, verify. A user cannot use the dashboard to tell whether their security posture improved this week, which is the only reason to open a dashboard rather than the history list.
findings.recommendation:
Change what the dashboard aggregates, not how it draws it; the drawing already follows the design language (one inline strip, one severity bar, no card grid).

1. In app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts, replace the severityBreakdown query at :46-54 with a latest-scan-per-URL aggregate: `SELECT DISTINCT ON (url) summary FROM scan_history WHERE user_id = $1 ORDER BY url, scanned_at DESC` as a CTE, then sum over that. Now Critical and high means open critical and high across the hosts you track, and it falls when you fix something.
2. Apply the same CTE to the topVulnerabilities query at :55-62, so Most common findings ranks by how many distinct hosts have the issue.
3. Add a delta. Compute the same latest-per-URL sum as of seven days ago and return it as `severityBreakdownPrior`, then render the change beside the Critical and high cell using the TrendBadge component that already exists at dashboard.tsx:118. That is the what changed since I was last here answer, in the component the page already has.
4. Retitle the cell to `Open critical and high` so the semantics are stated, and keep Scans run and Hosts covered as lifetime counters since those are honest as totals.

findings.title: Four signed-in pages open with the same four-cell aggregate strip, and on /history three of its four cells are derivable from the other one and from the heading directly above it
findings.description:
The identical container `grid grid-cols-2 sm:grid-cols-4 gap-px bg-border overflow-hidden rounded-md border border-border` opens four pages: /dashboard (components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:148 and :261), /history (components/history/history-stats.tsx:66), /shares (components/shares/shares-stats.tsx:64) and /assets (components/assets/assets-stats.tsx:53). All four hold four cells built from a `Cell` or `StatCell` function with the same body: a StatIcon, a `text-2xl font-semibold tabular-nums` number and an `text-[11px] text-muted-foreground` label. Adjacent pages therefore open with an identical template, which is what CLAUDE.md's layout-patterns-to-avoid list and design-language.md tell-tale 6 call out.

On /history it is also redundant content. The h1 subtitle at app/history/page.tsx:579-585 already reads `{scans.length} scans on record`, and the very next element, HistoryStats at :588, opens with a Total scans cell holding the same `scans.length` (history-stats.tsx:55, :67-72). Of the remaining three cells, Came back clean (:56) and Had findings (:57) are complementary filters of the same array and sum back to the first cell, so three of the four numbers carry no information the reader did not already have. Only Findings total (:58-61) is new.
findings.impact: Every signed-in list page looks like every other signed-in list page above the fold, and the strip costs a screenful before the reader reaches the thing the page is for. On /history specifically the reader is shown the same number twice in adjacent elements.
findings.recommendation:
Keep the strip where it earns its place and vary the others, following the nine-different-layouts principle the landing page demonstrates.

- /history: delete HistoryStats entirely (remove the import and the call at app/history/page.tsx:588, delete components/history/history-stats.tsx and its skeleton branch). Fold the one number worth keeping into the existing subtitle at :579-585: `{n} scans on record, {m} findings across them, kept for {retention}`. That removes a component and a screenful and loses nothing.
- /shares: replace the four cells with the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, whose own docblock explains it reads as one bar rather than five cards. Clean, warnings and unsafe are proportions of one whole, which is exactly what that component is for.
- /assets: same substitution, the four cells are Hosts scanned plus a three-way safety split.
- /dashboard: keep the strip. It is the one page where four independent counters are the right shape, and it is already paired with the activity sparkline rather than standing alone.

findings.title: The domain portfolio UI renders at two URLs because the move to /attack-surface never removed the copy in the profile Developer tab
findings.description:
DomainsSection (components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:97, 515 lines) has two importers. app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 renders it as a top-level page reached from the HistoryViewTabs strip, and that file's own doc comment at :12-14 states the reason: the domain-verification UI already existed but was buried in the profile Developer tab, so this surfaces it as its own tab. components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx still lists it as a fourth sub-tab at :82 and still renders it at :754, reachable at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=domains.

The two surfaces are the same component with different chrome: /attack-surface gives it an h1, an explanatory paragraph about what verifying a domain unlocks, and the History/Assets/Attack Surface/Public Scans tab strip; the profile copy gives it a sub-tab label and nothing else. Verifying a domain from one and then opening the other shows two independently fetched copies of the same list.
findings.impact: Two URLs for one feature, so a user who bookmarks or is linked to one never discovers the other, and the profile copy is the worse of the two because it has none of the explanatory framing that tells the user what domain verification is for. It also doubles the maintenance surface: any change to the surrounding affordances has to be made twice or the two drift.
findings.recommendation: Finish the move. Delete the `{ id: "domains", label: "Domains", icon: ShieldCheck }` entry from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS at components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:82 and the `{activeSection === "domains" && ...}` branch at :754, and drop domains from the DeveloperSection type. In its place put a one-line pointer in the Developer tab's header, `Verified domains moved to Attack surface`, linking to ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, so anyone with the old deep link lands somewhere useful. Add a redirect from ?tab=developer&dtab=domains to /attack-surface in the dtab handling at app/profile/page.tsx:110-120 for the same reason.

findings.title: Scheduled scans and webhooks sit three levels deep under Account Settings while Badge, a one-time embed snippet, is a top-level nav item
findings.description:
The signed-in nav (components/scanner/header.tsx:26-33) has eight entries: Scanner, History, Repos, Compare, Shared, Teams, Badge, Profile. Badge is /badge, a page that generates an embeddable status badge snippet, which a user configures once and never returns to. It sits at the same level as History.

Scheduled Scans, the product's recurring-monitoring feature with its own documentation section at app/docs/scheduled-scans, is at /profile?tab=developer&dtab=schedules: Profile in the nav, then the Developer tab (app/profile/page.tsx:645-651), then the Scheduled Scans sub-tab (profile-developer-tab.tsx:81). Three levels, and the page it lives on is titled Account Settings (app/profile/page.tsx:679). Webhooks are in the same place (:80). Both are things a user returns to, filed under settings; the header's DEVELOPER_HREF constant at header.tsx:23 already acknowledges the depth problem by hard-coding a shortcut to the Developer tab, but that shortcut is not a nav item.

Meanwhile Assets, Attack Surface and Public Scans are sub-tabs of History via HistoryViewTabs (components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13), which is a sensible grouping and shows the pattern already exists.
findings.impact: The two features that create recurring engagement, scheduled scans and webhooks, are the hardest to find, and the one that creates none is the most prominent. A user setting up monitoring has to guess that a scheduling feature lives behind a tab called Developer inside a page called Account Settings.
findings.recommendation: Rebalance without adding nav width. Replace the Badge entry at components/scanner/header.tsx:32 with a Monitoring entry pointing at a new /monitoring route, and give that route the same HistoryViewTabs-style sub-strip holding Scheduled Scans, Webhooks and Alerts. Move SchedulesSection and WebhooksSection there by import, exactly as app/attack-surface/page.tsx:54 already does for DomainsSection, and remove their sub-tab entries from DEVELOPER_SECTIONS (profile-developer-tab.tsx:80-81) so the Developer tab is left with API Keys alone, at which point rename that tab to API. Move Badge to the profile Social tab, next to the other share and embed affordances, which is where a one-time embed snippet belongs.

findings.title: The finding detail puts two owner-workflow widgets above the evidence and the fix, so How to fix it, which its own comment calls the reason anyone opened this page, is the sixth block down
findings.description:
IssueDetail renders in this order (components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx:701-948): Back to findings button (:703), the header with severity, category, KEV and EPSS chips, title and description (:719-787), the AI verdict banner when present (:789-813), FindingFeedback (:815-822), RemediationControl (:824-832), Evidence (:834), the What this means / If left unfixed pair (:837-859), and finally How to fix it at :862. The comment above that section, at :861, reads: Fix: the reason anyone opened this page.

FindingFeedback and RemediationControl are both always-expanded owner cards, not collapsed rows. RemediationControl (:265-530) is a five-option status picker plus assignee, due date and note fields with its own save button. FindingFeedback is an accuracy-reporting widget. Neither is what the reader came for on a first read; both are things you do after you have decided the finding is real, which requires reading the evidence and the fix that sit below them.
findings.impact: Every reader scrolls past a status picker and a feedback prompt to reach the fix. On a scan with a dozen findings that is a dozen scrolls past the same two widgets. It also inverts the workflow: the page asks you to triage the finding before it has shown you the evidence for it.
findings.recommendation: Reorder the fragment in components/scanner/issue-detail.tsx so it reads header, evidence, what it means, how to fix, working example, then triage. Concretely, move the FindingFeedback block (:815-822) and the RemediationControl block (:824-832) to sit after the Working example section at :888-926 and before the references footer at :928. Keep the AI verdict banner (:789-813) where it is, since it changes how you read the evidence. To keep triage one click away without keeping it at the top, add a compact status pill to the header row at :729-763 showing the current remediation status and scrolling to the control when clicked, using the pill idiom at design-language.md D3.

findings.title: The DNS and port panels are the only entry points to their own on-demand fetch endpoints, but both return null when the data is missing, so a scan run without the port-scan option can never have one added
findings.description:
Port scanning is opt-in at scan time: lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:330-333 only starts the sweep when the `portScan` flag is set, and :841 spreads `portScan` into the result only when a result exists. DNS is the same shape, :767-769 reads a per-host cache and :838 spreads `dnsRecords` only when it is populated, so a cold cache means no records on the scan.

Both panels bail out when the field is absent: components/scanner/port-scan-panel.tsx:104 is `if (!portScan) return null;` and components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:187 is `if (!records || groups.length === 0) return null;`. The refresh control lives inside those panels (port-scan-panel.tsx:76-99, dns-records-panel.tsx:120-140), so it disappears with them.

The endpoints behind those controls have no such precondition. app/api/v3/history/[id]/ports/route.ts:87-104 checks ownership, resolves the hostname, runs the sweep and merges the result into result_meta whether or not one was there before; the DNS route at app/api/v3/history/[id]/dns/route.ts:72-74 does the same. The prop doc in scan-result-detail.tsx:62 even describes the intent as `Owner only: enables the DNS + port on-demand fetch/refresh controls`, but on-demand fetch is unreachable: the control can only ever refresh data that already exists.
findings.impact: A user who ran a scan without ticking the port-scan option, or whose DNS cache was cold, has no way to add that data to the saved scan. Their only recourse is running the whole scan again, which spends a daily quota slot and produces a second history row for the same host, polluting the aggregates described in qols-10. A working, owner-gated, rate-limited endpoint ships in the product and no user can reach it in the case it was built for.
findings.recommendation: Give both panels an empty state instead of returning null, on the owner's own surfaces only. In components/scanner/port-scan-panel.tsx, replace the `return null` at :104 with a guard that returns null only when `scanId` is undefined (the public /shared and /host views pass no refreshScanId), and otherwise renders the same collapsed header row with the headline `Not scanned` and the existing refresh button relabelled `Run port sweep`. Apply the identical change to components/scanner/dns-records-panel.tsx:187, labelled `Fetch DNS records`. Both reuse the existing premium gate and upgrade-modal branches unchanged. Update the prop doc at scan-result-detail.tsx:62 to match what the control then actually does.

findings.title: Half of .github/labeler.yml uses an invented schema the labeler action silently ignores, so the step named "Apply size label" has never applied a size label
findings.description: actions/labeler takes the label name as the top-level key and accepts only `changed-files`, `base-branch`, `head-branch`, `any` and `all` as matcher keys. .github/labeler.yml gets this right for four blocks (`ci` line 24, `config` line 29, `security` line 35, `docs` line 39) and wrong for the other two. The `size` block (lines 3-16) has a top-level key `size` whose entries are `{label: "size/xs", files: [...]}`, and the `dependencies` block (lines 18-21) uses `{label: "dependencies", from-branch: [...]}`. `label`, `files` and `from-branch` are not matcher keys. I confirmed against the action's source (src/api/get-label-configs.ts): an unrecognised key is not an error, it hits `core.info(\`An unknown config option was under ${label}: ${key}\`)` and produces no matcher, so the labels `size`, `size/xs`, `size/s`, `size/m`, `size/l` and the branch-based `dependencies` rule are never applied. The step at .github/workflows/label.yml:16 is literally named "Apply size label". Separately, label.yml:7-8 declares `permissions: pull-requests: write` only; declaring any permission sets every unlisted scope to `none`, including `contents`, while the action's documented usage requires `contents: read` to read the configuration file from the repository.
findings.impact: PR triage silently does not work. Maintainers see no size labels, and the `dependencies` label the stale.yml exemption logic and the auto-merge ignore flow both reason about is never applied from the branch name (dependabot supplies it from .github/dependabot.yml:12-14 instead, which masks the breakage). Nothing in the log makes this visible except an `info`-level line nobody reads.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the `size` and `dependencies` blocks in .github/labeler.yml to the real schema: one top-level key per label (`size/xs:`, `size/s:`, ...) with `- changed-files: - any-glob-to-any-file: [...]`, and `dependencies: - head-branch: ["^dependabot/"]`. Note that labeler matches on paths, not diff size, so if a real size label is wanted use a line-count action instead. Add `contents: read` to the permissions block in .github/workflows/label.yml:7.

findings.title: Any tag matching `v*`, including a release candidate or an old-line backport, overwrites `:latest` and is published as the newest release that every self-hosted updater offers
findings.description: docker-publish.yml triggers on `push: tags: v*` (lines 5-6) and unconditionally tags and pushes `$IMAGE:latest` alongside `$IMAGE:${VERSION}` (lines 51 and 54), with no check that the tag is newer than the current `latest` and no prerelease detection. release.yml:289-292 then runs `gh release create` with no `--prerelease` flag, so the GitHub release is a normal one. app/api/version/route.ts:12 fetches VERSION_CHECK_URL, which is `/releases/latest`, and passes the tag to `compareVersions`. lib/updater/version-compare.ts:29 splits on `.` and maps `Number`, so `"3.8.0-rc.1"` becomes `[3, 8, NaN, 1]` and line 45's `latestParts[i] || 0` turns the NaN into 0, making the release compare exactly equal to 3.8.0. The repository already has tags of this shape: `v1.9.4-patch.1`, `v1.9.5-patch.1`, `v2.1.0-patch.1` are in both `git tag` and the live GHCR tag list. docker-publish.yml also declares no `concurrency`, so two tags pushed close together race on `:latest`.
findings.impact: Cutting a release candidate or a patch for an older line silently republishes it as `:latest` in GHCR and as the newest GitHub release. Every self-hosted instance's version banner then reports "behind" and the admin updater offers to apply it, so a backport of 3.6.x would be pushed to installs already running 3.7.x, and an RC would be offered to production self-hosters as a stable update. There is no way to publish a prerelease from this pipeline at all.
findings.recommendation: In docker-publish.yml, gate the `:latest` tag on the tag being a clean `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` and being the highest such tag (`git tag --sort=-v:refname | head -1`), and skip it otherwise. In release.yml:289, pass `--prerelease` when the tag contains a hyphen. Give docker-publish.yml a `concurrency: group: docker-publish` block. Fix compareVersions in lib/updater/version-compare.ts to strip and compare a prerelease suffix instead of coercing it to 0.
