Three parameterize the expiry from getSetting('EMAIL_2FA_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES'): app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-send/route.ts:74, app/api/v3/auth/login/route.ts:230, app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:421, each using `NOW() + ($4 * INTERVAL '1 minute')`. The fourth, sendDiscordEmail2FACode in lib/discord/discord-utils.ts:28-:31, writes `NOW() + INTERVAL '10 minutes'` as a literal inside the SQL string with no getSetting call anywhere in the file. It is live, not dead: app/api/v3/auth/discord/callback/route.ts:314 invokes it on the real Discord sign-in flow for any account with email 2FA enabled.
findings.impact: The admin panel's 'Email 2FA code expiry' control silently applies to three of four sign-in flows. Set it to 3 minutes to harden the deployment and a Discord sign-in still issues a 10-minute code, which is exactly the window the operator tried to close. Set it to 15 and a Discord user's code dies at 10 with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: In lib/discord/discord-utils.ts, read `await getSetting('EMAIL_2FA_CODE_EXPIRY_MINUTES')` and use the same `NOW() + ($4 * INTERVAL '1 minute')` parameterized form the other three sites use.

findings.title: The admin content table buckets the 0-10 danger score at 4 and 7 while the engine's tiers and the two other renderers use 5 and 8, so a 'safe' host shows amber and a 'caution' host shows red
findings.description: lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts's getDangerScore anchors the score to the safety tier: tierBase safe 0 / caution 5 / unsafe 8 (:312-:316) and tierCap safe 4 / caution 7 / unsafe 10 (:317-:321). So the bands are safe 0-4, caution 5-7, unsafe 8-10. Two renderers encode exactly that: components/host/danger-score-trend-utils.ts:19-:23 (`score >= 8` critical, `score >= 5` medium, else success), covered by tests/components/host/danger-score-trend.test.ts:30-:41 which assert 4 is success and 7 is medium; and extension/src/lib/badge.ts:27, whose doc comment at :18-:24 records that an earlier extra yellow band at 3-4 was removed precisely because it disagreed with the tier. components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:367-:371 reimplements the buckets inline as `danger_score >= 7` destructive, `danger_score >= 4` severity-medium, else muted. A score of 4 (top of the safe band) renders amber and a score of 7 (top of the caution band) renders red.
findings.impact: The admin Public Scans table disagrees with the host trend chart, the browser extension badge, and the engine's own verdict on the same number for the same host. An admin triaging the public-scan corpus by colour is looking at two off-by-one bands, and the regression the extension explicitly documented fixing is live again in the admin panel.
findings.recommendation: Promote tierColorForScore out of components/host/danger-score-trend-utils.ts into a shared module (it has no host-page dependency) and call it from components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:367 instead of the inline ternary. Better still, export the two boundaries from lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts so the engine, the two web renderers and extension/src/lib/badge.ts all read one pair of numbers.

findings.title: Both user-visible scoring engines, the safety verdict and the SSL letter grade, are built entirely from unnamed literals with zero registry entries, so the false-positive rate is untunable
findings.description: getSafetyRating decides safe/caution/unsafe from four bare comparisons: criticalExploitWeight >= 1 (:260), highExploitWeight >= 2 (:264), mediumExploitWeight >= 3 (:276), highHardeningWeight >= 5 (:282). getDangerScore adds SEVERITY_WEIGHTS critical 4 / high 2 / medium 1 / low 0.3 / info 0.05 (:298-:304), the tierBase and tierCap tables (:312-:321), a fallback weight of 0.1 (:327), and the multipliers 1.5 exploitable / 0.15 hardening / 0.05 other (:335-:337). getEngineConfidence adds a base of 97, a 94 timed-out variant (:368), a per-severity averaging table (:373-:379), a default confidence of 85 for a finding that carries none (:385), and a 0.3/0.7 blend with a floor of 50 (:392-:394). lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts is the same story: deductions of 55, 70, 40, 20, 10 and 5, bonuses of 3, and the letter cutoffs 95/80/65/50/35 at :231-:236. A grep of lib/config/registry.ts for 'safety', 'danger' or 'confidence' returns only the three ADAPTIVE_CONFIDENCE / ENGINE_FEEDBACK entries (registry.ts:2731-2751), none of which touch any of the numbers above. The per-check static confidence values are equally scattered as literals across roughly 40 files (lib/scanner/checks/page-checks/links.ts:124 confidence 45, disclosure.ts:135 confidence 55, framework-fingerprint.ts:111 confidence 92, and so on).
findings.impact: An operator running VulnRadar against a fleet where five missing hardening headers is normal has no way to stop every host being labelled 'caution'; the only lever the admin panel offers is turning adaptive confidence on or off. A security team that wants a stricter or looser bar has to fork lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts, which puts them off the upgrade path for a scanner whose whole value is the checks it ships.
findings.recommendation: Name and export the four getSafetyRating comparison thresholds and the two ssl-grade letter tables as CONFIG_ constants in lib/config/config-values.ts and register them in lib/config/registry.ts under the existing scanner section, the same way SCANNER_THREAT_INTEL_API_TIMEOUT_MS and ENGINE_FEEDBACK_NOISE_THRESHOLD_PERCENT already are. The scoring weights themselves can stay as named constants without registry entries; the tier boundaries are the ones an operator actually needs.

findings.title: Four security-relevant rate limits are inline numeric literals that never reach the admin registry, unlike the seventeen that do
findings.description: lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:247-:276 exposes seventeen named rate limits, each carrying a `limit` name so checkRateLimit resolves the live admin override (registry keys RATE_LIMIT_*_MAX_ATTEMPTS / _WINDOW_MINUTES). Four call sites bypass that entirely by passing raw numbers: app/api/v3/auth/forgot-password/route.ts:49-:53 (per-email reset cap, maxAttempts 3 / windowSeconds 60*60), app/api/v3/auth/signup/route.ts:130-:134 (per-email signup cap, 5 / 60*60), app/api/v3/domains/route.ts:69-:73 (domain add, 20 / 3600) and app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:39-:42 (domain verify, 30 / 3600). None of the four has a registry key. This is distinct from AUDIT-009#dup-01, which was about routes importing the wrong RATE_LIMITS export; lib/config/constants.ts:352-:360 records that collision as resolved. These four never reference either export.
findings.impact: An operator responding to a signup-flood or reset-flood incident can tighten every limiter in the admin panel and still leave the two per-email counters, which are the ones that actually stop the attack described in each site's own comment, at their compiled values. The two domain limiters are the documented numbers in app/docs/api/page.tsx:843 and :876, so the docs also become uneditable truth.
findings.recommendation: Add four entries to RATE_LIMIT_DEFAULTS and RATE_LIMITS (forgotPasswordEmail, signupEmail, domainAdd, domainVerify) in lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts with matching registry keys, then spread them at the four call sites the way every other limiter does.

findings.title: The CLI's default 300-second timeout is the single-scan budget, so `vulnradar scan --crawl` in CI exits 1 as 'Timed out' on a crawl the server still has 600 seconds left to finish
findings.description: cli/lib.mjs:5-:14 declares DEFAULTS with `timeout: 300` and `crawl: false`. cli/vulnradar.mjs:64 turns that into `const deadline = Date.now() + opts.timeout * 1000` and the poll loop at :65-:85 gives up at the deadline, printing 'Timed out after 300s waiting for scan ${scanId}.' at :88-:90 and calling process.exit(1) at :91. Server-side, 300 is exactly CONFIG_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS (lib/config/config-values.ts:544) for a single-URL scan, but a crawl runs under CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 900 (:551), enforced by the crawl watchdog at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:361-:364. The CLI passes --crawl through but never adjusts its own deadline, and neither cli/lib.mjs:130 ('Give up waiting for the scan (default 300)') nor app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 and :154 warns that --crawl needs a larger --timeout.
findings.impact: A CI job that runs `vulnradar scan --crawl` against a site of any size fails red on a scan that is still running and will complete successfully. The user sees a timeout error, the pipeline blocks the merge, and the scan quietly finishes and lands in history a few minutes later, which reads as the tool being unreliable rather than as a default being wrong.
findings.recommendation: In cli/lib.mjs, make the effective default conditional on the crawl flag (300 for a single scan, 900 for --crawl) while still honouring an explicit --timeout, and say so in the --timeout help text at :130 and in app/docs/cli/page.tsx's flag table.

findings.title: FEATURE_API_KEYS gates only key creation, so turning the feature off leaves every previously issued key authenticating against the whole API
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-011#drift-09, which enumerated the half-gated flags as PDF_REPORTS, SCHEDULED_SCANS, WEBHOOKS and TEAMS but did not cover FEATURE_API_KEYS. A whole-repo grep for the string 'FEATURE_API_KEYS' outside lib/config returns exactly one hit: app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:38, inside the POST handler only. GET at :26-:32 lists keys ungated, and more importantly the authentication path never consults the flag at all: lib/api/api-keys.ts validates and rate-limits keys with no getSetting reference to it, so every route reached through the API-key auth path (scan, scan/bulk, scan/crawl, history, domains and the rest) continues to accept an existing key after the operator turns the feature off. The registry help at lib/config/registry.ts:673-:680 presents the flag as an on/off switch for the feature.
findings.impact: An operator disabling API keys, which is the action you take when a key may have leaked or when you are locking a self-hosted deployment down to browser sessions only, closes the door on issuing new keys and leaves every existing key fully functional. The admin panel reports the feature as off while it is still serving traffic.
findings.recommendation: Check FEATURE_API_KEYS inside the API-key validation function in lib/api/api-keys.ts (fail closed with the existing invalid-key response) rather than only at the creation endpoint, following the DOMAIN_REVERIFY_ENABLED pattern at lib/domains/reverify-worker.ts:59 that AUDIT-011#drift-09 identified as correct.

findings.title: Three documentation surfaces state crawl limits that match no value in the code, including a citation of a MAX_PAGES constant the named file does not contain
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:364 reads 'Returns up to 20 URLs (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/discover/route.ts).' That route contains no identifier MAX_PAGES: it resolves getSettings(['CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES', ...]) at :73-:80 and passes it to discoverPages at :111. CONFIG_CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES is 500 (lib/config/config-values.ts:594), admin-editable at lib/config/registry.ts:1859, so the documented number is off by 25x and the pointer is dangling. app/docs/developers/page.tsx:69 repeats 'Discover up to 20 crawlable URLs'. Separately app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 ('Crawl and scan up to 15 pages instead of a single URL') and app/docs/developers/page.tsx:64 ('Deep-crawl and scan up to 15 pages') state 15, which matches nothing: the real per-request cap is the plan's page-selection limit, free 25 / core 50 / pro 100 / elite 250 (lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts:18-:23), min()'d against CONFIG_CRAWL_SCAN_MAX_PAGES = 500 (config-values.ts:603) at lib/scanner/execute-crawl-scan.ts:355-:358, and unbounded when billing is off (app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:256-:259). The runtime error text at app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:267 interpolates the real number correctly, so a user reading the docs and then hitting the API is told two different limits.
findings.impact: A developer sizing an integration against the published API docs plans for 20 discovered URLs and 15 crawled pages, and either under-uses a feature they are paying for (elite gets 250) or writes pagination logic for a cap that does not exist. The dangling MAX_PAGES citation also sends the next maintainer to a file that has not had that constant since crawl discovery moved to the settings registry.
findings.recommendation: In app/docs/api/page.tsx:364 replace the number and the citation with the setting name (CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES, default 500). In app/docs/cli/page.tsx:135 and app/docs/developers/page.tsx:64,:69 state the per-plan table from lib/billing/crawl-page-limits.ts rather than a single number, the way app/docs/api/page.tsx:196 already does for bulkScanUrls.

findings.title: The destructive Button renders white on hsl(0 91% 71%) at 2.75:1 in the default dark theme, so every delete and cancel confirmation is below AA
findings.description: components/ui/button.tsx:14-15 defines `destructive: "bg-destructive text-destructive-foreground"`. app/globals.css:238-239 sets the dark theme's `--destructive: 0 91% 71%` with `--destructive-foreground: 0 0% 100%`; computed contrast is 2.75:1. The light theme (:192-193, `0 84% 60%` with white) computes to 3.78:1. AA needs 4.5:1 for the button's text (h-10 text-sm, not large text) and 3:1 even as a UI component, so the dark value fails both. Dark is the default theme (app/layout.tsx:151 hardcodes className="dark", ThemeProvider defaultTheme="dark"). The same pair backs `--success: 142 70% 45%` with `--success-foreground: 0 0% 100%` (globals.css:261-262) at 2.32:1 dark and 3.35:1 light. Only `--warning` gets this right, pairing hsl(38 92% 50%) with a near-black foreground at 8.39:1 (:218-219), and the light --primary-foreground was already fixed the same way with the comment at globals.css:179-184 explaining exactly this reasoning.
findings.impact: The destructive variant is what confirms account deletion, scan deletion, team removal and subscription cancellation. Its label is the least readable text in the product for a low-vision user, on the one control where misreading it is most costly.
findings.recommendation: In app/globals.css set `--destructive-foreground` to a near-black in both blocks the way --warning-foreground already is (`0 0% 9%` gives ~8:1 on both destructive fills), or darken `--destructive` itself to about `0 72% 42%` and keep white. Apply the same treatment to --success/--success-foreground at :216-217 and :261-262.

findings.title: The AI chat textarea, the support-ticket reply box and four other user-facing inputs have only a placeholder, no accessible name
findings.description: A scan of all 144 Input/Textarea/input/textarea/select elements in app/, components/ and lib/ found these with no id + htmlFor pair, no aria-label and no wrapping <label>: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1541 (the AI assistant's message box, mounted on every page via ChatWidget in app/layout.tsx:190); components/contact/support-tickets.tsx:609 (the reply box on a support ticket, available on every tier); components/history/history-notes.tsx:82 (scan notes); components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:79 (rename a team); app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx:406 (request-body textarea, the sibling of AUDIT-011#docs-07's :514 which cited only the param inputs); components/admin/features/support-inbox.tsx:344 (staff reply). Each has a `placeholder` only, and a placeholder is not an accessible name: it is not exposed as the field's name by the accname algorithm when it is the sole source in several screen-reader/browser pairings, and it disappears the moment the user types. This is the same defect AUDIT-011#docs-07 filed against the playground, present on the general product surface rather than in docs. app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx:88-91 publishes "Form Labels: All form inputs have associated labels for clarity."
findings.impact: A screen-reader user who tabs into the AI support widget hears "edit, blank" with no indication of what the field is for, and the same on a support-ticket reply. Voice-control users cannot say "click <field name>" because there is no name to speak. The published claim is false on the product's own support channel.
findings.recommendation: Add `aria-label` where a visible label would crowd the layout (chat-widget.tsx:1541 `aria-label="Message ${BOT_NAME}"`, support-tickets.tsx:609 and support-inbox.tsx:344 `aria-label="Reply"`, team-detail-header.tsx:79 `aria-label="Team name"`), and give history-notes.tsx:82 a real `useId()`-backed `<label htmlFor>` since it already has a visible "Notes" heading to reuse.

findings.title: The AI chat has no live region, so streamed assistant replies are never announced, and its slash-command autocomplete carries no combobox ARIA
findings.description: components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx contains exactly one ARIA announcement hook in 1600+ lines: `role="alert"` at :444. The message list at :1417-1419 is a plain scrolling `<div ref={scrollRef} className="h-full overflow-y-auto ...">` with no `aria-live`, no `role="log"` and no `aria-busy`, and assistant text is streamed into it token by token. The slash-command autocomplete at :1496-1528 renders a bare `<div>` of `<button>`s: the textarea has no `role="combobox"`, `aria-expanded`, `aria-controls` or `aria-activedescendant`, the list has no `role="listbox"`, and the items have no `role="option"` or `aria-selected`. Arrow-key movement itself is implemented (handleKeyDown at :1071-1091 handles ArrowDown/ArrowUp/Enter/Tab/Escape and tracks cmdHighlight), so the widget is operable by keyboard, it just publishes none of that state. The rest of the product does use live regions correctly, which makes this an outlier: 45 `aria-live` and 63 `role="status"` occurrences elsewhere, including components/scanner/scanning-indicator.tsx:281 and :293-297 for scan progress.
findings.impact: A screen-reader user asks the AI assistant a question and hears nothing at all: the reply streams into a silent container, so they must manually hunt back through the transcript to discover an answer arrived. Typing "/" pops a suggestion list that is never announced, and moving through it with arrows changes a highlight the user is never told about, so a blind user can select a slash command only by luck.
findings.recommendation: Add `role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text"` to the scroll container at chat-widget.tsx:1419 (polite, so a stream does not interrupt continuously), and set `aria-busy={isStreaming}` on it. On the textarea at :1541 add `role="combobox" aria-expanded={cmdSuggestions.length > 0} aria-controls="chat-cmd-list" aria-activedescendant={...}`; give the list at :1497 `id="chat-cmd-list" role="listbox"` and each button `role="option" aria-selected={i === cmdHighlight}` plus a stable id.

findings.title: The post-scan AI choice modal declares aria-modal but never moves focus into itself, traps nothing, and ignores Escape
findings.description: components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx:34-44 renders a fixed full-screen overlay whose panel carries `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby={titleId}` and nothing else: no ref, no tabIndex, no focus move on mount, no Tab containment, and no Escape handler. It is rendered from app/dashboard/page.tsx:980 at the end of every scan that produced findings, and it is the gate between the scan finishing and the user seeing results (the only ways past it are the "Verify with AI" and "Skip, show the raw findings" buttons). The codebase already has the fix: lib/hooks/use-modal-a11y.ts provides role/aria-modal/aria-labelledby plus Escape, a Tab focus trap and focus save-and-restore, and eleven other hand-rolled modals use it (components/modals/tos-modal.tsx:164, components/shared/notification-center.tsx:106, components/scanner/crawl-url-selector.tsx:92, components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:113, components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:67, components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:57 and five more). components/docs/docs-mobile-nav.tsx:52-61 solves the same problem inline. ai-choice-modal.tsx is the one that got neither.
findings.impact: On the main scan flow, a keyboard user's focus stays on whatever triggered the scan while a dialog that claims aria-modal="true" covers the page; they must Tab blindly forward, past the still-focusable page underneath, to find the two buttons. Escape does not dismiss it. Announcing aria-modal while leaving focus outside the dialog is worse than not declaring it, because assistive tech constrains the user to a subtree their focus is not in.
findings.recommendation: In components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx, call `useModalA11y({ open: true, onClose: onViewNow })` inside Shell and spread `dialogProps` onto the panel div at :36 and `titleProps` onto each `<h2 id={titleId}>`. That is a five-line change and reuses the hook the other eleven modals already share.

findings.title: The admin panel repeats the unlabeled-input pattern from AUDIT-011#docs-07 twenty times, including a bare select
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-011#docs-07, which filed the same defect only against app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx. The identical shape (a `<label>` with no `htmlFor` sitting above an `<Input>`/`<Textarea>`/`<select>` with no `id`) recurs across the admin surface: components/admin/features/mass-email-manager.tsx:291/295, :303/307, :316/320 (a `<select>` for the recipient segment), :332/337; components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:558/563, :602, :618; components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:864, :875, :903; components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:952, :991, :1413, :1428, :1490, :1724, :1780, :2187, :2196; components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:144 (a `datetime-local` field). Verified as genuinely unlabeled rather than implicitly wrapped: the checkboxes at engine-feedback-manager.tsx:346, :530, :915 and the cancel radios at profile-billing-tab.tsx:1572, :1603 ARE inside a `<label>` element and are fine, so the pattern was checked both ways.
findings.impact: A staff member using a screen reader hears a run of unnamed edit fields on the mass-email composer, the IP block-rule form and the user detail panel. Mass-email in particular has four unnamed controls in a row, one of which chooses who receives the blast, so an unnamed select decides whether an email goes to one person or every registered user. Admin is lower traffic than the scan flow, hence medium and not high.
findings.recommendation: Thread `useId()` through each block: `const id = useId()` then `<label htmlFor={id}>` / `id={id}` on the control. The user-facing forms already do this correctly (components/auth/login-form.tsx:121-123, components/teams/team-invite-form.tsx:88-90, components/contact/contact-form.tsx:201-208), so copy that shape.

findings.title: text-muted-foreground drops to 3.93:1 on bg-muted in light mode and 4.25:1 in dark, and the /40 through /70 opacity variants reach 1.67:1
findings.description: app/globals.css:189 sets light `--muted-foreground: 220 10% 42%` and :235 sets dark `220 8% 55%`. Computed ratios: light on --background 4.44:1 (just under the 4.5:1 AA floor), on --muted 3.93:1, on --secondary 4.13:1, on --accent 3.54:1; dark on --muted 4.25:1, on --accent 3.43:1, on --surface-3 4.32:1. `bg-muted` and `text-muted-foreground` appear together on the same element 119 times across app/ + components/. The same token is the placeholder colour for every field (components/ui/input.tsx:11 and components/ui/textarea.tsx:12 both set `placeholder:text-muted-foreground`), so light-mode placeholder text sits at 4.44:1 against the field's bg-background. Opacity variants make it far worse where they are used as real text: muted-foreground/70 computes to 2.63:1 on the light background and 3.26:1 on the dark one, /60 to 2.24:1 and 2.70:1, /50 to 1.93:1 and 2.23:1, /40 to 1.67:1 and 1.84:1 (components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1521 renders slash-command descriptions at text-muted-foreground/70, and the widget's own placeholder at /40).
findings.impact: Secondary text is the bulk of the copy in this UI: table meta, timestamps, hint lines under fields, empty-state prose, placeholder text. All of it sits at or under the AA floor on the muted and accent surfaces in both themes, and the opacity variants used for hints and descriptions are unreadable for low-vision users at under 2:1.
findings.recommendation: Darken light `--muted-foreground` to about `220 12% 35%` (≈6.3:1 on --background, ≈5.6:1 on --muted) and lighten dark to about `220 8% 65%` (≈6.4:1 on --muted) in app/globals.css:189 and :235. Then replace the /40, /50, /60 and /70 variants used for real text with the solid token; keep the opacity variants only for decorative glyphs that already carry an aria-hidden.

findings.title: The history scan-detail error state is unreachable: a failed detail load nulls the selected id, so the user is bounced back to the list with no message while the URL still says ?scan=
findings.description: app/history/page.tsx:556-570 contains a designed error state for the detail view: "This scan could not be loaded. It may have been deleted or fallen outside your retention window." plus a "Back to history" button. It is gated on `selectedScanId !== null && !detailLoading && !scanDetail` (the outer branch at :447 requires a non-null selectedScanId). loadScanDetail is the only thing that can produce that combination, and it never does: on a non-ok response it runs `setSelectedScanId(null); return;` at :131-134, and in its catch it runs `if (!isStale()) setSelectedScanId(null)` at :147-148. Both paths force the outer branch at :447 to false, so the list view renders instead and the error block is dead code on every failure path. scanDetail is only ever set from `mapHistoryDetailResponse(data)` (:137), which always returns an object, so there is no other route to it. Two further consequences of the same two lines: the URL is not cleaned (updateUrlWithScan is not called), so the address bar still reads ?scan=<id> while the list is on screen, and a reload silently repeats the bounce; and scanDetail is not cleared at the start of loadScanDetail, so a failed switch from scan A to scan B leaves A's data in state under a list view.
findings.impact: Clicking a scan that has been deleted, has aged out of retention, or hits a 500 does nothing visible: the row click appears to be ignored, then the page is back where it started. The user has no way to tell whether they misclicked, whether the scan is gone, or whether the server is broken. Deep links shared between teammates (/history?scan=abc) fail the same way, landing on a generic list rather than saying the link is dead, which is the one case where the message at :556 would have been exactly right.
findings.recommendation: Add a `detailError: string | null` state to app/history/page.tsx. In loadScanDetail, replace the `setSelectedScanId(null)` at :132 and :148 with `setDetailError(res.status === 404 ? "deleted or outside your retention window" : "couldn't be loaded")`, keeping selectedScanId set so the existing block at :556-570 renders. Add `setScanDetail(null)` at the top of loadScanDetail beside the existing `setCrawlInfo(null)` at :127 so a failed switch cannot leave the previous scan in state. Have the "Back to history" button at :562 call handleBackToList, which already clears ?scan= via updateUrlWithScan(null). Distinguish the two cases in the copy: 404 gets the retention sentence, 5xx gets a Retry button that recalls loadScanDetail.

findings.title: A failed team-members fetch renders "Members 0" over a blank list, "0 members, Your role: " with the role blank, and silently strips every management control from the owner
findings.description: app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 (`refreshMembers`) fetches GET /api/v3/teams/members and only acts inside `if (res.ok)`. On a non-ok response or a thrown request, `members`, `invites` and `currentRole` all keep their prior values (on first open: `[]`, `[]` and `""` from :59), `membersLoading` goes false in the finally at :291, and no error is recorded anywhere. components/teams/team-members-list.tsx then renders the loaded branch: :58-63 prints the header "Members" with the count `members.length`, which is 0, and :182-190 falls to a `divide-y` container with nothing in it, because there is no empty branch at all. The role explainer at :181 is gated on `members.length > 0` so it vanishes too. Separately, `currentRole` staying "" makes `hasTeamPermission("", ...)` false everywhere, so components/teams/team-detail-header.tsx:59-60 hides the rename control and the Invite button, and :132 renders `Your role: ` with an empty span. A team always contains at least its owner, so `members.length === 0` is not a state the data can produce: it is reachable only through a failed fetch, which means the blank card is always a lie.
findings.impact: A team owner opening their own team during a backend blip is told the team has zero members, sees their own role as blank, and finds the Invite and Rename controls gone. The natural reading is that they were removed from their own team or that their permissions were revoked. There is no retry, no message, and nothing distinguishes it from a real permission change. The identical shape applies to `handleViewMemberScans` at :459-479, where a failed fetch renders a member's scan list as empty, which in a compliance context reads as "this person has run no scans".
findings.recommendation: In app/teams/page.tsx:280-293 add an else branch setting the existing `actionError` state, which already has a rendered destructive band at :515-525, with "Couldn't load this team's members. Nothing has changed, try again." and keep the previous members array rather than showing zero. In components/teams/team-members-list.tsx add an explicit branch for `!loading && members.length === 0` that renders an error block rather than a blank div, since that state is unreachable from real data. Do not set `currentRole` from a failed response; leave the header's role chip and its permission-gated controls in a pending state instead of silently resolving to viewer-level.

findings.title: The extension popup writes scanInProgress.startedAt but never reads it, so a service-worker termination mid-scan leaves the popup permanently on "Scanning..." with the Scan button disabled and no way back
findings.description: extension/src/background/service-worker.ts:520-524 writes `scanInProgress = { url, mode, startedAt: Date.now() }` before running the scan and clears it in a `finally` at :551. The popup reconciles against it at extension/src/popup/popup.ts:1086-1089: `if (tabUrl && storage.scanInProgress?.url === tabUrl) { state.isScanning = true; state.mode = ...; watchInProgressScan(tabUrl); }`. Only `.url` and `.mode` are read; `startedAt` is written and never consulted anywhere in extension/src (grep confirms three write-side references and no read). watchInProgressScan (:946-965) then subscribes to storage changes and waits for `scanInProgress` to go null, with no deadline of its own. If the background context dies before its `finally` runs, which an MV3 service worker does on browser restart, extension reload, extension update, or a worker crash, and can do on a long crawl (extension/src/lib/constants.ts:38 allows crawlTimeoutMs of 910 seconds while the poll loop at extension/src/lib/scan.ts:186-196 drives itself with plain fetch and setTimeout), the key is never cleared. Every subsequent popup open on that tab reads the stale key, sets isScanning true, and waits on an onChanged event that will never fire. extension/src/popup/components/scan-button.ts:82 disables the Scan button on `props.isScanning` and :99-101 replaces its label with a spinner and "Scanning...", and the mode toggle at :69/:79 is disabled too. There is no cancel control and no reset in the popup UI.
findings.impact: The extension becomes permanently unusable for that URL. The user sees a spinner that has been running since before their browser restarted, cannot start a new scan, and has no affordance to clear it: the only recoveries are navigating away from that site, or clearing extension storage from the browser's settings. Because the state is keyed on the URL, this hits exactly the site the user is trying to check.
findings.recommendation: In extension/src/popup/popup.ts:1086, treat the record as dead when `Date.now() - storage.scanInProgress.startedAt` exceeds the mode's own ceiling (VULNRADAR.scanTimeoutMs or crawlTimeoutMs from extension/src/lib/constants.ts, plus a small margin): clear the key, leave isScanning false, and set `state.error` to "That scan was interrupted and its result was lost. Run it again." so the existing error banner at :206-215 renders it. Give watchInProgressScan (:946) the same deadline as a setTimeout so a popup that opens just inside the window still recovers rather than waiting forever. Optionally have the service worker clear a stale `scanInProgress` on its own startup, which is the cheapest catch-all for the browser-restart case.

findings.title: The AI verify modal closes silently on every failure, throwing away the server's actionable "you are out of AI credits" message and leaving the user unable to tell whether verification ran
findings.description: app/dashboard/page.tsx:810-844 (`handleDeepScan`) runs when the user clicks the AI verification action in AiChoiceModal. Every non-success path collapses to the same statement: `else { setShowAiModal(false) }` at :833-835 when the body has no findings array, at :836-838 when the response is not ok, and at :839-841 in the catch. components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx has no error prop and no error branch (its props are findings, loading, aiSummary, onDeepScan, onViewNow, :20-25), so dismissing it is the only outcome available. app/api/v3/scan/verify/route.ts:144-147 returns `{ error: quota.message }` with status 429 when checkAiUsageQuota denies the request, and the same route rate-limits at :67-70; both messages name the exact reason and remedy, and both are discarded. The result is that clicking "Verify with AI" and clicking "View now" produce a pixel-identical outcome.
findings.impact: The user cannot distinguish "AI verification ran and confirmed nothing" from "you have no AI credits left" from "the AI provider is down", because all three dismiss the modal and show the plain result. The quota message is the product's own upsell path and it is thrown on the floor. On a self-host with no AI provider configured the button is offered (aiAvailableRef gating at :271-279 only checks configured/aiDisabled) and then does nothing visible, which reads as a broken build.
findings.recommendation: Add an `error?: string` prop to components/scanner/ai-choice-modal.tsx and a branch that renders it inside the existing Shell (:28-46) above the two buttons, keeping the modal open with "View now" as the way out. In app/dashboard/page.tsx:836, read `data.error` off the non-ok response and pass it through instead of calling setShowAiModal(false); for a 429 whose message mentions credits, route to the same PremiumUpgradeModal already wired at :972-977, which is what that path exists for. The catch at :839 should set a network-flavoured message rather than dismissing.

findings.title: A 500 or a dropped connection on the admin data route renders "Access Denied: you do not have administrator privileges", mislabelling a server fault as an authorization one
findings.description: app/admin/page.tsx:277-306 (`fetchData`) handles exactly one non-ok status: 403 at :287-294, which sets twoFactorLockout when the body carries `code: "2fa_required"` and then setForbidden(true). Every other status falls straight through to `const data = await res.json()` at :296 with no res.ok check. A 500 whose body is a JSON error envelope assigns `data.stats` and `data.users` as undefined; a 502 from a proxy returning HTML throws on the parse. Both land in the catch at :301-304, which does `setForbidden(true)`. resolveAdminGate (:896-901) then returns "deny" and the page renders the block at :903-962: a ShieldOff icon, the heading "Access Denied", the body "You do not have administrator privileges to access this panel", and a "Back to Scanner" button. Nothing on that screen mentions a server error, and there is no retry.
findings.impact: During an outage or a database problem, the operator who most needs to reach the admin panel is told their account lacks permission. That sends them to check roles, 2FA enforcement and session state, which is the wrong debugging path, and the screen offers no retry so they cannot even confirm it is transient without reloading. It also permanently hides the real error: nothing anywhere on the page or in the network tab explanation surfaces the status code.
findings.recommendation: In app/admin/page.tsx:277-306 add a third terminal state alongside forbidden and twoFactorLockout, for example `loadFailed`, set on any non-403 non-ok status and in the catch. Render it through the same centred layout as the deny block at :903-962 but with a ServerCrash icon, the heading "Couldn't load the admin panel", the status code shown in mono the way app/error.tsx:88-90 shows error.digest, and a Retry button calling fetchData. Reserve setForbidden strictly for a real 403. Also move the `await res.json()` at :296 behind a res.ok check with a `.catch(() => null)` so a non-JSON body does not decide the state.

findings.title: A failed notification fetch renders "All caught up! You're on top of everything", so a pending team invite that could not load reads as an empty inbox
findings.description: components/shared/notification-center.tsx:289-311 fetches /api/v3/notifications/active. Its catch at :305-308 does `console.error` only, and the finally at :308-310 sets loading false. Nothing sets an error state; there is no error state to set. The render at :483-504 is a three-way ladder: loading, then `count === 0`, then the list. A failed fetch leaves the notifications array untouched (empty on first load) and lands on the middle branch, which prints a Bell glyph, "All caught up!" and "You're on top of everything". The dropdown carries per-user actionable items, not just marketing banners: the same list renders team invites with Accept buttons at :506-540, so a failure hides an action the user needs to take behind a confident claim that there is nothing to take. The poll interval at :313-317 means it self-heals on the next tick, which bounds the exposure but does not remove it, and a persistent 500 or a revoked session keeps it wrong indefinitely.
findings.impact: A user who was invited to a team, or who has an unread staff notification, is told they have nothing waiting. Invites have expiry windows, so a missed one is a real loss rather than a cosmetic one. The copy compounds it by being maximally confident, and it is the only place in the product that uses an exclamation mark and a platitude, which is exactly the voice the project rules out.
findings.recommendation: Add an `error` state to components/shared/notification-center.tsx set in the catch at :305 and on a non-ok response, and render a fourth branch before the `count === 0` branch at :491: a muted line reading "Couldn't load notifications" with a small text button that recalls fetchNotifications. Keep the empty branch for a genuine empty response, and rewrite its copy in the house voice while you are in there: "Nothing waiting" with "Invites, scan alerts and staff notices land here." instead of "All caught up! / You're on top of everything".

findings.title: Both privacy controls in the scan actions menu fail silently: the publicly-listed toggle rolls back with no message and "Make private" leaves the label unchanged, so the user cannot tell what their scan's visibility is
findings.description: components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:309-328 (`toggleSharePubliclyListed`) is the only optimistic mutation in the codebase (`setSharePubliclyListed(next); // optimistic` at :313). Its rollback is correct in mechanics and silent in effect: `if (!res.ok) setSharePubliclyListed(previous)` at :323 and the same in the catch at :325, with nothing set anywhere that the UI could render. The switch animates on, then animates back, and that is the entire feedback. `togglePrivacy` at :330-348 is the sibling: on a non-ok response it simply does not call `onPrivacyChanged`, and its catch at :344-346 carries the comment "Silently fail, matching requestShare's existing behavior"; the menu item label at :589-596 is derived from `currentIsPublic`, so after the spinner stops it reads exactly as it did before the click. `requestShare` at :289-306 is the third: on a non-ok response the share modal simply never opens. AUDIT-011#form-01 filed the same class for five other handlers including this file's Delete action at :505, and named app/shares/page.tsx:100-121's separate copy of the publicly-listed toggle, but not these three.
findings.impact: These are visibility controls on security scan results. A user who turns off public listing, or switches a scan to private, and whose request fails, is left with no signal at all and a reasonable belief that the change took: an optimistic toggle that snaps back within a few hundred milliseconds is easy to miss entirely, and the privacy menu item gives no motion to miss. The scan stays publicly listed and reachable at /host/<hostname> and via any share link. A silently reverted privacy control is worse than one that refuses loudly, because the user stops checking.
findings.recommendation: Add a shared `actionError: string | null` to components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx, set it in the non-ok and catch branches of all three handlers (:289-306, :309-328, :330-348), and render it as an inline destructive line inside the menu, matching the pattern already used for githubError at :355-360. Copy: "Couldn't change this scan's visibility. It is still public." The state of a privacy control must never be changed on screen without server confirmation or an explicit failure message; if the optimistic update at :313 is kept, pair the rollback with the message rather than letting it be the only signal.

findings.title: The extension popup has no first-run empty state and repeats the web app's "no findings equals clean" conflation with "No vulnerabilities detected."
findings.description: Two gaps in the popup's state set. First, the history sections at extension/src/popup/popup.ts:216-247 are each wrapped in `siteHistory.length > 0 ? ... : null` and `otherHistory.length > 0 ? ... : null`, so a freshly installed extension renders only the connect pill, the scan button and the footer: nothing tells the user what the panel will contain once they scan, and nothing distinguishes "you have not scanned anything" from "the history fetch failed" (extension/src/lib/scan.ts's refreshHistoryFromServer is called at :1054 and its failure just yields an empty array). Second, the result panel's zero-findings branch at :415 renders the bare string "No vulnerabilities detected.", and :381 adds a green `badge clean` chip when `r.summary.total === 0`. That is the same unqualified all-clear as the web app's, on a surface whose ScanResult also carries the `incomplete` field described in state-01, which the popup likewise never reads.
findings.impact: A first-run user sees an almost blank panel and cannot tell whether the extension is working. On the result side, an extension popup is the fastest, most casual read of a scan in the product, which makes it the place where a false all-clear is most likely to be believed and acted on. The `clean` badge is a positive assertion rendered from an absence.
findings.recommendation: Add an else branch to the history block at extension/src/popup/popup.ts:216 that renders a short prompt in the existing `.section` styling: "No scans yet. Hit Scan this page and the result lands here, with a trend arrow once you scan the same site twice." Add a distinct branch for a failed history load so it does not share that copy. Change the zero-findings copy at :415 to "No findings from the checks that ran." and gate the `clean` badge at :381 on `!r.incomplete?.length`, rendering a warn-toned chip naming the branches that did not finish when it is non-empty, which is the same fix as state-01 on the smaller surface.

findings.title: The web surface ships zero screenshots of the application, and the five finished 533x333 store screenshots in extension/public/store are referenced by no page, route, or asset in the repo
findings.description: Grepping app/, components/, public/, lib/ and scripts/ for "store_" returns zero matches outside extension/public/store itself, so store_1.png through store_5.png are used only in the Chrome Web Store and AMO listings. public/ contains exactly six files (favicon.ico, favicon.png, favicon.svg, gitlab, og-image.png, og-image.svg) and no product imagery. components/landing/ and app/landing/ contain zero next/image imports, zero , and zero .png/.jpg/.webp references. What the landing page does show is genuinely good and should not be discarded: components/shared/response-readout.tsx renders a live request/response readout in the hero, and components/landing/landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 hand-builds a complete finding card in JSX with real evidence and a real Nginx and Express fix. So the gap is not "the output is never shown", the output is shown well. The gap is that nothing shows the application: the dashboard, the history list, the two-scan diff at /compare that components/landing/landing-features.tsx:34-36 leans on as its closing argument, or the extension that is live on two stores. The five unused PNGs are, per audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md section E3, one of the three strongest visual artefacts in the repo, with an established composition (alternating side, two-tone white and #60a5fa headline, mono footnote, real UI over a browser-chrome mock).
findings.impact: A security scanner's report is its product, and a visitor deciding between this and a commercial scanner has no way to see whether the application is a real product or a landing page with an API behind it. Trust for an unknown vendor with roughly 50 users is bought largely with evidence that the thing exists. Meanwhile finished, on-brand art that cost real design effort reaches only Chrome Web Store browsers and never the site.
findings.recommendation: Copy extension/public/store/*.png to public/store/ and add five specific images to the web surface. (1) A full completed report from /dashboard, placed as a full-bleed band directly after the hero, showing the verdict header, the SeverityDistribution bar from components/scanner/severity-badge.tsx:129-190, and the first four findings collapsed. This is the missing "the product exists" proof. (2) A real screenshot of IssueDetail expanded on hsts-missing, replacing the hand-built <article> at landing-sample-finding.tsx:59-107 while keeping its left column copy verbatim: the JSX version is a drawing of the product, the screenshot is the product. (3) The /compare two-scan diff, added as a small figure inside components/landing/landing-features.tsx's accent block, because "what makes the diff between Tuesday and Friday readable" (:34-36) is the one claim the page argues hardest and never shows. (4) store_1.png reused as-is on a new /extension marketing page and in app/docs/extension/page.tsx. (5) The dashboard scan form with the category selector open, next to landing-categories.tsx:30-32's claim that checks are gated to the URL types they apply to. Use next/image with explicit width and height, wrap each in a rounded-xl border border-border/60 to match the card grammar in design-language.md D1, and give each a real alt describing the finding shown, not "screenshot".

findings.title: The hero answers what the product does but never who it is for or why to pick it over the free header checkers, both of which are already written further down the page
findings.description: Read as a first-time visitor, the first screen is components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:70-121: H1 "Scan any website for security issues.", one lead paragraph at :76-81, two buttons at :83-104, and a four-item stat strip at :106-121. What: answered plainly and it is good for search intent. Why this one: half answered, the lead names determinism ("a finding ID that does not change between runs"), server-side origin ("from our servers, not your browser") and pasteable fixes, which are the three real differentiators. Who: not answered at all. "Any website" addresses everyone, and the audience is not named until components/landing/landing-use-cases.tsx, section six of nine. Why not the free alternatives: not answered. The nearest thing is the bare token ["GPL-3.0", "licensed"] in the stat strip at :62, which does not say that being open source means you can read the rule that fired. The material for both is already written elsewhere in the repo and is stronger than what the hero has: landing-use-cases.tsx:3-8 names developers precisely, and components/auth/auth-split-layout.tsx:105-107 carries "Paste a URL. Get findings, not a grade out of ten", which is the exact contrast against Security Headers and Mozilla Observatory that the hero is missing.
findings.impact: A visitor who is not already looking for a scanner cannot place the product in one read, and a visitor who is comparing it against a free header checker is given no reason to prefer it before they scroll. Both answers exist on the page but arrive after the point where most visitors have decided.
findings.recommendation: Keep the H1 at components/landing/landing-hero.tsx:70-74, it is honest and it matches the query. Replace the single lead paragraph at :76-81 with two, which also fixes the who and the why-not-the-free-ones in the same edit. First: "For the developer who wants to know whether what they just shipped has a hole in it, and for whoever is responsible for every domain the company owns, including the four nobody remembers. Paste a URL and the request goes out from our servers, not your browser: {checkCount} checks come back with the response evidence behind each one, a finding ID that does not change between runs, and a config snippet you can paste straight into Nginx, Caddy, Express, or Next.js." Second, in text-sm text-muted-foreground to keep the type hierarchy: "The free header checkers give you a letter grade and stop. This gives you the rule that fired, the bytes it fired on, and the fix. The whole engine is GPL-3.0 in the public repo, so you can read every check or run the lot yourself." Both are inside the existing max-w-xl text-pretty measure and neither uses an em dash. Pair this with the CTA reorder in mkt-01 so the first screen also offers an action that needs no account.

findings.title: The landing page tells visitors there is no browser extension while the extension is live on both the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons, and nothing outside /docs links to either listing
findings.description: app/landing/page.tsx:70-73 answers "Do I need to install anything?" with "No. Scans run from our servers against a URL you provide. There is no agent, no browser extension, and nothing to deploy alongside your application." That answer is also emitted as FAQPage structured data at :110. components/landing/landing-features.tsx:3-4 repeats it: "No agent, no browser extension, no sidecar container, no YAML." Both are factually wrong. lib/config/config-values.ts:144-150 holds a live Chrome Web Store URL and a live AMO URL, with the comment at :147-148 recording that Firefox AMO review passed on 2026-08-15. extension/README.md:110-111 lists both listings as live. The extension ships history per site, PDF/SARIF/Markdown/JSON export from the popup, scheduled scans and desktop notifications (extension/README.md:5-11). CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL are consumed in exactly two files: app/docs/extension/page.tsx:113,139 and components/seo/structured-data.tsx:78-79. So a search engine is told about both listings and a human on the landing page is told they do not exist. components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:20-28 has no extension link and components/scanner/footer.tsx's Product column (Scanner, History, Compare, Badges, Pricing) has none either.
findings.impact: A shipped, reviewed, published product on two stores is invisible to every visitor who does not open the docs tree, and the one place the landing page mentions it, it denies it. The extension is also the product's strongest low-friction hook, since it turns "go to a website and paste a URL" into "click the toolbar on the page you are already on", which is exactly the argument store_1.png makes.
findings.recommendation: Fix both denials and add one link. app/landing/page.tsx:70-73 answer becomes: "No. Scans run from our servers against a URL you provide, so there is nothing to deploy next to your application. If you would rather have the scanner in your toolbar, the browser extension is on the Chrome Web Store and Firefox Add-ons, and it is optional." components/landing/landing-features.tsx:3-4 becomes title "Nothing to install", desc "No agent, no sidecar container, no YAML. The scanner runs on our infrastructure against a URL you give it. The Chrome and Firefox extensions are optional and call the same API with your own key." Add { href: "/docs/extension", label: "Extension" } to navLinks() in components/landing/landing-nav.tsx:20-28, or add an Extension entry to the footer Product column at components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-107 linking CHROME_WEB_STORE_URL and FIREFOX_ADDON_URL directly. Consider a public /extension page carrying store_1.png through store_5.png (see mkt-04), which gives the two store listings a canonical web destination they currently do not have.

findings.title: CONFIG_APP_DESCRIPTION is generic SaaS boilerplate and it is the single most syndicated sentence in the product: meta description, OpenGraph, Twitter, PWA manifest, three JSON-LD blocks and llms.txt
findings.description: lib/config/config-values.ts:131-132 sets CONFIG_APP_DESCRIPTION to "Scan websites for security vulnerabilities. Get instant reports with severity ratings, actionable fix guidance, and team collaboration tools." Every clause is a claim a competitor could paste verbatim: "instant reports", "actionable fix guidance", "team collaboration tools". It states no mechanism, names nothing precisely, and contains the adjective-only benefit claim that audits/AUDIT-011/design-language.md's triage heuristic (section G) flags as the marker of generic copy. It is re-exported as APP_DESCRIPTION at lib/config/constants.ts:175 and consumed at app/layout.tsx:52 (root meta description, the fallback for any page that does not call pageMetadata), :71 (OpenGraph description), :88 (Twitter description), app/manifest.ts:20 (PWA manifest), components/seo/structured-data.tsx:93, :112 and :148 (three JSON-LD descriptions), and app/llms.txt/route.ts:55, where it is the opening sentence of the machine-readable map that answer engines read. It is therefore the sentence that represents the product in every search result, every Slack and Discord unfurl, and every AI answer, while the nine landing sections immediately below it are written to a completely different standard.
findings.impact: The one sentence that travels furthest is the weakest in the codebase. Search snippets, link previews and AI answers about VulnRadar describe a generic scanner with collaboration features rather than a deterministic open-source engine, which is the opposite of the positioning the landing page spends nine sections building.
findings.recommendation: Replace lib/config/config-values.ts:131-132 with: "Open-source web vulnerability scanner. Paste a URL and get ${GENERATED_CHECKS_LABEL} deterministic checks back, each with the response evidence behind it, a finding ID that does not change between runs, and the config line that fixes it." If the interpolation is awkward at that point in the module, hardcode the label and add the same regeneration note the file already carries at :6-12. That lands around 200 characters, so also confirm the meta-description truncation: if a 155-character variant is wanted for search specifically, use "Open-source web vulnerability scanner. Paste a URL, get deterministic checks back with the response evidence, a stable finding ID, and the config fix." and keep the longer form for OpenGraph and JSON-LD. Note this value is also admin-overridable (lib/config/registry.ts:351-354), so a production override may be masking the constant: check the live settings row before assuming the shipped default is what renders.

findings.title: Plan copy sells raw numbers and platitudes instead of what a user can do, and the checkout page advertises a 30 and 90 day scan history that no plan actually has
findings.description: lib/billing/catalog.ts descriptions are the copy that appears under each plan name at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:83-85: "For individuals exploring security scanning" (:103), "Support VulnRadar development + 100 scans/day" (:133), "For power users - 150 scans/day" (:166), "Maximum power - 500 scans/day" (:198). "For power users" and "Maximum power" are exactly the adjective-only benefit claims CLAUDE.md bans, and none of the four says what the extra scans let you do. The feature bullets are the same shape: "Full vulnerability detection", "Security headers analysis", "SSL/TLS checks", "API access" (:106-109) are category nouns with no consequence attached, and every one of them is true on every plan, so the free card spends four of its eight bullets on things that are not differentiators. Separately there is a factual error. CONFIG_BILLING_FREE_RETENTION through CONFIG_BILLING_ELITE_SUPPORTER_RETENTION are all -1, meaning unlimited (lib/config/config-values.ts:1209-1212), yet catalog.ts:110 still says "30-day scan history" and :137 says "90-day scan history". app/pricing/page.tsx:44 strips those strings with a /scan history/i filter, but app/checkout/[productId]/page.tsx:280 renders plan.features.slice(0, 5) with no filter, so the Core checkout page, the highest-intent page in the funnel, tells a buyer they are getting 90-day history when every plan including free already keeps everything. catalog.ts:170 then sells "Unlimited scan history" as a Pro upgrade over Core, which the free tier also has. Finally components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 renders a "Most picked" badge driven by the hardcoded `popular: libPlan.id === "pro_supporter"` at app/pricing/page.tsx:55, which is a claim about other customers' behaviour that is not measured from anything.
findings.impact: A visitor cannot tell what changes when they pay, because the cards restate the same nouns at four price points and the one concrete difference they do state, retention, is wrong on the checkout page and identical across plans in reality. The Pro card's headline upgrade is something the free tier already includes. "Most picked" is an unbacked social-proof claim on a product with roughly 50 users, which is the kind of thing that is cheap to remove and expensive if noticed.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the four descriptions in lib/billing/catalog.ts in terms of what the tier lets you do: free (:103) "25 scans a day. Enough to keep an eye on everything you personally ship." core_supporter (:133) "100 scans a day and two running at once, for someone watching more than one property." pro_supporter (:166) "150 scans a day, a team of three, and 5,000 API calls a day. Enough to gate a real pipeline." elite_supporter (:198) "500 scans a day, unlimited webhooks and schedules, teams of ten. For an agency or a portfolio." Rewrite the free bullets (:105-114) to "Every check on every plan, nothing held back behind a tier", "25 scans a day, one at a time", "Unlimited history, diff any two runs", "5 URLs per bulk call, 3 schedules, 1 webhook", "REST API and one bearer token", "PDF, JSON, SARIF and Markdown export". Delete the "30-day scan history" string at :110 and "90-day scan history" at :137 outright so getRetentionLabel in app/pricing/page.tsx:26-31 is the only source, which also repairs the checkout page without touching it, and drop "Unlimited scan history" from the Pro list at :170 since it is not an upgrade. Either replace the "Most picked" badge at components/pricing/pricing-cards.tsx:78-79 with a factual label such as "Recommended", or drive `popular` from a real distribution query.

findings.title: Every honest trust signal the project owns is unlinked from the marketing surface: the public scan directory, the comparison pages, the 754 check pages, the free tools, the security page and the committed audit history
findings.description: What exists and is verifiable: /public-scans, a directory of real scans users chose to publish (app/public-scans/page.tsx, public per lib/config/public-paths.ts); /alternatives, five honest comparison pages whose own copy commits to "No invented competitor prices, no disparagement" (app/alternatives/page.tsx:47-48); roughly 754 /checks pages, each a real rule with its own fix guide; /tools, two free tools; /security plus /.well-known/security.txt; SECURITY-POSTURE.md, a public self-hardening checklist that opens with "We ship a scanner that grades other people's domains, so our own domain has to pass its own checks"; a live dogfood badge in README.md:18 pointing at a permanent shared report of vulnradar.dev; fourteen self-audits committed in audits/ (verified tracked with git ls-files, not ignored); a changelog; GPL-3.0; "Telemetry: None"; two live store listings. What links to any of it from the marketing surface: grepping components/landing/, app/landing/ and components/scanner/footer.tsx for "/checks", "/public-scans", "PUBLIC_SCANS", "/alternatives" and "/tools" returns zero matches. /public-scans is linked only from components/scanner/header.tsx (the logged-in app header) and two docs pages. components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-107's Product column lists Scanner, History, Compare and Badges, of which Scanner and History both require a session, so a logged-out visitor's footer is mostly redirects to /login. components/landing/landing-categories.tsx renders all eighteen categories as a table with counts and blurbs and not one cell is a link, so the highest-authority page on the site sends no traffic and no link equity into the 754-page check surface it is describing.
findings.impact: For a security product from an unknown vendor, trust is the purchase. This project has an unusually strong honest-signal inventory for its size, including a committed audit history and a published self-hardening checklist, and a visitor is shown none of it. Separately, the roughly 780 SEO pages have no inbound link from the landing page, so the main organic surface is orphaned from the site's strongest page.
findings.recommendation: Do not invent social proof, surface what exists. (1) Make every category row in components/landing/landing-categories.tsx link to /checks/category/{key}, both in the sm:hidden card list at :42-79 and the table at :81-146, and add a "See all {total} checks" link to /checks beside the count at :34-39. That is eighteen internal links from the site's strongest page into the SEO surface, and it makes the section clickable proof rather than a static table. (2) Add a Resources footer entry for /public-scans labelled "Public scans" and one for /alternatives labelled "Compared to other scanners", and a Product entry for /tools labelled "Free tools", in components/scanner/footer.tsx:60-150. (3) Extend the FACTS <dl> in components/landing/landing-open-source.tsx:6-13 with two rows that are the strongest available and currently invisible: ["Our own last scan", "Public, permanent report"] linking the shared report README.md:18 already uses, and ["Self-audits", "14, committed in the repo"] linking audits/ on GitHub. Verify the shared-report link still resolves before publishing it. (4) Note the honest caveat: /public-scans is opt-in and its empty state (components/public-scans/public-scans-empty-state.tsx:9) says "No public scans yet", so check it has content before linking it from the landing page, and seed it by publishing the team's own scans first.

findings.title: The GitHub README is the project's real front page and it has no screenshot, buries the value in a centered div, and lists twenty features as nouns without consequences
findings.description: README.md is 174 lines. The value proposition is split across a centered <div> block at :1-10 ("Open-source web vulnerability scanner. Paste a URL, get a structured security report in under 3 seconds. No agent to install.") and a bolded paragraph at :12-17. That opening is decent and matches the landing voice, though it repeats the speed claim from mkt-02. What it does not have: any image other than a 96px favicon at :3, so a visitor who lands here from the GPL license, a Hacker News link or a dependency graph never sees the product; any badge other than the self-scan badge at :18, so there is no license, CI or release signal in the standard place a developer looks; and a Features list at :28-45 of twenty bullets that are mostly nouns ("Scheduled scans, bulk scanning, and webhooks", "Teams with role-based access", "CVSS 3.1 base scores computed for every finding") rather than the consequence-carrying copy the landing page uses. Two bullets do carry consequence and show what the rest could be: "Stable finding IDs, so results can be diffed between runs and gated in CI" (:30) and "Self-updating embed badge: generate it once, it always shows the latest scan" (:33). The Getting Started block at :53-57 does lead with "Try it without an account at /demo", which is the right instinct and is undercut by mkt-01, since that demo cannot scan the reader's site. Self-Hosting at :57-82 is covered by mkt-03.
findings.impact: For an open-source project the README is where a developer decides in about fifteen seconds whether to try it, and this one asks them to read three paragraphs and a twenty-item list with nothing to look at. Neither the report UI nor the extension nor the diff view is visible anywhere on the page.
findings.recommendation: Restructure the top forty lines. Keep the logo and the H1. Replace the two-part pitch at :5-17 with one paragraph: "Open-source web vulnerability scanner. Paste a URL and get 795+ deterministic checks back, each with the response evidence behind it, a finding ID that does not change between runs, and the config line that fixes it. GPL-3.0, self-hostable, no telemetry." Immediately under it put a screenshot of a completed report (docs/screenshot-report.png, the same asset as mkt-04 item 1) at full width, then a single line of links: "Try it with no account · Docs · Self-host · Changelog". Keep the dogfood badge at :18 and add a GPL-3.0 badge and the CI status badge beside it. Rewrite the Features list at :28-45 so each bullet names the consequence, on the model of :30, and cut it to the ten that actually differentiate rather than twenty that include "Two-factor authentication" and "Admin email delivery log", which belong in the docs. Drop the "under 3 seconds" clause at :8 until mkt-02 is resolved.

findings.title: The docs quickstart is API-first: step one is create an account and step two is generate an API key, so a curious reader is never shown the sixty-second path
findings.description: app/docs/page.tsx:35-59 defines quickStartSteps as: 1 create an account, 2 generate an API key, 3 POST to /api/v3/scan, 4 read the findings. That is the correct quickstart for someone who has already decided to integrate, and it is the wrong first screen for someone who arrived from search to find out what this is. The DocsHero at :115-127 does open with a good one-liner ("Paste a URL, get a ranked list of what is wrong with it and how to fix each one") and four real stats, so the "what is this" half is present, but there is no zero-friction action anywhere above the fold: /demo is not linked from the hero or the quickstart, and neither is the browser extension, although both are entries in DOCS_NAV further down. The docs are also the only place the extension is discoverable at all (see mkt-06), and app/docs/extension/page.tsx contradicts itself about that: the Firefox card at :123-146 carries a green "Live" badge and an Add to Firefox button pointing at the real AMO listing, and then the very next DocsSteps block at :150-157 tells the reader to load a temporary add-on via about:debugging "until the AMO listing is live". lib/config/config-values.ts:147-148 records that AMO review passed on 2026-08-15, so that step is stale.
findings.impact: A reader who lands on /docs from a search for "what is VulnRadar" or "open source vulnerability scanner" is handed a four-step API onboarding as the first actionable thing on the page, when a one-click scan exists. The extension page then gives contradictory install instructions on the same screen, which reads as an abandoned page and undercuts the two live store listings it is trying to send traffic to.
findings.recommendation: Insert a step zero in app/docs/page.tsx:35-59 and renumber: { step: 1, title: "Scan one URL", description: "Open the demo and scan a URL with no account at all. Everything below is the same engine with your own history and API key attached." } with a link to ROUTES.DEMO. Add two chip links beside the DocsHero stats at :115-127, one to /demo and one to /docs/extension, so the two no-setup paths are visible before the API. In app/docs/extension/page.tsx, delete the temporary-add-on step at :150-157 or move it under a separate "Build from source" heading with the stale "until the AMO listing is live" clause removed, so the Live badge and the instructions agree.

findings.title: A shared scan report has no per-report metadata or image: every share link is titled "Shared Scan Report", described with the site-wide app description, and carries the generic marketing OG card
findings.description: app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx:7 is the only metadata source for the route and it calls privatePageMetadata("Shared Scan Report", "/shared"). lib/seo/metadata.ts:130 expands that to pageMetadata with description = APP_DESCRIPTION (the generic site description), image = SEO_OG_IMAGE ("/og-image.png", the static marketing card), and canonical/og:url = APP_URL + "/shared", a path that has no route at all (there is no app/shared/page.tsx). app/host/[hostname]/layout.tsx:8 does the same with "Host Report" and "/host". Nothing per-report reaches the head. There is no opengraph-image.tsx anywhere in the repo and no use of next/og or ImageResponse (grepped across app/, components/, lib/, scripts/): zero dynamic social images exist. The data needed is already available server side by token: app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:30 selects sh.url, sh.summary, sh.findings_count and sh.scanned_at from scan_history by SHA-256 token hash, with the expiry and revocation gates already written. The page itself cannot supply it (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:1 is "use client" and fetches in useEffect), but the layout is a server component and can export generateMetadata({ params }). The rendering toolchain also already exists: public/og-image.svg is a 1200x630 template whose right-hand card is literally a mock scan result ("your-domain.com / RISK SCORE 2 of 10 / TOP FINDINGS"), and scripts/build-og-image.mjs rasterizes it with sharp.
findings.impact: The strongest visual asset the project owns (AUDIT-011 names the OG image one of its three best artifacts) is spent showing a fake domain and fake findings, while the real ones are one query away. A share of a genuine report previews identically to a share of the homepage, so nothing in the unfurl tells a reader that someone scanned a specific site and found specific problems. That is the entire viral mechanic of this product category, unused. Note the privacy math is favourable: whoever the unfurler is already holds the token, which grants the full report, so putting the hostname and severity counts in the head leaks nothing the link does not already grant.
findings.recommendation: Add `export async function generateMetadata({ params })` to app/shared/[token]/layout.tsx that hashes the token the same way app/api/v3/shared/[token]/route.ts:24 does, selects url, summary and scanned_at, and returns pageMetadata({ noIndex: true, title: `Security scan of ${hostname}`, description: `${critical} critical, ${high} high and ${medium} medium findings on ${hostname}, scanned ${date} by VulnRadar. Open the full report.`, image: `/shared/${token}/opengraph-image` }). Fall back to the current generic strings when the token misses, is expired, or is revoked, so an invalid link leaks nothing. Then add app/shared/[token]/opengraph-image.tsx using ImageResponse from next/og (bundled with next 15.5.23, no new dependency) at size 1200x630, laid out as the right-hand card of public/og-image.svg: hostname, risk score out of 10, and the top five finding titles with severity dots in the --severity-* colours. Do the same for app/host/[hostname]/. twitter.card is already "summary_large_image" via lib/seo/metadata.ts:116, so nothing else changes.

findings.title: The 36-character title clamp on /checks pages collapses 22 distinct check pages onto 8 identical titles, and puts an ellipsis in the title of 348 of the 749
findings.description: app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:69 builds the metadata title as `How to fix: ${clamp(check.title, 36)}`, using the local clamp() at line 38 which cuts at a word boundary and appends "...". The root template then appends " | VulnRadar". I ran the exact same clamp over all 749 non-disabled entries in lib/scanner/checks-data/*.json (the set getAllChecks() returns, lib/seo/checks-content.ts:127): 348 of 749 titles come out truncated with an ellipsis, and 8 title strings are produced by more than one check, covering 22 pages. The worst is "How to fix: Permissions-Policy... | VulnRadar", which is the title of five different pages: /checks/permissions-policy-publickey-credentials-get-blocked, -ambient-light-sensor-blocked, -picture-in-picture-blocked, -window-management-blocked and -attribution-reporting-blocked. "How to fix: Missing..." is the title of three (cross-origin-resource-policy-report-only-missing, coep-missing, xpcdp-missing). "How to fix: Hard-coded secret in source..." is the title of three. "How to fix: document.cookie write missing..." is the title of three. The same string is also the og:title and twitter:title (lib/seo/metadata.ts:73, 98, 117). 84 titles still exceed 60 characters after the clamp, so the clamp does not even achieve its stated goal on those.
findings.impact: Five URLs competing for the same title on a distinct long-tail query is the classic keyword-cannibalisation shape: Search Console reports them as duplicate titles, Google picks one and demotes or omits the rest, and the five specific Permissions-Policy directives a searcher typed are invisible. Beyond the collisions, an ellipsis in the title of 46 percent of the organic surface reads as broken to a human scanning results, and the part cut off is always the part that distinguishes the page ("ambient-light-sensor", "picture-in-picture") because the shared prefix comes first.
findings.recommendation: Replace the fixed 36-character head clamp at app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:69 with a tail-preserving builder. Drop the redundant local clamp() at lines 38-43 (it is a buggier copy of clampText in lib/seo/metadata.ts:19: it omits the `lastSpace > 0` guard, so a title with no space in the first N characters loses its last character instead of being hard-cut) and import clampText. Build the title as `${check.title} fix` and clamp the whole string to 48 so the suffix fits in 60, but when the clamped result is not unique across getAllChecks(), fall back to `${check.title}` truncated from the distinguishing end, or append the category label: "Permissions-Policy ambient-light-sensor allowed" is 47 characters and needs no truncation at all. A one-time uniqueness assertion in a test over getAllChecks() (there is no test for this today) stops the collision class from coming back when checks are added.

findings.title: 682 of the 749 /checks meta descriptions end mid-sentence in an ellipsis, because the template concatenates description plus riskImpact and then hard-clamps the result to 155 characters
findings.description: app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:72 builds the description as clamp(`${check.title} is a ${severity}-severity ${label} finding. ${check.description}${check.riskImpact}`), where the comment at lines 70-71 says riskImpact is appended so terse descriptions still fill the 150-character window. Running the same construction over all 749 checks: the median length is 153 and the maximum is 157, both effectively at the cap, and 682 of 749 end with "..." because the appended riskImpact almost always overflows. No two descriptions are identical (I checked: zero duplicate groups across all 749, and zero duplicates in the raw `description` field itself), so the thin-content risk the brief asks about is not duplication here. It is that nearly every snippet Google can show is a sentence cut in half. Example shape: "<title> is a high-severity content finding. <full description>. <first two thirds of the risk sentence>...".
findings.impact: Google shows the meta description verbatim when it matches the query. 91 percent of the organic surface therefore presents a snippet that stops mid-clause, which reads as a scraped or broken page and costs click-through on the pages the whole /checks investment exists to win. The information that was cut is the risk consequence, which is the part that would make someone click.
findings.recommendation: Change app/checks/[id]/page.tsx:72 to append riskImpact only when it fits whole. Compute `const base = `${check.title} is a ${check.severity}-severity ${label.toLowerCase()} finding. ${check.description}`;` then `const desc = check.riskImpact && (base.length + 1 + check.riskImpact.length) <= 155 ? `${base} ${check.riskImpact}` : base;` and pass clampText(desc) as a final safety net. Because the raw description field is already unique for all 749 checks, most pages will then end on a complete sentence with no ellipsis at all. For the checks whose base is itself over 155 (measure after the change), shorten the boilerplate lead-in from "X is a high-severity content finding." to "High-severity content finding." which buys back the title length.

findings.title: Nine of the twenty docs pages are fully indexable with their own metadata and JSON-LD but are missing from sitemap.xml, because the sitemap hand-lists docs routes while components/docs/docs-nav.ts is the real source of truth
findings.description: lib/seo/routes.ts:25 declares STATIC_PUBLIC_ROUTES, whose header comment claims a new public page "only has to be added once and cannot end up in the sitemap while being disallowed in robots.txt". It hand-lists 11 docs routes: /docs, /docs/api, /docs/api/playground, /docs/setup, /docs/extension, /docs/self-hosting, /docs/developers, /docs/architecture, /docs/webhooks, /docs/rate-limits, /docs/config. components/docs/docs-nav.ts:13 declares DOCS_NAV, which drives the sidebar, mobile drawer, breadcrumb and pager and contains 20 entries. The nine in DOCS_NAV but not in the sitemap are: /docs/scheduled-scans, /docs/triage, /docs/teams, /docs/sharing, /docs/account-security, /docs/github, /docs/ai, /docs/reports and /docs/cli. All nine have their own layout.tsx with pageMetadata (index:true, a real canonical, keywords) plus BreadcrumbList and TechArticle JSON-LD, so they are built to rank and then left out of the discovery file.
