findings.description: exportCompliance (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:276-280) calls generateComplianceReport and downloads the result as `text/markdown` with a `-compliance-<date>.md` filename. lib/reports/compliance-report.ts maps every finding onto PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and OWASP ASVS controls (via lib/reports/compliance-mappings.ts, 17 KB of mappings) and is genuinely substantial work, but the only output is a plain .md file. app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:37-42 offers the same four formats and compliance is likewise md-only there, while pdf is available for the standard report. The named audience for this report, in the module's own docblock (compliance-report.ts:14-18), is "an engineer or a GRC reviewer", and a GRC reviewer's tooling is documents, not .md files. The menu label is also "Compliance report" (:569) while every sibling entry says "Export as X", so the format is not signalled anywhere before the download lands.
findings.impact: The most enterprise-facing artifact in the product is the only one that arrives in a format its intended reader cannot open in the tool they use. A reviewer handed a .md file either opens it as plain text with the pipe tables unrendered, or asks the engineer to convert it, which is the friction this feature exists to remove.
findings.recommendation: Two steps, in order. First, cheap: change the menu label at components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:569 to "Export compliance crosswalk (Markdown)" so the format is honest before the click, matching the sibling labels. Second, add a PDF path: refactor lib/reports/pdf-report.ts so the layout primitives (addText, addLine, addRect, addTextRight, the page assembly at :435-513) become an exported `PdfBuilder`, then add lib/reports/compliance-pdf.ts that consumes the same ControlBucket structure compliance-report.ts already builds (:100-120) and renders it as a cover page naming the four frameworks and the disclaimer, one section per framework, and one table per control with its findings. Wire it as `format=compliance-pdf` in app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:37 and as a second menu entry. That refactor also pays for itself against dsnx-02, dsnx-09 and dsnx-10, since all three touch the same primitives.

findings.title: A completed scan pushes a history entry, so Back wipes the results and Forward then triggers a full document reload into /history
findings.description:
On completion, `updateUrlWithScan` calls `setQueryParams({ scan: String(id), mode: null, screenshot: null, port_scan: null, active_probes: null })` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:290-296 with no options object. lib/ui/url-state.ts:140-141 defaults to `pushState` when `opts.replace` is falsy, so finishing a scan pushes a new browser history entry.

The consequences chain. Pressing Back returns to the pre-scan URL, which fires `LOCATION_CHANGE_EVENT` through the bridge at url-state.ts:29-48, which runs `syncFromUrl` (page.tsx:305-330), which sees no `scan` param with `status === "done"` and clears `result`, `scanHistoryId`, `crawlInfo` and the rest (:309-319). The results are gone. Pressing Forward then returns to `?scan=<publicId>` with `status` now `"idle"`, so the same effect takes the other branch at :326-329 and runs `window.location.href = \`${ROUTES.HISTORY}?scan=...\``, a full document navigation into a different route.

By contrast the same helper is called with `{ replace: true }` for the clearing case at :298, so the intent to replace rather than push is already present in the file, just not on the completion path.
findings.impact: Back after a scan destroys the result the user is looking at, and Forward, the obvious undo, does not restore it: it reloads the whole application into the History page. Minor because the scan is saved and reachable, but it makes the browser's own controls behave unpredictably on the product's main flow.
findings.recommendation: Pass `{ replace: true }` at app/dashboard/page.tsx:290 so a finished scan replaces the launch URL rather than stacking on it. Back then leaves the dashboard entirely, which is what the user means. If the push is deliberate so that Back acts as "clear this result", then the Forward branch must be a soft navigation instead: replace `window.location.href` at :328 with `router.replace(...)` from `next/navigation`, which is worth doing regardless, since a full document load to reach a scan the user was just looking at is the slowest possible path on the page whose whole pitch is speed.

findings.title: Eleven distinct confirmation implementations exist, including two raw window.confirm calls in the extension and eight ad-hoc rebuilds of the same AlertDialog
findings.description: Eleven separate confirmation mechanisms are in use. Five are shared components: the Radix primitive components/ui/alert-dialog.tsx, rebuilt ad hoc with its own header, footer and state machine in eight places (app/shares/page.tsx:203, app/teams/page.tsx:648, app/history/page.tsx:640, components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:809, components/profile/tabs/developer/domains-section.tsx:479, components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:807, components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:260 and :826); components/admin/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx, a complete documented generic used only inside components/admin; components/admin/shared/admin-password-confirm-dialog.tsx; components/shared/save-confirmation-modal.tsx; and a plain components/ui/dialog.tsx pressed into service as a confirmation at components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx:1695. Six are bespoke one-offs: a hand-rolled overlay at components/profile/tabs/profile-billing-tab.tsx:1532, the inline danger-zone panel at components/profile/tabs/profile-privacy-tab.tsx:480, three inline expand-in-place password panels at components/profile/tabs/profile-security-tab.tsx:814, :911 and :1308, a nested inline confirm at components/admin/users/user-detail-panel.tsx:1576, a two-click "click again" pattern at components/admin/users/gift-subscription-modal.tsx:191, and raw window.confirm at extension/src/options/options.ts:199 and :1101, the only two in the codebase. Recorded here so the next audit does not re-derive it: the two most dangerous user-facing actions are correctly gated hardest, account deletion requiring both a typed DELETE and the current password (components/profile/tabs/profile-privacy-tab.tsx:502-537) and clear-history naming the exact scan count in its copy (app/history/page.tsx:659-664). Merged from qols-05, which additionally documents that the admin panel alone chooses between three different confirmation dialog components depending on the action.
findings.impact: Eight copies of one dialog is eight places to fix when the copy, busy behaviour or focus handling changes, and it is why some handle failure and others cannot: app/history/page.tsx:667-669 renders clearError inside the dialog, while components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:809 has nowhere to put an error, which is part of why qolf-04 exists. The extension's window.confirm renders unstyled OS chrome inside an otherwise themed options page.
findings.recommendation: Move components/admin/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx to components/shared/confirm-dialog.tsx unchanged, add an optional error slot rendered above the footer the way app/history/page.tsx:667-669 does, and replace the eight ad-hoc AlertDialog call sites with it. The confirm-action registry in components/profile/tabs/profile-developer-tab.tsx:85-118 and :431-453, one ConfirmAction union plus one getConfirmCopy function covering four destructive actions, is the right shape and should be the model for the teams and history call sites. Replace the two window.confirm calls in extension/src/options/options.ts with the extension's own dialog markup. Where qolf-09 introduces undo for an action, remove that action's confirmation at the same time rather than shipping both.

findings.title: The compare run fails silently, leaving the picker on screen with no explanation when a diff is rejected
findings.description: runCompare (app/compare/page.tsx:54-65) sets loading, fetches the compare endpoint with a and b, and does `if (res.ok) setDiffResult(data)` with no else, plus `catch { /* ignore */ }` at :61-63. setLoading(false) then runs at :64 either way. The same function is the deep-link handler at :79, so a stale or invalid ?a=&b= pair in a bookmarked URL takes the same path.
findings.impact: Pressing Compare on two scans the server refuses to diff (different hosts, a scan deleted since the list loaded, a permissions failure) stops the spinner and returns the user to the same picker with both scans still selected and no message, so the only available conclusion is that the button is broken. A shared /compare?a=..&b=.. link whose scans have aged out of retention behaves identically.
findings.recommendation: Add an error state to app/compare/page.tsx, set it from data.error in an !res.ok branch and from the catch, and render it above the Compare button at :275-292 using the same destructive-tinted box the rest of the app uses. For the deep-link path at :78-82, distinguish "these two scans cannot be compared" from "one of these scans no longer exists" and offer handleReset (:200) as the recovery action.

findings.title: Disconnecting an OAuth provider sets a success message and then immediately reloads the page, so the confirmation is dead code the user never sees
findings.description: components/profile/tabs/profile-social-tab.tsx:129-131 calls setSuccess with a disconnect confirmation and then window.location.reload() on the next line, so the banner at app/profile/page.tsx:688 is never painted before the document is torn down. The Discord disconnect at :555-558 is identical and additionally discards the server's message on failure at :560 in favour of a generic string, the only place on this tab that does. The user's only feedback for a successful disconnect is a full page refresh.
findings.impact: Disconnecting a sign-in provider is a security-relevant change with no confirmation that it happened. On a slow connection the refresh reads as an unexplained page reset, and a user who is not sure whether it worked will try again.
findings.recommendation: Replace the reload with a targeted state update: the handler already knows which provider was removed, so drop it from the local connections list and call refreshAuthCache() from components/providers/auth-provider, the way components/shared/onboarding-tour.tsx:101 does after its own mutation. Then the success message survives. If a reload is genuinely required, move the message to the toast from qolf-07 with a sessionStorage handoff read after the reload. Also stop discarding data.error at :560.

findings.title: The teams member list has no search, sort or pagination and the selected team is not addressable by URL, so Back leaves the page entirely
findings.description: app/teams/page.tsx imports nothing from lib/ui/url-state, so no state on the page reaches the URL: selectedTeam (:56), searchQuery (:49), viewingMember (:89) and scanPage (:95) are all useState. Opening a team is openTeam (:296) mutating state in place with no history entry, so browser Back navigates off /teams entirely rather than returning to the team list, and a team cannot be linked or bookmarked. The member list rendered at :588-603 has no search, no role filter, no sort and no pagination, and pending invites are interleaved with members with no way to isolate them.
findings.impact: Sharing "the acme team page" with a colleague is impossible; the only shareable thing is /teams. Back behaving as leave-the-page is the kind of small wrongness users learn to work around by never using Back on that page. The member list is fine at five seats and unusable at fifty, which is the size at which a team feature starts to matter commercially.
findings.recommendation: Back selectedTeam with useQueryParam("team", "") from lib/ui/url-state.ts:170, the same hook app/repos/page.tsx:134 uses for ?repo, resolving the team from the loaded list on mount so a deep link works, and do the same for viewingMember. Add a name and email search plus a role filter above the member list, both URL-backed per qolf-10, and reuse the existing PaginationControl past roughly 20 members. Separately: there is no member role-change mutation in the UI at all, roles are set only at invite time (:70-72), so an owner who invites someone as a viewer must remove and re-invite them to promote them.

findings.title: The /attack-surface page lights no navigation item, so a top-level destination reads as being outside the app
findings.description: isNavActive at components/scanner/header.tsx:88-98 treats /public-scans and /assets as belonging to the History nav item, because both are tabs under components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx. That tab list has four entries (:8-13) and the fourth, ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE, is not in the header's check at :95-97. /attack-surface is also not in NAV_LINKS (:25-34), so navigating there leaves every nav item unlit.
findings.impact: The header stops telling the user where they are on one of the four pages reachable from the history tab strip, which is a small but real "did I leave the app" moment on a page that is otherwise a first-class destination with its own heading and description.
findings.recommendation: Add ROUTES.ATTACK_SURFACE to the disjunction at components/scanner/header.tsx:95-97 alongside PUBLIC_SCANS and ASSETS. Better, export the TABS array from components/history/history-view-tabs.tsx:8-13 and derive the check from it, so the next tab added there cannot desynchronise the header again.

findings.title: Nine admin tables skipped the mobile card alternate their five siblings ship, and two have no scroll container at all
findings.description: The house pattern is a hand-written mobile card list plus a desktop table, as in components/landing/landing-categories.tsx:42 and :81. Six admin surfaces follow it with a md:hidden card list: components/admin/teams/teams-list.tsx:327, components/admin/staff/staff-list.tsx:953, components/admin/audit/audit-log.tsx:350, components/admin/features/ip-rules-manager.tsx:704, components/admin/features/ai-chats-manager.tsx:281, and app/admin/page.tsx:1299 with its mobile list at :1497. Nine do not and rely on the overflow-auto in components/admin/shared/data-table.tsx:124-134 and components/ui/table.tsx:9 with no min-w, so columns compress rather than scrolling: components/admin/features/engine-feedback-manager.tsx:373 (nine columns), :557 and :680; components/admin/features/content-manager.tsx:333 and :422; components/admin/features/blocked-data-manager.tsx:562 and :834; and components/admin/features/billing-overview-manager.tsx:238 (six columns) and :305, which use a bare Table with no scroll area at all.
findings.impact: At 390px the nine-column engine-feedback table gives each column about 40px, so its text-[11px] uppercase tracking-wider headers wrap letter by letter and the rows are unreadable. Admin is staff-only so the user count is tiny, but on-call moderation from a phone is exactly when it gets used.
findings.recommendation: Give the nine a md:hidden card list matching what components/admin/teams/teams-list.tsx:327 already does, showing the two or three columns that identify the row plus its actions, and add hidden md:block to the existing table. Fix the two bare tables first by wrapping them in TableScrollArea, and give every TableScrollArea a min-w sized to its column count so the table scrolls cleanly instead of compressing.

findings.title: components/admin/config.ts still exports a five-entry tab table against the panel's twenty, and a 25-entry label map against the panel's inlined 31
findings.description: Extends AUDIT-013#dead-01 with the exact current counts, because the restructure in qols-01 has to fix this to avoid recreating it. ADMIN_TABS (components/admin/config.ts:7-17) lists users, teams, notifications, admins, audit. The live panel has 20, declared three times over in app/admin/page.tsx: VALID_TABS at :112-133, the ActiveTab union at :152-172, and NAV_GROUPS_RAW at :689-835. ACTION_LABELS (config.ts:262-288) holds 25 toast strings; the map the panel actually reads is inlined in handleAction at app/admin/page.tsx:530-562 and holds 31, the six extras being notify_account_changes, toggle_ai_ban, verify_email, unverify_email, send_notification and send_email. ACTION_META (config.ts:27-259) is a third list, 37 entries, and it is the only one of the three that is genuinely live: audit-log.tsx reads it for badge rendering.
findings.impact: The tab list has four declaration sites that must be edited together, and the toast-label map has two, so adding a destination or an action silently half-lands. That is the mechanism that produced the current 20-tab sprawl, and without fixing it the restructure will drift back the same way.
findings.recommendation: Replace ADMIN_TABS in components/admin/config.ts with a single `ADMIN_SECTIONS` array carrying key, label, icon, group and the permission or minHierarchy gate, moved verbatim out of NAV_GROUPS_RAW (app/admin/page.tsx:689-835). Derive VALID_TABS and the ActiveTab union from it with `(typeof ADMIN_SECTIONS)[number]["key"]`, so the three declarations become one. Delete the inlined label map at app/admin/page.tsx:530-562 and import ACTION_LABELS, after adding the six missing keys to it. Leave ACTION_META alone.

findings.title: Every daily-activity tooltip on the dashboard reports 0 issues, because the API hardcodes the field it renders
findings.description:
The dashboard's 14-day activity strip renders a tooltip per bar at components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:320-328, whose second line is `{d.scans} scans` followed by, when `d.scans > 0`, ` · ${d.issues} issues` (:324-325). `issues` comes from the API's dailyActivity mapping at app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:99-105, which builds each row as `{ day: row.day, scans: Number(row.scans) || 0, issues: 0 }`. The literal 0 at :102 is the only value that field ever takes; the underlying query at :63-77 selects only day and a scan count and never touches findings. The client's own normalisation at dashboard.tsx:244-248 preserves it as 0.

So every tooltip on a day with any activity reads `3 scans · 0 issues`, on an account whose Findings by severity panel two hundred pixels below shows hundreds of findings.
findings.impact: The tooltip states, for every active day, that the scans that day found nothing. It contradicts the rest of the page and it is the only per-day findings figure the product offers, so a user checking whether a bad week was actually bad is told no.
findings.recommendation: Either populate it or remove it. To populate: extend the weekly-activity query at app/api/v3/dashboard/route.ts:63-77 to also sum findings_count per day, `COALESCE(SUM(sh.findings_count), 0)::int as issues`, and pass `Number(row.issues) || 0` through the mapping at :102 instead of the literal. To remove: delete the `issues` field from the mapping and delete the conditional clause at components/scanner/dashboard.tsx:324-325. Populating is the better answer, since a per-day findings figure is one of the few things on that page that answers what changed since I was last here.

findings.title: The extendedPanels prop on ScanResultDetail and its entire alternate branch are dead, and its doc comment describes a caller that does not exist
findings.description:
`extendedPanels` is declared at components/scanner/scan-result-detail.tsx:53, defaulted to true at :96, and branched on at :150. Its doc comment at :50-56 states that the host-aggregate report sets it false because its data source only carries response headers. A repo-wide grep for extendedPanels across app/ and components/ returns three hits, all inside scan-result-detail.tsx itself. app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:272-288, the host-aggregate report the comment names, does not pass it. So the false branch at :211-218, which renders a response-headers-only version of the More about this host block, has never rendered.

Because the host report takes the true branch, it renders the full panel set. The panels that have no data return null on their own (threat-intel-panel.tsx:36, software-inventory-panel.tsx:35, dns-records-panel.tsx:187, port-scan-panel.tsx:104), which is why nothing looks broken and why the dead branch has gone unnoticed.
findings.impact: A reader of this file is told the host report behaves one way when it behaves another, which is the kind of stale comment that makes the next person reorder the panels wrongly. It is eight lines of unreachable JSX plus a prop that every caller must now reason about.
findings.recommendation: Delete the prop declaration at :53, the default at :96, the ternary at :150 and :211-218, and the doc comment at :50-56, leaving the extended block unconditional. Do this as part of the reorder in qols-08 so the file is touched once. If the response-headers-only variant is still wanted for the host report, make it real by passing `extendedPanels={false}` from app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:272 and keeping the branch; but nothing in the current host API response justifies it, since the panels already self-suppress.

findings.title: The SBOM covers only the Docker image, so the two browser-extension zips attached to the same release ship with no bill of materials at all
findings.description: docker-publish.yml:82-91 runs `anchore/sbom-action` with `image: ghcr.io/.../vulnradar:${{ github.ref_name }}`, so the CycloneDX SBOM describes only what is inside the server image. release.yml:117-148 separately builds the browser extension (`npm ci`, `build:chrome`, `build:firefox`) and attaches `vulnradar-chrome-vX.Y.Z.zip` and `vulnradar-firefox-vX.Y.Z.zip` to the same GitHub release; I confirmed against the live releases API that v3.6.0 through v3.7.2 each carry both zips plus one `.sbom.cdx.json`. The extension is a separate package with its own lockfile (194 packages per AUDIT-013#subdeps-02) and none of it appears in the image, so none of it appears in the SBOM. SECURITY.md:82-83 describes the SBOM as a "full software bill of materials" for the release without qualifying that it excludes the extension.
findings.impact: A downstream consumer running SBOM-based vulnerability scanning against the release believes they have covered everything VulnRadar ships. They have not covered the two artifacts that execute in an end user's browser with host permissions, and those are also the artifacts with no Dependabot monitoring (AUDIT-013#subdeps-02).
findings.recommendation: Add a second `anchore/sbom-action` invocation in release.yml after the extension build, pointed at `${RUNNER_TEMP}/extension-src/extension` with `path:` instead of `image:`, and attach it as `vulnradar-extension-vX.Y.Z.sbom.cdx.json`. Amend SECURITY.md:82 to name what each SBOM covers.

findings.title: release.yml swallows a failed SBOM download with continue-on-error and passes an empty run-id on the manual-publish path, so a release can ship without the SBOM SECURITY.md promises and nothing reports it
findings.description: release.yml:150-168 downloads the SBOM artifact and carries `continue-on-error: true` at line 168. Its `run-id` at line 164 is `${{ github.event.workflow_run.id }}`, which is empty on the `release: published` trigger declared at lines 46-48, so on the path SECURITY.md:105 documents as "Manual: create + publish the release first, then push the tag" the download cannot resolve a run and fails. The failure is then invisible: the next step's `shopt -s nullglob` at line 219 makes `*.cdx.json` expand to nothing, and "Build artifact list" at lines 253-255 only appends the SBOM `if [ -f ... ]`. So a release simply comes out one asset short with a green workflow. SECURITY.md:77-83 states that every tagged release is accompanied by a CycloneDX SBOM. I verified against the live releases API that v3.5.1 through v3.7.2 all do carry one today, because the later `workflow_run` run clobbers the assets, so this is a latent silent-degradation path rather than a current break: it materialises whenever docker-publish.yml itself fails (whereupon release.yml's `if` at lines 62-64 also skips the workflow_run path entirely).
findings.impact: A release that lost its SBOM looks identical to one that did not. The maintainer gets no signal, and a consumer verifying against SECURITY.md's list finds an asset missing with no explanation.
findings.recommendation: Drop `continue-on-error: true` at release.yml:168 and instead set a step output, then fail the "Build artifact list" step (or write a `::warning::` plus a `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` line) when the SBOM is absent. Default `run-id` to `${{ github.event.workflow_run.id || '' }}` guarded by an `if: github.event_name == 'workflow_run'` so the manual path does not attempt a download it cannot satisfy.

findings.title: sha256sums.txt is never signed, so on the documented cosign-absent path the updater's checksum check compares a tarball against a manifest fetched from the same host and adds no integrity guarantee
findings.description: release.yml:222 writes `sha256sums.txt` and lines 230-232 sign only the source tarball (`cosign sign-blob --bundle vulnradar-${TAG}.tar.gz.cert vulnradar-${TAG}.tar.gz`). Nothing signs the sums file. lib/updater/apply.ts:87 requires `sha256sums.txt` and treats a mismatch as a hard failure, while lib/updater/cosign.ts:44-51 returns `attempted: false` and does not fail when the cosign binary is missing, with the message "the release was still checksum-verified" and the module header asserting "checksum verification still runs and is a hard gate either way". On a host without cosign (bare Node, Pterodactyl-style panels, which that same header names as the common case) both the tarball and the unsigned sums file come from the same GitHub release, so an attacker who can alter release assets alters both and the check passes.
findings.impact: The updater's fallback integrity story is weaker than its own comments claim. Only self-hosters running the published Docker image are actually protected, because Dockerfile:59 and 84 bundle the cosign binary; everyone else gets a check that cannot detect a compromised release host or a compromised maintainer account.
findings.recommendation: Sign `sha256sums.txt` in release.yml alongside the tarball (`cosign sign-blob --bundle sha256sums.txt.cert sha256sums.txt`), attach the bundle, and have lib/updater/apply.ts verify that bundle before trusting the sums file. Reword the header in lib/updater/cosign.ts so it no longer describes the checksum path as an integrity gate when cosign is absent.

findings.title: CI runs a floating Node 22.x while the Dockerfile pins 22.11.0, so CI can pass on a runtime feature the published image does not have
findings.description: .nvmrc contains `22`, package.json declares `engines.node: ">=22.0.0"`, and ci.yml passes `node-version: "22"` at lines 33, 58, 89 (via 95-98), 127 and 189, all of which resolve to whatever the newest 22.x is on the runner at job time. Dockerfile:11 and 62 pin `node:22.11.0-alpine` for both the builder and the runner stage, and release.yml:115 also uses `node-version: "22"` for the extension build. Nothing reconciles the two. This is a different axis from AUDIT-013#deps-03 (base images being stale and not covered by a dependabot docker ecosystem) and AUDIT-013#subdeps-08 (cli/ declaring `>=18`): here the same Node major is used everywhere but the minor is pinned in one place and floating in the other.
findings.impact: A change relying on anything added after Node 22.11.0 typechecks, tests and builds green in CI and then throws at runtime inside the published image, with no CI job able to catch it. The gap is real: CI today runs a 22.x roughly a year newer than 22.11.0.
findings.recommendation: Replace `node-version: "22"` with `node-version-file: .nvmrc` in every setup-node step in ci.yml and release.yml, and put the exact pin (`22.11.0`) in .nvmrc so CI, the Dockerfile and local development all agree. Bump all three together.

findings.title: The prebuild knowledge compilers drop a bad source with a warning and still exit 0, and their only staleness guard is mtime-based so it can never fire in CI or a Docker build
findings.description: package.json's `prebuild` chains the four `scripts/compile-*-knowledge.mjs` scripts with `&&`, so a non-zero exit does fail `npm run build`. But each script only exits non-zero on total failure, never on partial failure. scripts/compile-legal-knowledge.mjs:269-272 warns "missing <path>, skipping" and `continue`s past a legal page that has moved, and only exits 1 if `totalSections === 0` across every page (lines 307-310). scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs:143-147 warns and skips a checks-data JSON file that fails to parse or is not an array (`readJsonSafe` swallows the parse error at line 60). scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:545-546 exits 1 only when zero docs pages are found. The CI drift gate at .github/workflows/ci.yml:80-82 regenerates from the same tree and diffs, so it produces the identical truncated file and passes; I verified separately that `git diff --exit-code --ignore-matching-lines='compiled from'` does correctly ignore the date line and still exits 1 on a real content change, so that gate works as intended for its actual purpose (an edited source with a stale committed output). The only in-script drift detector is mtime-based (scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:614-623 and scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs:295-306, both computing `daysStale > 30` from `statSync().mtimeMs`), and git does not record mtimes, so on any fresh clone (CI, the Docker build's `COPY . .`, a self-hoster's `git clone`) every file carries the checkout time and `daysStale` is approximately zero. That warning cannot fire in any environment that produces a shipped artifact, and it is a `console.warn` that would not fail the build even if it did.
findings.impact: Renaming or breaking a single legal page or checks-data category silently shrinks the compiled AI knowledge, the build stays green, the CI drift gate stays green, and the assistant answers about retention policy or an entire check category from nothing. There is no signal anywhere.
findings.recommendation: In scripts/compile-legal-knowledge.mjs replace the `continue` at line 271 with `process.exit(1)`, since PAGES is a fixed list and a missing entry is a bug. In scripts/compile-checks-knowledge.mjs make a non-array or unparseable checks-data file fatal. Add a floor assertion to each script (expected page count, expected minimum check count) so a silent shrink fails loudly. Delete the two dead mtime staleness blocks: ci.yml:80-82 already covers the case they were meant to catch.

findings.title: SECURITY.md's release-verification snippet fails as written: it names the checksum file with the wrong case and pipes a five-file manifest into sha256sum -c after telling the reader to download one file
findings.description: SECURITY.md:81 lists the asset as "**SHA256SUMS.txt**", but release.yml:222 writes `sha256sums.txt` (lowercase), lib/updater/apply.ts:87 looks it up as `sha256sums.txt`, and lib/updater/github-release.ts's `findAsset` is documented as a "Case-sensitive lookup by exact asset filename". The live release assets confirm the lowercase name. Separately, the verification command at SECURITY.md:110-111 is `curl -sL .../sha256sums.txt | sha256sum -c -`, but release.yml:220 builds that file from `(*.tar.gz *.zip *.cdx.json)`, so it lists five artifacts. A reader who downloaded only the tarball, which is what the surrounding text describes, gets "No such file or directory" for the two extension zips and the SBOM, a "WARNING: 4 listed files could not be read" line, and a non-zero exit, so the documented verification appears to fail on a perfectly good release. Merged from doc-18, which found the same SECURITY.md:81 case mismatch from the documentation side and adds one further defect: the artifact list at :77-88 omits the two extension zips that release.yml attaches, and those carry the extension's own version rather than the app version.
findings.impact: A security-conscious self-hoster following the project's own SECURITY.md either 404s on the filename or sees the integrity check report failures on a valid release, and has no way to tell that from a real tamper signal. For a security product this is the one document that has to be exactly right.
findings.recommendation: Change SECURITY.md:81 to `sha256sums.txt` and change the command at line 110 to `sha256sum --ignore-missing -c -`, or list the full asset set the reader is expected to download first.

findings.title: The dependabot auto-merge workflow's header promises patch and minor updates but the condition only ever matches patch
findings.description: .github/workflows/dependabot-auto-merge.yml:3 states "Auto-merge patch and minor dependabot updates after CI passes" and line 4 says "Major updates (e.g. next major bump) are NOT auto-merged", implying minor is in scope. The condition at line 30 is `steps.metadata.outputs.update-type == 'version-update:semver-patch'` and nothing tests for `semver-minor`, so every minor bump sits waiting for a human despite the documented behaviour. The header also names "after CI passes" as the gate, which per ci-03 is not enforced.
findings.impact: Minor bumps queue up unattended because a maintainer reading the header believes they are handled automatically. Combined with .github/dependabot.yml's grouped updates (where `update-type` reports the highest change in the group), most weeks' PRs fall outside the patch-only condition and no one is watching for them.
findings.recommendation: Either extend the condition at dependabot-auto-merge.yml:30 to `(update-type == 'version-update:semver-patch' || update-type == 'version-update:semver-minor')`, or correct the header at line 3 to say patch only. Decide deliberately: minor bumps of the grouped `next-stack` and `ui` groups are exactly the ones a human should look at.

findings.title: Releases are cosign-signed but carry no build provenance, and nothing verifies that the git tag matches the version the image reports
findings.description: docker-publish.yml signs the image (lines 70-76) and release.yml signs the source tarball (lines 230-232), both keyless via Fulcio and Rekor. A cosign signature attests who signed, not what went into the artifact: there is no `actions/attest-build-provenance` step, no `--provenance` on the build (the build is a plain `docker build` at line 49, so buildx provenance is not produced either), and no SLSA attestation anywhere. Separately, nothing in either workflow checks that the pushed tag agrees with `package.json` (`3.7.2`) or `lib/config/config-values.ts:17` (`CONFIG_APP_VERSION = "3.7.2"`), which is the value the running container reports from app/api/version/route.ts and which the self-updater compares against the GitHub tag. A tag pushed without the matching version bump produces an image that permanently reports itself "behind" and re-offers the same update.
findings.impact: A verifier can confirm a release was signed by this repository's Actions identity but cannot confirm which commit, workflow inputs, or base image produced the layers, which is the property SLSA provenance exists to give and the one a security product's consumers are most likely to ask for. The missing tag-versus-version check makes a mismatched release possible with no signal until self-hosters see a permanent update prompt.
findings.recommendation: Add `actions/attest-build-provenance` after the push in docker-publish.yml (the job already has `id-token: write`) or switch to `docker/build-push-action` with `provenance: mode=max`, and attest the release tarball in release.yml the same way. Add a first step to docker-publish.yml that fails if `${GITHUB_REF_NAME#v}` does not equal `node -p "require('./package.json').version"` and CONFIG_APP_VERSION.

findings.title: The Docker sections of the docs describe a smoke-test service, a DB_PORT binding and an env_file that the compose file does not have, and describe db:create two contradictory ways on two pages
findings.description: Static comparison of the four self-host docs against docker-compose.yml. (1) app/docs/setup/page.tsx:570-571 and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:241-242 both say the compose provisions "Postgres + app + healthcheck + smoke test"; there are two services in docker-compose.yml:12-112 and no smoke-test service. (2) app/docs/setup/page.tsx:631-633 tells the operator to set DB_PORT=5432 under a "# Ports" heading described as "Used by docker-compose.yml"; DB_PORT appears nowhere in either compose file and the postgres service publishes no ports at all, deliberately. (3) The env_file claim at app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:243-244 is covered in host-03. (4) db:create is described as the fresh-install initialiser in README.md:81-82 and as the recovery command in instrumentation.ts:127-128, but correctly as a side-by-side clone for testing an upgrade on a copy of production at app/docs/setup/page.tsx:731-745; the script's own header (scripts/create-fresh-db/create-fresh-db.mjs:3-18) agrees with the setup page. Related: AUDIT-009#migration-06 recorded that db:create and db:migrate cannot be driven non-interactively, which is a further reason README.md:82's one-liner would not work even with the script present.
findings.impact: An operator comparing the docs against the shipped compose finds three things that are not there, which erodes trust in the rest of the page, and the two contradictory descriptions of db:create mean whichever page they read first determines whether they expect a fresh install or a clone.
findings.recommendation: Delete the "smoke test" clause at app/docs/setup/page.tsx:571 and app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:242, drop DB_PORT from the setup page's env block at :633 or add a ports mapping to the postgres service, and make README.md:81-82 match the setup page's accurate description of db:create once host-01 and host-02 are resolved.

findings.title: .dockerignore patterns are root-anchored, so nested .env files (marketing/.env exists in this tree), the .claude worktree copy, audits/ and databases/ all enter the build context for the documented local-build path
findings.description: Static analysis. Docker matches .dockerignore patterns against the whole context-relative path using filepath.Match semantics, where * does not cross a /, and only ** crosses directories. So `.env`, `.env.*` and `.env*.local` at .dockerignore:4-6 exclude only root-level dotenv files, and `node_modules` at :1 excludes only the root node_modules. A directory listing of this working tree shows ./marketing/.env present, which is not matched by any pattern; .claude/ (which per the audit brief holds a full second checkout at .claude/worktrees/agent-ad8a7d09dcde23fcc/, including its own node_modules), audits/, databases/ (gitignored at .gitignore:12 and described there as holding real pre-migration database backups), and cli/ are not listed either. Dockerfile:27 is `COPY . .`, so all of that lands in the builder stage. It does NOT reach the published image: the runner stage copies only public, .next, node_modules, package.json and next.config.mjs (Dockerfile:75-79), so the final artifact is clean. The exposure is the build context transfer and the builder layer cache on whatever machine runs the documented `docker compose -f docker-compose.dev.yml up -d --build` (docker-compose.dev.yml:14).
findings.impact: Local image builds copy hundreds of megabytes of irrelevant tree, including a second full checkout, into the daemon and the layer cache, slowing every build. A nested .env with real values sits in the builder layer, which is retained in the local build cache and would be pushed if anyone ever added a cache-export or a stage that copies more broadly. Real but bounded, because the shipped image is unaffected today.
findings.recommendation: Change the patterns in .dockerignore to their recursive forms (`**/.env`, `**/.env.*`, `**/node_modules`) and add `.claude`, `audits`, `databases`, `marketing`, `coverage`, `graphify-out` and `docker-compose.dev.yml`. Keep the `!.env.example` re-include after the broadened dotenv rules.

findings.title: The version endpoint is listed as `/api/version` under a `/api/v3` base URL, so the documented full path 404s
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:1168-1174 sets the Endpoints section's stated Base URL to `{APP_URL}/api/v3`, and every other card's `path` is relative to it. The version card at :618-637 sets `path: "/api/version"`, which components/docs/docs-endpoint-card.tsx:36-38 renders verbatim, and EndpointTable (:1201-1208) lists it the same way. Composed against the stated base that reads `{APP_URL}/api/v3/api/version`; the real route is app/api/version/route.ts, i.e. `{APP_URL}/api/version`, and there is no /api/v3/version route in the tree.
findings.impact: A reader following the base-URL convention gets a 404 on the one endpoint on the page that needs no authentication, which is exactly the one people try first to check connectivity.
findings.recommendation: Either move the version route to app/api/v3/version/route.ts and change the card's path to `/version`, or annotate the card in app/docs/api/page.tsx:618-621 that this endpoint is version-independent and lives at `{APP_URL}/api/version`.

findings.title: The GET /finding-types response example reports 754 checks and per-category counts that predate the 43 page checks, contradicting the note directly below it
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:645-686 shows `"count": 754` with a `categories` map matching the legacy JSON files exactly (content 144, headers 138, cookies 29, information-disclosure 47, secrets-extended 58, supply-chain 14). app/api/v3/finding-types/route.ts:6-19 serves `allCheckDefs` and `getCategoryCounts()`, and lib/scanner/registry.ts:242 defines `allCheckDefs = [...legacyCheckDefs, ...pageCheckDefs]` with getCategoryCounts (:375-382) counting the same combined list. The generated constants at lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts give 754 legacy + 43 page = 797 across 18 categories, and the page checks land in six existing categories (content +11, cookies +8, headers +7, information-disclosure +6, secrets-extended +4, supply-chain +7), so the real response is count 797 with six of the eighteen category numbers higher than shown. The note at :689 in the same card already states 797/18 from the generated constants, so the card contradicts itself.
findings.impact: Minor and self-mitigating (the note at :689 tells readers to read the count from the response), but the example is the part people copy into fixtures and tests.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the example in app/docs/api/page.tsx:645-686 from lib/scanner/registry.ts's getCategoryCounts, or interpolate EXACT_CHECK_COUNT the way :689 already does so it cannot go stale again.

findings.title: Four Bearer-capable endpoints are missing from the API reference, and one of them is cross-referenced as if it were documented "below"
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:250 tells the reader the AI-verify endpoint "Shares its per-account rate limit with POST /scan/verify-batch below", but no card for /scan/verify-batch exists anywhere on the page or in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts (grep for verify-batch across app/docs finds only this line and a passing mention at app/docs/ai/page.tsx:336). Grepping app/api for BEARER_PREFIX/validateApiKey returns 16 API-key-capable routes; the reference's 28 cards cover 11 of them, leaving /scan/verify-batch, /history/[id]/report (documented only in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:198 and app/docs/reports), /scan/reputation (app/api/v3/scan/reputation/route.ts:82, the endpoint the browser extension uses) and /scan/discover/progress/[requestId] (a documented-nowhere progress poll that app/api/v3/scan/discover/route.ts:97 accepts a `requestId` body field to enable) undocumented on the API reference page.
findings.impact: The one dangling "see below" reference sends a reader hunting for a section that does not exist. More materially, an integrator reading the reference has no way to discover batch AI verification, report export, or the discovery progress stream, all of which work with the key they already hold.
findings.recommendation: Add endpoint cards for POST /scan/verify-batch, GET /history/{id}/report (linking to /docs/reports) and GET /scan/discover/progress/{requestId} in app/docs/api/page.tsx's `endpoints` array, and document the `requestId` body field on the POST /scan/discover card so the progress endpoint is reachable.

findings.title: The crawl-discover doc cites a 20-URL cap from a `MAX_PAGES` constant that does not exist; the real cap is CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES = 500
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:364 states "Returns up to 20 URLs (MAX_PAGES in app/api/v3/scan/crawl/discover/route.ts)". That file contains no MAX_PAGES identifier; it resolves `CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES` through getSettings (app/api/v3/scan/crawl/discover/route.ts:74-79), whose shipped default is 500 (lib/config/config-values.ts:594, registry entry at lib/config/registry.ts:1859-1862). The same card's :366 claim of "the standard per-IP scan rate limit (100/hour)" is per-user, not per-IP (the key is `scan:${userId}`, see apidoc-05).
findings.impact: A caller sizing a crawl preview budgets for 20 URLs and gets up to 500, and the cited constant name gives a maintainer nothing to grep for.
findings.recommendation: Replace app/docs/api/page.tsx:364 with the real setting name and value (CRAWL_DISCOVER_MAX_PAGES, default 500, admin-configurable) and correct the rate-limit scope wording at :366.

findings.title: The rate-limits page advises splitting load across "up to 3 active API keys per user"; the cap is per-plan 1 / 3 / 10 / unlimited
findings.description: app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:450-453 recommends "Use multiple keys. You can have up to 3 active API keys per user. Split workload by key to get separate quotas." lib/billing/catalog.ts sets apiKeys to 1 (free, :117), 3 (core, :149), 10 (pro, :181) and -1 (elite, :212), enforced in app/api/v3/keys/route.ts:78-86 via withinPlanLimit. app/docs/api/page.tsx:1142-1145 states this correctly ("one on the free tier, more on paid plans"), so the two pages disagree.
findings.impact: A free user follows the advice, hits the 1-key ceiling with a 400, and has no way to tell from this page whether that is a bug or their plan. A Pro user misses seven of the ten keys they are entitled to.
findings.recommendation: Replace the flat 3 in app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:452 with the per-plan table from lib/billing/catalog.ts, or link to the API reference's correct wording.

findings.title: The per-IP limits table lists a 1-per-minute limit on POST /auth/2fa/email-send that has no CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_* pair and is not an IP limit
findings.description: app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:225-229 lists "POST /api/v3/auth/2fa/email-send: 1 attempt / 1 minute" in a table introduced at :190-196 as "IP-based rate limits ... configured in lib/config/config-values.ts as CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_*_ATTEMPTS + _WINDOW_MINUTES pairs". No CONFIG_RATE_LIMIT_2FA_EMAIL_SEND_* pair exists (grep of lib/config/config-values.ts:457-538 lists all 16 pairs and there is none). app/api/v3/auth/2fa/email-send/route.ts:45-58 implements a per-user resend cooldown instead, reading EMAIL_2FA_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS and querying email_2fa_codes for a recent row, keyed on the pending-2FA cookie's userId, not on the IP. The same table omits nine limits that do have registry pairs and are enforced: browserSession 20/60, aiChat 60/60, aiVerify 20/60, aiSummary 20/60, adminReauth 10/15, billingVerify 5/5, teamInvite 20/60, scanTags 60/60 and publicScans 60/1.
findings.impact: An operator tuning the limits looks for a setting that does not exist, and the real knob (EMAIL_2FA_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS) is not mentioned. The nine omitted limits mean the table reads as complete when it covers half the enforced set.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 2fa/email-send row in app/docs/rate-limits/page.tsx:225-229 with the EMAIL_2FA_RESEND_COOLDOWN_SECONDS cooldown, add the nine missing rows from lib/rate-limiting/rate-limit.ts:20-68's CONFIGURABLE_LIMITS map, and add a column stating what each limit is keyed on (IP, user, or account).

findings.title: Two accepted URL schemes are missing from the docs, and POST /scan's own 400 message lists 6 of the 15 protocols it accepts
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:50 lists the accepted schemes as "http/https/ws/wss/ftp/ftps/ssh/smtp/imap/imaps/pop3/pop3s/mongodb". lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:86-101's SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS also accepts `sftp:` and `smtps:`, which isValidUrl (:117-124) checks against directly. Separately, the 400 body app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:265-273 returns on a rejected scheme reads "Invalid URL. Supported protocols: http://, https://, ws://, wss://, ftp://, ftps://", naming 6 of the 15 accepted schemes, so a caller who mistypes an ssh:// URL is told ssh is unsupported.
findings.impact: Two working schemes are undiscoverable, and the runtime error message actively contradicts the docs for the nine protocol schemes it omits.
findings.recommendation: Add sftp and smtps to app/docs/api/page.tsx:50, and build the error string in app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:269 from SUPPORTED_PROTOCOLS instead of a hardcoded six-item list.

findings.title: The API-key 429 on POST /scan hardcodes "50 requests per 24 hours" regardless of the key's actual limit
findings.description: app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:123-130 returns `{ error: "Rate limit exceeded. 50 requests per 24 hours.", limit: rateLimit.limit, used, remaining, resets_at }`. The structured fields are correct, but the human-readable string is a literal 50 while the real limit is the key's daily_limit, itself set from the plan's apiRequestsPerDay (see apidoc-08): 25 on free, 100 on core, 5000 on pro, 999999 on elite. app/docs/api/page.tsx:1392-1399 documents the 429 body as carrying the true numbers, which it does, so only the message disagrees.
findings.impact: A Pro user cut off after 5,000 requests reads that their key allows 50 and opens a support ticket; a free user cut off at 25 reads 50 and assumes a bug.
findings.recommendation: Interpolate `rateLimit.limit` into the message at app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:125, matching the wording app/api/v3/history/route.ts:187 already uses.

findings.title: Extends AUDIT-011#drift-31: the browser-sessions endpoints return six status codes the docs never list, including a 402 and a 503 a client must distinguish
findings.description: AUDIT-011#drift-31 covered the wrong TTL default (300 vs the real 360 at lib/config/config-values.ts:913-914) and the two undocumented body fields (`ttl`, `viewport`). New here is the error inventory. app/docs/api/page.tsx:547-553 lists only 401 and 503 for POST /browser/sessions; the route also returns 429 (per-user session rate limit, app/api/v3/browser/sessions/route.ts:76-81), 402 ("Browserbase minute quota exceeded", :88-94, the only 402 in the entire API), 400 (non-http/non-IPv4 url, and a failed validateScanTarget, :103-114), 503 with a different meaning ("Live-browser capacity is full right now", :131-136, distinct from the documented "not configured"), 502 ("BrowserBase returned a session with no id", :152-158) and 500 (ownership-row insert failure, :194-205). GET (:578-588) and DELETE (:609-615) omit 400 ("Missing session id.", :245 and :306) and 403 (another user's session, :262 and :322). The docs also never mention the 30-second floor applied by `Math.max(30, Math.min(requested, MAX))` at :52.
findings.impact: The two 503s mean opposite things: one is permanent for the deployment (BrowserBase not configured, retry never helps) and one is transient (capacity full, retry in a moment). A client cannot tell them apart from the docs, and has no branch at all for the 402 that fires when the plan's monthly minutes run out.
findings.recommendation: Extend the three browser-session cards in app/docs/api/page.tsx:547-615 with 400, 402, 403, 429, 500 and 502, split the two 503 meanings into distinct rows, and document the 30-second minimum TTL alongside the 360-second maximum fix from AUDIT-011#drift-31.

findings.title: The docs-knowledge compiler's staleness warning can never fire, and its page scan misses any nested docs page
findings.description: scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs:609 writes the output file, and :614-625 then compares `statSync(OUTPUT).mtimeMs` against the newest page.tsx mtime to warn when "docs were edited N days after this knowledge file". Because the stat runs after the write, knowledgeMtime is always the current time and newestPage is always in the past, so `daysStale` is always negative and the `> 30` branch is unreachable. Separately, listDocPages (:66-81) reads only the immediate children of app/docs, so app/docs/api/playground/page.tsx is silently skipped: the run compiles 19 of the 20 docs pages, and the generated extraction-summary table (lib/ai/docs-knowledge.md:2163-2181) lists 19 routes with no playground row.
findings.impact: The guard that was written to catch exactly the drift this section audits for is dead code, and any future docs page nested one level deeper (the pattern app/docs/api/playground already established) is excluded from the AI assistant's knowledge with no warning.
findings.recommendation: Move the mtime read in scripts/compile-docs-knowledge.mjs to before the writeFileSync at :609, and make listDocPages (:66-81) walk app/docs recursively for page.tsx instead of reading one directory level.

findings.title: The OpenAPI report endpoint marks `format` required though it defaults to json, and its enum omits the accepted `markdown` alias
findings.description: lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:206-215 declares the `format` query parameter on /history/{id}/report as `required: true` with `enum: ["sarif", "pdf", "md", "compliance", "json"]`. app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts:60-62 reads `searchParams.get("format") || "json"` and lowercases it, so the parameter is optional and defaults to json, and FORMATS (:36-43) also accepts `markdown` as an alias for `md`. app/docs/reports/page.tsx:40 and :70 document both facts correctly, so the spec is the outlier.
findings.impact: A generated client makes format a mandatory argument and rejects the `markdown` value the API accepts, and a spec-driven validator flags a legal request as invalid.
findings.recommendation: In lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:206-215 drop `required: true`, add `default: "json"`, and add `"markdown"` to the enum.

findings.title: The version endpoint doc claims current/latest may be populated from cache when status is unknown; the route always sets latest to null on that path
findings.description: app/docs/api/page.tsx:632-635 notes for GET /api/version: "status: up-to-date | behind | ahead | unknown" and "When status is unknown, current/latest may still be populated from cache." app/api/version/route.ts has exactly two unknown paths, the non-ok GitHub response (:19-27) and the catch (:44-52), and both hardcode `latest: null`. `current` is always the compiled APP_VERSION and is never cache-derived. The `next: { revalidate: 3600 }` cache at :15 is on the upstream fetch, and a cache hit produces a normal status, never `unknown`.
findings.impact: A self-hosted updater that trusts `latest` when status is unknown dereferences null.
findings.recommendation: Change the note at app/docs/api/page.tsx:634 to "when status is unknown, latest is null and release_url points at the releases index".

findings.title: Five request-body fields the scan endpoints accept are documented nowhere, including the two that change a scan's privacy and cost
findings.description: Diffing the documented request bodies against what each route parses: POST /scan (app/docs/api/page.tsx:41-44) omits `isPublic` (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:232, resolved through resolveScanIsPublic at :348-351), `captureScreenshot` (:236) and `portScan` (:241). POST /scan/crawl (:323-326) omits `scanners`, `captureScreenshot`, `portScan`, `auth` and `isPublic` (app/api/v3/scan/crawl/route.ts:200-222, :419-422). POST /scan/authenticated (:139-147) omits `scanners` and `isPublic` (app/api/v3/scan/authenticated/route.ts:116/129), and its documented response omits the `dangerScore` and `engineConfidence` fields the route returns (:538-548). POST /scan/discover (:381-384) omits `requestId` (app/api/v3/scan/discover/route.ts:96-97), the field that enables the progress endpoint. lib/api/openapi-spec.ts documents `isPublic` on BulkScanRequest (:781-786) but on none of the others.
findings.impact: `isPublic` decides whether a scan is world-readable and whether it feeds host reputation (app/api/v3/scan/route.ts:344-351); an API caller has no documented way to set it and gets the account default silently. `portScan` and `captureScreenshot` are billable capabilities reachable only from the web UI as far as the docs are concerned.
findings.recommendation: Add these fields to the request-body examples and note lists on the POST /scan, /scan/crawl, /scan/authenticated and /scan/discover cards in app/docs/api/page.tsx, and to the ScanRequest schema in lib/api/openapi-spec.ts:696-720, calling out that portScan shares the DOMAIN_NOT_VERIFIED gate with active-probes.

findings.title: RESOLVED IN HEAD: SECURITY-POSTURE.md published the production origin IP and port, which remains in git history
findings.description: At audit time SECURITY-POSTURE.md:131 and :163 published the production origin address and port inside an nginx proxy_pass block, in a git-tracked file in a public GPL repository, in the same document whose section B configures the Cloudflare proxy that exists to keep that origin hidden. RESOLUTION: the owner directed the address be replaced rather than the origin rotated. Both occurrences now carry 203.0.113.10, an address from the RFC 5737 documentation range, labelled in place as an example and explicitly not the real origin. The working tree is clean of it. IMPORTANT CAVEAT, which is why this finding is retained rather than deleted: the real address remains reachable in git history at the commit that first added the file, and in every existing clone and fork, so the edit removes the signpost and not the exposure.
findings.impact: Reduced but not eliminated. Anyone reading the current file learns nothing, but the original value is recoverable from history by anyone who already has or later obtains a clone. Publishing an origin behind Cloudflare lets a reader connect to it directly, which bypasses the edge entirely: DDoS absorption, the WAF and edge rate limiting all stop applying, and the protections described elsewhere in this same document stop being load-bearing.
findings.recommendation: The durable fix does not depend on secrecy and makes the history exposure moot: restrict the origin host firewall to Cloudflare published IP ranges (cloudflare.com/ips, refreshed periodically), or front the origin with a Cloudflare Tunnel so it has no public inbound listener at all. Both are server-side configuration and neither requires rewriting history or rotating the address. Rewriting history to drop the original commit is possible but was deliberately not done: a force push to a public repository breaks every existing clone and fork while the value survives in those copies regardless.

findings.title: The six database pool tunables are documented on /docs/config and set in the production environment but appear nowhere in .env.example
findings.description: lib/database/db.ts:44-76 reads six pool tunables through its tunable() helper: DATABASE_POOL_MAX, DATABASE_POOL_MIN, DATABASE_IDLE_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS and DATABASE_QUERY_TIMEOUT_MS. app/docs/config/page.tsx:823-845 documents all six under 'Database pool tuning (optional)'. None of the six appears in .env.example, set or commented. Comparing key names only, the working tree's .env.local sets exactly two variables that .env.example does not have, and both are from this group (DATABASE_POOL_MAX and DATABASE_CONNECTION_TIMEOUT_MS), so the production deployment relies on tunables the shipped template does not mention. A bad value here is not silently ignored: lib/database/db.ts:49-54 throws on any non-finite or negative value.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who copies .env.example gets no template or comment for the six knobs the docs tell them to reach for, so they either miss them or guess the spelling and hit the throw at lib/database/db.ts:49. The three-way disagreement (read by code, documented in the docs, absent from the example) is exactly the drift .env.example exists to prevent.
findings.recommendation: Add a commented 'Database pool tuning (optional)' block to .env.example listing all six keys with their shipped defaults from CONFIG_DB_* in lib/config/config-values.ts, mirroring the wording at app/docs/config/page.tsx:823-845.

findings.title: Two documented defaults disagree with the code, and .env.example points readers at the wrong docs page for the CONFIG_* reference
findings.description: lib/config/config-values.ts:907-909 documents the tunable as 'CONFIG_BROWSERBASE_MAX_TTL_SECONDS = 300 (5 min hard cap, matches the product promise and prevents runaway sessions)', while :913 sets it to 360 and :911-912 and :1307 both describe it correctly as 6 minutes. The stated default is 60 seconds below the shipped one, which is the same class of error AUDIT-011#drift-31 found on the API reference page for the same subsystem. Separately, .env.example:329-330 tells the reader 'See docs/setup for the full reference' for the CONFIG_* values; the CONFIG_* reference is /docs/config (components/docs/docs-nav.ts:82-85), and /docs/setup is the install guide. CLAUDE.md:118 also gives TOTAL_CHECKS_LABEL as 'e.g., "310+"' where lib/config/check-stats.generated.ts:8 generates "795+".
findings.impact: Small individually, but the browserbase one is a doc-comment that sits four lines above the constant it misdescribes, so anyone tuning session length believes they are lowering a cap that is already lower than reality. The .env.example pointer sends a self-hoster to a page that does not have what they were promised.
findings.recommendation: Fix the comment at lib/config/config-values.ts:908 to 360 (6 min) so it matches :911-913, change .env.example:330 to 'See /docs/config for the full reference', and either update the CLAUDE.md example to the current label or drop the number since it is generated.

findings.title: Extends AUDIT-011#drift-28: CONTACT_EMAIL is still documented as a working override on /docs/config and is wired through .env.example, both compose files and CI, while nothing reads it
findings.description: AUDIT-011#drift-28 established that CONTACT_EMAIL is parsed at lib/config/env.ts:85 but never consulted, because app/api/v3/contact/route.ts:146 sends to NOREPLY_EMAIL. What is new is how far the dead variable is plumbed: app/docs/config/page.tsx:987-995 still tells self-hosters that CONTACT_EMAIL and SUPPORT_EMAIL 'override the addresses used by contact/support emails' (SUPPORT_EMAIL is genuinely read at lib/config/constants.ts, CONTACT_EMAIL is not), .env.example:84 sets it, docker-compose.yml:69 and docker-compose.dev.yml:57 both forward it, and .github/workflows/ci.yml:179 sets it. Five surfaces carry a variable with zero readers, one of which promises behaviour.
findings.impact: A self-hoster sets CONTACT_EMAIL as documented, forwards it through compose as the shipped compose file already does, and contact mail still goes somewhere else with no error. The doc sentence pairs it with SUPPORT_EMAIL, which does work, so the failure looks like a bug rather than a documentation error.
findings.recommendation: Pick one: honour it in app/api/v3/contact/route.ts, or delete it from lib/config/env.ts:85, app/docs/config/page.tsx:990, .env.example:84, both compose files and ci.yml:179. If it is kept, split the doc sentence so only SUPPORT_EMAIL is described as an override.

findings.title: The extension README's project-structure tree omits package-source.mjs, misplaces the popup and options entry points, and lists 7 of the 16 files in src/lib
findings.description: extension/README.md:115-138 draws the project structure. The scripts/ block at :124-127 lists build.mjs, generate-icons.mjs and package.mjs but not package-source.mjs, even though the README's own prose at :28-30 describes it and extension/package.json's `build` script chains it third. The src/ block at :131-137 puts html and css inside src/popup/ and src/options/, but popup.html, popup.css, options.html, options.css and welcome.html all sit at src/ root; src/popup/ holds popup.ts plus a components/ directory and src/options/ holds only options.ts. src/lib is described as 'api, auth, storage, types, categories, format, theme' (7) where the directory has 16 files, and src/content/ is described as 'detector (page metadata)' while it also contains reputation-card.ts.
findings.impact: Minor, but the tree is the first thing a new contributor reads to find where a change goes, and the two entry-point directories are exactly where they would look for the popup markup. Everything else in this README checks out: '18 check families + 6 service probes' at :7 matches extension/src/lib/categories.ts exactly, every documented npm script exists, and the firefox strict_min_version claim matches manifest/firefox.json:15.
findings.recommendation: Regenerate the tree at extension/README.md:115-138 from an actual listing, add package-source.mjs, and move the html and css entries to the src/ root level where they live.

findings.title: Seven in-app logo renders hardcode /favicon.svg or /favicon.png while LOGO_URL exists as both a constant and an admin setting, so a self-hoster's configured logo appears only in email and JSON-LD
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts:205 defines `LOGO_URL = process.env.LOGO_URL || `${APP_URL}${CONFIG_LOGO_URL}``, .env.example:94-95 documents the LOGO_URL override, and lib/config/registry.ts registers LOGO_URL as a build-tier setting. Only two places consume it: lib/email/email.ts:111-113 (the email header image) and components/seo/structured-data.tsx:92 (Organization logo). Seven other renders hardcode the asset path instead: app/manifest.ts:27 and :28 (PWA install icons), app/layout.tsx:63, :64 and :66 (favicon and apple-touch-icon), components/shared/themed-logo.tsx:27 (the shared logo component used in the header and footer) and components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1345. Separately, components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:56 builds the admin's email preview with a hardcoded `${appUrl}/favicon.svg`, so the preview diverges from the real email whenever LOGO_URL is set.
findings.impact: A self-hoster who sets LOGO_URL to their own mark sees it in outgoing email and in structured data, and nowhere in the product. Every header, footer, browser tab, PWA install icon and AI chat avatar keeps rendering public/favicon.svg. The practical workaround (overwrite public/favicon.svg and public/favicon.png) is fine but undocumented, and it is not available on the pinned-image Docker path where public/ is baked in. The admin email preview showing a different logo than the mail that actually goes out is a small correctness bug on top.
findings.recommendation: Either use the constant where it is a same-origin path (components/shared/themed-logo.tsx:27 and components/ai-chat/chat-widget.tsx:1345 can use CONFIG_LOGO_URL, the relative form, rather than the absolute LOGO_URL), or document in app/docs/config/page.tsx's branding section that the in-app logo is the file public/favicon.svg and LOGO_URL only affects email and structured data. Fix components/admin/shared/email-preview-html.ts:56 to use LOGO_URL either way so the preview matches lib/email/email.ts:111-113.

findings.title: public/og-image.png bakes "VulnRadar" and "vulnradar.dev" into the pixels of the social card, and no documentation mentions the script that regenerates it
findings.description: lib/config/config-values.ts:226 exposes CONFIG_SEO_OG_IMAGE = "/og-image.png" as a configurable SEO value, and lib/config/registry.ts registers SEO_OG_IMAGE, SEO_OG_IMAGE_WIDTH and SEO_OG_IMAGE_HEIGHT as admin-editable. The file the path points at is fixed content: public/og-image.svg:43 draws the wordmark "VulnRadar" and :58 draws "vulnradar.dev", and public/og-image.png is the 110 KB rasterisation of it. The config comment at :222-225 names the regeneration step ("edit public/og-image.svg then run `node scripts/build-og-image.mjs`"), but that instruction appears nowhere a self-hoster reads: grepping app/docs/ and README.md for "og-image" or "build-og-image" returns nothing, and the branding section of app/docs/config/page.tsx does not mention it.
findings.impact: A renamed fork that changes CONFIG_APP_NAME and CONFIG_APP_URL still shares a social card reading "VulnRadar / vulnradar.dev" on every Twitter, LinkedIn, Slack and Discord unfurl of their own domain, which is the single most visible piece of branding the product emits. The fix is a two-minute SVG edit plus one script, but it is only discoverable by reading a comment in config-values.ts. On the pinned-image Docker path the asset cannot be changed at all, since public/ is baked into the image.
findings.recommendation: Add a short "Social card" bullet to the branding subsection of app/docs/config/page.tsx (near the CONFIG_LOGO_URL bullet at :238) and to the rebrand block in app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx:140-155: edit public/og-image.svg, run `node scripts/build-og-image.mjs`, rebuild. Better, have scripts/build-og-image.mjs read APP_NAME and the APP_URL hostname from lib/config/config-values.ts and substitute them into the SVG's two text nodes at build time, so a rename regenerates the card automatically and the asset stops being a third hardcoded copy of the brand.

findings.title: The CLI's default API base is a bare literal with no environment variable, unlike its own API token which has VULNRADAR_TOKEN
findings.description: cli/lib.mjs:6 sets `apiBase: "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3"` in DEFAULTS. parseArgs at :56-57 accepts `--api-base <url>`, and app/docs/cli/page.tsx:129-132 documents it as "API base URL, for a self-hosted instance", so the CLI is genuinely repointable, unlike the extension in hc-02. What is missing is the env form: the sibling value on the next line, :26, reads `apiKey: process.env.VULNRADAR_TOKEN || undefined`, and the docs at app/docs/cli/page.tsx:110-112 specifically tell CI users to prefer the environment variable over the flag. There is no VULNRADAR_API_BASE. app/docs/cli/page.tsx:131 also prints the literal "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3" as the documented default rather than deriving it, so a self-hosted instance's own CLI docs page advertises the hosted origin.
findings.impact: A self-hoster using the CLI in CI has to repeat `--api-base https://scanner.theirdomain.com/api/v3` on every invocation in every workflow file, while the token next to it comes from the environment. Forgetting it once sends a scan request, with their API key in the Authorization header, to vulnradar.dev, where the key is not valid: the key leaks to a third-party host in exchange for a 401. Low severity because the flag exists and the failure is loud, but the asymmetry with VULNRADAR_TOKEN is an easy trap.
findings.recommendation: In cli/lib.mjs, change :6 to read `apiBase: process.env.VULNRADAR_API_BASE || "https://vulnradar.dev/api/v3"` so the flag still wins and the env is the CI-friendly default, and add the variable to the options table and the CI guidance in app/docs/cli/page.tsx:110-132. Add a line to cli/README.md as well. The docs table's "Default" cell at :131 can stay literal (it is accurate for an unmodified CLI) but should gain "or VULNRADAR_API_BASE".

findings.title: Renaming a fork requires editing 221 literal "VulnRadar" strings in 54 files that APP_NAME does not cover, concentrated in the changelog, the SEO comparison pages and the extension
findings.description: Scope of the measurement: a Node scan of app/, components/, lib/, extension/src/, cli/, public/ and .github/ over .ts, .tsx, .mjs, .json, .svg, .yml, .html and .css, with // and /* */ comments stripped first, counting the literal token "VulnRadar" outside the config layer's own definition. Result: 221 occurrences across 54 files. The distribution matters more than the total. lib/changelog/data.ts has 84 (historical release notes, correctly frozen, should never be templated). lib/seo/alternatives.ts has 23 (the competitor-comparison pages, prose that reads as first-person product claims). lib/config/registry.ts has 12 (help text). extension/src/ has 44 across 10 files, on top of the separate hardcoding in hc-02. app/docs/api/page.tsx has 8 (Python SDK sample code, `from vulnradar import VulnRadar`). The genuinely templated surfaces are in good shape by contrast: every scanner User-Agent derives from APP_NAME (lib/scanner/execute-scan.ts:376, execute-crawl-scan.ts:149, async-checks.ts:2701, crawl-discovery.ts:31, cve-enrichment.ts:111, osv-lookup.ts:88, software-inventory.ts:839, lib/ai/verify-findings.ts:146, lib/admin/alert-webhook.ts:71), and all four report exporters use APP_NAME and APP_URL throughout (lib/reports/pdf-report.ts, markdown-report.ts, sarif-report.ts, compliance-report.ts).
findings.impact: GPL-3.0 makes a rebranded fork a legitimate and expected use, and the product markets itself as self-hostable, so this is a real cost to quantify rather than a defect. The honest number is that APP_NAME covers the app chrome and the reports, and roughly 220 further edits cover everything else, of which maybe 60 are actually user-visible on a renamed instance (the SEO comparison pages, the API docs SDK samples, five OAuth error messages at app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts:193, :215, :281, :493, :536, and the extension surface). The changelog's 84 should stay as they are. One value is a wire protocol and should not be renamed at all: lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:27 sets `SIGNATURE_HEADER = "X-VulnRadar-Signature"`, which every existing customer receiver parses.
findings.recommendation: Do not attempt a blanket rename. Fix the three cheap clusters and document the rest. (1) The five OAuth error messages in app/api/v3/auth/oauth/[provider]/callback/route.ts should use APP_NAME, they are one-line template changes on user-facing error copy. (2) lib/seo/alternatives.ts should take the product name from APP_NAME in its shared VR answers block at :43 rather than repeating the literal 23 times. (3) The extension gets APP_NAME from VULNRADAR.appName in extension/src/lib/constants.ts:7 already; the 44 literals should use it. Then add a "Renaming a fork" subsection to app/docs/self-hosting/page.tsx listing what APP_NAME does and does not cover, naming lib/changelog/data.ts and lib/webhooks/delivery.ts:27 as deliberately not renameable.

findings.title: The port scanner's six network-behaviour constants have no registry entries while every comparable scanner knob does, so connect timeout and 24-way concurrency cannot be tuned
findings.description: lib/scanner/port-scan.ts:248-:255 declares CONCURRENCY = 24, PER_PORT_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 1500, BANNER_READ_WINDOW_MS = 400, OVERALL_DEADLINE_MS = 12_000 and MAX_BANNER_BYTES = 256, plus PORT_SCAN_TTL_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000 at :468. A grep of lib/config/registry.ts for 'port' returns no matching key. The equivalent knob for the other fan-out scanner is configurable: CONFIG_SUBDOMAIN_DISCOVERY_HTTP_CONCURRENCY = 25 (lib/config/config-values.ts:585) has a registry entry. A seventh related literal sits in a different file: app/api/v3/history/[id]/ports/route.ts:89 passes AbortSignal.timeout(20_000) to scanPorts, a number that must stay above OVERALL_DEADLINE_MS but has no comment saying so and no shared constant tying the two together.
findings.impact: 1500 ms is aggressive for a target more than one continent away, and a filtered port on a slow path is reported as closed rather than as unknown. In the other direction, 24 simultaneous connects across the curated port list is what an IDS flags as a port sweep, and a self-hoster scanning their own estate through a firewall they do not control has no way to slow it down short of editing the file.
findings.recommendation: Add PORT_SCAN_CONCURRENCY, PORT_SCAN_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS and PORT_SCAN_OVERALL_DEADLINE_MS to lib/config/config-values.ts and lib/config/registry.ts alongside the existing SUBDOMAIN_DISCOVERY_HTTP_CONCURRENCY entry, and derive the 20_000 in app/api/v3/history/[id]/ports/route.ts:89 from the deadline setting rather than restating it.

findings.title: Thirty-one routes reimplement the rate-limit message instead of using the shared helper, and the inline copies render 'Try again in 1 minute(s).'
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts:297-:298 defines ERROR_MESSAGES.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS(resource, minutes), which pluralizes correctly: `minute${minutes > 1 ? 's' : ''}`. Thirty-one call sites compute `Math.ceil(rl.retryAfterSeconds / 60)` themselves and build their own sentence; the distinct strings include 'Too many 2FA attempts. Try again in N minute(s).', 'Too many AI requests...', 'Too many BrowserBase sessions...', 'Too many domains added recently...', 'Too many tag changes...' (app/api/v3/scan/tags/route.ts:53), 'Too many verification attempts...' (app/api/v3/domains/[id]/verify/route.ts:47), 'Too many requests. Please try again in N minute(s).' and 'Too many contact requests. Please try again in N minute(s).'. Every inline copy uses the literal 'minute(s)' and so prints 'Try again in 1 minute(s).' on the common single-minute case, and the set is split between 'Try again in' and 'Please try again in' for the same event. ERROR_MESSAGES is imported by zero client components (a grep for it across components/ and app/ .tsx files returns nothing), so it is a server-only table.
findings.impact: Users see the parenthetical-plural tell on the most common rate-limit response, and the same 429 is worded three different ways depending on which endpoint they hit. Changing the wording once means editing thirty-one files.
findings.recommendation: Route the thirty-one sites through ERROR_MESSAGES.TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS, extending it with an optional resource-specific noun where the current copy carries one, so the pluralization and the sentence shape live in one place.

findings.title: ERROR_MESSAGES.WEAK_PASSWORD has no callers and states a minimum of 8 characters four lines below the constant that sets it to 12
findings.description: lib/config/constants.ts:294 declares `WEAK_PASSWORD: 'Password must be at least 8 characters long.'`. The same file exports PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH = CONFIG_PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH at :255, and that value is 12 (lib/config/config-values.ts:314) and admin-editable (lib/config/registry.ts:2130). A whole-repo grep for WEAK_PASSWORD returns exactly one hit, the declaration itself, so nothing renders it today. Its live counterpart does it correctly: components/auth/reset-password-form.tsx:101 interpolates `At least ${PASSWORD_MIN_LENGTH} characters` and :106 sets minLength from the same constant.
findings.impact: No user impact today because the string is dead, but it is a loaded gun: the next route that reaches for the obvious ERROR_MESSAGES entry for a weak password ships a message that contradicts the enforced minimum, on a deployment where the operator may have raised it further.
findings.recommendation: Either delete WEAK_PASSWORD or turn it into a function of the resolved minimum, `WEAK_PASSWORD: (min: number) => \`Password must be at least ${min} characters long.\``, matching the TOO_MANY_ATTEMPTS shape three lines above it.
