findings.title: Route-level loading and error boundaries are missing on 61 of 71 pages, but almost every gap is already covered by an in-page state ladder, so the real exposure is narrower than the raw count suggests
findings.description: Measured for this audit, extending AUDIT-011#drift-13 rather than re-filing it. loading.tsx exists for /admin, /assets, /compare, /dashboard, /history, /pricing, /profile, /repos, /shares, /teams (10). error.tsx exists for the same set minus /pricing and /repos (8, plus app/error.tsx and app/global-error.tsx). not-found.tsx exists once, at the root. Of the 61 pages without a route-level loading.tsx, the ones that actually block on data almost all carry their own in-page gate: /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] render SharedScanSkeleton (app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:137, app/host/[hostname]/page.tsx:135), /public-scans renders PublicScansTableSkeleton (:134), /badge renders BadgeSkeleton (:88), /browser/[id] gates at :519, all three /checkout/* pages render CheckoutSkeleton (for example app/checkout/credits/page.tsx:65-67), and /dashboard wraps its own content in Suspense with a real skeleton fallback (app/dashboard/page.tsx:169). The 17 pages that are async server components (all of /legal, /tools, /alternatives, /checks, /security, /landing) resolve from the local registry and config rather than the database, so a missing loading.tsx there costs a paint, not a hang. The genuinely uncovered blocking surfaces are the ones filed separately above and in AUDIT-011#auth-08 (/login, /signup, /reset-password prerender `Suspense fallback={null}`) and #ck-06 (/contact's ticket list returns null while loading). Recorded so the next audit does not re-derive the 61-page number as if it were 61 blank screens.
findings.impact: None directly. This is a negative result: the loading.tsx count understates the product's actual coverage, and prioritising by that count alone would spend effort on static pages while the real blank-screen and never-resolving cases (state-04, state-06, state-08) sit elsewhere.
findings.recommendation: When acting on AUDIT-011#drift-13, prioritise error.tsx over loading.tsx: the segments that most need a boundary are /host/[hostname], /shared/[token] and /browser/[id], where a render-time throw on untrusted server data currently escapes to the full-screen app/error.tsx and destroys the public page chrome. loading.tsx can be skipped entirely for the 17 async server pages.

findings.title: Positive result: DashboardErrorState, the results-list filtered-empty block, /public-scans, /demo, /browser/[id] and repo-detail are the correct in-repo models for these states and should be reused rather than reinvented
findings.description: Recorded so the fixes above have something concrete to copy and so the next audit does not re-derive it. components/scanner/dashboard-error-state.tsx:43-76 classifies a scan failure into seven kinds (blocked, network, rate_limit, validation, server, auth_failed, generic) from the message and status, and :78-onward gives each one a title, an icon, a severity-toned rail and a description that states what happened and then what to do about it, plus a retry. It is the best error component in the product and the only one that distinguishes retryable from permanent. components/scanner/results-list.tsx:597-621 is the model empty state: it says why the list is empty ("N findings are hidden"), what to do, and offers a one-click Reset filters. app/public-scans/page.tsx:134-145 is the model three-way ladder (skeleton, then error, then empty, then data) in a single page. components/repos/repo-detail.tsx:242-255 is the model four-way ladder, spoiled only by the missing finally described in state-04. app/demo/page.tsx:68-92 and app/browser/[id]/page.tsx:519-546 both carry designed error branches. app/shared/[token]/page.tsx:139-158 is the model "this thing does not exist" state, with a specific explanation and a conversion CTA rather than a bare 404. All of them use the established design language: dashed border-border on bg-card/50 for empty, destructive or severity tones for error, and no shadow beyond the shadow-xs baseline.
findings.impact: None. This is coverage of what is already right, so remediation does not invent a seventh visual grammar for an error block.
findings.recommendation: When fixing state-05, state-07, state-10, state-11 and state-16, reuse these: the classified-kind approach from dashboard-error-state.tsx for anything that needs to distinguish retryable from permanent, the dashed empty block (`rounded-md border border-dashed border-border bg-card/50 px-4 py-12 text-center`) with a title, a why line and an action for anything genuinely empty, and a destructive-toned inline band for a load failure inside an otherwise working page. Do not introduce a new shell.

findings.title: AI answer engines cannot reach any of this because Cloudflare AI Crawl Control blocks them at the edge, which is a dashboard toggle and not a code change
findings.description: Recorded so nobody spends a day on it in code. The app does its part: app/robots.ts and app/llms.txt/route.ts exist, lib/config/public-paths.ts explicitly allowlists /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt, /robots.txt and /sitemap.xml for session-less crawlers with a comment explaining that AI crawlers carry no cookie, and components/seo/structured-data.tsx emits SoftwareApplication and FAQPage JSON-LD on the landing page including both extension store URLs. None of that reaches an AI crawler, because Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control feature overrides the application's own robots.txt at the edge and disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended. This was confirmed in prior work as the reason AI assistants do not know the product exists. It is fixed by turning the feature off in the Cloudflare dashboard. Related and separately filed: AUDIT-012#fe-01 found the root layout's await headers() forces all 311 routes dynamic so Cloudflare caches no HTML, which affects crawl budget for the roughly 780 SEO pages, and AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 found the npm name vulnradar is unclaimed while /docs/cli advertises npx vulnradar.
findings.impact: None directly. It explains why the marketing surface described in the other findings does not appear in AI answers, and it prevents a future auditor from proposing code fixes for an edge configuration problem.
findings.recommendation: No code change. The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for vulnradar.dev. Once that is done, the llms.txt and JSON-LD work already in the repo starts being read, and mkt-07's APP_DESCRIPTION rewrite becomes the sentence AI answers actually quote, which is a reason to do mkt-07 before or alongside the toggle.

findings.title: Negative results: the nine landing sections, the demo copy and the pricing hero already meet the voice standard, so a future audit should not re-review them

Zero adjective-only benefit claims of the Lightning Fast / Deep Analysis / Developer First class. The -1 unlimited sentinel is guarded in all three places it is rendered (app/landing/page.tsx:41-47, components/pricing/pricing-faq.tsx, app/pricing/page.tsx:26-31). The findings in this file are about what is missing or what is now false, not about the standard of the prose.
findings.impact: None. Records the parts of the selling surface that are correct so the next audit spends its time on mkt-01 through mkt-04 rather than re-reading nine sections of good copy.
findings.recommendation: No action. When acting on the other findings in this file, preserve these strings verbatim rather than rewriting around them, in particular components/demo/demo-info.tsx, which mkt-01 keeps and only retitles.

findings.title: Verified correct: all 71 pages have page-specific metadata, all 749 check descriptions are unique, the OG image is a correct 1200x630, and there is no indexable duplicate of a scan result
findings.description: Recording what I verified as correct so the next audit does not re-derive it. (1) Metadata coverage is complete: I walked all 71 page.tsx files and resolved each to the nearest metadata source. Zero fall back to the root default. 45 use pageMetadata (indexable, canonical, OG, Twitter, googleBot directives), 25 use privatePageMetadata (noindex, nofollow, nocache), and the only inline case is app/page.tsx, which is a bare `redirect("/landing")` with no content of its own. (2) Hand-written copy is in range: across all 44 description strings and 61 title strings in app/**, zero titles exceed 60 characters with the " | VulnRadar" suffix, zero descriptions exceed 160 except one 163-character TechArticle description const at app/docs/api/playground/layout.tsx:11 (the meta description in the same file is 154), and no two pages share a description. (3) All 749 generated check descriptions are unique, and so are all 749 raw `description` fields in the checks-data JSON. (4) public/og-image.png is exactly 1200x630 at 107.6 KB, twitter.card is "summary_large_image" everywhere (lib/seo/metadata.ts:116), and metadataBase is set (app/layout.tsx:118) so relative image and canonical paths resolve absolute. (5) No indexable duplicate of a scan result exists: there is no /history/[id] page, and /shared/[token] and /host/[hostname] are both noindex, so the same report is never indexable at two URLs. (6) trailingSlash is not set in next.config.js, so Next 308-redirects /path/ to /path and there are no trailing-slash duplicates; the only query-parameter surface on an indexable page is /public-scans?page=N, which canonicalises to /public-scans. (7) The sitemap is 805 URLs (33 hand-listed, 18 categories, 5 alternatives, 749 checks), far under the 50,000-URL and 50 MB limits, so no sitemap index is needed yet. (8) /llms.txt and /llms-full.txt both exist as real routes (app/llms.txt/route.ts, app/llms-full.txt/route.ts) and are among the only 5 prerendered routes in the build. (9) Alt text is a non-issue for discoverability: there are 7 `` elements in all of app/ and components/, and the only one on an indexable page is inside a code sample in app/docs/sharing/page.tsx:386 which already carries an alt. (10) app/layout.tsx:177 renders SiteStructuredData without a nonce while every other JSON-LD call site passes one; this is cosmetic, since a `script type="application/ld+json"` is a data block that the HTML spec returns from before the CSP inline check, so it is not blocked.
findings.impact: None. These are the checks a discoverability audit would otherwise repeat, and the SEO foundation here is genuinely above average for a project this size: a single pageMetadata helper, a routes.ts that derives the generated surfaces from the same loaders the pages use, real JSON-LD across six types, and llms.txt.
findings.recommendation: No action. Use this as the baseline: the defects filed in seo-01 through seo-21 are the delta from an otherwise sound implementation, not a missing foundation.

findings.title: AI crawler access is blocked by Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt at the edge, not by app/robots.ts, so this is a dashboard toggle and no code change will fix it
findings.description: Recording this so nobody spends a day on the wrong file. app/robots.ts:19-43 already declares an explicit AI_CRAWLERS group naming GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-Web, anthropic-ai, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended, Googlebot, Applebot-Extended, CCBot, cohere-ai, Bytespider, Amazonbot and Meta-ExternalAgent, and grants them `Allow: /` with only the same private paths everyone else is denied. The application code is correct and needs no change. Cloudflare's Managed robots.txt (AI Crawl Control) overrides the origin's robots.txt at the edge and Disallows GPTBot, ClaudeBot, CCBot and Google-Extended, which is the confirmed reason AI assistants do not know this product. That is a Cloudflare dashboard setting on the zone, not anything reachable from this repo.
findings.impact: The product publishes /llms.txt, /llms-full.txt and 749 per-check remediation guides specifically so answer engines can cite them, and the edge blocks the crawlers that would read them. Fixing the app's robots.txt would change nothing, because the origin file never reaches those crawlers.
findings.recommendation: The owner toggles Managed robots.txt / AI Crawl Control off in the Cloudflare dashboard for the zone. Verify afterwards by fetching https://vulnradar.dev/robots.txt with `User-Agent: GPTBot` and confirming the response matches what app/robots.ts generates. Do not modify app/robots.ts for this.

findings.title: Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning and an IAST agent are real competitor features that this product should deliberately never build, and saying so is part of the answer
findings.category: list (a) ranks 16 to 18: the deliberate do-not-build list
findings.description: Three capabilities appear in the peer set and belong at the bottom of the ranking with a stated reason rather than in a backlog. (1) Container, IaC, cloud and SCA scanning: Snyk is the only vendor of the eight spanning SAST, SCA, container, IaC, secrets, DAST and SBOM, and the best tool in that space is Trivy, which is free, Apache-2.0, 37,679 stars, emits SARIF 2.1.0 and CycloneDX/SPDX, and would take years to match. VulnRadar's nearest existing capability is deliberately narrow and correct: lib/scanner/github-repo-scan.ts:1 reuses the secrets-extended detectors verbatim against repo file contents, and lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts plus osv-check.ts correlate detected libraries against OSV for the live URL. (2) An IAST agent: only Acunetix ships one (AcuSensor, for PHP, ASP.NET, Java and Node.js), and none of the other seven has a comparable server-side sensor. It would require a per-runtime agent, an installation story, and version support forever, and it directly contradicts the product's own repeated promise that there is nothing to deploy alongside your application (components/landing/landing-features.tsx:4, app/checks/page.tsx's "0 agents to install"). (3) An internal or behind-the-firewall scanning agent, which Snyk and Intruder both ship as a Docker or Kubernetes workload: for this product the self-host path is the answer to that requirement and is strictly better, since the whole scanner runs inside the network rather than a relay.
findings.impact: None if left alone. The risk this finding addresses is the opposite one: each of these is impressive on a competitor's feature matrix, and a small team that chases them spends quarters reaching parity in a market it is not in, while the cheap items in comp-02, comp-03, comp-04, comp-06 and comp-07 stay unbuilt.
findings.recommendation: Record all three as permanent non-goals in AGENTS.md or a short ROADMAP note so they stop reappearing. For (1), do the interop instead of the feature: document the pairing in app/docs ("Trivy for images and dependencies, VulnRadar for the deployed URL"), and since both emit SARIF 2.1.0, both already land in the same GitHub Security tab with no work. For (3), make the self-host answer explicit on the relevant /alternatives rows rather than building an agent: "They give you a relay container. This runs the whole scanner inside your network." That claim depends on comp-01 being fixed first.

findings.title: Position on the 2026 agentic-pentest shift: VulnRadar should deliberately not compete, and should use its determinism as the counter-position
findings.description: Every major vendor launched an agentic AI pentest product this year: Invicti Agentic Pentest (announced 29 to 30 July 2026, parallel specialised agents for SQLi, RCE, XSS, SSRF, XXE, insecure deserialization, path traversal and NoSQLi, max $500 per pentest, 24-hour turnaround), Intruder AI Pentesting from $3,500 per test, Astra autonomous agents, and Snyk Evo Continuous Offensive Security. All are aimed at the buyer who needs a pentest report for an auditor, and all are priced 10x to 100x below a human pentest (audits/AUDIT-014/research-competitors-commercial.md, "The 2026 industry shift"). Three facts from this codebase determine the right answer. First, the product's headline promise is the opposite claim: components/landing/landing-features.tsx:26 to :32 is titled "Run it twice, get the same answer twice" and states "There is no model in the detection path deciding today that something is medium when yesterday it was low", which is what makes lib/scanner/regression-alert.ts's diff and the CI gate in .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml meaningful at all. Second, an agentic pentest requires unattended exploitation against a live target, which this product has structurally refused: the nine active probes are opt-in and gated behind verified domain ownership (lib/scanner/active-probe-catalog.ts:117), and there is no out-of-band channel (comp-11). Third, AI is already used here on the correct side of that line, for triage rather than detection: lib/ai/verify-findings.ts attaches aiVerdict and aiConfidence that re-weight the safety rating (lib/scanner/safety-rating.ts:27 to :40) without changing what the deterministic engine found.
findings.impact: Entering this market would cost the product the one claim it currently wins on, and it would compete on turnaround and exploitation depth against vendors with dedicated infrastructure, insurance and legal cover. Ignoring it silently is also a cost: "why not just buy a $500 agentic pentest" is now a live objection at every price point above free, and there is no answer to it on the site.
findings.recommendation: Do not compete on agentic pentesting. Take the counter-position explicitly, because determinism is a differentiator only if someone states what it is against. Add an FAQ entry to app/landing/page.tsx's buildFaq array, in the existing blunt voice, along these lines: "Do you do AI pentesting? No. The detection engine is deterministic: the same URL produces the same finding IDs every run, which is what lets you fail a build on a specific ID and diff Tuesday against Friday. We use a model to triage and explain findings, never to decide whether one exists." Keep the AI confined to lib/ai/verify-findings.ts's triage role and to the assistant, and never let a model reach the detection path. If a pentest-report artifact is ever wanted, build the attestation page described in comp-14, which is the deliverable that buyer actually needs, rather than the exploitation engine.

findings.title: Verified negative results: five capabilities the prior competitor hypothesis listed as gaps already exist and are complete, so the next audit does not need to re-check them
findings.description: The prior session's candidate list (compliance reports, Jira integration, proof-based exploit evidence, CVE and port scanning, SSO/auth-flow scanning, cloud and container scanning, IAST agent) was a hypothesis. Five items are wrong or substantially wrong and are closed here. (1) Compliance reports EXIST and are complete: lib/reports/compliance-mappings.ts:43 covers PCI DSS 4.0, SOC 2 TSC, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Annex A, OWASP ASVS 4.0, HIPAA and GDPR, with a documented OWASP-Top-10 backbone and an honest unmapped-findings path, rendered by lib/reports/compliance-report.ts and exported at app/api/v3/history/[id]/report/route.ts. (2) SARIF EXISTS and is complete: lib/reports/sarif-report.ts:1 to :253 emits SARIF 2.1.0 with rule descriptors, security-severity and tags, wired to both the export menu (components/scanner/scan-actions-menu.tsx:556) and the API. (3) CVE and port scanning EXIST: lib/scanner/port-scan.ts (749 lines), lib/scanner/protocols/banner.ts, lib/scanner/software-inventory.ts (1,202 lines), lib/scanner/osv-check.ts and lib/scanner/cve-enrichment.ts. (4) Authenticated scanning EXISTS in three modes with a real browser-rendered login path; see comp-05 for what is actually missing. (5) A GitHub Action EXISTS at .github/actions/scan-gate/action.yml (195 lines, complete poll-and-gate); see comp-02 for what it does not do. Also verified and worth recording: the SSL letter grade is computed in-house from a live handshake (lib/scanner/ssl-grade.ts:1 to :30) and is NOT derived from the SSL Labs API, so the SSL Labs v4 prohibition on commercial use does not apply to this product, a risk the research explicitly flagged for checking.
findings.impact: None directly. Recording it prevents the next audit or roadmap session from re-filing five gaps that are already shipped, which is the failure mode that turns a competitive review into busywork.
findings.recommendation: Supersede the earlier seven-item competitor-gap list with this section's ranked list. Of the original seven, only proof-based exploit evidence (comp-11) and Jira (comp-08, and reframed toward closing the GitHub loop first) survive as real gaps, cloud/container and IAST move to the permanent non-goal list (comp-16), and the other three are done. Separately, one item outside section 20's scope but adjacent to it: AUDIT-013#subdeps-01 found the npm name `vulnradar` is unclaimed while /docs/cli advertises `npx vulnradar`, which is a distribution gap of the same kind as comp-02's missing Marketplace listing and should be fixed in the same pass.
